articles.title: Discussing Future Treatment and Care in the ICU: Perspectives From Patients.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Treatment in the intensive care unit (ICU) is usually predicated on curative treatment, but continuing all available treatment options may not always be beneficial for the patient or in line with their wishes. However, patients admitted to the ICU are often assessed as incapable of making decisions regarding their care; hence conversations about wishes for treatment are postponed. This study aimed to investigate the experiences of patients who participated in a conversation concerning treatment and care following ICU discharge based on the Danish version of the Recommended Summary Plan for Emergency Care and Treatment (ReSPECT) form.

abstract.label: METHOD
abstract.text: Semi-structured telephone interviews were conducted with patients who had a conversation about future treatment and care with an intensivist using the ReSPECT form during an ICU admission between November 2024 and July 2025. Relatives who participated in the conversation and were present during the interviews were asked to elaborate on their experiences of the conversation's timing and how they felt about participating in the conversation. Data was analysed using content analysis.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Nineteen patients were included in the study, of whom 15 patients (83%) participated in a telephone interview. Two themes were identified: Timing of the conversation and Clarifying goals of care and options. Based on these, four sub-themes were identified, two for each theme: Too soon, but not much later; Wishes in accordance; Hard, but necessary and Communicating in an understandable manner. Most patients were satisfied with having had a conversation about future treatment and care. Patients found the conversation relevant and necessary. The intensivists were praised for their communication skills and their ability to know and explain recommendations for future treatment and care. However, most patients believed that the conversation was conducted too soon after recovering from intensive care. They would have preferred to have had the conversation later during their admission.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Most participating ICU patients found a conversation about future treatment and care relevant but preferred it to be held after ICU discharge. Future research should investigate the benefits of incorporating intensivists in these conversations in general wards.

abstract.label: EDITORIAL COMMENT
abstract.text: In this prospective study, former ICU patients were interviewed and asked about their experiences and opinions regarding a structured ReSPECT discussion that had been conducted in the end of their ICU stay. The goal of that interview was advance care planning, involving the patients and their family members. This study reports a qualitative analysis of interviews conducted at least 4 weeks later. Two main themes and four subthemes were identified. Almost all patients remembered having had the discussion, but the content was less clearly remembered. ICU physicians' communication skills were appreciated. The study assesses a function of our daily work from patient and family perspective, and discusses important issues such as optimal timing of the advance care planning.

articles.title: [The modern challenges and innovations in training of paramedical personnel].
articles.journal: Probl Sotsialnoi Gig Zdravookhranenniiai Istor Med
articles.journal_full: Problemy sotsial'noi gigieny, zdravookhraneniia i istorii meditsiny

abstract.text: The system of paramedical personnel training is on threshold of significant transformations caused by necessity to adapt to new requirements in health care and education policy. The analysis of current state of training demonstrated presence of such serious problems as normative restraints, deficiency of personnel and insufficient integration of digital technologies. It affects quality of both education and practical readiness of graduates. The implementation of innovative methods, including e-learning, simulation trainers and technologies of virtual and augmented reality becomes key tool to enhance efficiency of educational process. The practical implementation of these approaches in secondary medical education institutions demonstrated increase in motivation of students and improvement of material mastering. However, it still experiences the number of technical and organizational restrictions.

articles.title: [The age structure of patients hospitalized on beds of medical emergency service in the Russian Federation].
articles.journal: Probl Sotsialnoi Gig Zdravookhranenniiai Istor Med
articles.journal_full: Problemy sotsial'noi gigieny, zdravookhraneniia i istorii meditsiny

abstract.text: The state program of the Russian Federation "The Development of Health Care" sets the task to increase the efficiency of emergency medical care provision that is implemented including the development of emergency medical care in hospital conditions.The purpose of the study is to examine age composition of patients hospitalized at emergency medical care beds in the Russian Federation in 2016-2025.The normative legal documents regulating organization of emergency medical care in hospital conditions, data from the Federal statistical observation form № 30 for 2016-2025 concerning the number of children and adults admitted on emergency medical care beds were analyzed. The methods of descriptive statistics were applied.As a result of implementation of organizational technologies of emergency medical care provision in hospital conditions in the Russian Federation in 2016-2025, it is determined that the rate of hospitalization of children on emergency medical care beds increased from 1.76 to 2.66 per 1,000 population aged 0-17 years, adults - from 1.4 to 8.41 per 1,000 population aged 18 years and older. The rate of hospitalization of children on short-stay emergency medical care beds decreased from 1.62 to 0.89 per 1000 population aged 0-17 years. This indicator for adults increased from 0.98 to 5.18 per 1000 population aged 18 years and older. The rate of hospitalization of children on day stay emergency medical care beds increased from 0.14 to 1.77 per 1000 population aged 0-17 years, adults - from 0.42 to 3.23 per 1000 population aged 18 years and older.

articles.title: Management of Patients After Cardiac Arrest.

abstract.text: Cardiac arrest remains a significant cause of morbidity and mortality, although contemporary care now enables potential survival with good neurologic outcome. The core acute management goals for survivors of cardiac arrest are to provide organ support, sustain adequate hemodynamics, and evaluate the underlying cause of the cardiac arrest. In this article, the authors review the current state of knowledge and clinical intensive care unit practice recommendations for patients after cardiac arrest, particularly focusing on important areas of uncertainty, such as targeted temperature management, neuroprognostication, coronary evaluation, and hemodynamic targets.

articles.title: Vaping and E-Cigarettes: An Emergency Department Survey.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To characterise vaping practices and perceptions in a non-consecutive cohort across four Sydney Emergency Departments (EDs) prior to 2024 Australian legislative changes restricting disposable vapes.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: An anonymous digital survey of up to 40 questions was conducted from May 2023 to January 2024 in patients and visitors aged > 14 years. It assessed demographics, vaping and smoking practices, perceived addiction, side effects and attitudes. Participants were recruited via posters and distribution of linked QR codes.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 1263 surveys initiated, 1049 (83.1%) were completed. Among respondents who answered the vaping-status question 51.1% (614/1202) reported ever vaping with 34.4% (211/614) vaping daily. Respondents were more often able to report the puff count and duration of their most recently purchased device (> 85%) than puffs per day or sessions per day (≈60%). Disposable vapes and fruit/candy flavours were most reportedly used. Addiction and anxiety relief were frequently selected reasons for vaping, and daily vapers reported higher perceived addiction scores. Symptoms occurring during or shortly after vaping were commonly reported, most frequently cough (174/308, 56.5%), breathlessness (165/308, 53.6%) and chest pain (98/308, 31.8%). Daily vapers more commonly perceived vaping as safer than cigarettes (101/198, 51.0% vs. 88/568, 15.5% in never vapers) and as an effective smoking cessation aid (105/197, 53.3% vs. 83/571, 14.5%).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: In this multicentre, non-consecutive survey, vaping was commonly reported, particularly among younger respondents, with frequent daily use and perceived addiction. These findings highlight the importance of asking about vaping and awareness of patterns of use, perceived addiction and reported symptoms.

articles.title: Rural Pathologies: A Late Presentation Special.

abstract.text: Patients in rural and remote Australia often present later and with more advanced disease compared to major and regional cities. Drawing on experience as a junior doctor in the Cape and in rural emergency departments, this article explores how geographic isolation, limited resources, health literacy challenges and inequities in access shape these presentations. Cases include a critically unwell patient managed overnight in a makeshift intensive care bay when weather delayed retrieval, a family of young children with Norwegian Scabies, and a partial finger amputation complicated by weekend staffing shortages. The article reviews Australian evidence on sepsis, scabies and its link to rheumatic heart disease and trauma outcomes, all of which tend to be more challenging to manage. Timely care in rural and remote communities depends on early recognition, clear communication and close collaboration between rural generalists, FACEMs, retrieval services and specialist teams.

articles.title: Predictors of Return to Work Following Major Trauma in New Zealand.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: This study aimed to identify physical and psychological predictors of return to work (RTW) in a cohort of major trauma patients in New Zealand.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A retrospective cohort study was conducted at Christchurch Hospital involving patients identified from the New Zealand Major Trauma Registry. Full-time workers (n = 130) who sustained major trauma between 2016 and 2020 completed self-reported questionnaires assessing post-injury work capacity, PTSD (PCL-5), anxiety and depression (HADS) and perceived social support (MSPSS). Univariable and multivariable analyses were performed to determine predictors of decreased RTW following injury.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Older age, longer hospital length of stay (LOS) and ICU admission were all significantly associated with decreased RTW in the univariable analysis. Probable anxiety and depression were also significantly associated with decreased RTW, while meeting PTSD thresholds did not yield a significant association. In the final multivariable analysis, older age (OR 1.08, p < 0.01), longer LOS (OR 1.04, p = 0.048) and those with probable depression (OR 5.29, p = 0.01) were significantly associated with decreased RTW.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Probable depression is a strong, independent psychological predictor of reduced RTW following major trauma. These findings highlight the need for integrated post-trauma care models that incorporate routine psychological screening and early intervention to address both the physical and psychological needs of patients suffering from major trauma.

articles.title: The Umbrella Project-The Impact of Education on Staff Knowledge, Attitudes and Confidence in Caring for Mental Health Patients Within the Emergency Department.
articles.journal_full: International journal of mental health nursing

abstract.text: To evaluate the impact of a structured mental health education program on emergency department nurses' knowledge, attitudes and confidence in caring for people experiencing mental health distress. Mental health presentations to emergency departments continue to increase, placing greater responsibility on emergency nurses to provide safe, compassionate and evidence-based care. Despite this, many nurses report feeling underprepared to assess and manage mental health presentations due to limited education and training. Emergency department nurses completed anonymous pre-training, post-training and 3-month follow-up surveys measuring self-reported knowledge, attitudes and confidence. Quantitative data were analysed using descriptive statistics and qualitative responses using reflexive thematic analysis. Eight nurses completed the pre- and post-training surveys, with four completing the 3-month follow-up. Knowledge and confidence improved across all domains immediately following education, with the greatest gains in trauma-informed care, mental health legislation, suicide-related communication and management of complex behaviours. Positive attitudes towards mental health care remained consistently high, while qualitative findings demonstrated perceived improvements in clinical practice. A targeted mental health education program improved emergency nurses' perceived knowledge, confidence and application of key mental health care principles. These findings support the integration of targeted mental health education into emergency nursing professional development to strengthen workforce capability and improve care for people presenting with mental health concerns.

articles.title: Implementation and Performance of a Clinical Debriefing Programme in a Paediatric Emergency Department: A Descriptive Qualitative Review.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: Clinical debriefing should be standard practice in healthcare, but in most emergency departments implementation lags behind evidence. This post-implementation evaluation examined the performance of a clinical debriefing programme in a tertiary care paediatric emergency department, exploring implementation, key enablers and barriers to use.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This qualitative descriptive, post-implementation study used semi-structured interviews, with deductive analysis guided by a context-mechanism-outcome framework.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Twenty-one multidisciplinary staff were interviewed. Debriefing became embedded in routine practice through organisational endorsement, structured facilitation and inclusive participation. Participants reported improved clinical reasoning, emotional regulation, psychological safety and interprofessional relationships. Debriefing strengthened support for junior staff, enhanced relational co-ordination across disciplines, facilitated more timely quality and safety actions and built nursing capacity to lead debriefs. Time was the principal barrier, but reframing debriefing as an integral component of clinical care enabled its routine delivery.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Clinical debriefing was embedded in routine practice through interactions between organisational context and implementation mechanisms, with successful implementation relying on both the intervention and the conditions enabling it. Benefits for clinical practice, staff well-being, teamwork, enhanced support for the junior workforce and timely quality improvement initiatives were described. This study advances current understanding and provides direction for teams seeking to implement or optimise debriefing within their own departments.

articles.title: Prehospital Analgesia in Trauma: A Systematic Review of Current Evidence.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: Pain management is integral to prehospital trauma care. However, due to multiple challenges, pain is frequently undertreated despite important physiologic and psychologic implications. Among these challenges is uncertainty regarding the safety and effectiveness of pharmacologic agents administered enroute. We aimed to evaluate the level of evidence for the safety and effectiveness of prehospital pharmacologic analgesia for acutely injured adult trauma patients.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: An electronic database search of PUBMED, Google Scholar, Cochrane Library, Embase and Scopus for studies that reported on safety and/or effectiveness of prehospital pharmacologic analgesia for acutely injured adults (aged > 15 years) from January 1st, 2014, to January 1st, 2026. Non-original studies, paediatric studies, studies of non-pharmacologic agents or non-systemic administration (e.g., topical) were excluded.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Seventeen studies, involving 17,115 patients, met the inclusion criteria. The studies consisted of 6 randomized controlled trials, 5 retrospective cohort studies, one retrospective comparative study, one retrospective observational study, two prospective observational studies, one prospective cohort study and one non-randomized clinical trial. Agents included opioids, ketamine, methoxyflurane and paracetamol. Apart from one study of opioid therapy, no drug-attributed serious adverse events were reported. Minor adverse effects such as nausea, dizziness, dysphoria, agitation and drowsiness were common. All agents demonstrated effectiveness to varying levels.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Current evidence demonstrates an overall favourable safety and effectiveness profile of prehospital analgesia for adult trauma patients. However, considering the wide prehospital prevalence of injury-related pain, evidence is limited by scope, methodology and variations of treatment protocols.

articles.title: Aligning the Electronic Health Record With Age-Friendly Care in Hospitals: Qualitative Multisite Study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: The geriatric 4Ms framework conceptualizes 4 evidence-based elements (ie, Mobility, Mentation, Medication, and what Matters) that are important to high-quality care for older adults. Improving on these measures is central to the Age-Friendly Health Systems initiative. Electronic health records (EHRs) are critical to modern health systems including being able to review patient information and act on geriatric health concerns.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: This study aimed to examine how clinicians use a commercial EHR to access 4Ms-relevant information during inpatient and emergency care of older adults to inform the design of scalable, age-friendly 4Ms EHR tools.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We interviewed clinicians and clinical staff (n=20), including physicians, advanced practice providers, nurses, pharmacists, and physical therapists from 5 large academic health systems across the United States regarding their experiences using the EHR during inpatient and emergency care for older adults. All included health systems used the same EHR and had geriatric quality programs in place. Participants completed virtual interviews that included narrated walkthroughs of their local EHR builds in response to 3 brief clinical vignettes focused on falls, home care needs, and delirium. Interviews were screen-recorded with audio and transcribed for coding and thematic analysis.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Major themes spanned the 4Ms and consisted of (1) difficulty finding information about the 4Ms, (2) poor 4Ms data quality, (3) sparse EHR data sharing, (4) variable intrafacility practices, and (5) homegrown 4Ms EHR tools. Interviewees shared some examples of tools that had been implemented in their practice settings that increased access to 4Ms data, including documentation search workarounds, trackboards, and alerts.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Among a sample of clinicians and clinical staff representing large academic medical centers, 4Ms data in the EHR were characterized by multilevel barriers related to access and accuracy. Alternatively, interviewees demonstrated innovative EHR-embedded tools to improve accessibility of some 4Ms-relevant data. These findings inform the future development and refinement of a comprehensive geriatric 4Ms EHR tool for the emergency department and inpatient setting.

articles.title: Prevalence of Persistent Severe Hypertension and Rates of Treatment Among Pregnant Patients in the Prehospital Setting.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP) contribute to maternal and fetal morbidity and mortality and require time-sensitive intervention. In April 2025, the American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG), in collaboration with the National Association of EMS Physicians (NAEMSP) and the National Association of EMTs (NAEMT), published new guidelines on the prehospital management of elevated blood pressure in pregnancy. The objective of this study was to determine the prevalence of persistent severe hypertension among pregnant patients encountered by prehospital clinicians, characterize baseline frequency of pre-guideline treatment, and establish a benchmark to inform implementation of these guidelines.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a retrospective observational cohort study using the 2024 ESO Data Collaborative public release research dataset (January 1 to December 31, 2024). We identified all 9-1-1 ground EMS scene responses for patients documented as pregnant beyond 20 wk of gestation. We excluded injury-related encounters and patients outside the World Health Organization-defined childbearing age range (15 to 49 years). Consistent with the new guidelines, we defined persistent severe hypertension as at least two documented blood pressure measurements with systolic blood pressure ≥ 160 mmHg or diastolic blood pressure ≥ 110 mmHg. We defined guideline-adherent treatment as administration of both magnesium sulfate (MgSO₄) and an antihypertensive medication (labetalol, hydralazine, or nifedipine).

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: We identified 39,546 eligible 9-1-1 ground EMS scene responses for patients beyond 20 wk of gestation. The prevalence of persistent severe hypertension was 3.1% (n = 1,234/39,546). Among these patients, 77 (6.2%) received magnesium sulfate only, 19 (1.5%) received an antihypertensive medication only, and 10 (0.8%) received guideline-adherent treatment with both magnesium sulfate and an antihypertensive medication.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Approximately 1 in 32 pregnant patients beyond 20 wk of gestation encountered by prehospital clinicians had persistent severe hypertension. In the year prior to dissemination of the 2025 ACOG, NAEMSP, and NAEMT-supported guidelines, fewer than 1% received guideline-adherent treatment with both magnesium sulfate and an antihypertensive medication. These findings establish a national benchmark and identify opportunities to improve prehospital care through protocol development, medication availability, clinician education, and implementation of updated guidelines.

articles.title: Diving into decomposition: detection of volatile organic compounds from submerged human remains using thin-film SPME and GC × GC-TOFMS.

abstract.text: Locating submerged human remains is critical for forensic investigations, yet effective search operations rely heavily on human remains detection (HRD) dogs, whose training depends on an accurate understanding of the volatile organic compounds (VOCs) released as decomposition odour. Despite this need, little is known about VOCs emitted from submerged human remains. This study evaluated a sampling strategy for collecting VOCs from submerged human remains, established a baseline VOC profile, and assessed VOC stability during short-term storage. A donated amputated limb was submerged in water in a glass jar under controlled laboratory conditions. Water was sampled throughout decomposition, and VOCs were extracted using direct immersion (DI) and headspace (HS) thin-film solid-phase microextraction (TF-SPME) and analyzed using thermal desorption comprehensive two-dimensional gas chromatography time-of-flight mass spectrometry (TD-GC × GC-TOFMS). VOC stability was evaluated using three aliquots of the same water sample analyzed immediately, after one week of refrigerated storage (4 °C), or after one week of frozen storage (-20 °C). HS and DI provided complementary VOC profiles, with 352 and 351 compounds detected, respectively, including 325 compounds common to both methods. Nitrogen-containing compounds and esters and analogues were the most diverse chemical classes, whereas sulfur-containing compounds and acids exhibited the highest normalized peak areas. Frozen storage generally retained more VOCs than refrigerated storage, supporting freezing as the preferred approach for short-term sample preservation. Overall, combining the HS/DI TF-SPME sampling strategy with TD-GC × GC-TOFMS enabled comprehensive characterization of VOCs from submerged human remains.

articles.title: Advancing ventilation during cardiopulmonary resuscitation: a question of optimizing quality, ventilation parameters or both?

abstract.label: PURPOSE OF REVIEW
abstract.text: Ventilation is provided to most patients during cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR). International guidelines emphasize the need for effective intra-arrest ventilation while acknowledging uncertainty regarding the optimal ventilation parameters. This review will discuss how new studies challenge prior beliefs on key ventilation parameters, will highlight challenges and potential solutions for high-quality ventilation and will suggest a translational research approach to advance intra-arrest ventilation.

abstract.label: RECENT FINDINGS
abstract.text: A recent observational study reported that higher ventilation rates during in-hospital cardiac arrest may be positively associated with return of spontaneous circulation, challenging common beliefs. Additionally, a pivotal observational study on bag-valve-mask ventilation during out-of-hospital cardiac arrest found that ventilation was frequently ineffective and if so, associated with reduced survival and neurological function. Scoping and systematic reviews on intra-arrest ventilation parameters, ventilation feedback devices and mechanical ventilation have uncovered uncertainties regarding fundamental aspects of intra-arrest ventilation.

abstract.label: SUMMARY
abstract.text: This review contextualizes the scientific debate on how to optimize intra-arrest ventilation by healthcare professionals. It covers emerging evidence on bag-valve-mask ventilation quality along with controversies around the optimal intra-arrest ventilation parameters, ventilation feedback devices and mechanical ventilation during CPR. Finally, implications for clinical practice are provided, and a translational approach is proposed to advance intra-arrest ventilation.

articles.title: An Evaluation of ICU Follow-Up Clinic Attendance and Subsequent Healthcare Resource Utilization in Wales, United Kingdom: A Retrospective, Population-Level Data-Linkage Study.

abstract.label: IMPORTANCE
abstract.text: Postintensive care syndrome encapsulates the long-term physical, psychologic, and cognitive impairments often seen among ICU survivors. Post-ICU follow-up clinics may support recovery and reduce avoidable healthcare utilization, but population-level evidence remains limited.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: To identify patient characteristics associated with follow-up clinic attendance and evaluate differences in healthcare resource utilization (HRU) across three groups: invited and attended, invited but did not attend, and not invited.

abstract.label: DESIGN SETTING AND PARTICIPANTS
abstract.text: A retrospective cohort study using anonymised, linked administrative data from the Secure Anonymised Information Linkage Databank in Wales, United Kingdom. Adults (≥ 18 yr) with ICU admissions between 2016 and 2023 who survived to discharge were included. Follow-up clinic data were obtained from three regional health boards (healthcare organizations responsible for delivering National Health Services in Wales) with follow-up clinic availability.

abstract.label: MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES
abstract.text: HRU outcomes included ICU readmissions, emergency department attendances, hospital admissions (elective and emergency), hospital bed days, outpatient appointments, and general practitioner (GP) events. Multivariable models assessed associations between clinic attendance and HRU.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 6491 eligible patients, 761 attended a follow-up clinic, 1473 were invited but did not attend, and 4257 were not invited. Among invited patients, attendance was associated with increasing age, comorbidity, deprivation, and ICU length of stay. Compared with attendees, nonattendees and those not invited had higher adjusted odds of ICU readmission (odds ratio [OR] = 2.81 and 2.22, respectively), elective admissions, and hospital bed days. No significant differences were observed for emergency admissions or GP events. Attendees were more likely to have 4 or more (non-follow-up clinic) outpatient appointments.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE
abstract.text: Clinic attendance was associated with differences in several HRU domains. Variability in access and engagement suggests potential inequalities in post‑ICU recovery pathways. Standardizing referral practices and expanding clinic availability may improve outcomes for ICU survivors.

articles.title: Caregiver-Reported Signs and Symptoms of Autonomic Dysfunction in Koolen-de Vries Syndrome.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To evaluate whether autonomic signs and symptoms are overrepresented in people with Koolen-de Vries syndrome (KdVS).

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: In this observational study, individuals with KdVS and their caregivers were recruited at an international advocacy summit and through social media invitations facilitated by the KdVS Foundation. Caregivers of people with KdVS completed the Pediatric Autonomic Symptoms Scale (PASS) questionnaire and were invited to provide anecdotal reports of their experiences with possible autonomic dysfunction. Data were compared with previously published cohorts of healthy controls, individuals with familial dysautonomia (FD), autism spectrum disorder (ASD), or nonspecific neurodevelopmental disorders (NDD).

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Thirty-seven individuals with KdVS participated. PASS scores of individuals with KdVS were significantly higher than healthy controls (p < 0.0001) and individuals with ASD (p < 0.0005), similar to those with FD, and not significantly different from those with nonspecific NDDs. In at least 8 cases, the autonomic signs and symptoms required emergency department visits or hospitalization.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: Autonomic signs and symptoms are relatively common in individuals with KdVS and can significantly affect quality of life and function.

articles.title: Epidemiology of Table Tennis-Related Injuries Presenting to Emergency Departments in the United States, 2005-2024: A NEISS Database Analysis.
Firearm Injury Prevention in Undergraduate Medical Education in the United States: Current Landscape, Barriers, and Future Directions.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Firearm injuries remain a leading cause of preventable death in the United States (US), with physicians uniquely positioned to contribute to firearm injury prevention (FIP). Despite this, there is a lack of recent national assessment of FIP inclusion in US undergraduate medical education (UME). Thus, we looked to assess how medical schools currently incorporate FIP into curricula and what challenges affect its implementation.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We distributed a REDCap-based survey to medical education leadership at all LCME- and COCA- accredited medical schools in the US between April and December 2024, assessing FIP curricular content, timing, modes and settings of instruction, assessment strategies, extracurricular opportunities, and perceived barriers to implementation.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Fifty-five institutions (27%) responded, with 64% reporting the inclusion of FIP content in their curricula. Most schools (62%) introduced FIP during clinical years, particularly in pediatrics, emergency medicine, and surgery, and some schools (51%) integrated content preclinically. Common curricular topics included firearm safety counseling, access screening, and identifying risk factors. Only 27% of schools reported formally assessing FIP knowledge. The most frequently cited barriers to implementation were limited curricular time and political/ideological concerns.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Our findings suggest encouraging progress in the incorporation of FIP education within UME compared to the most recent previous data, but they also highlight significant variability and persistent gaps. Broader adoption of standardized FIP curricula, earlier integration during training, and development of robust assessment strategies may enhance awareness and preparedness among future physicians to address firearm injury as a vital public health issue.

articles.title: Microvascular Resistance Reserve and Outcomes in Angina and Nonobstructive Coronary Artery Disease.

abstract.label: IMPORTANCE
abstract.text: Coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMD) is highly prevalent in patients with angina and nonobstructive coronary arteries (ANOCA). Microvascular resistance reserve (MRR) is a novel index to assess CMD independently of epicardial disease and driving pressures, but the long-term prognostic value of continuous thermodilution-derived MRR in patients with ANOCA is unknown.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To assess the prognostic value of continuous thermodilution-derived MRR and its association with clinical outcomes and symptom burden in patients with ANOCA.

abstract.label: DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS
abstract.text: This prospective, multicenter cohort study within the Netherlands Registry of Invasive Coronary Vasomotor Function Testing (NL-CFT) included patients between July 2020 and June 2025 in 4 clinical centers in the Netherlands. Follow-up for clinical events and patient-reported symptoms was completed for up to 3 years. Clinical events were adjudicated by investigators blinded to CFT results. Consecutive patients with ANOCA who underwent continuous thermodilution were included.

abstract.label: EXPOSURE
abstract.text: Abnormal MRR (CMD) was defined as less than 2.1, gray zone as 2.1 to 2.7, and normal microvascular function as 2.7 or greater.

abstract.label: MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES
abstract.text: The primary clinical outcome was a composite of all-cause death, acute coronary syndrome, stroke, clinically indicated revascularization, repeat angiography without intervention, and unplanned hospital admittance or emergency department visit due to angina or heart failure. Secondary outcomes included angina at baseline and follow-up. Symptoms were assessed using the patient-reported Seattle Angina Questionnaire (SAQ) scores.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 553 included patients (mean [SD] age, 59.1 [9.6] years; 459 female [83.0%]) with a mean (SD) follow-up of 27.5 (16.1) months, CMD was observed in 94 patients (17.0%). The main composite outcome did not differ across the 3 MRR categories (18 of 94 patients with abnormal [19.1%] vs 21 of 98 patients with gray zone [21.4%] vs 76 of 361 patients with normal [21.1%] MRR; log-rank P = .85). Individual outcomes did not differ between groups. There was no overall longitudinal interaction between MRR and SAQ summary scores. While low MRR (abnormal vs normal groups) was not associated with an increased symptom burden at baseline, it was associated with worse angina at follow-up (mean [SD] SAQ summary score, 53.0 [16.7] vs 60.1 [16.6]; P = .04) and less clinically relevant improvement (9 of 30 patients [30.0%] vs 52 of 88 patients [59.1%]; P = .02).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE
abstract.text: In this study, CMD assessed by continuous thermodilution-derived MRR was not associated with clinical outcomes.

articles.title: Updated Staging System to Define Cardiogenic Shock Severity A Cardiogenic Shock Working Group Report.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Cardiogenic shock (CS) severity is defined by the Society for Cardiovascular Angiography and Interventions stages and modifications from the Cardiogenic Shock Working Group (CSWG). Lactate thresholds, treatment intensity, and cardiac arrest modifiers remain incompletely defined. We aimed to refine the 2022 CSWG staging criteria using contemporary data.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Patients with CS from heart failure (HF-CS) or myocardial infarction (MI-CS) enrolled in the multicenter CSWG registry (2021-2025) were analyzed. Associations between systolic blood pressure (SBP), lactate, treatment intensity, and in-hospital mortality, which is considered a surrogate for CS severity, were examined. External application of the updated system was performed in an independent US health system.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 11,640 patients (60.5% HF-CS, 26.1% MI-CS), SBP and lactate demonstrated graded relationships with mortality across thresholds (SBP <60, 60-<90, ≥90 mm Hg; lactate 0-2, >2-5, >5-10, >10 mmol/L). Mortality increased incrementally with treatment intensity. The 2026 staging system, incorporating these thresholds and the number of vasoactive drugs and temporary mechanical circulatory support devices (stage C: 1-2, D: 3-4, E: ≥5), demonstrated progressive mortality across stages. Compared with previous CSWG staging, 28.4% of patients classified as stage D and 56.4% of patients classified as stage E were reclassified, with lower mortality among those reclassified to less-severe stages. Out-of-hospital cardiac arrest functioned best as a stage modifier, whereas in-hospital cardiac arrest corresponded to stage E. Findings were consistent across HF-CS and MI-CS. The 2026 CS staging system was evaluated in 1,417,637 patients in a geographically and structurally diverse health care system and demonstrated a graded, monotonic increase in mortality across stages A-E.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Using fewer clinical variables, the 2026 CSWG criteria provide a simple framework for CS severity staging that is applicable among patients with HF-CS and MI-CS and can be standardized across clinical trials and health care settings.

articles.title: Operational end-of-life trajectory categories among patients who died in the emergency department: associations with resuscitative and palliative care in a five-year retrospective cohort.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Emergency departments (EDs) increasingly care for patients approaching the end of life, yet the relationships between patterns of decline and final ED care remain poorly characterised. The objective was to describe the distribution of retrospectively assigned trajectory-oriented categories among ED decedents and examine associations with care processes.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This single-centre retrospective cohort study included adults who died in the ED between 2018 and 2022. Categories were acute event/low comorbidity (T1), terminal malignancy or pre-existing exclusive palliative/comfort-focused care (T2), advanced chronic disease with acute decompensation (T3), frailty/dementia or high comorbidity with severe functional dependency (T4), and residual unclassified cases (T5). Primary outcomes were CPR and documented initiation of exclusive palliative/comfort-focused care; documented end-of-life recognition or discussion was secondary.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 628 patients, 1.3% were T1, 10.8% T2, 10.0% T3, 49.4% T4, and 28.5% T5. CPR ranged from 75% in T1 to 24% in T2 and T4 (p<0.001). Exclusive palliative/comfort-focused care was initiated in 35% of T2 and 11% of T3-T5 patients (p<0.001). End-of-life recognition or discussion ranged from 12% in T1 to 51% in T2 (p=0.034).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Frailty and dementia represented the main trajectory of death in the ED, while nearly one-third of patients could not be classified within the predefined categories. A pragmatic trajectory-oriented framework may help interpret observed patterns of care. However, retrospective assignment and the large residual group make these findings hypothesis-generating; prospective validation is required before decision-support use.

articles.title: Health and Care Characteristics of Ageing Adults With Profound Intellectual and Multiple Disabilities Living in French Facilities.
articles.journal_full: Journal of applied research in intellectual disabilities : JARID

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Life expectancy among individuals with Profound Intellectual and Multiple Disabilities/Polyhandicap (PIMD/PLH) has increased, making information essential for age-appropriate care. This study compared health characteristics and care use between younger and older adults with PIMD/PLH in institutions.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This cross-sectional study used data from the French PIMD/PLH cohort. Inclusion criteria were (i) age > 3 years; (ii) PIMD/PLH diagnosis. Data on health characteristics and health care consumption were included. Adults were compared by age (≤ 45 vs. > 45 years).

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Mean age was 34.5 ± 6.0 in the younger group and 55 ± 5.9 in the older group. While overall polyhandicap severity was similar, older adults exhibited a greater dependency level. Gastroesophageal reflux and symptomatic osteoporosis were more prevalent in the younger group; dental disorders, chronic pain, and sleep disorders predominated in the older group. Older adults received less medical and paramedical care.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: This study highlights the need for lifelong medical and rehabilitative care in PIMD/PLH.

abstract.label: TRIAL REGISTRATION
abstract.text: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT02400528.

articles.title: Functional Health Illiteracy in Cancer Patients and Caregivers in the Era of Precision Medicine and Immunotherapy: A Narrative Review.

abstract.text: Functional health illiteracy is a significant barrier to equitable cancer care for patients and caregivers, a challenge that is exacerbated by precision medicine and immunotherapy. This review article aimed at synthesizing current evidence on functional health illiteracy among cancer patients and caregivers and examines its interaction with the demands of precision medicine and immunotherapy. The article also outlines practical strategies to mitigate the impact of health illiteracy on therapy adherence, decision-making, and clinical outcomes. Articles published between 2010 and 2025 were identified through searches of PubMed, CINAHL, and PsycINFO. Policy reports from the National Cancer Institute, the Institute of Medicine, and the American Society of Clinical Oncology were also included to provide contextual background. Consistency in article selection was assessed using the K coefficient. Approximately 36-50% of cancer patients were found to be unable to effectively use health information. Older adults, racial and ethnic minorities, and individuals with lower incomes are disproportionately affected. The complex terminology of precision oncology further complicates matters for patients and caregivers, who must manage intricate drug regimens and monitor for immune-related side effects at home. Low health literacy is associated with reduced clinical trial enrollment, decreased therapy adherence, increased emergency department visits, and poorer survival. Interventions, including plain-language use, culturally tailored instructions, digital health skill development, and organizational modifications, have demonstrated efficacy in enhancing health literacy among cancer patients and caregivers. These approaches improve access to medical information, reduce misunderstandings, and support self-management. As precision medicine evolves, aligning clinical complexity with targeted health literacy strategies is essential to optimize adherence, decision-making, and clinical outcomes.

articles.title: Impact of Audit-Based Implementation of Professional Safety Standards on Safety Climate and Nursing Errors in Emergency Departments: A Quasi-Experimental Study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Nursing errors remain a major patient safety concern in emergency departments. Audit-based implementation of professional safety standards has been proposed to improve safety climate and reduce errors, but its effectiveness has not been fully established.

abstract.label: AIM
abstract.text: Nurses' safety and professional performance directly influence patient outcomes, particularly in high-pressure emergency departments (EDs). This study evaluated the impact of auditing the implementation of professional safety standards on the safety climate and nursing errors among ED nurses.

abstract.label: STUDY DESIGN
abstract.text: A quasi-experimental pre- and post-intervention study was conducted among emergency nurses at Baqiyatallah Hospital in Tehran, Iran. Safety climate was appraised using the Safety Climate Questionnaire (SCQ), and nursing errors were measured by the Nursing Error Questionnaire (NEQ). These validated instruments were administered pre- and post-intervention. The intervention consisted of a structured online audit-based education programme with a focus on professional safety standards, supplemented by the introduction of a 'Common Emergency Department Procedures Handbook'.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 115 nurses completed both the pre- and post-intervention assessments and were included in the final analysis. The total safety climate score significantly improved post-intervention (p = 0.006). However, this improvement was driven mainly by the nursing education dimension (p < 0.001), while other domains (including supervisor attitudes, communication, burnout and error reporting) showed no statistically significant changes. The total nursing error score diminished marginally (91.96 vs. 90.90), but this reduction was not statistically significant (p = 0.729).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Audit-based education was associated with an improvement in the overall safety climate score, largely driven by the nursing education domain. However, isolated audit-based educational interventions may have limited influence on underlying organisational and communication-related factors and did not significantly reduce nursing errors. Sustainable improvements may require combining audit and education with system-level strategies, managerial engagement and workload management within emergency departments.

abstract.label: RELEVANCE TO CLINICAL PRACTICE
abstract.text: Audit-based education may improve safety climate among emergency nurses, but reducing nursing errors may require broader organizational and communication-based strategies.

articles.title: Management of acute situations in institutionalised Parkinsonian patients: A survey in Seine-Saint-Denis, France.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: Patients with Parkinson's disease (PD) or atypical parkinsonian syndromes (PS) living in long-term care facilities face complex medical needs, yet little is known about their medical follow-up and reasons for emergency department referrals and hospitalisations in this setting. This study aimed to describe the prevalence of PD/PS among residents of long-term care facilities (EHPADs) in the French Seine-Saint-Denis department, their medical follow-up, and the frequency and reasons for emergency department referrals and hospitalisations.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective study covered the year 2023. All 66 EHPADs in the department were contacted to complete a facility-level questionnaire on PD/PS prevalence and emergency referrals. Facilities with PD/PS residents were then invited to complete a patient-level questionnaire collecting demographic, clinical and follow-up data, and details regarding emergency referrals and hospitalisations.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Thirty-five EHPADs (53%) responded, representing 3398 residents. Thirty facilities reported 144 residents with PD or PS, corresponding to a prevalence of 4.24% [95% CI: 3.60-4.98%]. Sixteen (53.3%) EHPADs reported at least one PD/PS resident referred to the emergency department, resulting in 62 referrals during the year, corresponding to an incidence rate of 0.43 [95% CI: 0.33-0.55] referrals per PD/PS resident-year. Eight EHPADs (26.7%) completed the patient-level questionnaire, providing data on 34 residents (median [Q1-Q3] age: 80 [75-85], 73.5% with PD). Over one-third (38.2%) did not have a designated neurologist during 2023. Nine patients (27.3%) were referred to the emergency department, mainly for axial disorders (33.3%) and infections (33.3%). Nine patients (26.5%) were hospitalised. Exploratory analyses showed that hospitalisation was significantly associated with emergency referral (P=0.02) and a last general practitioner consultation that was less often for routine care (P=0.048).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: PD and PS were frequently identified among residents of participating EHPADs, yet a substantial proportion of patients lack neurological follow-up. Emergency referrals and hospitalisations affected approximately one-quarter of patients, often for potentially preventable causes. These findings suggest that preventive strategies, multidisciplinary follow-up, and improved access to neurologists may help reduce avoidable hospitalisations.

articles.title: Potential involvement of TLR4/MyD88 signaling in the neuroprotective effects of NBP in DEACMP.

abstract.text: Delayed encephalopathy after carbon monoxide poisoning (DEACMP) is a major neurological complication following acute carbon monoxide (CO) poisoning and is associated with persistent neuroinflammatory responses, hippocampal injury, and cognitive dysfunction.Previous studies have suggested that NBP exerts neuroprotective effects in DEACMP; however, the molecular mechanisms underlying these effects remain incompletely understood.We established a DEACMP mouse model using a static CO inhalation protocol and investigated the effects of NBP on cognitive function, hippocampal pathology,microglial reactivity, inflammatory cytokine expression, and TLR4/MyD88-related signaling alterations through behavioral, histopathological, and molecular analyses.After 21 days of NBP treatment, DEACMP mice showed improved spatial learning and memory, reflected by reduced escape latency, increased time spent in the target quadrant, and more platform crossings in the Morris water maze, without differences in swimming speed.HE staining demonstrated attenuated hippocampal injury in NBP-treated animals.Western blot and real-time quantitative PCR analyses showed reduced protein expression and mRNA levels of TLR4,MyD88,and Iba1 .Immunofluorescence analysis showed reduced Iba1 immunoreactivity and attenuation of activation-associated microglial morphological changes in the NBP-treated group.ELISA showed that NBP attenuated the DEACMP-associated inflammatory imbalance, with reduced TNF-α, IL-6, and IL-1β and increased IL-10.Correlation analyses further linked higher TLR4/MyD88 expression with greater microglial and pro-inflammatory responses and poorer cognitive performance.Collectively, NBP treatment alleviated cognitive impairment, hippocampal injury, microglial activation, and inflammatory imbalance in DEACMP mice, with partial reversal of disease-associated abnormalities as identified by recovery analysis.These effects were accompanied by attenuation of TLR4/MyD88-related inflammatory alterations, suggesting the potential involvement of this signaling axis in NBP-mediated neuroprotection.

articles.title: Just the facts: approach to the older patient with bilateral shoulder pain.
[Regression analysis of transfusion requirements of severely injured patients in clinical emergency care-A feasibility study].

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: The acute management of severely injured patients with hemorrhagic shock and coagulopathy often requires the use of packed red blood cells (PRBC) and fresh frozen plasma (FFP). Using a single center dataset of the TraumaRegister DGU® of the German Trauma Society (Deutsche Gesellschaft für Unfallchirurgie, DGU) , this study aims to retrospectively estimate the required amounts of PRBCs and FFP from initial emergency room management to the end of any potential emergency surgery.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A total of 721 primary treated patients from 2020-2023 at a level I trauma center were analyzed. A random forest model was used to regressively estimate the number of required PRBC and FFP units. Attributes included vital signs, laboratory findings, interventions and surgical indications from the prehospital care and emergency room phases.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: In this study PRBCs were administered in 13.2% of cases (median 4, min-max 0-27 units PRBC), and FFP in 10.7% (median 4, min-max 0-28 units FFP). In the PRBC model the correlation coefficient (CC) was 0.70 (95% confidence interval, CI 0.70-0.71), with an R2 of 0.50 (0.49-0.50). The mean absolute error (MAE) and root mean squared error (RMSE) were 0.63 (0.63-0.63) and 1.81 units PRBC (1.81-1.82), respectively. The false negative rate was 0.03 (0.02-0.03), corresponding to a specificity of 0.82 (0.81-0.82) and an underprediction of 9.8%. For the FFP model, the CC was 0.74 (0.73-0.75), R2 was 0.55 (0.54-0.56), MAE was 0.58 (0.58-0.58) and RMSE was 1.71 units FFP (1.70-1.71). The false negative rate was 0.01 (0.00-0.01), resulting in a specificity of 0.82 (0.82-0.82) and an underprediction of 8.8%.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The standard dataset of the TraumaRegister DGU® appears to enable regression-based estimation of the PRBC and FFP units required for severely injured patients in the time window of transfer from the trauma room to the operating room, showing a clinically acceptable model fit for the first time. To improve individual prediction accuracy, future models should be developed and validated using a multicenter cohort and the dataset should be expanded to include real-time parameters as well as attributes reflecting individual transfusion triggers.

articles.title: New decompression gas CF₄/O₂: reducing DCS risk and ameliorating injuries in male rats.

abstract.text: Decompression sickness (DCS) remains a major risk in diving. Prolonging decompression reduces inert gas load but increases operation time and underwater exposure. We tested a carbon tetrafluoride-oxygen mixture (CF₄/O₂) as a decompression gas in two rat decompression protocols: 6 ATA compressed air and 9 ATA helium-oxygen (heliox). Switching to CF₄/O₂ 10 min before decompression significantly reduced DCS incidence in both protocols: air, 68% (19/28) to 11% (3/28); heliox, 68% (15/22) to 18% (4/22). Mortality was significantly reduced in the compressed-air protocol (29% [8/28] to 0 [0/28], P = 0.004) but not in the heliox protocol (14% [3/22] to 0 [0/22], P = 0.233). Echocardiography showed fewer or no intracardiac bubbles after CF₄/O₂. In the heliox protocol, CF₄/O₂ significantly modulated some pulmonary function parameters; in the compressed-air protocol, pulmonary function changes were time-dependent and did not differ significantly between groups. CF₄/O₂ also reduced lung inflammation, endothelial injury, and histological damage in both protocols. In a 28-day repeated hyperbaric exposure protocol assessing selected serum biochemical endpoints, CF₄/O₂ did not increase serum alanine aminotransferase, aspartate aminotransferase, creatinine or urea; however, this protocol did not include post-exposure histopathology or haematology, so safety conclusions are limited to the measured endpoints. These findings support the tested CF₄/O₂ gas-switching strategy under the specific conditions used. Shorter decompression protocols were not tested, and shortening decompression time remains a potential application rather than a demonstrated outcome.

articles.title: Pericardio-Peritoneal Collection in an Extremely Premature Infant: Diagnostic and Therapeutic Insights.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Central venous catheterization is frequently performed in premature infants. Chest radiography may not guarantee optimal position between inferior vena cava and right atrium.

abstract.label: CASE SUMMARY
abstract.text: An extremely premature infant (22 weeks' gestation) with an appropriately placed umbilical catheter developed abdominal distension, cardiomegaly, refractory hypotension and oxygenation failure. Point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) confirmed the clinical suspicion of peritoneal and pericardial collections and drainage led to clinical improvements.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: Umbilical vein catheter extravasation into the peritoneal cavity led to ascites followed by pericardial effusion via pericardioperitoneal canals.

abstract.label: TAKE-HOME MESSAGES
abstract.text: Informed interpretation of clinical signs and chest radiographs, knowledge of POCUS, and inclusion of simulation-assisted procedural learning in neonatal and pediatric cardiology training programs would be beneficial. POCUS is not only useful to confirm central catheter position, but also to diagnose and manage acute complications.

articles.title: Prescriptions for seizure cluster rescue therapy are not associated with decreased pediatric ED utilization.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: Seizure clusters, or acute repetitive seizures, are a phenomenon often experienced by patients with epilepsy and pose a significant treatment challenge for clinicians. Several rescue medications have been approved by the Food and Drug Administration for the treatment of seizure clusters - including diazepam rectal gel, intranasal midazolam, and intranasal diazepam - which are commonly prescribed for prolonged seizures or status epilepticus (SE). Conflicting evidence exists relating to the impact of seizure cluster treatment on hospital care utilization and health-related quality of life (HRQoL). We hypothesized that children prescribed rescue medication specifically including an indication for seizure clusters would have fewer seizure-related Emergency Department (ED) visits compared to those prescribed rescue medications only for SE.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This study was a cross-sectional cohort study from a single pediatric center. A total of 3216 children with epilepsy and rescue medications were included. Measured characteristics included sociodemographic factors, epilepsy features, HRQoL, and healthcare utilization. We modeled the probability of having ED visits for seizures in the 12 months following prescriptions of rescue medication for either SE only or both SE and seizure clusters.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: There was no difference in ED utilization between patients receiving a rescue prescription for SE only (n = 48, 3.1%) or both SE and seizure clusters (n = 64, 3.8%) (OR 1.12; 95% CI 0.74-1.71; p = 0.6). A multivariable model was created to evaluate factors associated with ED utilization. The acute social needs score was the only measured variable associated with increased odds of having a subsequent ED visit (OR 1.37; 95% CI 1.22-1.53; p < 0.001).

abstract.label: SIGNIFICANCE
abstract.text: There was no difference in ED utilization between patients receiving a rescue medication prescription including seizure clusters and those only for SE. The social needs score was the only measured variable in this study associated with increased ED visits. These results highlight that prescribing rescue medications for cluster seizures may have less impact on healthcare utilization than acute social needs.

abstract.label: PLAIN LANGUAGE SUMMARY
abstract.text: Seizure clusters are repetitive seizures that are poorly defined, and the consequences of treating them are unclear. While some providers prescribe benzodiazepines for use during these episodes, others do not. Using a large single-center database of over 3000 children, we found that having a prescription for a benzodiazepine to use during cluster seizures did not reduce emergency department (ED) use compared to patients with prescriptions for treating only life-threatening prolonged seizures. In this dataset, the only patient characteristic associated with ED utilization was the presence of an acute social need, such as food insecurity, suggesting that interventions targeting social needs may be more effective in reducing healthcare utilization in children with epilepsy.

articles.title: Defining best practice for very old patients following unplanned intensive care admission: protocol of the Delphi consensus study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Very old patients (≥80 years) represent a rapidly increasing proportion of intensive care unit (ICU) admissions across Australia and New Zealand. Care of this population is characterised by substantial prognostic uncertainty and variability in ICU triage, treatment limitation and post-ICU pathways. In particular, the role and implementation of time-limited ICU trials remain inconsistent.

abstract.label: AIMS
abstract.text: To establish multidisciplinary consensus on best-practice management of very old patients following unplanned ICU admission in Australia and New Zealand, including the role, structure and implementation of time-limited ICU trials.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We will conduct a modified, multiround Delphi consensus study. A multidisciplinary, multispecialty panel of expert clinicians (intensive care, geriatrics, emergency medicine), doctors in training, nurses, allied health professionals, ethicists and health service leaders across Australia and New Zealand will be recruited through purposive and snowball sampling. Participants will rate statements using the Likert scale across multiple rounds. Anonymised aggregated feedback will be provided to participants between rounds to facilitate convergence of opinion. Consensus will be defined a priori using predefined thresholds and median scores. Quantitative analyses will include descriptive statistics and exploratory subgroup comparisons, while free-text responses will undergo thematic analysis.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The primary outcome is to establish multidisciplinary consensus on best-practice management of very old patients following unplanned ICU admission, including the role and implementation of time-limited ICU trials. Secondary outcomes include identifying areas of agreement and variation across groups and convergence across Delphi rounds. A tertiary outcome is to explore barriers and facilitators to implementation to inform a structured decision-making framework.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: This study will generate consensus-based recommendations and a structured framework for the use of time-limited ICU trials in Australia and New Zealand ICUs. By addressing current practice variability, it aims to support transparent, patient-centred decision-making and inform future research and policy in the care of very old critically ill patients.

articles.title: Empirical linezolid target attainment in critically ill patients: integrating local susceptibility data and dosing strategies.

abstract.text: Linezolid is important for treating infections caused by Gram-positive bacteria resistant to first-line agents. Severe infections often require empirical therapy before pathogen identification and susceptibility testing. This evaluation aims to compare different empirical linezolid dosing strategies in intensive care unit (ICU) patients to improve pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic target attainment while minimising toxicities. Three dosing strategies were compared: (i) standard dosing, (ii) therapeutic drug monitoring (TDM)-guided dosing, and (iii) a theoretical model-informed precision dosing (MIPD) strategy based on Bayesian forecasting with a population pharmacokinetic model. Each scenario was combined with an ICU-specific minimal inhibitory concentration (MIC) distribution comprising more than 19,000 isolates collected over 10 years. Data from 117 critically ill patients with 2184 TDM samples were available. Linezolid resistance was highest in ICU isolates (9.6%) compared with isolates from the intermediate care unit (4.3%), general wards (3.6%), and emergency room (1.6%). Among ICU isolates, resistance increased significantly over the 10-year study period, from 6.3% in 2015 to 11.4% in 2024. Empirical target attainment was 36.6% with standard dosing and 48.5% with TDM-guided dose adaptation, in two different ICU cohorts that showed 35.9% and 59.4% baseline target attainment, respectively. Theoretical MIPD projected target attainment in 71.4-81.6% of patients. After excluding resistant isolates, the corresponding values were 40.5%, 53.7%, and 79.0-90.3%, respectively. Integrating a large contemporary ICU-specific MIC distribution with patient-level pharmacokinetic data, our results suggest MIPD may represent a promising strategy improving target attainment, in contrast to standard regimens and TDM-guided dosing which failed to achieve adequate target exposure in ICU patients.

articles.title: Point-of-care ultrasound in Ireland: a cross-sectional survey of practice, education and governance among healthcare professionals.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Anecdotal evidence suggests widespread Point-of-Care Ultrasound (POCUS) use in Ireland, but it is underexplored. Some professional societies have issued curricula and guidelines, but little is known about access to ultrasound education and guidance. This cross-sectional survey explores the current landscape of POCUS among healthcare professionals in Ireland.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A cross-sectional, online survey explored POCUS use, education pathways, and governance practices among healthcare professionals in Ireland. A novel 44-item survey was developed using SurveyMonkey and disseminated through national professional organisations from May-August 2023.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: From 411 responses, 38% (n = 158/411) use or previously used POCUS, with the highest uptake in emergency medicine (67%, n = 68/101), intensive care (82%, n = 14/17), and anaesthesiology (81%, n = 13/16), likely due to recognised pathways. POCUS use remains low in general practice (31%, n = 15/49) and sports medicine (30%, n = 10/33). Governance concerns highlighted include 56% (n = 78/139) of POCUS users operate within a scope of practice and 68% have no protocol for escalating incidental findings. 57% (n = 59/103 store) store their images-72% (n = 42/58) on the device itself, and 36% (n = 21/58) on USB drives. Just 51% (n = 77/151) had a mentor during their training. Respondents who completed competency assessments were significantly more likely to store their images (68% vs 40%, p = 0.006) and reported higher self-reported confidence scores for ultrasound machine parameters.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: These findings provide an initial snapshot of the POCUS landscape in Ireland, highlighting both the high levels of interest and the uneven nature of current implementation.

articles.title: Non-optimum temperatures and injury-related emergency room visits among people with disabilities and non-disabilities in Korea: a nationwide time-stratified case-crossover study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Non-optimum temperatures have become more frequent and intense under the climate change, posing serious public health risks, particularly to people with disabilities (PWDs).

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: We investigated the risk of injury-related emergency room (ER) visits due to non-optimum temperatures among PWDs and non-disabled individuals (NDs).

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We obtained ER visit and district-level daily mean temperature data (2002-2019) from the Korea National Health Insurance Service and ERA5-Land, respectively. We utilized a distributed lag non-linear model to analyze associations between extreme temperatures and injury-related ER visits using a nationwide, time-stratified case-crossover design, using the minimum morbidity threshold as the reference. Data were stratified by disability type, severity, and injury site.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: ER visits were increased under both extreme cold and heat for PWDs (odds ratio [OR] 1.049, 95% confidence interval [95%CI] 1.021-1.077; OR 1.342, 95%CI 1.304-1.381, respectively), but only under extreme heat for NDs (OR 1.037, 95%CI 0.987-1.089; OR 1.351, 95%CI 1.280-1.427, respectively). Differences between PWDs and NDs were not significant. Increased ER visits occurred under extreme heat for severe PWDs and under extreme heat and cold for mild PWDs; however, differences between the two groups were not significant. Increased ER visits were associated with physical disabilities under both extremes, but only with intellectual disabilities under extreme heat. Relative to other disability types/severities, increased ER visits were more strongly associated with elbow/forearm injuries under both extremes.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Heterogeneous temperature-related injury risks within PWDs can inform adaptation strategies tailored to specific temperature conditions and disability-related characteristics.

articles.title: A Study of Staff Experiences of Delivering Prehospital Emergency Services in India in the Context of the EMS Agenda 2050 Objectives.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: Emergency care services are crucial to the delivery of modern healthcare. This study investigated prehospital staff experiences in delivering emergency care in a low- to middle-income country (LMIC) India. The study was guided by the EMS Agenda 2050 principles for people-centred and technology-enabled health systems. The study was performed with emergency medical staff from the city of Gandhinagar, India, which is designated as a future smart city.

abstract.label: METHOD
abstract.text: This research used purposive and snowball sampling with 23 participants (ambulance drivers, emergency medical technicians, paramedics and first-aiders) from government, non-governmental and private organisations. Online semistructured interviews explored current prehospital care practices, challenges and opportunities. NVivo software was used for qualitative analysis, with a reflexive thematic analysis approach used to derive themes and present findings.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The thematic analysis identified four primary themes with subthemes: (1) job satisfaction and challenges, (2) attitudes and emotions, (3) technological factors and (4) efficiency and caring. Findings highlight opportunities for technological interventions to enhance citizen awareness and training, support relatives during emergencies, provide bystanders with medically safe guidance and facilitate digitalisation in prehospital care.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: This research advances understanding of the human and operational realities of prehospital care in a future smart-city context. Healthcare professionals demonstrated expertise and empathy in managing complex emergencies while recognising the importance of their role in caring for critically ill and injured patients. Although digital technologies are increasingly integrated into practice, hands-on skills and experiential judgement remain fundamental to effective care. The findings underscore the need for stakeholder collaboration, enhanced professional training and innovative citizen awareness initiatives to strengthen resilient prehospital care systems.

articles.title: Stroke-CORE: master study protocol of the national cohort of the specialty network stroke within the network university medicine in Germany.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Although Germany has a strong history of stroke research, it currently lacks a national harmonised infrastructure for clinical stroke research. To address this gap, the stroke-specific Specialty Network (SN Stroke) of the Network University Medicine (NUM) was established as a comprehensive research platform. Hereby we present the protocol of the Stroke-CORE cohort (COhort for REsearch in Stroke) within SN Stroke enrolling a large representative cohort of patients with acute ischeamic stroke or intracerebral haemorrhage in Germany.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Stroke-CORE is a national, prospective, longitudinal, multi-centre cohort study with a decentralised biobank, structured as a modular umbrella protocol. Adult patients with acute ischaemic stroke or intracerebral haemorrhage, and paediatric stroke patients are enrolled at participating hospitals. Data collection follows four adaptive levels, ranging from a core clinical data set (Level 1) to modules covering the whole stroke care pathway (Level 2), biosamples (Level 3), and voluntary additional modules (Level 4), with follow-up at discharge, 90 days, 180 days (optional), and annually. Enrolment started in August 2026 across 12 initial sites, with a target of 12,750 patients being recruited by 2030.

abstract.label: PERSPECTIVE
abstract.text: Stroke-CORE represents a nationally harmonised cohort spanning prehospital care, acute treatment, rehabilitation, prevention, aftercare, and paediatric stroke. Its adaptive modular design allows continuous expansion with new modules, data streams, and biobanking initiatives without protocol revision. As a sustainable national research platform, Stroke-CORE aims to address key knowledge gaps, facilitate recruitment for clinical trials, and accelerate translational, clinical and outcomes research.

abstract.label: TRIAL REGISTRATION
abstract.text: The protocol is registered at German Clinical Trials Register (DRKS00039775, July 8th, 2026).

articles.title: Stroke care in Germany: evidence gaps and priorities for health services research and quality assurance.
authors: Commission Health Services Research and Quality Assurance of the German Stroke Society (“Deutsche Schlaganfall Gesellschaft, DSG”)

abstract.text: Stroke remains one of the leading causes of morbidity and mortality in Germany and worldwide. Within this position paper by the Commission Health Services Research and Quality Assurance of the German Stroke Society, we summarize current data on stroke epidemiology, healthcare delivery, and quality assurance of stroke in Germany, identify evidence and knowledge gaps across the stroke care pathway, and derive priorities for future health services research and quality assurance. Based on registry and routine administrative data, approximately 253,000 incident and recurrent strokes were estimated to occur in Germany in 2023. Although age-standardized stroke mortality rates had declined substantially since the 1980s, this trend has reached a plateau since 2018. Acute care is predominantly administered in certified stroke units, characterized by high process and outcome quality. However, areas for improvement remain in post-acute care and in structured outpatient aftercare, particularly regarding appropriate care for patients with persistent functional impairments and unmet needs. Future research priorities include for example the utilization of real-world data to document long-term outcomes, the expansion of quality assurance to specific entities such as subarachnoid hemorrhage, and the evaluation of telemedical frameworks in pre-hospital settings. Systematic implementation of Patient-Reported Outcome Measures (PROMs) in research and clinical practice could facilitate the identification of unmet needs and the development of patient-centered care models. In light of recent legislative advancements (e.g., the Health Data Use Act, European Health Data Space) and technological innovations (e.g., AI-driven applications), new opportunities are emerging to bolster health services research and further optimize the management of stroke patients.

articles.title: inproTeamED - clinical reasoning in the emergency department as an individual and interprofessional process: a qualitative analysis.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: Patients in the emergency department (ED) are assessed and treated by the ED-Team consisting of nurses and physicians. The clinical assessment (CA) of emergency patients and the clinical reasoning (CR) of both professions play a decisive role in determining the quality of emergency care. This pilot study explores CR in daily routine practice of the ED on a cognitive-individual level, relying on the Dual-process Theory and on a social-interprofessional level, arguing interprofessional collaboration (IPC) as a part of CR. At least, organizational-structural factors influencing CR are analyzed as a third level.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This is a qualitative study of 13 semi-structured individual interviews with nurses and physicians from three EDs in Germany, analysed using content analysis and methodological fundation.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: In the individual-cognitive CR, both physicians and nurses groups identified similar key factors for CA and used Systems 1 and 2 of the Dual-process Theory in their CR. On the social-interprofessional level, IPC was generally described positively, naming characteristics of good IPC and communication barriers were reported as rare. As possible organizational-structural factors influencing CR working experience as a prerequisite, size and region of the ED, age structure of the team and digitization were found.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: This pilot study provides insights into the CR of nurses and physicians in the ED and analyzes CR on an individual-cognitive, a social-interprofessional and an organizational-structural level, allowing to conclusions regarding the prerequisites for successful ED-teams.

articles.title: Fall-risk in genetic variable cytochrome P450 enzymes and exposure to anticholinergic drugs - a pilot-analysis from the ADRED-study.

abstract.label: AIMS
abstract.text: The use of anticholinergic (AC) drugs in older adults is associated with falls, but it is not clear how to differentiate the individual risk. The aim was to analyze associations of pharmacogenetic slow CYP2D6 and CYP2C19 metabolism of AC drugs with falls in older adults.

abstract.label: PATIENTS AND METHODS
abstract.text: Cohort study of adverse drug reactions in emergency departments (ADRED-study). Patients ≥65 years, with use of ≥three drugs, and pharmacogenetic results for CYP2D6 and CYP2C19. Anticholinergic burden scores (ABS) derived from medication were analyzed, differentiating for ABS derived from drugs metabolized via CYP2D6 (ABS2D6) and CYP2C19 (ABS2C19).

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: N = 659 patients were included. ABS2D6 showed a significant association with falls in logistic regression analysis of OR 1.57 [95%CI 1.09-2.26].
