abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Timely follow-up after mental behavioral health (MBH) crises can improve health outcomes; moreover, it is a national quality metric. We aimed to improve the completion of 7-day follow-up after emergency department (ED) discharge for youth with an MBH concern from 28.7% of discharges to 50.0% within 12 months.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We used quality improvement methods from November 1, 2024, to October 31, 2025, across 3 primary care sites and 2 ED sites. Baseline data, literature reviews, and lived experience identified key drivers and failure modes. We developed 2 interventions: (1) direct phone outreach after discharge and (2) increased access in pediatric primary care (PPC). The primary outcome measure was the percentage of ED MBH discharges with a completed follow-up appointment within 7 days of discharge. Process measures included the percentage of patients who received a postdischarge outreach call and who followed up within PPC. The balancing measure was return ED MBH visits within 30 days.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The mean follow-up percentage increased from 28.7% (n = 258) to 40.3% (n = 334). Follow-up for Medicaid-insured patients increased from 24% to 35% and remained stable for commercially insured patients (42%), decreasing our equity gap by 11%. Outreach calls occurred following 52.4% of discharges. Follow-up visits within PPC increased from 3.5% of discharges to 10.7% of discharges. There was no change in return ED visits within 30 days of ED discharge.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Increasing access to pediatric primary care and implementing timely postdischarge follow-up calls can improve follow-up within a large healthcare system for patients discharged from the ED for MBH concerns.

articles.title: Advanced Analytics Show Domain-Specific Performance Changes After Anterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstruction in National Football League Players.

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: To evaluate return to play, performance, and assess performance changes after anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction using advanced statistics in National Football League players.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: National Football League players who underwent anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction (ACLR) between 2017 and 2024 were identified using publicly available databases and injury reports. Demographic and outcome data for 1 year preinjury to 2 years postinjury were obtained. Return to play was defined as being listed as active for a regular season game after injury. Return to performance was defined as returning to greater than 90% of preinjury performance. Our primary performance outcome was Sports Information Solutions points above replacement (PAR). Binary logistic regression was used to determine factors associated with return to play and return to performance. Preinjury and postinjury performance data at the first and second postinjury year were compared with paired t-tests.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: We included 237 players in return-to-play and 173 players in return-to-performance analyses. Of players, 75.5% returned to play; players with more preinjury games played, more index games played, starters, and players with greater preinjury PAR were more likely to return to play (P = .03, P < .001, P < .001, P < .001, respectively). Fifty-one percent of players who returned to play returned to performance; younger age and players with lower preinjury PAR were significantly more likely to return to performance (P = .004, P < .001). Total PAR was significantly decreased at the postinjury year 1 and year 2 seasons (P = .002, P = .004), driven at both time points by significantly decreased rushing (P = .02, P = .001) and pass coverage (P = .003, P = .03) PAR.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: After anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction, National Football League players with more preinjury games played and higher preinjury performance are more likely to return to play; younger players with lower preinjury performance are more likely to return to performance; and there is a significant decrease in overall performance 1 and 2 years after injury, driven by decreased rushing and pass coverage performance.

abstract.label: LEVEL OF EVIDENCE
abstract.text: Level IV, retrospective case series.

articles.title: Pygmy blue whale feeding drives greater nocturnal than diurnal song production.

abstract.text: Effective management of threatened and migratory species requires monitoring of critical behaviours, such as foraging. Passive acoustic monitoring can provide cost-effective, long-term observations on the relative abundance of vocal animals across large spatial scales. However, linking specific sounds to behavioural contexts can be challenging, especially for cryptic and aquatic species. This study combined passive acoustic and biologging data to explore whether observed periods of greater nocturnal than diurnal song production were linked to feeding by eastern Indian Ocean pygmy blue whales, Balaenoptera musculus brevicauda. The proportion of time available for singing was modelled as a function of geographical region, diel period and the presence or absence of feeding dives with generalized linear mixed models, based on 130.1 days of diving data. Top-ranked models indicated less time was available for singing during diurnal feeding periods compared to nocturnal feeding periods and non-feeding periods during the day and night. These findings suggest that diurnal feeding by pygmy blue whales reduces the time available for song production. Therefore, greater nocturnal than diurnal song production may provide an acoustic indicator of population-level feeding activity for pygmy blue whales between the Perth Canyon and offshore of the northwest shelf of Western Australia.

articles.title: Injury mechanism and return to play duration in non-contact muscle injuries in elite football players: a case series.

abstract.text: A retrospective case series was conducted to compare return to play (RTP) duration in elite football players from a first-division team with lower-limb non-contact muscle injuries (NCMIs). Cases were compared according to symptom timing onset and the presence (typical) or absence (atypical) of a typical injury mechanism, such as a specific movement or identifiable moment during which the injury occurred. During the study period, 43 NCMIs were recorded in 28 football players, including 37 with typical mechanism and six without. RTP duration was substantially shorter following atypical than typical injuries (median 2.5 days [IQR 0.5-3.0] vs 12.0 days [IQR 8.0-24.0], respectively; Mann-Whitney U = 221.0, p < 0.001; Cliff's δ = 0.991, player-cluster bootstrap 95% CI 0.958-1.000). No injury recurrences were observed among the atypical injuries for at least nine months after RTP. Given the limited number of participants, cases and the exploratory nature of the study, these preliminary findings should be interpreted cautiously.

articles.title: Central Command During Exercise: Hierarchical Integration of Feedforward and Feedback Cardiovascular Control.

abstract.text: Cardiovascular regulation during exercise has traditionally been explained by the interaction between central command, a feedforward neural mechanism originating in higher brain centers, and peripheral cardiovascular reflexes, particularly the exercise pressor reflex and arterial baroreflex. Although central command is widely recognized as initiating autonomic adjustments in proportion to perceived effort, accumulating evidence indicates that its role extends well beyond the generation of parallel autonomic drive. In this review, we synthesize experimental findings spanning spinal and brainstem neurophysiology to integrative studies in intact animals and humans, showing that descending signals associated with central command may access the neural circuitry involved in processing peripheral cardiovascular information and regulating autonomic output. Neurophysiological studies identify multiple sites of interaction, including inhibitory gating of group III/IV muscle afferent transmission within the spinal dorsal horn and modulation of barosensory processing within the nucleus of the solitary tract. At the integrative level, studies of the arterial baroreflex, exercise pressor reflex, and trigeminally mediated diving reflex further demonstrate that central command can selectively regulate reflex expression and modify interactions among competing autonomic inputs rather than summating with them. Together, these observations support a conceptual evolution of central command from a feedforward initiator to a hierarchical autonomic organizing system (CHAOS) that dynamically integrates central command with peripheral cardiovascular feedback according to behavioral context. This CHAOS framework provides a unifying physiological interpretation for findings traditionally considered within individual reflex systems and offers a broader perspective on cardiovascular regulation during exercise and other conditions imposing competing autonomic demands.

articles.title: Efficacy of Apparent Diffusion Coefficient Sampling in Muscle Tears and Intersex Differences in Professional Football Players: A Cohort Study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is the gold standard for monitoring the evolution of muscle injuries in athletes, although no established quantitative measure of recovery currently exists.

abstract.label: HYPOTHESIS
abstract.text: Apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) values may provide a quantitative measure of muscle healing, and sex-related differences may exist in the evolution of muscle injuries.

abstract.label: STUDY DESIGN
abstract.text: Single-center retrospective observational cohort study.

abstract.label: LEVEL OF EVIDENCE
abstract.text: Level 2a.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Twenty-six professional football (soccer) players (13 male ,13 female) undergoing MRI for muscle injury were retrospectively selected between October 2020 and June 2024. All athletes underwent MRI at baseline (T0) and at 2-week follow-up, including diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) acquisitions with b values of 0-100-800 s/mm². Two musculoskeletal radiologists measured ADC values within the index lesions at each examination. Changes in ADC between the two time points (ΔADC) were assessed using a paired-samples t test, while sex-related differences were evaluated using the Mann-Whitney U test.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The overall mean ADC value at the lesion site decreased from 2.06 ± 0.35 mm2/s at T0 to 1.61 ± 0.30 mm2/s at follow-up corresponding to a mean ΔADC of 0.44 ± 0.20 and a 21.84% reduction. The difference between T0 and follow-up was statistically significant (t = 8.12; P < 0.001). Mean ΔADC values were 0.32 ± 0.20 mm²/s in male players and 0.56 ± 0.25 mm²/s in female players, respectively, with a statistically significant difference between sexes (z = -2.95; P = 0.003). When only hamstring injuries were considered, female players showed a significantly greater decrease in ADC over time than male players (Mann-Whitney U test; exact P = 0.02), with mean ΔADC values of 0.56 ± 0.30 and 0.26 ± 0.08 mm²/s, respectively.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Muscle injury is associated with an acute increase in ADC values followed by a progressive decrease during healing. ADC may therefore represent a quantitative imaging biomarker for monitoring muscle recovery.

abstract.label: CLINICAL RELEVANCE
abstract.text: ADC measurement within muscle tears may provide a quantitative assessment of healing status and support individualized rehabilitation strategies in athletes. Sex-related differences may exist in injury pathophysiology and recovery patterns relevant to safe return to play.

articles.title: Integrative review of consumers' experiences of care in emergency departments for suicidality.
Will a sweet treat make cough retreat? In children presenting with acute cough due to upper respiratory tract infection, does honey treatment reduce cough severity?
Is Doppler ultrasound superior to nuclear scintigraphy for diagnosing testicular torsion?
Do trends in alcohol harm mirror consumption? An analysis of adolescent ambulance attendances.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: Adolescent alcohol consumption has declined across many high-income countries since the early 2000s, yet it remains unclear whether these reductions have led to less alcohol-related harm, particularly among higher-risk groups.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Using the National Ambulance Surveillance System, we examined ambulance attendances for alcohol intoxication among adolescents (10-19 years) in Victoria, Australia, from January 2012 and December 2023. Multivariable regression, stratified by gender, assessed monthly changes in attendance rates per 10 000 by remoteness, adjusting for seasonality and COVID-19 lockdowns.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 25 928 attendances were recorded. A small but significant monthly decline in alcohol intoxication ambulance attendance was observed among males in major cities (B = -0.01 [0.01], P < .001). No significant trends were identified for males in regional areas or for females in metropolitan or regional areas.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Despite declining adolescent alcohol consumption, intoxication-related ambulance attendances have remained largely stable over the past decade. The modest decline among males in metropolitan areas was considerably smaller than survey-reported declines in consumption, suggesting that population surveys capture different drinking patterns than those leading to acute harms. These findings highlight the need for ongoing monitoring and targeted prevention strategies, particularly for high-risk subgroups and regional populations.

articles.title: Enhanced Pediatric Emergency Readiness through Regional Collaboration: Recent Advances in the Field.

Who Benefits From Aggressive Surgery? Predictors of Survival and Short-Term Functional Status After Decompressive Craniectomy for Penetrating Traumatic Brain Injury in the Gaza War: A Consecutive Wartime Cohort.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: Operative series of penetrating traumatic brain injury (pTBI) are vulnerable to treatment-selection bias because patients with adverse features are often managed non-operatively. We evaluated all-cause in-hospital mortality and short-term discharge function in a consecutive wartime cohort under a permissive decompressive craniectomy policy.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We retrospectively analyzed a two-center 2025 registry including 151 consecutive patients with CT-confirmed pTBI who underwent decompressive craniectomy. The primary outcome was all-cause in-hospital mortality; the secondary outcome was discharge Glasgow Outcome Scale (GOS) among survivors with internally consistent entries. Mortality associations were assessed using Fisher exact tests and a 4-covariate Firth penalized logistic model with bootstrap optimism correction and post-hoc intercept recalibration.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Mortality was 67/147 (46%; 95% CI 37.4-54.0); assigning the 4 unresolved cases as survivors or deaths yielded a whole-cohort range of 44%-47%. Bilaterally fixed and dilated pupils were associated with 10/12 deaths (83%) and remained the only independent predictor in the prespecified model (OR 9.38, 95% CI 1.48-59.4). Transventricular injury carried 13/20 mortality (65%), whereas bihemispheric trajectory was not associated with death. Among 80 survivors, 60 had internally consistent discharge GOS and 41/60 (68%) had GOS 4-5. Three-month GOS was available in only 12/151 patients.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Severe trajectory features were not uniformly fatal, whereas bilaterally fixed and dilated pupils remained the strongest independent prognostic marker. The findings argue against absolute futility judgments based on trajectory alone. Because discharge function was incompletely ascertained and longer-term follow-up was limited, these data demonstrate survivability under a permissive wartime operative policy rather than long-term functional benefit.

articles.title: Traumatic Emergency Thoracotomy for Resuscitation in Shock (TETRiS): a national service evaluation of resuscitative thoracotomy practice outside the operating theatre.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Resuscitative thoracotomy (RT) is performed in patients with traumatic cardiac arrest or peri-arrest to treat potentially reversible causes of circulatory collapse. Optimal patient selection and timing remain uncertain, and existing evidence is largely retrospective, often excluding prehospital deaths. This prospective service evaluation examined contemporary RT practice and outcomes across a national major trauma system, including prehospital and emergency department settings.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Prospective 12-month observational study across 20 UK Helicopter Emergency Medical Services and 26 Major Trauma Centre Emergency Departments, using the PHOTON, TERN, and NaTRIC research networks.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 116 patients underwent RT, of which 82 (70.7%) were performed prehospital. Median age was 30 years, 97 patients (83.6%) were male, and 81 (69.8%) sustained penetrating injury. Suspected cardiac tamponade was the most common indication for RT (72/116 [62.1%]), although operative findings demonstrated exsanguinating haemorrhage in 82 patients (70.7%). Overall, 50 patients (43.1%) achieved return of spontaneous circulation and eight (6.9%) survived to hospital discharge. Survival was strongly associated with pathophysiological cause, duration of arrest, and physiological state at the time of intervention, with substantially better outcomes observed in patients with cardiac tamponade than exsanguination. Patients undergoing emergency department RT demonstrated shorter arrest durations, more favourable physiology, and higher survival than those undergoing prehospital RT. There were no survivors beyond 10 min of traumatic cardiac arrest.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: In this prospective national evaluation of RT practice, outcomes were strongly associated with the pathophysiological cause and duration of arrest, and the residual physiology present at the time of intervention. The most favourable outcomes were observed in patients with cardiac tamponade and those undergoing RT before irreversible physiological deterioration.

articles.title: Cross-cultural adaptation, consensus using Delphi method and content validity of the first French emergency department patient-reported experience measure.
articles.journal_full: Journal of epidemiology and population health

abstract.label: AIM
abstract.text: The aims of this study were 1) to perform cross-cultural adaptation of the ED PREM into the French ED PREM; 2) to seek consensus on this version using the Delphi method and 3) establish its content validity.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This study was designed following the Consensus-based Standards for the selection of health Measurement Instruments guidelines. A cross-cultural adaptation of the ED PREM, renamed the French ED PREM, was performed. Consensus was sought through a Delphi method involving an expert committee, including the original developer and patient partners. Content validity was assessed with 50 patients and 7 healthcare professionals in the first round, and 10 patients in the second round, evaluating the relevance, comprehensibility, and comprehensiveness of the French ED PREM. The endpoint was an item-level content validity index (I-CVI) > 0.78 and a scale-level content validity index (S-CVI) > 0.90 without suggestions for revision.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Consensus was achieved in two rounds, with 100% expert participation and agreement. All French ED PREM items achieved a robust content validity (I-CVI > 0.78, S-CVI > 0,90) and demonstrated excellent agreement among evaluators beyond chance (k > 0.74).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Through a rigorous cross-cultural adaptation of the ED PREM, this international collaborative research has demonstrated the content validity of the French ED PREM. This work contributes to the international harmonization of patient experience measures and may facilitate future comparisons across healthcare systems.

articles.title: Barriers and Priorities for Strengthening Prehospital Trauma Care in Hawassa, Ethiopia.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Prehospital emergency care remains underdeveloped in Ethiopia, particularly outside Addis Ababa. This study assessed frontline provider perspectives on barriers and priorities for strengthening prehospital trauma care in Hawassa.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We surveyed 57 emergency care personnel at Hawassa University Comprehensive Specialized Hospital and Hawassa Dispatch Center in April-May 2025. The 35-question survey, adapted from the World Health Organization Prehospital Emergency Care Assessment Tool, assessed infrastructure, workforce, protocols, communication, and governance. Direct operational questions were analyzed among prehospital personnel only. Questions addressing the prehospital-hospital interface were summarized separately for prehospital and hospital-based personnel.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among prehospital personnel, long distances to facilities were the leading infrastructure challenge (47%, 7/15), whereas inadequate training (47%, 7/15) and burnout (40%, 6/15) were the main workforce concerns. Airway management was the top training priority (67%, 10/15 first choice). Top protocol gaps were poor adherence (40%, 6/15) and inadequate training (27%, 4/15). Among prehospital and hospital-based personnel, respectively, equipment use and maintenance was selected as the leading training need by 40% (6/15) and 33% (14/42), whereas emergency medical procedures were selected by 33% (5/15) and 29% (12/42). Staff recruitment and retention was the leading funding priority in both groups, selected by 47% (7/15) and 45% (19/42), respectively. Improved infrastructure and road conditions were selected as the highest priority for addressing ambulance response times among 67% (10/15) and 62% (26/42), respectively.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Emergency care personnel identified gaps in infrastructure, equipment, training, protocols, and coordination. Priorities for intervention included restoring the emergency hotline, standardizing ambulance equipment, providing xABCDE-focused training, and implementing standardized handover protocols.

articles.title: Use of Portable Ultrasound by Nonradiologists to Triage Women With Abnormal Clinical Breast Examination Findings: A Prospective Study in India.

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: Clinical breast examination (CBE) is widely used for breast cancer screening and evaluation of symptomatic women in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). However, its limited specificity leads to high false-positive rates and unnecessary referrals. We evaluated a point-of-care triage strategy using portable ultrasound devices (PUDs), performed by nonradiologist clinicians, to improve the positive predictive value (PPV) of CBE and reduce referrals.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Women age 40-75 years with abnormal CBE findings were recruited from two settings: asymptomatic women identified through community-based screening and symptomatic women presenting to breast clinics. Trained nonradiologist clinicians used PUDs to classify findings as triage-negative (no abnormality/benign) or triage-positive (suspicious). All participants underwent standard diagnostic evaluation irrespective of PUD findings.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 319 women were enrolled (149 screening; 170 diagnostic). PUD triage was positive in 44.3% of women in the screening group and 72.4% in the diagnostic group. Breast cancer was diagnosed in 37 (24.8%) women in the screening group and 121 (71.2%) in the diagnostic group. PUD triage identified all cancers in the screening setting and all but nine in the diagnostic setting, yielding an overall sensitivity of 94.3% and specificity of 76.7%. Use of PUD substantially improved PPV and reduced referrals by approximately 50%.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Point-of-care ultrasound performed by trained nonradiologist clinicians can effectively triage women with abnormal CBE findings, improving PPV and reducing unnecessary referrals. This approach may enhance efficiency of breast cancer early detection programs in LMICs. Further studies are warranted to assess performance in routine program settings.

articles.title: Brace for impact: A roadmap for the future of mental health in large-scale combat operations.
articles.journal_full: Military psychology : the official journal of the Division of Military Psychology, American Psychological Association

abstract.text: Large-scale combat operations (LSCO) are expected to present critical challenges to military units in terms of austere conditions, the potential for misinformation, specific LSCO-related threats, and the limitations of access to traditional medical care. As part of a special issue of Military Psychology dedicated to the topic of mental health in LSCO, 25 articles address these challenges. Articles cover key threats such as mass casualty events, drone warfare, and threats to the community. Articles also identify how traditional military mental health support may need to be adapted to take prolonged field care into account, with a focus on mental health support becoming the responsibility of individuals, informal peers, trained peers, and leaders. Furthermore, the articles address special topics such as the impact of LSCO on medical personnel burnout, attitudes toward novel solutions such as mindfulness, and training models for integrating mental skills into simulations and field-based exercises. Collectively, these articles inform the development of a schematic model of LSCO Mental Health. In addition, future research topics provide direction for assessing, preventing, and intervening with mental health health and cognitive strain in the LSCO context. By bringing this array of articles together, the field can prepare more effectively to meet the psychological demands of the LSCO battlespace.

articles.title: PhysBridge: Response-supervised grid pretraining with physics-constrained local correction for transferable power-system intelligence.

abstract.text: Operating modern power grids requires coordinated solutions for optimal dispatch, state estimation, price prediction, and contingency analysis, yet these tasks are usually modeled separately. We present PhysBridge, a response-oriented pretraining framework in which historical windows provide context while solver-generated perturbation responses, active constraints, and local sensitivities define the pretraining targets. PhysBridge combines a temporal-graph encoder with a Primal-Dual Response Bridge (PDR-Bridge) that performs safeguarded local refinement and outputs transferable primal, projection-dual, sensitivity, and health tokens. Across IEEE 14-, 30-, 57-, 118-, and 300-bus systems, the benchmark contains 26.3 million solver-generated perturbation-response pairs; in the 300-bus transfer setting, pretraining uses only the 21.04 million nominal pairs from the 14-, 30-, 57-, and 118-bus source topologies. Across three runs on unseen IEEE 300-bus transfer with 10% labels, PhysBridge obtains a 2.21±0.05% OPF cost gap, 96.3±0.2% feasibility, 1.84±0.05 $/MWh LMP MAE, and 91.6±0.3% contingency/fault event macro F1. Relative to a matched rollout-only model trained on the same source corpus without response targets or bridge refinement, these values correspond to a 50.8% lower OPF gap and a 7.4 percentage-point higher event F1. The bridge requires 12.4 ms per 300-bus forward pass and activates fallback on 4.6% of stressed windows. Comparisons with supervised-only OPF specialists that do not receive matched solver-generated pretraining are interpreted as task-relevant performance under the proposed pretraining regime, not as architecture-only superiority.

articles.title: An Empirical Snapshot of Local Nutrition Governance Capacity in the Rasuwa District of Nepal Before the Flood Surge of August 2026.

abstract.text: On August 26, 2026, flash floods swept through the Rasuwa district of Nepal, causing mass casualties and severe destruction. Research on disasters has led to valuable recommendations on how governments can be more attentive to warning signs and react more rapidly, and how tapping into local capacity and know-how can lead to more effective responses. However, in most crises not much is known about individual or institutional capacities that predated a shock or what resources donors and governments subsequently should bolster to support emergency responses and build resilience. In this Commentary, we draw on the self-reported data of civil servants and other local professionals tasked with implementing the national multisectoral nutrition strategy in Rasuwa. Data collection in 2024 predated the flood by roughly 2 years. The survey measured routine governance capacity, not disaster-response capacity specifically, and yet such data offer some insights into local capacity before the latest disaster and help our understanding of which elements were already under strain. The aim of this Commentary is not to report full survey findings but to highlight observations most relevant to the 2026 Rasuwa flood. Broadly, we suggest that routine governance research on nutrition and other technical topics of relevance can serve as a baseline for disaster recovery and that global calls for the localization of aid require much deeper understanding and measurement of local capacity to act.

articles.title: Opioids as the earliest acute treatment for emergency department headache and short-term all-cause emergency department return: A two-center comparative cohort study.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To compare first-line emergency department (ED) treatment classes for acute headache on short-term all-cause ED return.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: In-ED pain relief anchors acute headache trials but is recorded incompletely in routine care. All-cause ED return has not been used to compare first-line treatments; guidelines favor dopamine-receptor antagonists over opioids for acute migraine.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Retrospective two-center cohort of adults treated for headache in the ED (MIMIC-IV-ED, 2011-2019; MC-MED, 2020-2022); first-line treatment was the earliest qualifying acute agent. The primary contrast was opioids versus guideline-preferred dopamine-receptor antagonists. The primary outcome was 72-h all-cause ED return among discharged patients; 7-day return was secondary. Estimates, adjusted for prespecified confounders available in both databases, are reported as risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs), pooled and site-specific.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 13,285 treated adults (10,799 MIMIC-IV-ED; 2486 MC-MED), MIMIC-IV-ED opioid recipients were older than dopamine-antagonist recipients (median 48 vs. 39 years) and more often high-acuity at triage (980/1895 [51.7%] vs. 900/3056 [29.5%]). First-line opioids were associated with higher 72-h all-cause ED return (adjusted risks 6.8% vs. 3.8%; RR 1.78; 95% CI 1.31-2.32) and 7-day return (10.7% vs. 6.6%; RR 1.62; 95% CI 1.28-1.99). The MC-MED estimate was directionally concordant but anchors direction only (85 opioid-treated discharged patients). Restricting to a headache-coded or headache-triaged return attenuated the association, which was no longer statistically significant (72-h RR 1.31; 95% CI 0.91-1.88).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Patients selected for first-line opioids were older and higher acuity and returned more often within 72 h and 7 days at both health systems. These risk-adjusted associations, conditional on discharge, reflect all-cause ED utilization rather than confirmed headache recurrence and do not establish that changing first-line class would change return rates. The attenuated headache-specific result is as consistent with administrative undercoding as with no association and is not a justification for prescribing opioids.

articles.title: A NATA Task Force: Preventing Exertional Heat Stroke Death in American Football Linemen.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Linemen make up over 90% of all exertional heat stroke (EHS) deaths in collegiate and secondary school American football deaths.

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: This document aims to accomplish 3 purposes: (1) briefly summarize the need for specific risk reduction recommendations for EHS in secondary school and collegiate American football linemen, (2) provide new recommendations for the reduction of EHS in football linemen developed with Delphi procedures to build consensus, and (3) summarize the evidence for the existing and new best-practice recommendations that currently exist for EHS risk reduction.

abstract.label: DESIGN
abstract.text: Delphi-based Task Force Recommendations.

abstract.label: LEVEL OF EVIDENCE
abstract.text: Level 3.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A multidisciplinary group of experts was convened to build consensus on EHS risk reduction strategies for secondary school and collegiate football linemen. The process involved a narrative review of relevant literature, followed by iterative rounds of anonymous Delphi surveys to refine and validate the recommendations.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 20 recommendations were identified, scored, and retained for EHS risk reduction in American football linemen. Key recommendations include the education of coaches and strength and conditioning coaches on EHS risk reduction and treatment, the implementation of heat acclimatization protocols, and weather-based exercise modifications. The recommendations emphasize the importance of the avoidance of high-intensity aerobic testing during transition periods and the importance of having on-site cooling modalities.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The high rates of EHS in American football linemen highlight the need for targeted risk reduction strategies. In American football, the design and implementation of workouts for linemen must differ from other players on the team. Linemen require position-specific work-to-rest ratios and tailored training programs.

abstract.label: CLINICAL RELEVANCE
abstract.text: By adhering to best practices and continuously updating guidelines based on emerging evidence, the safety and well-being of American football players can be significantly enhanced. These recommendations provide a comprehensive framework for reducing the risk of EHS and improving outcomes for American football linemen.

articles.title: Breakout Session 7: Design and Construction.
articles.journal_full: Disaster medicine and public health preparedness

abstract.text: Establishing leadership and management structures for alternate care facilities (ACFs) presented governance challenges distinct from those of conventional hospital operations and were frequently shaped as much by political and inter-organizational dynamics as by clinical need. Symposium participants summarized operational lessons from leading ACFs across multiple jurisdictions and partnership models. Effective ACFs typically mirrored hospital executive structures while operating under hybrid governance models that distributed authority, liability, and resources across multiple hospital systems and state agencies. Hospital Incident Command System frameworks provided necessary scaffolding but were insufficient on their own; success depended on pre-existing inter-agency relationships and on credible leaders with the gravitas to mobilize resources across organizational boundaries. Persistent challenges included credentialing and electronic medical record access delays, political directives that superseded clinical judgment, and severe interpersonal conflict. Recommended best practices include pre-identifying ACF leaders, embedding human resources and behavioral health support, and clearly defining the ACF mission throughout activation.

articles.title: Alternate Care Facilities Symposium-Breakout Session 6: Site Selection.
articles.journal_full: Disaster medicine and public health preparedness

abstract.text: The use of alternate care facilities (ACFs) is an often-considered mechanism to increase care capacity during a patient surge event; however, robust guidance on appropriate site selection is limited. During the Alternate Care Facilities Symposium, we conducted a facilitated breakout session with participants to explore their experience in selecting ACF sites during prior emergencies. This was done to determine best practices regarding the site selection process, as well as successes, challenges, and lessons learned. Participants reported that site feasibility was primarily driven by pre-existing infrastructure, regulatory constraints, and operational factors rather than physical size or political mandate. Large congregate spaces and decommissioned hospitals frequently proved unsuitable, while successful sites were typically non-congregate, located near partner hospitals, and able to support patient dignity, safety, and privacy. Political pressures often resulted in facilities that were underutilized or operationally constrained, while infrastructure deficiencies created major barriers. Given that site selection is a critical determinant of ACF success, early multidisciplinary assessments, realistic capacity planning, and pre-activation walkthroughs and training exercises may improve future emergency response preparedness.

articles.title: Breakout Session 1: Patient Selection Criteria.
articles.journal_full: Disaster medicine and public health preparedness

abstract.text: This summary focuses on findings from the Patient Selection Breakout Session of the Alternate Care Facility (ACF) Symposium. Findings demonstrate that patient selection criteria were primarily shaped by community needs and operational constraints rather than clinical factors alone. Participants described using local population needs as a starting point to define ACF eligibility. Resource availability emerged as the dominant determinant of admission criteria, often superseding traditional clinical thresholds. External pressures from hospital systems frequently drove expansion of criteria to include higher-acuity patients requiring balancing of resources and capabilities. Successful selection criteria were characterized by iterative, multidisciplinary reviews incorporating frontline staff and strong interagency collaboration. Key challenges included clinician hesitancy to transfer patients to the ACF, limited external communication regarding capabilities, and persistent tension between flexible criteria and standardized guidance for dissemination. Additional barriers included staffing limitations, facility design constraints, and unanticipated logistical factors. External influences, including political decision-making, at times disrupted operational alignment with frontline realities. Patient selection represents a dynamic, resource-driven process requiring continuous reassessment. These findings support the need for flexible, resource-informed selection criteria, coordination with hospital partners, incorporation of frontline expertise into decision-making, and integration of discharge planning services to expand appropriate patient populations while maintaining quality care.

articles.title: Seasonal Variation in Preschool Hearing Screening Outcomes.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: To determine whether pass and referral rates for pure-tone audiometry (PTA) and otoacoustic emissions (OAE) demonstrate seasonal variation in preschool-aged children, and to explore whether these patterns may be associated with middle ear pathology related to upper respiratory tract infections.

abstract.label: DESIGN
abstract.text: We conducted a secondary analysis of a randomized controlled trial comparing single-stage OAE versus 2-stage PTA plus OAE screening in preschool children from 2023 to 2026. A total of 7416 children completed at least 1 screening modality in at least 1 ear. Children who failed screening underwent tympanometry to characterize middle ear status. Multivariable logistic regression models were used to assess the association between screening season and failure rates, adjusting for age, home language, and teacher-reported concerns. In addition, a time series model using national upper respiratory infection emergency department visit data was developed to estimate seasonal variation in middle ear effusion rates.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Failure rates were higher for OAE than PTA and demonstrated clear seasonal patterns. OAE failure rates peaked in spring (17.9%) and winter (15.2%) and were lowest in summer (8.5%) and fall (10.3%). PTA showed a similar pattern, with the highest failure rates in spring (8.3%), followed by winter (5.5%), and the lowest in summer (3.1%) and fall (3.6%). In adjusted analyses, the odds of failure for both OAE and PTA were significantly lower in summer and fall compared with winter (PTA: summer odds ratio (OR) = 0.54, p = 0.004; fall OR = 0.60, p = 0.01; OAE: summer OR = 0.47, p < 0.001; fall OR = 0.57, p < 0.001). For PTA, the odds of failure were significantly higher in spring compared with winter (OR = 1.50, p = 0.004), whereas no significant difference between spring and winter was observed for OAE (OR = 1.15, p = 0.09). Pairwise comparisons demonstrated significantly higher odds of failure in spring compared with summer and fall for both modalities (all p < 0.001). Tympanometry in failed ears most commonly demonstrated type B patterns across all seasons, consistent with middle ear pathology. Modeled effusion rates closely paralleled observed screening failure rates, with shared seasonal peaks and summer nadirs.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Hearing screening failure rates in preschool children vary by season, with higher failure rates observed in winter and spring. These patterns may be driven in part by seasonal variation in middle ear pathology associated with upper respiratory infections. The timing of screening may influence referral rates and should be considered when designing preschool hearing screening programs.

articles.title: Depth sets the recovery clock: evidence for a time-at-pressure effect in sea lions.

abstract.text: All air-breathing marine vertebrates face the same fundamental trade-off: time spent foraging underwater must be offset by surface recovery between dives. For decades, the dominant view in diving physiology has been that post-dive duration (PDD) reflects the repayment of oxygen debt and clearance of carbon dioxide and lactate. Using more than 800 000 dives from five sea lion species across 18 colonies spanning tropical to subpolar waters, we quantified how PDD scales with dive depth and duration and evaluated whether this pattern is consistent with metabolic recovery interpretations or instead points to depth-linked constraints. We found that PDD increases primarily and linearly with depth, while dive duration contributes to PDD only at greater depths, a relationship conserved across species despite pronounced differences in body mass, dive physiology and foraging ecology. Our findings conflict with predictions of metabolic recovery interpretations and point to a pressure-linked mechanism in which time at depth and resulting inert-gas loading shape surface recovery. By highlighting pressure-linked inert-gas management as a central candidate mechanism for surface interval regulation in inhalation divers, our study revises a central assumption in diving physiology, with broad consequences for understanding foraging efficiency, habitat accessibility and vulnerability to environmental change in air-breathing marine vertebrates.

articles.title: Comparing Internal Self-Assessment and External Evaluation of Hospital Safety Index (HSI) for Disaster Response: A Cross-Sectional Study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Hospitals must ensure preparedness and safety to maintain services during disasters. Results from the Hospital Safety Index (HSI) often indicate that hospitals are safe and capable; however, it is important to verify whether these assessments are consistent across different evaluators. This study compared hospital safety scores between internal evaluators (hospital staff) and external evaluators.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This cross-sectional study was conducted in 2022 using documented hospital safety assessment data from hospitals supervised by Kermanshah University of Medical Sciences (KUMS) in western Iran. Independent-samples t-tests, the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC), and Bland-Altman plots were used to compare mean scores and assess agreement between evaluators.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: For structural safety, the difference between internal and external evaluators was not significant (95% CI, -9.19 to 9.67). In contrast, the differences were pronounced for non-structural safety (95% CI, 7.00 to 20.63) and functional safety (95% CI, 10.56 to 28.84), with both confidence intervals excluding zero. Agreement between evaluators was poor across most hospital safety domains (ICC < 0.05).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Internal evaluators rated their hospitals significantly safer than external evaluators did. Given the pronounced differences in non-structural and functional safety, and the poor inter-rater agreement across most domains, relying solely on internal assessments may mislead hospital managers about disaster preparedness. Hospital managers should therefore regard external evaluation as an opportunity to reveal their hospital's vulnerabilities in disaster safety.

articles.title: Instrumental Support Calls vs. Caring Contacts Texts to Prevent Suicide in Adolescents and Adults: The SPARC Randomized Clinical Trial.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: The authors sought to determine whether augmenting usual suicide care with follow-up in the form of instrumental support calls (ISC) or two-way Caring Contacts texts (CC) works best to reduce suicidal ideation and behavior (SI/SB) in adolescents and adults.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: The Suicide Prevention Among Recipients of Care (SPARC) Trial is a pragmatic comparative effectiveness randomized clinical trial stratified by age, with participants randomized in a 1:1 ratio to ISC or CC. Participants were adolescents (12-17 years, N=723) and adults (18+ years, N=797) who screened at risk for suicide in emergency departments (N=9) and primary care clinics (N=36) between May 2021 and July 2022; primary data collection was completed in August 2023. Outcomes included Columbia-Suicide Severity Rating Scale SI/SB score at 6 months (primary) and 12 months (secondary).

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Adolescents (N=723; mean age, 14.9 years [SD=1.6]) were mostly female (75%), White (84.1%), and non-Hispanic (84.2%). Adults (N=797; mean age, 38.3 years [SD=15.9]) were mostly female (70%), White (89.1%), and non-Hispanic (90%). At 6 months, outcomes were similar by condition among adolescents, but among adults, SI/SB scores were significantly higher among those receiving CC compared to those receiving ISC (adjusted difference in means [ADM]=0.50, 95% CI=0.12, 0.88). At 12 months, adolescents' SI/SB scores were significantly lower in the CC compared with the ISC condition (ADM=-0.64, 95% CI=-1.11, -0.18), but outcomes were similar by condition among adults.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: The best suicide prevention follow-up care may vary by age, with adolescents benefiting most from longer-term connection-focused two-way CC and adults benefiting most from more intensive early instrumental support through ISC.

articles.title: HipSAFE: detecting hip fractures on ultrasound imaging using deep learning in a porcine cadaveric model.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: Hip fractures require timely diagnosis and surgical intervention, and current approaches require diagnosis with pelvic radiographs in emergency departments. Portable, diagnostically reliable point-of-care ultrasound (US) could reduce unnecessary transfers and shorten time to surgery. The objective of this work was to evaluate, in a porcine cadaver model, the accuracy of HipSAFE, a deep-learning-assisted US tool intended to reduce operator dependence and support pre-hospital hip fracture triage by nurses and paramedics.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: The bilateral hind limbs of 15 juvenile porcine cadavers (30 hips) were imaged by operators with no sonographic training before and after inducing a displaced iatrogenic pertrochanteric hip fracture. The limbs were split at the cadaver level into training (n = 16), validation (n = 6) and held-out test (n = 8) sets. Frame-level classifiers (MobileNetV3, EfficientNet-Lite and ResNet) were pre-trained on ImageNet and fine-tuned. Cine clip predictions used a moving average with Youden index threshold calibration. Model F1-scores were compared against the diagnostic radiologists using a femur-level paired bootstrap test with Holm correction.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Cine clip performance was reported on the 78 clips collected by 31 operators on 4 cadavers (8 femurs). Most architectures achieved high cine clip performance. EfficientNet-Lite0 reached an F1-score of 0.944 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.920-0.980), sensitivity of 89.5% (95% CI, 75.9%-95.8%) and specificity of 100.0% (95% CI, 91.2%-100.0%); the majority voting ensemble reached an F1-score of 0.932 (95% CI, 0.903-0.967). The operators achieved an F1-score of 0.667 (0.581--0.750) and the two diagnostic radiologists achieved an F1-score of 0.684 (95% CI, 0.531-0.800). Although growth plates were present in intact and fractured femurs, the Grad-CAM attribution maps suggest that the models had difficulty distinguishing growth plates from fracture features.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: In this pre-clinical setting, a lightweight, deep-learning pipeline accurately identified hip fractures on US imaging, motivating future work on the feasibility of US with deep learning for pre-hospital hip trauma triage.

articles.title: Province-wide assessment of emergency care capacity and skills in a rural provincial health system: A facility-based cross-sectional assessment in Battambang, Cambodia.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Emergency care capacity remains critically limited in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), particularly in rural areas where specialists and infrastructure are scarce. In Cambodia, stroke and ischemic heart disease are leading causes of mortality, and trauma burdens are increasing alongside rapid infrastructure development. Evidence on emergency equipment availability and frontline provider skills at the facility level in rural provinces remains limited.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A facility-based cross-sectional assessment was conducted across all seven public referral hospitals in Battambang Province, Cambodia, in January 2023. Emergency equipment availability was evaluated through structured interviews and direct visual confirmation against the World Health Organization (WHO) Guidelines for Essential Trauma Care. Clinical skill examinations were administered to physicians (two scenario-based cases: acute stroke with airway compromise; traumatic injury with tension pneumothorax and intra-abdominal bleeding) and nurses (a Basic Life Support [BLS] scenario assessed in pairs). Hospitals were stratified by Complementary Package of Activities (CPA) level: CPA1 (basic care only), CPA2 (including surgery and intensive care), and CPA3 (highest provincial level).

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: At Complementary Package of Activities (CPA)1 (basic care only) hospitals, intubation equipment and 12-lead electrocardiogram were each available in only 25% of facilities. None had a crash cart, blood transfusion capacity, basic metabolic panel, or coagulation testing. In the stroke scenario, airway patency was confirmed by 28.6% of physicians at CPA1 hospitals, compared with 70.0% at CPA2 hospitals (including surgery and intensive care), 57.1% at the CPA3 hospital (highest provincial level), and 75.0% at the Provincial Health Department. In the trauma scenario, no physician at CPA1 hospitals correctly performed spinal immobilization with the spine kept straight or thoracentesis at the correct anatomical location. Among 38 nurse pairs, 97.4% initiated chest compressions promptly, but only 21.1% demonstrated correct compression technique, and 13.2% provided effective bag-valve-mask ventilation. Deficiencies in equipment and clinical skills were most pronounced at CPA1 hospitals.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Emergency care capacity in Battambang Province was substantially limited, with the greatest deficiencies at CPA1 hospitals. Recurrent low-cost training and targeted strengthening of basic emergency care should be prioritized at lower-level facilities.

articles.title: A scoping review evaluating artificial intelligence applications across various injury prevention domains.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Artificial intelligence (AI) has become increasingly utilized for injury prevention across diverse clinical and community settings including machine learning (ML). This scoping review aimed to synthesize the current literature on the applications and predictive performance of AI across multiple injury prevention domains.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This scoping review searched five major databases, including PubMed, Embase, ScienceDirect, ProQuest, and the Cochrane Library, to identify studies evaluating AI applications for injury prevention published through May 2026. Eligible studies included original U.S.-based, English-language research across self-harm and suicide, abuse and violence, fall prevention, and sports injury prediction. Studies were excluded if they lacked measurable prevention outcomes or sufficient methodological detail, or focused on injury treatment rather than prevention, to ensure relevant and interpretable evidence for synthesis.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Nineteen studies met the inclusion criteria. ML models generally outperformed or matched traditional screening methods for self-harm and suicide prediction (AUC 0.81-0.82), while multimodal approaches achieved the highest predictive accuracy (AUC 0.90). In abuse and violence prevention, AI predicted intimate partner violence with an AUC of 0.88 and identified cases before formal disclosure. AI also improved fall risk assessment by accurately categorizing patient risk levels, predicting future falls, and mitigating fall injuries through wearable airbag technology. ML models predicted future sports-related injuries (AUC 0.76-0.84), while identifying modifiable risk factors including workload, strength deficits, prior injury burden, and concussion history.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: ML-based prediction showed promise for risk stratification in self-harm, suicide, intimate partner violence, and recurrent victimization. Additionally, AI predicted fall risk and identified athletes at risk for future sports-related injuries while detecting modifiable risk factors, including workload, prior injury burden, and strength deficits. Although these findings suggest that AI and ML may have potential applications in supporting earlier risk identification, informing targeted prevention strategies, and facilitating more personalized approaches to injury prevention, the limited available evidence warrants careful interpretation.

articles.title: Awake intubation in a Japanese tertiary emergency department: a single-center retrospective descriptive study.
articles.journal_full: The American journal of emergency medicine

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Evidence on awake intubation in emergency departments (EDs) is limited. We aimed to describe patient characteristics, intubation indications, procedural practices, and outcomes for awake intubation in the ED.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This single-center retrospective descriptive study included consecutive adult patients who underwent tracheal intubation at a tertiary ED in Japan from April 2020 through December 2025. Patients intubated during cardiac arrest were excluded. Operational definition for awake tracheal intubation required topical upper airway anesthesia, no neuromuscular blockers before or during the initial attempt, and documented preservation of consciousness and spontaneous ventilation throughout that attempt. Outcomes included first-pass success, adverse events related to airway management, and definitive airway management, including rescue.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Eighty-four patients underwent awake tracheal intubation, representing 5.5% of intubations in patients without cardiac arrest (84/1531). Upper airway infectious diseases were present in 54 patients (64.3%); airway-related indications accounted for 63 cases (75.0%). Emergency physicians performed 79 initial attempts (94.0%); a flexible bronchoscope was used initially in 49 patients (58.3%). First-pass success occurred in 63 patients (75.0%; 95% confidence interval, 64.4%-83.8%). Seven patients (8.3%) experienced adverse events related to airway management. Eighty patients (95.2%) achieved definitive airway management without a surgical airway. Four patients (4.8%) required a surgical airway, all after first-pass failure.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Awake intubation, performed primarily by emergency physicians, was used to manage upper airway infectious diseases with actual or impending obstruction in a tertiary ED. A flexible bronchoscope was used initially in over half of cases and most patients were intubated without a surgical airway.

articles.title: Predictors of Treatment Engagement and Homework Completion in Cognitive Remediation Therapy for Schizophrenia and Depression.
articles.journal_full: The Journal of nervous and mental disease

abstract.label: AIM
abstract.text: Cognitive remediation (CR) improves neurocognition and functioning in severe mental illnesses. However, there is inconsistent information regarding predictors of who might engage with CR.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We investigated two measures of CR engagement: session attendance and homework completion. Across two studies, we examined baseline differences between treatment and homework "engagers" and "non-engagers" (<50% of sessions or homework) among individuals with schizophrenia (N = 70) and depression (N = 74).

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: In schizophrenia, treatment engagers were older, had been out of hospital for longer, and were enrolled in executive training-focused CR, whereas homework engagers had higher neurocognitive functioning. Only CR type (i.e., executive training) predicted session attendance in schizophrenia. No significant differences were found between treatment or homework engagement groups for depression.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: These findings highlight the difficulty in predicting who may or may not engage with CR, which has implications for how decisions are made around offering CR to patients with severe mental illness.

articles.title: Fatal Opioid-Like Toxidrome Associated With a 7-Hydroxymitragynine Kratom Product.

abstract.text: Kratom (Mitragyna speciosa) use has increased in the United States, with the market shifting from traditional leaf preparations to concentrated products containing concentrated or chemically processed alkaloids such as 7-hydroxymitragynine (7-HMG) and mitragynine pseudoindoxyl. These formulations may deliver supraphysiologic opioid-receptor agonist doses with poorly characterized toxicity. A 42-year-old man was found dead at home after reportedly ingesting 3 tablets of a commercial "7-HMG" product and several beers. Postmortem examination revealed purge fluid at the mouth and nose, severe bilateral pulmonary edema, distended bladder, and no evidence of trauma or injection drug use. Quantitative analysis of the remaining tablet showed 29 mg 7-HMG and 0.58 mg mitragynine pseudoindoxyl, with minimal mitragynine. Postmortem blood contained 37.3 ng/mL 7-HMG and 76 ng/mL mitragynine pseudoindoxyl, whereas gabapentin and other medications were present at subtherapeutic concentrations. Compared with an estimated 1 to 4.5 mg 7-HMG in a typical high dose of dried kratom leaf powder, this ingestion delivered approximately 87 mg 7-HMG (19-fold to 87-fold greater 7-HMG exposure than a high-dose botanical leaf preparation). Given the high μ-opioid receptor activity of 7-HMG and its in vivo conversion to the even more potent opioid agonist mitragynine pseudoindoxyl, the postmortem findings are most consistent with a fatal opioid-like toxidrome associated with exposure to concentrated kratom alkaloids. This case illustrates the emerging risk posed by new kratom-branded products containing purified or chemically enriched alkaloids at doses far exceeding traditional preparations.

articles.title: Associations Between Diagnostic Blood-Based Biomarkers and Neuroimaging Findings in Mild Traumatic Brain Injury.

abstract.label: STUDY OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: Mild traumatic brain injury (mTBI) is a prevalent and resource-intensive injury in the emergency department (ED). The blood-based biomarkers glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) and ubiquitin c-terminal hydrolase L1 (UCH-L1) have demonstrated diagnostic potential for acute structural brain injury. Our objective was to clinically validate a US Food and Drug Administration-approved plasma test to aid in the identification of intracranial injury in patients with mTBI presenting to the ED and assess its integration with existing protocols.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This single-center validation study enrolled 104 adult patients with suspected mTBI undergoing head computed tomography (CT) for evaluation between October 2023 and June 2024 at a Level I trauma center. Peripheral blood draw was completed within 12 hours postinjury and processed at the hospital clinical laboratory. Sensitivity, specificity, and predictive values for the test were calculated and compared with a standard clinical decision rule (Canadian Head CT Rule). ED length of stay and diagnostic turnaround times were examined.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Within the cohort (n=104), 83 patients had elevated biomarker levels (GFAP >30 pg/mL or UCH-L1 >360 pg/mL), and 11 patients had intracranial injury identified on CT. The combination plasma test demonstrated high sensitivity (0.91 [95% confidence interval {CI} 0.59 to 1.00]) but low specificity (0.22 [95% CI 0.14 to 0.31]) for predicting intracranial injury on CT with low positive predictive value (0.12 [95% CI 0.06 to 0.21]) and high negative predictive value (0.95 [95% CI 0.76 to 1.00]). These findings are consistent with prior studies (pooled sensitivity 0.97 [95% CI 0.95 to 0.98]; specificity 0.28 [95% CI 0.23 to 0.34]). False-positive cases (78%) were older than true-negative cases (median 72 years [interquartile range (IQR) 54 to 83] versus 58.5 years [IQR 38.25 to 66]). Median turnaround time for the GFAP/UCH-L1 test was 2 hours faster than head CT (1.09 hours [IQR 0.87 to 1.65] versus 3.28 hours [IQR 2.37 to 4.70]).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Blood biomarkers for mTBI have potential as an initial rule-out tool for intracranial injury prior to obtaining CT imaging; however, large multicenter studies are needed to clarify its impact on ED resource utilization, length of stay, and acute and long-term costs and benefits to patients and health care systems.

articles.title: Ambient Artificial Intelligence Scribe Use and Objective Documentation Effort Among Emergency Physicians.

abstract.label: STUDY OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: Ambient artificial intelligence (AI) scribes ("AI scribes") are purported to reduce emergency department (ED) documentation burden, but ED evidence is largely single-site, uncontrolled, or self-reported, with exposure inferred rather than measured. We evaluated AI scribe use among attending emergency physicians across a multisite network, with exposure and outcomes read directly from the electronic health record.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Across 20 EDs (3 academic and 17 community), AI scribe use was flagged per note from the patient consent statement within the ED note. Analyses were restricted to attending physicians and, to isolate the physician's own documentation, excluded teaching encounters and attestation notes identified from standardized attestation text. Endpoints, computed over the mature-adoption window (December 2025 onward, when Epic audit-log data are retained), were active time in the note (primary), note length, note-start time, completion lag, and 72-hour ED return. Within-physician models (physician and calendar-month fixed effects, clustered by physician) compared each adopter's AI-scribed notes with their own unassisted notes, adjusting only for pre-exposure case mix.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 275 attending physicians, 31% of encounters were AI-scribed. Physicians spent less active time in AI-scribed notes (median 10.0 versus 12.5 min-2.4 minutes after adjustment), started them about 15 minutes later (median 31 versus 17 minutes after first seeing the patient, and produced notes about 14% longer [median 5,220 versus 4,468 characters; within-physician +629 characters]). Note completion was not delayed (-6 minutes), and 72-hour ED return was not increased (-0.8 percentage point; 95% confidence interval -1.5 to -0.1).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Among emergency physicians, AI scribe use was associated with less active time in the note, deferred note-start, and longer notes, without delaying completion or increasing short-term returns, with effect sizes consistent with ambulatory randomized data.

articles.title: Who's on Airway? Trainee Tracheal Intubation Frequency and Outcomes Within the National Emergency Airway Registry for Pediatric Emergency Medicine (NEAR4PEM).

abstract.label: STUDY OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: We aimed to describe trainee performance and tracheal intubation outcomes in academic pediatric emergency departments.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a multicenter retrospective observational study of intubations performed between January 2021 and December 2023, using data from the National Emergency Airway Registry for Pediatric Emergency Medicine. Eligible encounters included children who underwent intubation with the first-attempt proceduralist identified as an emergency medicine resident, a pediatric resident, or a pediatric emergency medicine (PEM) fellow. The primary outcome was first-attempt success. The secondary outcome was adverse airway outcomes, defined as desaturation or tracheal intubation-associated adverse events. We compared intubation outcomes across trainee groups.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Over the 1,404 encounters during the study period, 642 (48%) were primary intubations performed on pediatric patients by an emergency medicine, pediatric or PEM trainee. A total of 343 (53%) first attempts were by emergency medicine residents, 254 (40%) by PEM fellows, and 45 (7%) by pediatric residents. The overall trainee first-attempt success rate was 471/642 (73%). First-attempt success by emergency medicine residents (75%) and PEM fellows (74%) were similar, and higher than first-attempt success by pediatric residents (58%). After accounting for potential confounders, there was no difference between emergency medicine residents and PEM fellows in first-attempt success (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 0.84, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.56 to 1.28) or adverse airway outcome (aOR 1.4, 95% CI 0.96 to 2.18). In adjusted analysis, pediatric residents had a lower first-attempt success (aOR 0.41, 95% CI 0.20 to 0.82) and a higher adverse airway outcome (aOR 2.14, 95% CI 1.08 to 4.27) than emergency medicine residents.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: There was no difference in first-attempt success and adverse airway outcomes between emergency medicine residents and PEM fellows. Pediatric residents have lower first-attempt success and higher adverse airway outcomes than emergency medicine residents.

articles.title: Prehospital damage-control amputation and packed red blood cell transfusion for severe bilateral lower-limb crush injury in a remote setting: a case report.

abstract.text: Prehospital damage-control amputation in civilian emergency systems is rare, especially combined with prehospital packed red blood cell transfusion. We report a 30-year-old man with bilateral lower-limb crush injury after entrapment in an industrial roller machine in a remote area. Despite initially preserved blood pressure, he developed marked hemodynamic deterioration and arrived at the hospital with a blood pressure of 74/49 mmHg. Both limbs were non-salvageable. Prehospital bilateral amputation with vascular ligation was performed on scene, followed by transfusion of one local unit of packed red blood cells (~200 ml). He survived after stump revision, intensive care, and rehabilitation. This case describes the sequential use of prehospital hemorrhage control and packed red blood cell transfusion during the same prehospital episode in a patient with a life-threatening entrapment injury and delayed transport.

articles.title: Delayed Transverse Colon Stricture Following Blunt Abdominal Trauma: A Case Report With Diagnostic Dilemma.

abstract.text: This case report describes a 26-year-old woman who developed a delayed transverse colon stricture following a motor vehicle crash (MVC). She was a restrained rear-seat passenger in a rollover collision and sustained blunt abdominal and back injuries, two right rib fractures, superficial lacerations, and T11-L1 vertebral injury requiring surgical management. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) performed after the MVC demonstrated no obvious bowel or solid visceral organ injury. Approximately 3 years later, she developed progressive abdominal pain, cramping, fullness, constipation, and a 10-pound weight loss. Colonoscopy demonstrated a severe, nontraversable stenosis of the transverse colon. Subsequent CT demonstrated marked stool burden and dilatation of the ascending and proximal transverse colon proximal to the stenotic segment. She later presented to the emergency department with worsening abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting and was diagnosed with large bowel obstruction secondary to the transverse colon stricture. She underwent robotic-assisted transverse colon resection with colonic lavage and primary colo-colonic anastomosis. Histopathologic examination demonstrated moderately active chronic colitis with transmural inflammation, glandular architectural distortion, mucosal ulceration, and cryptitis, raising consideration of inflammatory bowel disease. However, no granulomas or dysplasia were identified. The postoperative course was uncomplicated, and at approximately 2 years of follow-up, she remained asymptomatic without recurrent gastrointestinal symptoms or other clinical features suggestive of inflammatory bowel disease. This case highlights the diagnostic challenge of distinguishing a delayed posttraumatic colonic stricture from inflammatory bowel disease when chronic inflammatory histopathologic changes are present in a patient with remote blunt abdominal trauma.

articles.title: Persistent Pediatric Cervical Lymphadenopathy: A Case Report of Kikuchi-Fujimoto Disease Mimicking Infection and Malignancy.

abstract.label: CASE PRESENTATION
abstract.text: A 10-year-old female presented with 2 months of unilateral cervical lymphadenopathy despite several courses of oral antibiotics. She presented to the emergency department due to persistent pain and swelling along with new fever. On presentation, she was febrile to 39.0°C. Physical examination revealed significant left-sided cervical and submandibular lymphadenopathy with tenderness, warmth, and overlying erythema. Initial labs were notable for leukopenia (2.6 × 103/μL), thrombocytopenia (135,000/μL), and elevated liver enzymes. Computed tomography (CT) of the neck demonstrated necrotic left cervical lymphadenopathy with prominent right cervical lymph nodes. An infectious workup, including testing for Epstein-Barr virus, Cytomegalovirus, human immunodeficiency virus, coccidioidomycosis, tuberculosis, and microbial cell-free DNA sequencing, was negative. Initial fine-needle aspiration (FNA) and core needle biopsy showed predominantly necrotic tissue. Cultures obtained during the biopsy showed no growth, and flow cytometry was negative for leukemia/lymphoma markers. Intravenous (IV) ceftriaxone administration resulted in improvement in neck swelling and fever resolution. Histopathologic examination from excisional biopsy revealed histiocytic necrotizing lymphadenitis consistent with Kikuchi-Fujimoto (KFD) lymphadenitis. Comprehensive autoimmune serologies were negative. Naproxen was prescribed to help with residual inflammation.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: KFD should be considered in children presenting with prolonged cervical lymphadenopathy refractory to antibiotics. This case illustrates several diagnostic challenges inherent in making this diagnosis. The patient's prolonged unilateral cervical lymphadenopathy, necrotic imaging findings, and transient improvement with antibiotics strongly suggested bacterial lymphadenitis or malignancy. However, the persistence of symptoms despite multiple appropriate antibiotic courses, the development of cytopenias and elevated liver enzymes, and ultimately nondiagnostic cultures represented key findings prompting reconsideration of the initial differential diagnoses. This case also highlights the importance of considering excisional biopsy when core biopsy is nondiagnostic.

articles.title: Baseline Clinical Predictors and Toxicological Drivers of In-Hospital Poisoning Mortality in Resource-Constrained Emergency Care: A Firth Penalized Regression Analysis.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Evidence regarding clinical characteristics and determinants of mortality among patients with acute poisoning in agricultural regions of Ethiopia remains limited. This study aimed to evaluate baseline clinical predictors associated with in-hospital mortality among acutely poisoned patients in a low-resource tertiary emergency department.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A retrospective observational study was conducted among consecutive acute poisoning cases presenting to Asella Referral and Teaching Hospital (October 2022-September 2024). Of 372 screened cases, 7 patients who left against medical advice were excluded, yielding a final analytical cohort of 365 patients. Sociodemographic, toxicological, and clinical data were extracted from medical records. The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality. Multivariable Firth penalized logistic regression was performed to minimize small-sample bias given sparse outcome events (15 deaths). A sensitivity model additionally adjusted for sex and rural residence.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The median age of patients was 22.0 years (IQR: 19.0-27.0); 230 (61.8%) were aged 15-24 years, 199 (53.5%) were female, and 245 (65.9%) were rural residents. Insecticides were the predominant poisoning category (157; 42.2%). Aluminum Phosphide (AlP) exposure occurred in 43 (11.6%) patients, resulting in 12 deaths (case-fatality rate: 27.9%; 95% CI 15.3%-43.7%). Overall in-hospital mortality was 4.1% (15/365; 95% CI 2.3%-6.6%), with AlP accounting for 80.0% of all cohort deaths. In the primary multivariable Firth model, AlP exposure (aOR 30.48, 95% CI 7.88-117.95) and admission Glasgow Coma Scale < 15 (aOR 19.90, 95% CI 5.09-77.88) were strongly and independently associated with in-hospital mortality. These associations remained robust in sensitivity analyses.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Impaired consciousness at admission (GCS < 15) and Aluminum Phosphide exposure serve as critical baseline indicators for rapid, low-cost risk stratification. While these exploratory parameters highlight high-risk groups, prospective multi-center validation across diverse hospital tiers is required before formal integration into clinical triage algorithms.

articles.title: Preventive Immunomodulatory Effects of Doxycycline and Hyperbaric Oxygen Therapy on Serum Tumor Necrosis Factor-α and Interleukin-6 Levels in a Rat Model of Malaria.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Malaria remains a major global health problem causing morbidity and mortality. Although doxycycline is widely used as an effective malaria chemoprophylactic agent, its use is limited in certain populations (doxycycline should not be given to children under 8 years of age and pregnant women). These limitations, together with the growing challenge of antimalarial drug resistance, necessitate the exploration of adjunctive and alternative prophylactic strategies. Hyperbaric oxygen therapy (HBOT), which involves inhalation of 100% oxygen under increased atmospheric pressure, has demonstrated immunomodulatory and anti-inflammatory effects in various infectious diseases.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: This study is aimed at evaluating the preventive immunomodulatory effects of doxycycline and HBOT, alone or in combination, on the serum levels of proinflammatory cytokines tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α) and interleukin-6 (IL-6) in a Plasmodium berghei rat model.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: An in vivo experimental study was conducted using 24 female BALB/c mice (7-10 weeks old), randomly assigned into four groups: control group (CG), doxycycline group (DG), hyperbaric oxygen therapy group (HG), and combined doxycycline-hyperbaric oxygen therapy group (DHG). All groups were infected with P. berghei ANKA. Serum TNF-α and IL-6 levels were measured and compared among the groups.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Significant differences in TNF-α (p = 0.012), IL-6 (p = 0.010), and parasitemia (p = 0.001) were observed among the four groups. TNF-α levels were significantly lower in DG, HG, and DHG than in CG (p = 0.037, p = 0.004, and p = 0.004, respectively), whereas no significant differences were observed among the treatment groups. IL-6 was significantly lower in HG and DHG than in CG (both p = 0.004), whereas the difference between DG and CG was not statistically significant (p = 0.150). All treatment groups showed significantly lower parasitemia than CG (all p = 0.001). HBOT and DHG also showed lower parasitemia than DG (p = 0.020 and p = 0.006, respectively), whereas no significant difference was observed between HG and DHG (p = 0.952).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Both doxycycline and HBOT exert immunomodulatory effects by reducing TNF-α and IL-6 levels in experimental malaria.
