The present findings suggest that doxycycline and HBOT may modulate systemic inflammatory responses during experimental malaria. Combination of doxycycline and HBOT shows a favorable anti-inflammatory profile against malaria-associated inflammation.

articles.title: Physiological monitoring and physiology-informed strategies in cardiac arrest: current evidence and clinical translation.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Despite advances in cardiac arrest management, survival with favorable neurological outcomes remains limited. Physiological monitoring may complement standardized resuscitation by providing real-time information about circulatory effectiveness, reversible causes, and treatment responses. However, whether physiology-guided interventions improve patient-centered outcomes remains uncertain. This narrative review examines the current evidence and clinical applicability of physiological monitoring during resuscitation, physiology-informed rescue strategies, and individualized post-cardiac arrest care.

abstract.label: MAIN BODY
abstract.text: During cardiopulmonary resuscitation, invasive arterial pressure monitoring, waveform capnography, and echocardiography provide complementary information about the circulation generated by chest compressions and potential mechanisms of resuscitation failure. Although observational and experimental studies support their physiological relevance, no adult diastolic pressure target or pressure-guided vasopressor strategy has been validated to improve survival or neurological recovery. Recent randomized trials of transesophageal echocardiography have demonstrated physiological or procedural effects without establishing clinical benefit. Among rescue strategies, extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation has yielded inconsistent results across randomized trials, with potential benefits dependent on patient selection, intervention timing, and system capabilities. Resuscitative endovascular balloon occlusion of the aorta has not improved clinical outcomes in randomized evaluation, while head-up resuscitation remains investigational. Following the return of spontaneous circulation, randomized trials have challenged the benefits of uniformly higher blood pressure and oxygenation targets, mild hypercapnia, and deeper or prolonged temperature control. Individualized approaches incorporating cerebral autoregulation, venous congestion, and cardiopulmonary physiology are physiologically appealing but lack prospective validation.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Physiological assessment may complement established resuscitation algorithms by refining clinical decisions during and after cardiac arrest. However, improvements in physiological measurements should not be equated with improved patient outcomes. Future trials should determine whether predefined, physiology-guided treatment strategies improve survival and neurological recovery.

articles.title: Digital health information-seeking behavior correlates of parental cyberchondria severity in Pediatric care.

abstract.label: AIM
abstract.text: Limited evidence addresses whether digital health information-seeking behaviors are independently associated with parental cyberchondria in pediatric settings. We examined these associations after adjustment for sociodemographic characteristics and psychological well-being.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This cross-sectional study was conducted in the pediatric ward of a hospital in eastern Türkiye from August 2024 to January 2025 using convenience sampling. Eligible participants were adults accompanying a child aged 0-18 years who could consent and complete the questionnaire. Of 482 invited parents, 27 declined and 455 completed a self-administered questionnaire in the child's room. Hierarchical linear regression with HC3 robust standard errors included 451 complete cases.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The 16 item-level indicators increased explained variance by 50.0 percentage points (ΔR2 = 0.500, p < .001); the final model explained 57.6% (adjusted R2 = 0.553). Higher scores were associated with reliance on non-health-professional rather than health-professional sources (B = 3.531, 95% CI [0.340, 6.721], p = .030), greater search frequency (B = 1.771, 95% CI [0.909, 2.633], p < .001), pre-hospital searching (B = 3.412, p = .002), increased worry about the child's health (B = 2.952, p = .004), and sleep pattern disruption (B = 3.617, p < .001).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Digital health information-seeking behaviors were associated with parental cyberchondria severity. These findings, derived from parents of children receiving care in a pediatric clinical setting, may inform health-informatics-supported pediatric nursing care by providing insight into parents' digital health information-seeking experiences and related communication needs. Causality cannot be inferred because of the cross-sectional design.

abstract.label: PATIENT OR PUBLIC CONTRIBUTION
abstract.text: No patients or members of the public were involved in the design, conduct, analysis, interpretation, or reporting of this study. Parents participated only as questionnaire respondents.

articles.title: Evaluation of the management of patients with suspected epileptic seizures in emergency departments: The EPI-Lepsie study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND AND IMPORTANCE
abstract.text: In France, epileptic seizures account for approximately 1.6% of emergency department (ED) admissions, nearly 60% of which involve patients with known epilepsy. At least half of these patients could potentially be managed on an outpatient basis. Despite established national guidelines, data on actual ED practice patterns and guideline adherence remain scarce.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To evaluate the management of adult patients presenting with suspected epileptic seizures across French EDs, and to identify clinical and organisational determinants of hospitalisation.

abstract.label: DESIGN, SETTING AND PARTICIPANTS
abstract.text: The EPI-Lepsie study was a national, multicentre, prospective observational study. Consecutive adult patients (age≥18 years) admitted to 93 French EDs over a three-day period (18-21 May 2021) with suspected epileptic seizures were enrolled through the Initiative Recherche Urgence (IRU) network of the Société française de médecine d'urgence (SFMU).

abstract.label: OUTCOME MEASURES AND ANALYSIS
abstract.text: The primary outcome was hospitalisation at ED discharge. Secondary outcomes included EEG performance, access to neurological consultation, post-discharge follow-up, and 30-day outcomes. Hospitalisation determinants were assessed by mixed logistic regression (ED as random intercept), adjusted for age, sex, seizure aetiology, risk factors, neuroimaging, and EEG results.

abstract.label: MAIN RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 350 included patients (61.8% male; median age 50 years [IQR: 33-68]), EEG was requested in 102 cases (29.1%) but performed in only 54 (15.4%). Neurological consultation was requested in 163 patients (46.6%) and obtained in 146 (41.7%). After ED care, 210 patients (60.2%) were discharged home, of whom 133 (66.5%) had no scheduled neurological follow-up. Hospitalisation occurred in 128 patients (36.6%). In multivariate analysis, abnormal neuroimaging was the strongest independent predictor (adjusted OR 8.70, P<0.0001). Failure to perform a requested EEG was associated with hospitalisation in 81.2% of cases versus 46.3% when EEG was completed. Inter-centre variance accounted for 19.9% of total variance.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: This study demonstrates that a substantial proportion of epilepsy-related ED admissions do not require hospitalisation. Improving access to EEG and neurological consultation, combined with standardised risk-stratification pathways for patients with known epilepsy, could meaningfully reduce avoidable admissions and enhance continuity of care.

articles.title: Localization of Non-Compressible Torso Hemorrhage with Contrast-Enhanced Ultrasound: A Swine Model.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Non-compressible torso hemorrhage (NCTH) remains a leading cause of preventable death in civilian and military trauma. In settings without cross-sectional imaging, the Focused Assessment with Sonography in Trauma (FAST) is used to detect hemoperitoneum but is limited in evaluating the retroperitoneum, is highly operator dependent, and cannot reliably localize bleeding. Contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS) has demonstrated high sensitivity for solid organ pathology, but its role in detecting and localizing NCTH is not well defined.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: NCTH was induced in 18 swine (70-90 kg) via laparoscopic solid organ injury or endovascular injury to an aortic branch vessel. Standard FAST and CEUS were performed pre- and post-injury in a non-randomized, paired fashion. Outcomes included successful visualization of contrast extravasation with accurate localization of hemorrhage and time to hemorrhage detection.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Both CEUS and FAST detected hemoperitoneum in all cases. CEUS identified active contrast extravasation from solid organ and vascular injuries in 78% of cases and improved detection of low-volume hemoperitoneum. CEUS also detected hemorrhage in the retroperitoneum. Time to detection was similar between modalities.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: CEUS is a feasible adjunct to FAST for detecting and localizing NCTH. This swine model provides a reproducible platform for evaluating portable hemorrhage localization technologies in austere environments.

articles.title: Effects of prehospital blood pressure on 90-day functional outcomes in patients with acute ischemic stroke due to large vessel occlusion.
articles.journal_full: Journal of stroke and cerebrovascular diseases : the official journal of National Stroke Association

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Prehospital blood pressure (BP) could influence cerebral circulation and outcomes in acute large vessel occlusion (LVO). We investigated the association between prehospital BP and 90-day functional outcomes and explored effect modification by endovascular thrombectomy (EVT).

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We analyzed 1,106 patients with acute LVO transported by emergency medical services between 2018 and 2024. Prehospital systolic BP (SBP, mmHg) measured at the scene was categorized into four groups: <120, 120-149, 150-179, and ≥180 groups. The primary outcome was a 90-day modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score of 0-2. Secondary outcomes included mRS 0-3 and hemorrhagic complications. Subgroup analyses for the primary outcome were also conducted.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Mean age was 79 years, and 51% were male; 60% underwent EVT. The SBP <120, 120-149, 150-179, and ≥180 groups included 120, 403, 403, and 180 patients, respectively. Cardioembolic stroke was most common and decreased with increasing SBP. Compared with SBP <120 mmHg, SBP ≥180 mmHg was associated with lower odds of mRS 0-2 (adjusted OR, 0.43; 95% CI, 0.22-0.84; p = 0.01), with similar trends for mRS 0-3. This association was significant in EVT-treated patients but not in non-EVT patients (interaction p = 0.007). Hemorrhagic complications were similar across groups.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Elevated prehospital SBP (≥180 mmHg) was associated with worse 90-day functional outcomes in acute LVO, especially following EVT. These findings highlighted the potential clinical relevance of prehospital BP assessment in patients with LVO. Further investigation should be considered for prehospital BP status in addition to the in-hospital managements.

articles.title: Overwintering under the ice: seasonal shifts in cold and hypoxia stress physiology of three winter-active pond insects.
articles.journal: Comp Biochem Physiol B Biochem Mol Biol
articles.journal_full: Comparative biochemistry and physiology. Part B, Biochemistry & molecular biology

abstract.text: Winter poses harsh physiological challenges for insects living in temperate ponds due to the combination of low temperatures and reduced oxygen levels (hypoxia). Despite these stressors, water boatmen (Hesperocorixa sp.), backswimmers (Notonecta sp.) and diving beetles (Laccophilus maculosus) remain active year-round in eastern Nova Scotia, including in ice-covered ponds. However, the underlying mechanisms that allow pond insects to survive overwintering have not been widely studied. We hypothesized that cold and hypoxia tolerance would improve from September to March in these insects, with changes in whole-animal and biochemical correlates of tolerance to both stressors. We collected insects from the field and stocked them in outdoor freshwater mesocosms. Every two months, between September 2023 and April 2024, we characterized whole animal responses and biochemical changes. Whole insect cold tolerance assays indicated a trend of improved ability to sustain voluntary muscle control (critical thermal minimum) at lower temperatures in winter-collected insects and higher internal fluid freezing temperatures (supercooling points). There were no changes in whole animal correlates of hypoxia tolerance over time (surface respiration frequency, submersion and surface time). Concentrations of potential cryoprotectants like proline, myo-inositol and trehalose increased in multiple insect taxa during winter but were relatively low compared to terrestrial insect studies. As lactate dehydrogenase activity did not change, there is little evidence that the insects experienced functional hypoxia sufficient to induce anaerobic metabolism. Overall, this research has established a baseline cold and hypoxia tolerance dataset in understudied pond insects.

articles.title: Point-of-care ultrasound during diaphragmatic isometric contraction for estimating inspiratory muscle strength in healthy individuals.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Diaphragm ultrasound (DUS) provides a non-invasive assessment of diaphragm structure and function. However, the physiological information captured may depend on both the parameter measured and the contractile condition during acquisition. Whether diaphragm thickness during maximal isometric inspiratory effort more closely reflects inspiratory pressure-generating capacity than conventional DUS indices remains unclear.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To investigate the association between maximal inspiratory pressure (MIP) and diaphragm thickness during maximal isometric inspiratory effort in healthy adults and compare it with conventional DUS parameters.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Seventy-six healthy volunteers (≥18 years; 40 males) were enrolled. Diaphragmatic excursion (DE), diaphragm thickness at rest, during maximal inspiration and maximal isometric inspiratory effort, and thickening fraction (TF) were assessed by DUS. The highest of three measurements was analyzed. Correlation and regression analyses adjusted for age, sex, and height were performed.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Median age was 43 years and BMI 22.8 kg/m². MIP correlated with TF (r = 0.39, p = 0.035), DE during deep inspiration (r = 0.46, p = 0.011), and most strongly with diaphragm thickness during maximal isometric inspiratory effort (r = 0.95, p < 0.0001). Resting diaphragm thickness correlated inversely with MIP (r = -0.39, p = 0.034). In multivariable analysis, thickness during maximal isometric inspiratory effort remained independently associated with MIP.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: In healthy adults, diaphragm thickness during maximal isometric inspiratory effort showed the strongest association with MIP among DUS parameters. These proof-of-concept findings support further investigation of this measurement as an ultrasound-based marker of inspiratory muscle strength, including setting in which conventional MIP assessment may not be feasible.

articles.title: Global, regional, and national burden of unintentional poisoning, 1990-2023: results from the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Unintentional poisoning is a preventable cause of injury-related morbidity and mortality, yet global patterns, trends, and inequalities remain incompletely characterised. Within the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) framework, unintentional poisoning includes poisoning by carbon monoxide and poisoning by other means, a category largely informed by pesticide poisoning codes plus some indirect capture of other poisoning as part of the GBD re-distribution process. Poisonings by pharmaceuticals and illicit substances are not captured in the GBD definition of poisoning. We aimed to quantify this GBD-defined burden and assess regional variation, sociodemographic gradients, and case fatality between 1990 and 2023.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We analysed GBD 2023 estimates for 204 countries and territories, modelling deaths, incidence, and disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs) using standard GBD cause-of-death and non-fatal estimation methods with 95% uncertainty intervals. We stratified results by age, sex, region, and Socio-demographic Index (SDI), and derived case fatality from modelled deaths and incidence.

abstract.label: FINDINGS
abstract.text: In 2023, unintentional poisoning from carbon monoxide and other means caused 2·54 million incident poisonings, 69 805 deaths, and 3·68 million DALYs globally, with age-standardised DALY rates declining by 47·5% since 1990. Carbon monoxide accounted for 641 932 poisonings, 30 890 deaths and 1·34 million DALYs, with the highest burdens in central and eastern Europe and central Asia. Most regions showed substantial long-term declines, and the global age-standardised DALY rate for carbon monoxide poisoning declined by 58·2% since 1990. Poisoning by other means caused 1·90 million incident cases, 38 914 deaths, and 2·34 million DALYs, with the greatest burden in sub-Saharan Africa. Most regions showed declining age-standardised DALY rates for poisoning by other means; however, there was no clear change (with the 95% uncertainty interval including zero) in the global estimate, driven by wide uncertainty intervals in several regions (including sub-Saharan Africa). Mortality and DALYs were inversely associated with SDI, and derived case fatality was highest in low-SDI regions.

abstract.label: INTERPRETATION
abstract.text: Global reductions in GBD-defined unintentional poisoning by carbon monoxide and other means are consistent with decades of regulatory and environmental interventions. These include bans of highly toxic pesticides, improved heating and ventilation systems, emissions controls, and adoption of carbon monoxide alarms. Stark inequalities persist in some regions and in low-SDI settings. Compared with previous GBD publications, this study provides a detailed global assessment of unintentional poisoning by carbon monoxide and other means up to 2023, integrating incidence, DALYs, and comparative case fatality across regions.

abstract.label: FUNDING
abstract.text: Gates Foundation and the Australian National Health and Medical Research Council.

articles.title: Developing an introductory training programme for newly employed nurses in the ambulance service through participatory action research.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Newly employed nurses entering the ambulance service face clinical, organisational and cultural challenges. Although transition-related support needs have been described, less is known about how such knowledge can be translated into organisationally feasible introductory training programmes.

abstract.label: AIM
abstract.text: To explore how organisational and pedagogical challenges in introductory training for newly employed nurses were identified, interpreted, negotiated and translated into a revised programme through participatory action research (PAR).

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A qualitative PAR design was conducted between 2020 and 2024 in one Swedish ambulance service organisation. Newly employed nurses, clinical supervisors, the management group (total duration 2 h and 14 min) and the research group contributed at different phases and levels of participation. The primary analytic material comprised two video-recorded management group meetings, field notes, and researcher reflections. Previously analysed interview, focus group and questionnaire findings were integrated as experiential and evaluative material. Narrative process analysis reconstructed how identified challenges were interpreted, negotiated, and translated into programme interventions, and how these were reconsidered following implementation.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Four interrelated challenges were consolidated: a theory-heavy programme structure, variation in supervision, limited leadership connection and role ambiguity. Organisational interpretation and negotiation translated these into three interconnected interventions: restructuring theory and practice, preparing selected clinical supervisors and integrating peer learning during clinical placement, with leadership connection and role clarification embedded across the programme. Reflection on implementation indicated that theory-practice integration, supervision, leadership and peer learning were interdependent and required continued organisational and pedagogical support.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: PAR provided a structured process for moving from empirical knowledge about professional transition to organisationally embedded and contextually feasible programme development. Supporting newly employed nurses requires alignment between programme design, supervision, leadership and workplace learning.

abstract.label: REGISTRATION
abstract.text: Not registered.

articles.title: An anti-inflammatory melanocortin fusion polypeptide augments whole blood resuscitation of hemorrhagic shock in a rodent polytrauma model.
articles.journal_full: The journal of trauma and acute care surgery

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Severe trauma induces a cytokine storm that is associated with impaired resuscitation and recovery. We investigated the impact of AQB-565, an anti-inflammatory melanocortin fusion polypeptide, as a novel treatment adjunct for whole blood resuscitation of hemorrhagic shock using a rat polytrauma shock model.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Hemorrhagic shock with polytrauma was induced in 64 Sprague-Dawley rats. The rats were randomized to receive one of four intravenous treatments at 15 minutes posthemorrhage (T15): saline control, AQB-565, tranexamic acid (TXA), or combined AQB-565+ TXA. The rats were given autologous transfusion of shed whole blood at 60 minutes and as needed thereafter to achieve mean arterial pressure (MAP) of 60 mm Hg for up to 3 hours. Survival, hemodynamics, cytokine profiles, and hemorrhage volumes were compared between groups.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: There was a significant overall effect of treatment group on MAP (two-way rmANOVA p=0.02) that coincided with blood transfusion. MAP was significantly increased at T105 with AQB-565+TXA versus saline control (p=0.046). Inflammatory plasma cytokines, including interleukin-6, were significantly decreased with AQB-565 versus control groups (ANOVA p values ≤0.01). Seventeen (26.6%) rats died before 3 hours. There was a trend towards increased survival for treatments containing AQB-565 versus controls that was not statistically significant (Kaplan-Meier log rank p=0.06).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: A melanocortin pathway-activating polypeptide suppressed inflammation and improved hemodynamic response to whole blood transfusion in this hemorrhagic shock model.

articles.title: Fulminant non-autoimmune diabetes presenting as fatal diabetic ketoacidosis in a 2-month-old infant with genetically confirmed Wolcott-Rallison syndrome.
articles.journal_full: Diabetic medicine : a journal of the British Diabetic Association

abstract.label: AIMS
abstract.text: Wolcott-Rallison syndrome (WRS) is a rare autosomal recessive monogenic disorder caused by mutations in the EIF2AK3 gene. Characterized by permanent early-onset non-autoimmune diabetes and multisystem dysfunction, it should be strongly suspected in infants presenting under 6 months of age, particularly in consanguineous families.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A 2-month-old female infant presented to the emergency department with severe respiratory distress, persistent vomiting and dehydration, initially having been evaluated for infantile colic.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Laboratory analysis revealed fulminant diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) (pH 6.85, plasma glucose 40.1 mmol/L, base excess -29 mmol/L). Despite aggressive PICU management, the patient rapidly developed diffuse cerebral oedema, systemic capillary leak, DIC-like coagulopathy with normal transaminases and refractory circulatory shock, leading to death 55 h after admission. Pancreatic autoantibodies were negative, with profoundly suppressed insulin (<0.4 mU/L) and C-peptide levels. Genetic analysis identified a homozygous loss-of-function EIF2AK3 variant, c.1565G>A (p.Trp522*), confirming WRS.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: WRS can present with fulminant DKA and progress to catastrophic multiorgan collapse early in infancy. This case highlights the crucial need to consider monogenic non-autoimmune diabetes in early-infantile DKA and underscores the clinical challenge of distinguishing primary metabolic organ failure from secondary complications of severe DKA and shock. Early molecular diagnosis remains vital for family counselling.

articles.title: A Diagnostic-Focused Mobile Stroke Unit Model Integrated with Emergency Medical Services for Scalable Prehospital Stroke Care.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Mobile stroke units (MSUs) have demonstrated important clinical benefits in acute ischemic stroke, but broad implementation remains constrained by resource, staffing, and operational barriers. This article describes an emergency medical services (EMS)-integrated diagnostic-focused MSU (DF-MSU) model designed to improve implementation feasibility and scalability.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A conceptual design approach was used based on findings from a previous global survey of MSU programs. The model was guided by three design principles: cost reduction, operational simplification, and integration with existing EMS while preserving the CT-based diagnostic function of MSUs.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The DF-MSU model separates CT-based diagnosis from treatment and transport, which are integrated with existing EMS systems. After CT evaluation in the DF-MSU at the emergency scene or rendezvous point, the patient is transferred to an EMS vehicle, where the physician and, when available, the nurse provide diagnosis-specific treatment and continued care during transport. This EMS-integrated model may reduce resource requirements, staffing needs, and operational complexity, and may offer a feasible and scalable alternative in regions where conventional MSU deployment is challenging.

articles.title: Stroke knowledge and intended care-seeking behavior among adults with hypertension and type 2 diabetes: A cross-sectional study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Stroke health literacy refers to the ability of non-medical individuals to recognize stroke symptoms and make timely decisions, which is critical for improving outcomes. However, data on stroke knowledge and intended care-seeking behavior in Bogotá, Colombia, remain limited.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To assess stroke symptom knowledge and intended care-seeking behavior among adults with hypertension and type 2 diabetes and to identify sociodemographic predictors of limited knowledge and suboptimal response.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A cross-sectional study was conducted between October 2023 and April 2024 in Bogotá, Colombia. A structured questionnaire was administered to 5,402 adults with hypertension and/or type 2 diabetes. Participants were recruited using a non-probabilistic sampling strategy, primarily from individuals under routine follow-up within the Bogotá public health network, and were identified through multiple recruitment strategies, including institutional databases. Surveys were conducted either by telephone or in person. Continuous variables were summarized using descriptive statistics, differences in categorical variables were assessed using chi-square tests, and binomial logistic regression models were applied to evaluate adjusted associations.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 6,050 respondents, 5,402 met inclusion criteria (median age 67 years; 46.3% male). Although most participants recognized that ischemic stroke can cause disability (89.6%) and death (91.1%), 32.5% reported no knowledge of stroke symptoms. Limited symptom knowledge was independently associated with male sex (OR 1.26, 95% CI 1.12-1.42), low educational attainment (OR 1.59, 95% CI 1.38-1.82), and low socioeconomic status (OR 2.20, 95% CI 1.85-2.60). Regarding intended response, 26.6% would not activate emergency medical services, and 52% reported they would schedule an outpatient appointment instead. Lower educational attainment was associated with greater likelihood of reporting non-emergency responses (all p < 0.001).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Despite high awareness that stroke can cause disability and death, substantial gaps in symptom recognition and intended response persist, particularly among socioeconomically disadvantaged individuals. These findings highlight the need for targeted strategies to improve stroke literacy in high-risk populations.

articles.title: An LLM-assisted real-time simulation framework for demand-responsive transport operations.

abstract.text: Demand-responsive transport (DRT) is a dynamic service whose performance depends not only on dispatching and routing algorithms but also on how externally submitted demand is captured, interpreted, and incorporated into operations. Although prior studies have largely emphasized algorithm-level optimization using pre-defined demand scenarios, integrated validation of externally submitted demand, user- and operator-facing interfaces, and operational analytics remains limited. This study proposes an LLM-assisted real-time DRT operation framework comprising Service User, System Manager, and Real-time DRT Simulator layers. The Service User layer uses function calling to transform unstructured trip requests into structured dispatch parameters. The System Manager combines function-calling-based quantitative analysis with retrieval-augmented generation to support natural-language access to operational data and domain knowledge. Based on Discrete Event System Specification, the simulator processes externally submitted and simulation-generated demands within a unified event structure under common dispatching and routing logic. Three experiments were conducted. Experiments 1 and 2 functionally evaluated the rider request-processing interface and the function-calling-based quantitative-query path of the System Manager, yielding average response latencies of 1.22 and 2.21 s, respectively. Experiment 3 independently evaluated the simulator through a system-level stress test using context-based synchronized demand. Across all scenarios, synchronized demand increased waiting times for the target passenger group. Although this group represented approximately 20% of successfully served passengers, it accounted for 26.5-28.5% of total waiting time. The effect appeared largely localized and was partially obscured in aggregate metrics because background-passenger performance was stable. These results demonstrate the functional feasibility of the LLM-assisted interfaces under the prototype conditions and show that synchronized-demand stress testing can reveal localized delay burdens that aggregate evaluations may overlook.

articles.title: Understanding the processes involved in sepsis recognition across clinical contexts to guide individualised management: A phenomenographic study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Sepsis is a highly heterogeneous condition, yet it is commonly recognised by application of standardised criteria, irrespective of clinical context. Understanding the complexity of sepsis recognition in the heterogeneous populations of patients with sepsis is critical to better target our resources to the needs of patients. Our aim was to examine nurses' clinical experiences to understand the processes involved in sepsis recognition across clinical contexts.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 26 nurses with various levels of experience in caring for patients with sepsis from multiple hospital settings. The interviews were phenomenographically analysed using the Arkelind method. The Cynefin framework was used to inform the organisation of findings according to contextual complexity.

abstract.label: FINDINGS
abstract.text: We identified four categories of description that represent different ways of experiencing sepsis recognition: recognise sepsis by following protocol-based care, recognise sepsis by following disease-specific care, recognise sepsis according to emergent care, and recognise sepsis according to emergency care. The categories emerged from various clinical contexts, ranging from the simple to the highly complex. This variability directed clinical management by helping nurses decide whether guidelines apply to the individual patient and how they should be integrated into clinical decision-making.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Despite its apparent simplicity, sepsis recognition is complex and context-dependent. Rather than relying on an identical strategy for all patients, effective clinical decisions require personalisation based on the characteristics of the clinical contexts. Our findings show that considering the availability of data, predictability and cause-and-effect relationships can inform the selection of an appropriate approach to sepsis recognition. This approach demands adaptability; however, unless we adopt an approach that is appropriate to the level of clinical complexity, significant improvements in sepsis recognition may not be seen. Prospective research is required to validate our findings.

articles.title: Co-exposure to planned power outages and wildfire PM2.5 and acute healthcare utilization in California: A time-stratified case-crossover study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: To prevent wildfires, electric utilities may preemptively de-energize power lines (public safety power shutoffs [PSPS]). These PSPS events may unintentionally harm health, particularly for those with pre-existing conditions like chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) or who rely on electricity-dependent medical equipment. Health impacts may worsen further if a wildfire occurs despite the power shutoff. To assess the effect of PSPS events, wildfire fine particulate matter (PM2.5) exposure, and their co-occurrence on cause-specific healthcare utilization.

abstract.label: METHODS AND FINDINGS
abstract.text: We identified PSPS events in California from 2013 to 2019, categorizing magnitude based on number of people without power by zip code. We leveraged zip code-level average daily wildfire PM2.5 estimates and respiratory, COPD-specific, cardiovascular, and psychiatric emergency department visits and unscheduled hospital admissions among adults aged 20+ from the California Department of Health Care Access and Information. Using a time-stratified case-crossover design, we estimated the impact of same-day and lagged PSPS events alone, wildfire PM2.5 alone, and their co-occurrence on healthcare utilization, adjusting for daily temperature. Severe PSPS events were associated with elevated odds of same-day respiratory encounters (OR = 1.06, 95% CI: 1.02, 1.11) and lag0-3 effects were similar. These associations were stronger for COPD. Compared to no PSPS or wildfire exposure, joint PSPS and 10 μg/m3 higher wildfire PM2.5 was associated with higher odds of respiratory encounters (1.16 [95% CI: 1.10, 1.22]), with evidence of multiplicative interaction. Associations were null for cardiovascular and psychiatric encounters. Limitations include exposure misclassification, because we assigned exposure at the residential zip code level, aggregating circuit-level data and not accounting for individual behavior or the potential for PSPS events to impact wildfire PM2.5 exposure.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: PSPS events may increase risk of respiratory events requiring acute care utilization, especially when they co-occur with wildfire PM2.5.

articles.title: A dive into the physiological responses to O2- and CO2-tables in freedivers.

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: Current literature focuses on maximal apneas to improve apnea duration, whereas in practice, apnea training often involves two distinct forms of timed-repeated submaximal apnea protocols: "O2-tables", intended to progressively decrease oxygenation and purportedly train O2 conservation, and "CO2-tables", intended to progressively accumulate carbon dioxide (CO2) and purportedly train hypercapnia tolerance. In apnea novices, O2- and CO2-tables failed to induce strong deoxygenation and CO2 accumulation, respectively. Therefore, the aim of this study was to compare physiological responses to maximal apneas, O2- and CO2-tables in apnea trained individuals.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: After medical screening, fourteen freedivers performed three apnea protocols: maximal apneas, O2-table and CO2-table. During apnea, heart rate (HR), muscle tissue oxygenation index (mTOI) and peripheral oxygen saturation (SpO2) were measured continuously. End-tidal carbon dioxide (EtCO2) was measured before and after apneas. Capillary partial pressure of CO2 (PCO2) was measured after the fourth and final apnea. Perceived Exertion (RPE) was rated after each protocol.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: RPE was lower after O2- and CO2-tables than after maximal apneas. Changes in HR and mTOI did not differ between O2- and CO2-tables. CO2-tables elicited greater increases in PCO2 and EtCO2 compared to O2-tables and maximal apneas. Maximal apneas induced greater changes in SpO2 than O2- and CO2-tables.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: These results suggest that, in freedivers, O2- and CO2-tables offer a less mentally and physically demanding alternative to repeated maximal apneas, allowing greater variation in apnea training while still targeting O2 conservation and CO2 tolerance, respectively.

articles.title: Addition of a McLaughlin cerclage to locking plate fixation of distal patellar pole fractures reduces interfragmentary displacement - a biomechanical human cadaveric study.
articles.journal_full: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: To investigate whether the addition of a McLaughlin cerclage to locking plate fixation of distal patellar pole fractures provides improved biomechanical construct stability and reduced interfragmentary displacement.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A distal patellar pole fracture was simulated in sixteen fresh-frozen human cadaveric knees by a horizontal osteotomy in the distal third of the patella. Subsequently, locking plate fixation was performed. In a randomized half of the specimens, an additional McLaughlin wire cerclage was applied. The specimens were then subjected to 3000 cycles of extension starting at 90° of flexion under a maximum tensile load of 320 N. Using a Digital Image Correlation (DIC) system, the interfragmentary displacement between the proximal and distal fragments was measured at 1, 10, 20, 30, 50, 100, 500, 1000, 2000, and 3000 cycles. Statistical analysis was performed using repeated-measures ANOVA and Welch's unpaired t-t test at 3000 cycles.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: An additional McLaughlin cerclage significantly reduced interfragmentary displacement under cyclic loading in comparison to locking plate fixation alone. After 3000 cycles, displacement was 2.27 ± 1.84 mm with plate fixation alone and 0.36 ± 0.22 mm with additional McLaughlin cerclage (mean difference 1.91 mm; 95% CI 0.38-3.45 mm; p = 0.0215).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: An additional McLaughlin cerclage reduced interfragmentary displacement in distal patellar pole fractures. In cases of unstable distal pole patella fractures, the additional use of a McLaughlin cerclage may therefore be considered to enhance construct stability.

articles.title: Trauma care performance and patient outcomes - insights from a major trauma centre in Sweden.
articles.journal_full: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: Trauma is a leading cause of death among individuals under 45 years of age. Evaluating trauma system performance over time is important but inherently difficult due to concurrent changes in patient demographics, case-mix and care processes. The aim of this study was to describe temporal changes in patient demographics, injury severity and trauma care at a major trauma centre in Sweden from 2017 to 2023. We hypothesised that risk-adjusted 30-day mortality decreased and that time to computed tomography was reduced over the study period.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A retrospective cohort study was conducted using data from the Karolinska Trauma Registry, including all trauma patients aged > 15 years fulfilling criteria for full trauma team activation, admitted between January 2017 and August 2023. Multivariable logistic regression was used to assess changes in 30-day mortality over time, adjusted for age, sex, injury severity category, ASA score and injury type. Time from arrival to computed tomography was analysed by linear regression and, because the distribution was skewed, by quantile (median) regression.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 5,615 trauma patients were included. Over the study period, the patient population became older, and ASA scores increased, while injury severity and the proportion of penetrating injury remained unchanged. In multivariable logistic regression with 2017 as reference, the odds of 30-day mortality in 2022-2023 were lower (OR 0.61, 95% CI 0.43-0.88, P = 0.008) after adjusting for confounders. Median time to computed tomography decreased from 31 to 21 min; the adjusted difference in 2022-2023 compared with 2017 was - 7.5 min by linear regression (P = 0.014) and - 10.4 min by quantile regression (95% CI - 11.5 to - 9.2, P < 0.001).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Our findings are consistent with improvements in trauma care within a mature trauma system, with shorter median time to computed tomography and lower 30-day mortality despite an aging population with increasing comorbidity. However, the specific drivers of these changes are difficult to identify, and future studies should explore how individual components of pre-hospital and in-hospital care contribute to trauma outcomes.

articles.title: Psychomotor Performance in Blended Versus In-Person Emergency Medical Technician Training: Retrospective Cohort Study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Blended learning is common in health professions education, but aggregate comparisons may obscure differences among knowledge, procedural skill, and integrated performance. Whether these domains differ after program-level changes under a common assessment system remains uncertain.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: We aimed to compare knowledge, psychomotor performance, and integrated scenario competence between blended and traditional in-person emergency medical technician level 1 certification training, and, as an exploratory secondary aim, to describe digital engagement and technology acceptance among blended-cohort participants who completed the survey.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We compared routinely collected certification records from traditional in-person (2020; n=603) and blended (2023; n=581) emergency medical technician level 1 cohorts. The primary outcome was psychomotor performance; secondary outcomes were knowledge, integrated scenario performance, and competency-threshold attainment. We estimated between-cohort differences with 95% CIs and adjusted linear regression. Equivalence was assessed using two 1-sided tests with expert-derived educational importance margins established through an instructor consensus exercise before the panel was provided with the between-cohort results (±5 points for knowledge, ±3 points for psychomotor performance, and ±4 points for integrated scenario performance). These margins represent educational consensus thresholds rather than externally validated clinical thresholds. Blended-cohort trainees were additionally offered a questionnaire on digital engagement and technology acceptance, analyzed by multiple linear regression on intention to use e-learning again.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Psychomotor performance was lower in the blended cohort (80.60, SD 9.70, vs 84.44, SD 10.80; mean difference 3.84, in-person minus blended, 95% CI 2.67-5.01; d=0.37; P<.001); the adjusted coefficient was -4.04 (95% CI -5.15 to -2.92; P<.001). Equivalence within the prespecified ±3-point margin was not demonstrated. Knowledge (difference -0.30, 95% CI -1.68 to 1.08) and integrated scenario performance (-0.94, 95% CI -1.89 to 0.00) fell within the prespecified ±5- and ±4-point margins, respectively. Psychomotor-threshold (521/581, 89.7%, vs 557/603, 92.4%; P=.10) and overall-certification rates (459/581, 79%, vs 474/603, 78.6%; P=.87) did not differ detectably. Knowledge-threshold attainment was higher in the blended cohort (516/581, 88.8%, vs 503/603, 83.4%; P=.007). Among the 236 blended-cohort participants who completed the survey, perceived benefits and positive attitudes toward digital learning were positively associated with intention to use e-learning again.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: The blended cohort had lower early psychomotor scores, whereas knowledge and integrated scenario differences fell within the prespecified margins. Programs adopting comparable models should assess psychomotor outcomes directly rather than infer them from knowledge or overall certification outcomes.

articles.title: Current concepts review on the limping child.

abstract.label: PURPOSE OF REVIEW
abstract.text: Diagnosing the cause of an atraumatic limp in children is challenging, as conditions with overlapping clinical presentations can range from self-limited processes to orthopedic emergencies. Knowledge of evolving risk factors, diagnostic practices, and management approaches is crucial to efficient treatment. This review synthesizes recent evidence on the evaluation of the limping child, focusing on key diagnoses including transient synovitis of the hip (TSH), septic arthritis of the hip (SAH), slipped capital femoral epiphysis (SCFE), and Legg-Calvé-Perthes disease (LCPD).

abstract.label: RECENT FINDINGS
abstract.text: For SAH and TSH, emerging evidence supports point-of-care ultrasound alongside clinical findings and inflammatory markers to improve diagnostic differentiation. In SCFE, increasing incidence, recognition of additional risk factors, variable pain presentations, and evolving approaches to surgical timing and contralateral risk have implications for diagnosis and management. For LCPD, current studies highlight variability in pain presentation, advances in radiographic classification, and individualized operative containment strategies.

abstract.label: SUMMARY
abstract.text: This review provides a synopsis of recent literature surrounding SAH, TSH, SCFE, and LCPD. Recent advances may facilitate earlier recognition, improve risk stratification, and support more individualized management for children presenting with a new limp. While this article highlights four important diagnoses, clinicians should maintain a broad differential of classic and atypical presentations of limping.

articles.title: Powerhouses of lethality: mitochondria in macrophage antimicrobial activity.

abstract.text: Macrophages employ multiple strategies to dispatch phagocytosed microbes, including bombardment with toxic compounds and radicals, or the deprivation of key nutrients. The lethality of macrophages depends on their ability to regulate levels of microbicidal effectors and proper targeting of these effectors to the phagosome, where many intracellular pathogens are detained. Mitochondria play important roles in establishing an antimicrobial phagosomal environment in macrophages, playing roles in both the production and targeting of these effectors. In response to infection, the mitochondrial network undergoes dramatic structural and functional perturbations that modulate macrophage microbicidal potential. As central coordinators of cellular metabolism, mitochondria control the abundance of metabolites that can either be toxic to ingested microbes or necessary for their growth. Mitochondria are also prolific producers of reactive oxygen species (ROS), which play direct roles in killing microbes and serve as signaling molecules to coordinate antimicrobial responses. While mitochondria are also known to play extensive roles in regulating cytokine production and proinflammatory responses, this review will focus on highlighting mechanisms by which mitochondria manipulate the macrophage microbicidal milieu.

articles.title: Left Anterior Descending Artery Also Lives at the Apex: A Cardiac Point-of-Care Ultrasound Blind Spot and the Risk of False Reassurance.
Predicting Return to Play After Achilles Tendon Injury in National Football League Players Using Machine Learning.

abstract.label: UNLABELLED
abstract.text: BackgroundNational Football League (NFL) players frequently experience Achilles tendon (AT) injuries. However, there is mixed evidence regarding factors influencing return to play (RTP) after AT injury. The objective of this study is to develop machine learning models to predict NFL players' likelihood of RTP within 1 year of an AT tear.

abstract.label: HYPOTHESIS
abstract.text: Machine learning models can predict 1-year RTP status in NFL players following AT tear.

abstract.label: STUDY DESIGN
abstract.text: Retrospective Cohort.MethodsA retrospective review was conducted to identify NFL players who sustained unilateral AT injuries from 2004 to 2024. Player demographics and performance data were recorded. Return to play was defined as generating playing statistics. Five machine learning models were developed: logistic regression, random forest classifier, XGBoost, Gaussian naive Bayes, and K-nearest neighbors. Accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 were used to assess model performance.ResultsOne hundred seventy-six NFL players were identified with an AT injury. One hundred eight players achieved RTP within 1 year (class 1), while 63 players did not (class 0). In the full cohort, injury etiology was the most influential feature associated with 1-year RTP, followed by pre-injury performance. Among the 99 players with a confirmed AT tear, 48 players achieved RTP within 1 year (class 1), while 51 players did not (class 0). Within the confirmed-tear cohort, draft round and games started were the leading predictors of 1-year RTP, which was best predicted by random forest with a mean accuracy of 0.69, precision of 0.68, recall of 0.70, and an F1-score of 0.69 for class 0.ConclusionMachine learning models that combine clinical and performance metrics of NFL athletes demonstrated potential for predicting 1-year RTP after AT injury and identifying factors associated with RTP.

abstract.label: CLINICAL RELEVANCE
abstract.text: Machine learning could be integrated into clinical decision-making and prognosis to refine rehabilitation approaches in NFL players.

abstract.label: LEVEL OF EVIDENCE
abstract.text: Level 3.

articles.title: Tomographic ultrasound (tUS) for thyroid volume determination.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Accurate thyroid volume determination is essential for treatment planning. This feasibility study evaluated the accuracy of a novel tomographic ultrasound (tUS) approach compared to 2D ultrasound, using contrast-enhanced computed tomography (ceCT) as reference standard.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: In this prospective, single-center study, 50 patients undergoing neck ceCT were enrolled. Thyroid volume was measured by 2D ultrasound (ellipsoid model), automatedvolume (tUS uncorrected), physician-corrected volume (tUS corrected) and ceCT. Linear regression for proportional bias, log-transformed Bland-Altman analysis, clinical error metrics and correction duration were evaluated.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: 2D ultrasound showed significant proportional bias (slope=-0.215, p<0.0001) and systematic underestimation (mean difference -6.0mL; geometric mean ratio 0.76). Corrected tUS eliminated proportional bias (p=0.0557) and reduced bias (mean difference +0.8mL; geometric mean ratio 1.04). Corrected tUS achieved lower MAE (4.42mL vs. 6.53mL) and MAPE (19.4% vs. 25.4%) than 2D ultrasound, placing 60.0% vs. 34.0% of cases within ±20% error limits. In enlarged glands (n=19), corrected tUS maintained superior accuracy (MAE 5.82mL, MAPE 12.4%) versus 2D ultrasound (MAE 11.35mL, MAPE 26.5%). Physician correction averaged 2:51minutes, independent of thyroid volume (r=-0.081, p=0.5784).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: In this feasibility study, physician-corrected tUS reduced the size-dependent systematic underestimation observed with 2D ultrasound and yielded volumes closer to ceCT, particularly in enlarged glands, within a clinically feasible workflow. Because the best-performing method required manual expert correction and the limits of agreement with ceCT exceeded the predefined clinical threshold, corrected tUS should be regarded as a promising semi-automated approach that requires further validation, including interobserver assessment, before it can be considered interchangeable with ceCT.

articles.title: Determining the Relationship Between Loneliness and Social Support in Adolescents Affected by the Earthquake: A Study From Turkey.
articles.journal_full: Disaster medicine and public health preparedness

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: This study was conducted to determine the relationship between loneliness and social support in adolescents affected by the earthquake.

abstract.label: METHOD
abstract.text: This descriptive correlational study was conducted in April-May 2023 with 549 adolescents aged 12-18 living in 11 provinces affected by the February 6, 2023, Kahramanmaraş-centered earthquake in Turkey. In this study, the snowball sampling method was used. Data were collected using a Descriptive Information Form, the UCLA Loneliness Scale, and the Multidimensional Scale of Perceived Social Support.Statistical analyses included independent t-test, one-way ANOVA with post hoc Tukey HSD and Dunnett's tests, Pearson correlation, and multiple regression analysis.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Most adolescents were significantly affected by the earthquake. Their loneliness score was below average, while their perceived social support score was above average. There was a significant negative relationship between loneliness and perceived social support. Key factors influencing loneliness included satisfaction with current living conditions, loss of relatives, and feelings of loneliness post-earthquake.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The findings highlight the critical role of social support in reducing loneliness among adolescents affected by the earthquake. Enhancing social support networks and addressing factors such as living conditions and loss experiences are crucial for improving the psychological well-being of disaster-affected adolescents.

articles.title: Teaching medical care in mass casualty incidents through advanced clinical simulation.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: The threat of intentional mass casualty incidents remains high, making healthcare response a priority. The Hartford Consensus and the THREAT protocol (Threat suppression, Hemorrhage control, Rapid Extrication to safety, Assessment by medical providers, Transport to definitive care) establish recommended actions. A key objective is training civilians as "immediate responders" for hemorrhage control. However, this emergency care training is often limited in medical schools. Francisco de Vitoria University incorporates clinical simulation, including emergency medicine content in the fifth year. This study aims to assess learning outcomes from an activity designed to familiarize students with the Hartford Consensus and THREAT protocol.

abstract.label: MATERIALS AND METHODS
abstract.text: Simulation Activity Development: Students gathered in an enclosed area. Basic principles of action during a terrorist attack were explained. A simulated attack unfolded, requiring students to escape, hide, or fight, and assist victims according to protocol. Wounded individuals were transported to a meeting point for a debriefing, followed by a final group meeting.

abstract.label: LEARNING OUTCOME ASSESSMENT
abstract.text: Students completed a questionnaire at the beginning and end of the activity, including technical and subjective questions about perceived preparedness. Statistical analysis used the Chi-square test to compare response frequencies. 112 fifth-year medical students completed the online questionnaire.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Seventy-one pre-activity and 41 post-activity questionnaires were completed. Perceived preparedness significantly improved: initially, 66.2% felt "no" prepared, which decreased to 4.9% after the activity (p < 0.001). Correct responses to "first thing to do in an attack" increased from 19.4% to 92.7% (p < 0.001). Understanding "improvised means" rose from 85.9% to 100% (p = 0.042). No statistically significant differences were observed for more technical questions like hemorrhage or cardiac arrest.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: Teaching through simulated environments offers undeniable learning benefits. While curriculum integration faces, simulation is a valuable tool in emergency training. Our cost-effective instructional methods proved successful, as shown by survey data. These engaging experiences facilitate knowledge acquisition. Replicating real-life conditions helps students appreciate inherent challenges. We conclude that using a simulated environment at the undergraduate level to train students as first responders in mass casualty incidents is an effective educational strategy.

articles.title: Educational content for public health nurses' on-site disaster response: A scoping review, guideline analysis and focus group interview study.

abstract.label: AIM
abstract.text: To identify and organize educational content for public health nurses' on-site disaster response.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Nurses play critical roles in emergency medical support and community-based disaster response. However, specialized education for public health nurses' on-site disaster response remains limited. Therefore, educational content relevant to their on-site disaster response must be identified and organized.

abstract.label: DESIGN
abstract.text: This was a framework-guided, multi-source study using a scoping review, guideline analysis and focus group interviews.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A scoping review was conducted to identify and map educational content to public health nurses' on-site disaster response. Database searches yielded 2870 records. Following the implementation of inclusion criteria, eight studies were included in the review and eight disaster-response guidelines were analyzed. To identify educational needs for on-site disaster response, focus group interviews were conducted with nine South Korean nurses who had been dispatched to disaster sites as part of the national disaster emergency medical response system.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Key needs related to understanding command systems, clarifying roles and interagency communication, increasing practical confidence, enhancing the usability of disaster manuals and understanding the flow of field emergency medical station operations were identified. Findings were integrated into a conceptual framework constituting the pre-disaster, disaster and post-disaster phases. Educational content included physical and psychological readiness, leadership and clinical competencies, reporting, communication, field emergency medical station operation and evaluation and debriefing.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: The conceptual framework can help organize phase-specific education across the disaster cycle. Future research is needed to validate the framework and empirically evaluate educational programs developed from it in improving public health nurses' on-site disaster-response competencies.

articles.title: Seatbelt Use and Traumatic Brain Injury Outcomes After Pediatric Motor Vehicle Collisions.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Seatbelts and age-appropriate restraints reduce crash-related injuries, but associations with specific pediatric traumatic brain injury (TBI) outcomes require further characterization.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To examine associations between documented seatbelt use, TBI severity, head computed tomography (CT) findings, and hospital admission after pediatric motor vehicle collisions.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective study reviewed trauma registry and medical record data from a Level I pediatric trauma center. Of 179 collision-related cases identified among 1,095 pediatric trauma records, 138 had documented seatbelt status. Categorical outcomes were compared using chi-square and exact tests. A multivariable logistic regression examined hospital admission in 96 complete cases.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: ED TBI severity was available for 97 patients: 74 mild, 6 moderate, and 17 severe. Seatbelt use was not significantly associated with severity (P = .098). Among 107 patients with available CT results, abnormal findings occurred in 17/56 (30.4%) with seatbelt use and 25/51 (49.0%) without seatbelt use (Pearson P = .048; Fisher exact P = .074). The prehospital Glasgow Coma Scale comparison was not significant (P = .075). Loss of consciousness and transfer status were associated with higher adjusted odds of hospital admission, whereas higher ED Glasgow Coma Scale scores were associated with lower odds.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Abnormal CT findings were less frequent with seatbelt use, ED TBI severity did not differ significantly. Missing data, limited sample size, and unmeasured crash characteristics constrain causal interpretation.

articles.title: Early fecal diversion versus no initial diversion in blunt open pelvic fractures: A systematic review and meta-analysis of pelvic infection and mortality.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: The benefit of routine early fecal diversion in blunt open pelvic fractures remains uncertain. We examined its association with pelvic infection and short-term mortality.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: MEDLINE/PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science Core Collection, and CENTRAL were searched from inception through 12 August 2026, with citation searching. Comparative observational studies were synthesized using crude risk ratios (RRs), REML random-effects models, modified Hartung-Knapp confidence intervals, and Mantel-Haenszel sensitivity analyses without continuity correction. Two reviewers independently selected studies, extracted data, and assessed ROBINS-I risk of bias and GRADE certainty.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Eighteen observational comparative reports were retained. Potential cohort overlap prevented a valid unique overall participant total. Eight cohorts contributed to broad pelvic infection (171 participants; seven estimable): RR 0.78 (95% CI 0.35-1.70; I²=19.6%). The stricter outcome-definition analysis included five cohorts (88 participants; four estimable): RR 0.72 (95% CI 0.07-6.97). Excluding two author-reported infected hematomas through an existing replacement sensitivity gave RR 0.84 (95% CI 0.34-2.05). Eight mortality cohorts (236 participants) yielded RR 0.82 (95% CI 0.33-2.07; I²=19.0%). Post-2006 evidence remained inconclusive for infection (three cohorts; RR 0.74, 95% CI 0.009-58.85) and mortality (five cohorts; RR 1.19, 95% CI 0.27-5.26). Diversion was preferentially used in patients with more severe injuries. All reports had Serious or Critical risk of bias; certainty was very low.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Available evidence does not establish a reduction in pelvic infection or short-term mortality with routine early diversion. Confounding, inconsistent outcome ascertainment, and imprecision prevent causal conclusions or exclusion of benefit in selected high-risk injuries.

articles.title: Associations of mental health, substance use and housing instability with hospitalisation outcomes for adults with diabetes complications: a retrospective cohort study in Maryland, USA.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Mental health disorders (MH), substance use disorder (SUD) and housing instability (HI) are frequently co-occurring vulnerabilities that complicate diabetes self-management, contributing to healthcare utilisation. However, limited research has examined their combined associations with hospitalisation outcomes among patients admitted for diabetes-related complications. We evaluated the individual and joint associations of MH, SUD and HI with emergency department-initiated admission (ED-IA) and 30-day, 60-day and 90-day readmission.

abstract.label: RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the Maryland statewide hospital discharge data repository (2016-2023). Patients aged ≥18 years with an index hospitalisation for diabetes complications were included. Multivariable logistic regression was used to estimate adjusted ORs (aORs) for the associations of MH, SUD and HI with ED-IA and readmission, adjusting for demographic, socioeconomic and clinical characteristics. Exposures were modelled individually and as composite categories to characterise associations for observed co-occurrence patterns.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 48 308 patients, 45.2% had MH, 34.3% had SUD and 1.3% had HI. Readmission occurred in 4.8%, 7.8% and 10.3% at 30, 60 and 90 days; 87.9% of index admissions originated in the ED. MH was associated with ED-IA (aOR 1.31) and readmission (30-day aOR 1.61; 60-day aOR 1.56; 90-day aOR 1.53). SUD was not associated with ED-IA but was associated with readmission (aORs 1.51, 1.63 and 1.70). HI was associated with ED-IA (aOR 1.68) but not readmission. Patients with all three vulnerabilities had the highest odds of ED-IA (aOR 2.84) and readmission (aORs 2.93, 2.78 and 3.15).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: MH, SUD and HI were independently and jointly associated with increased healthcare utilisation (ED-IA and readmission) among adults hospitalised for diabetes complications. These findings underscore the need for prospective research to evaluate whether integrated diabetes care models incorporating behavioural health interventions and housing support into comprehensive discharge planning reduce ED utilisation and hospital readmissions.

articles.title: Decreasing Controlled Substance Variances in an Adult Emergency Department.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Substance use disorder affects 10% to 15% of health care workers. The adult emergency department at a large medical center has a 60% higher controlled substance transaction rate than inpatient units, increasing the risk of diversion. Diversion involves unlawfully removing controlled substances, whereas variances result from incomplete documentation during transactions. Key contributing factors include inconsistent adherence to medication management policies, omission of barcode scanning before medication administration, and insufficient documentation of waste during controlled substance handling. The aim of this quality improvement project was to reduce variances by ensuring consistent barcode scanning and immediate documentation.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: An evidence-based intervention that incorporated standardized workflows and visual guidance was implemented for 15 weeks in the fall of 2025 to reduce controlled substance variances. By focusing on these key behaviors, the project sought to achieve lasting improvements in variance rates and patient safety.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: During the 15-week implementation period, 152 variances were observed. The weekly variance rates ranged from 5 to 19, with a median of 10. Of the variances, 50% (n = 76) involved failing to scan the medication into the electronic health record, 20.4% (n = 31) involved failing to document the disposal of unused controlled substances, 17.1% (n = 26) involved documentation errors, and 12.5% (n = 19) involved documenting a medication removal before administering it.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: This project revealed that workflow standardization and visual aids alone were insufficient in reducing variances related to controlled substance medications. Ongoing reminders, support, continued staff education, regular compliance monitoring, and a commitment to medication safety protocols are essential for sustainability, especially as patient volumes change.

articles.title: System Delay and Mortality in ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction: A Multicentre, Retrospective, Observational Study in Seoul.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Prompt recognition and early management of ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) are crucial for improving outcomes. This study investigates the association between system delay and in-hospital mortality in patients with STEMI.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Using data from the Seoul GOLDEN-time emergency medical system registry, a multicentre retrospective registry in Seoul, this study analysed patients with STEMI who were transported to an emergency department via emergency medical service for cardiac complaints between July 2020 and December 2022. System delay included the response time (first medical contact to an ambulance on the scene), scene time (ambulance on the scene to departure), scene-to-door time (departure to hospital arrival), and door-to-balloon time.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 654 patients with STEMI who received percutaneous coronary intervention, survivors had shorter overall system delay, prehospital time, scene time, scene-to-door time, and door-to-balloon time than non-survivors. A system delay > 127.5 minutes was associated with high mortality (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 2.07; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.05-4.13). Prolonged prehospital time (aOR, 2.35; 95% CI, 1.16-4.95), scene time (aOR, 2.61; 95% CI, 1.24-5.75), and door-to-balloon time (aOR, 2.20; 95% CI, 1.09-4.39) were each independently associated with mortality.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Prolonged system delays were associated with increased in-hospital mortality. These findings highlight the need for a comprehensive, system-level approach to reducing system delay across the entire STEMI care pathway.

articles.title: Clinical Characteristics of Spontaneous and Recurrent Pneumomediastinum and Risk Factors of Recurrence.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Spontaneous pneumomediastinum (SPM) is rare, and most existing knowledge comes from small case series. Although usually benign, SPM often leads to hospital admission and substantial healthcare resource use. This study aimed to characterize SPM and recurrent spontaneous pneumomediastinum (RSPM) in a large cohort and to explore factors associated with recurrence.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Patients with SPM hospitalized at Putian First Hospital between September 2011 and September 2023 were included. Clinical data were extracted from electronic medical records. Follow-up was performed to identify RSPM. Patients were divided into nonrecurrence and recurrence groups, and risk factors for recurrence were evaluated using univariate logistic regression.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 135 patients with SPM were included. Most patients were male (78.1%), with a median age of 20 years (interquartile range [IQR]: 17-32). A bimodal age distribution was observed, with peaks at 15-19 and 50-54 years. The most common symptom was chest pain (51.9%), and 54.0% of the patients had no identifiable trigger. Among the 9 patients with RSPM (6.7%), median age at recurrence was 25 years (IQR: 16-56) and median interval to recurrence was 6.5 months (range: 1-16.5). Dyspnea was the most common symptom at recurrence (66.7%), and 44.4% of the patients showed greater clinical and radiological severity than at initial presentation. Univariate analysis suggested that a history of bronchitis was associated with RSPM (OR: 11.71, 95% CI: 1.68-81.89); other potential factors included silicosis, pneumonia, and upper respiratory infection as a trigger.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: SPM predominantly affects young males and generally follows a benign course. Although recurrence is uncommon (6.7%), it may be more severe than the initial episode in nearly half of the cases. A history of bronchitis may be associated with recurrence, but this finding is exploratory. Age-specific preventive strategies and careful exclusion of secondary pneumomediastinum are essential.

articles.title: Hidden in Plain Sight: Gonorrhea-Associated Flexor Tenosynovitis-A Case Report.

abstract.text: Disseminated gonococcal infection (DGI) is an uncommon but potentially serious complication of Neisseria gonorrhoeae infection in which infection extends from a mucosal site to distant tissues. The literature describes two types of clinical presentation: an arthritis-dermatitis syndrome characterized by tenosynovitis, polyarthralgia, and skin lesions and a suppurative monoarthritis. In the former presentation, synovial fluid cultures are usually negative, whereas synovial fluid cultures are more often positive in the latter suppurative gonococcal arthritis. This distinction is important in the present case because Neisseria gonorrhoeae was recovered from the surgically drained collection associated with the fourth-digit flexor tendon sheath rather than from synovial fluid; therefore, we characterize the case as gonococcal flexor tenosynovitis associated with DGI rather than culture-proven septic arthritis. A 53-year-old man with well-controlled HIV presented with pain, swelling, and limited motion of the right fourth finger and shoulder after recent travel to Cuba and sexual contact with a new male partner with inconsistent condom use. Laboratory evaluation revealed leukocytosis and elevated inflammatory markers. Ultrasound of the finger demonstrated flexor tenosynovitis with a 10-mm abscess. Bedside incision and drainage was performed, and the surgical specimen grew Neisseria gonorrhoeae. The patient was treated with intravenous ceftriaxone followed by oral amoxicillin based on antimicrobial susceptibility results, with complete clinical recovery. This case highlights an unusual localized musculoskeletal manifestation of DGI in the absence of urogenital symptoms. Point-of-care ultrasound identified a drainable collection, while culture of the affected site established the diagnosis. DGI should be considered in atraumatic flexor tenosynovitis, particularly when there is a relevant sexual exposure.

articles.title: Violence Against Out-Of-Hospital Emergency Healthcare Professionals: A Qualitative Exploration of Lived Experiences, Microaggressions, and Coping Mechanisms.

abstract.label: AIM
abstract.text: To explore experiences of workplace violence among nurses and drivers working in prehospital emergency medical services in northeastern Italy.

abstract.label: DESIGN
abstract.text: A qualitative interpretative study.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A qualitative interpretative study was conducted using semi-structured interviews with a group of Italian healthcare professionals involved in out-of-hospital emergency care. Participants were recruited through purposive sampling and included nurses and ambulance drivers who had experienced at least one episode of workplace violence. Data were collected between May and August 2025 and analysed using inductive content analysis.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Fifteen participants were interviewed. Three main themes were developed: 'Violence is taken home', 'Microaggressions: the invisible violence', and 'Strategies: Si vis pacem, para violentiam'. Workplace violence had lasting emotional and professional consequences including fear, helplessness, and reduced well-being. Microaggressions, often normalized and influenced by gender and cultural factors, were under-recognized forms of violence. Participants described using communication and de-escalation techniques, situational awareness, and peer support, while perceiving organizational support as insufficient.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Workplace violence in prehospital emergency care has significant emotional and professional consequences and may be underreported. Microaggressions represent an important, often overlooked dimension requiring recognition and intervention.

abstract.label: IMPLICATIONS FOR THE PROFESSION AND/OR PATIENT CARE
abstract.text: Targeted training in communication and violence management, improved reporting systems, and structured psychological support are essential to mitigate the impact of workplace violence. Promoting a supportive organizational culture and addressing microaggressions may enhance staff well-being, patient safety, and quality of care.

abstract.label: IMPACT
abstract.text: Addressing both overt violence and normalized microaggressions, alongside strengthening organizational support, is essential to safeguarding healthcare professionals in prehospital emergency settings.

abstract.label: PATIENT OR PUBLIC CONTRIBUTION
abstract.text: No Patient or Public Contribution.

abstract.label: REPORTING METHOD
abstract.text: The Consolidated Criteria for Reporting Qualitative Studies (COREQ) checklist was used.

articles.title: Point-of-care ultrasound for confirming endotracheal tube placement in prehospital and critical care transport: a scoping review.

abstract.text: Point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) has demonstrated high pooled diagnostic accuracy for endotracheal tube (ETT) placement confirmation in adult Emergency Departments and Intensive Care Units,, but its translation to pre-hospital and Critical Care Transport (CCT) environments is unclear.
