articles.journal_full: Disaster medicine and public health preparedness

abstract.text: Health care systems face challenges with patient surge during disasters. Alternate Care Facilities (ACFs) represent one strategy for expanding health care capacity when hospitals become overwhelmed. ACF implementation guidance remains largely informed by retrospective reports and expert opinion. Recognizing that many operational lessons reside within the experiential knowledge of responders rather than the published literature, the authors developed a national symposium to systematically learn from experts with direct ACF operational experience. Informed by prior research, the symposium employed purposive recruitment, structured facilitator guides, rotating breakout groups, dedicated facilitators and note takers, and standardized discussion prompts to capture practice-based insights across operational domains. This manuscript describes the rationale, conceptual framework, planning process, and execution of the 2025 Alternate Care Facility Symposium. The methods described provide a reproducible approach for translating distributed experiential expertise into actionable knowledge to strengthen disaster preparedness. Summaries of the findings from this symposium are published separately.

articles.title: Breakout Session 10: Miscellaneous Topics.
articles.journal_full: Disaster medicine and public health preparedness

abstract.text: This final breakout session provided subject matter experts with an opportunity to discuss additional considerations that were not previously covered during the Alternate Care Facilities (ACF) Symposium. Participants reflected on operational experiences not otherwise captured and discussed barriers, mitigation strategies, and future priorities for ACF implementation. Several recurring themes emerged. Despite significant hospital strain, many ACFs experienced underutilization due to institutional reluctance to transfer patients, financial and political considerations, limited stakeholder engagement, and patient mistrust of nontraditional care settings. Participants described successful approaches to improving operations, including staff wellness initiatives, work-rest cycles, community engagement, and communication strategies to improve patient trust. Persistent challenges included patient refusal of transfer, difficulties coordinating care and patient movement across multiple ACFs within a region, loss of institutional knowledge following staff turnover, and leadership fatigue due to limited redundancy among key operational personnel. Participants emphasized the need for regional coordination mechanisms, centralized repositories of operational lessons learned, earlier integration of non-clinical operational leaders, and deliberate communication strategies to increase trust among referring hospitals and communities. These findings suggest that successful ACF implementation depends on institutional trust, regional coordination, workforce sustainability, and preservation of operational knowledge to support future emergency response efforts.

articles.title: Breakout Session 4: Clinical Operations.
articles.journal_full: Disaster medicine and public health preparedness

abstract.text: Alternate care facilities (ACFs) established during disaster response operations are required to deliver safe clinical care under severe operational, staffing, and infrastructure constraints. This breakout session explored real-world experiences managing clinical operations within ACFs, emphasizing lessons learned from frontline leaders responsible for patient flow, escalation of care, documentation, discharge planning, and support services. Participants described highly adaptive workflows shaped by limited laboratory, radiology, pharmacy, and electronic health record capabilities. Many sites relied on simplified triage models, selective laboratory testing, courier-based diagnostics, and external vendor partnerships to sustain operations. Clinical success was associated with integration of social work, discharge planning, culturally responsive care, and management of vulnerable populations, including patients with behavioral health and substance use disorders. Participants identified significant challenges related to fragmented medical records, EHR downtime, staffing fatigue, language barriers, and inability to replicate hospital-level ancillary services. Key recommendations included embedding social support services early in operational planning, standardizing workflows, developing culturally informed liaison infrastructure, and strengthening backup documentation training. Findings highlight that effective ACF clinical operations depend not only on medical capability, but also on flexible systems supporting communication, discharge coordination, and continuity of care during disaster conditions.

articles.title: Breakout Session 3: Leadership Structures.
articles.journal_full: Disaster medicine and public health preparedness

abstract.text: Establishing leadership and management structures for alternate care facilities (ACFs) presented governance challenges distinct from those of conventional hospital operations and were frequently shaped as much by political and inter-organizational dynamics as by clinical need. Symposium participants summarized operational lessons from leading ACFs across multiple jurisdictions and partnership models. Participants reported that effective ACFs typically mirrored hospital executive structures while operating under hybrid governance models that distributed authority, liability, and resources across multiple hospital systems and state agencies. Hospital Incident Command System (ICS) provided necessary scaffolding but was insufficient on its own; success depended on pre-existing inter-agency relationships and on credible leaders with the gravitas to mobilize resources across organizational boundaries. Persistent challenges included credentialing and electronic medical record (EMR) access delays, political directives that superseded clinical judgment, and severe interpersonal conflict that overwhelmed leadership without embedded human resources support. Recommended best practices include pre-identifying and training a cadre of ACF leaders, embedding human resources and behavioral health support within the leadership team, and clearly defining and protecting the ACF mission throughout activation and operations.

articles.title: Breakout Session 5: Policy Considerations and External Partner Coordination.
articles.journal_full: Disaster medicine and public health preparedness

abstract.text: The Policy Considerations and External Partner Coordination breakout session focused on participants' real-world experience with policies unique to alternate care facilities (ACFs), and also considered coordination between ACFs and external partners. These partners included state or local public health, state or local emergency management, regulatory agencies, and other response partners. Participants discussed who these partners were, how they built these connections, organizational relationships and culture that emerged, and how this impacted any aspect of the ACF planning, activation, and operations. Discussion focused on what participants did, rather than proposing solutions and solving problems.

articles.title: Breakout Session 2: Staffing Models.
articles.journal_full: Disaster medicine and public health preparedness

abstract.text: During the "Alternate Care Facility (ACF) Symposium: Understanding National Experiences in Planning and Operations," over 4 dozen ACF subject matter experts were invited to discuss their experiences with planning, activating, and running ACFs. The staffing model session focused on participants' experience with selecting the most appropriate staffing model, staffing ratio, supervision structure, staff recruitment, and education and training. The group identified several successful models, just-in-time training, and proposed approaches to ensure effective staff allocation during crises.

articles.title: Joint Effusion Doesn't Always Mean Fracture! Diagnosing Pulled Elbow on Point-Of-Care Ultrasound in a 6-Year-Old Girl: A Case Report.
articles.journal_full: Journal of paediatrics and child health

articles.title: Tractionless Hip Arthroscopy in Children With Suspected Septic Arthritis of the Hip: A Comparative Cohort Study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Tractionless hip arthroscopy has emerged as a portal-based alternative to traditional open arthrotomy for children requiring operative treatment for suspected septic arthritis of the hip. However, comparative clinical outcome data remain limited. The purpose of this study was to compare outcomes following tractionless hip arthroscopy and arthrotomy in children undergoing operative treatment for suspected septic arthritis of the hip.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We performed a retrospective cohort study of children who underwent operative irrigation and drainage for suspected septic arthritis of the hip between 2009 and 2025. The choice of operative approach reflected surgeon preference and increasing institutional experience with tractionless hip arthroscopy over the study period. Demographic characteristics, disease severity, operative variables, and postoperative outcomes were compared using unadjusted univariate analyses.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 164 children underwent operative treatment, including 34 treated with tractionless hip arthroscopy and 130 treated with arthrotomy. Children treated arthroscopically had higher initial inflammatory marker values and more frequent contiguous osteomyelitis. Operative time, hospital length of stay, repeat surgery, emergency department return, hospital readmission, and observed sequelae during available follow-up did not differ statistically between groups. The mean 48-hour C-reactive protein change was -2.7±6.7 mg/dL after arthroscopy and +0.23±6.0 mg/dL after arthrotomy (P=0.005); postoperative oral morphine equivalents were 12.9±22.1 and 28.6±55.2, respectively (P=0.020). These unadjusted secondary findings were considered exploratory.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Tractionless hip arthroscopy was feasible and was not associated with an obvious increase in short-term treatment failure in this exploratory cohort. The findings do not establish equivalence, superiority, or long-term comparative safety. Prospective multicenter investigation with longer follow-up is warranted.

abstract.label: LEVEL OF EVIDENCE
abstract.text: Level III-retrospective cohort study.

articles.title: Real-world diagnosis and treatment of individuals with migraine in the United States: The Migraine Insights in Diagnosis and Treatment (MIND) study.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: The objective of this study was to describe the real-world diagnosis and treatment patterns of individuals newly diagnosed with migraine in the United States (US).

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Over 10% of adults in the US are living with migraine. Recent data from large, population-based studies on the diagnosis and treatment of migraine among individuals in the US who are newly diagnosed with migraine are lacking.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: The Migraine Insights in Diagnosis and Treatment (MIND) study is a retrospective cohort study conducted using the Optum® Market Clarity database. The study included individuals with a first migraine diagnosis between July 1, 2018, and June 30, 2021 (index date), who were ≥18 years old on the index date, had ≥12 months of pre-index and ≥36 months of post-index continuous claims enrollment, and no diagnosis of migraine or use of migraine-specific medications in the pre-index period. Outcomes included index migraine diagnosis (e.g., migraine type, setting of diagnosis, specialty of the diagnosing healthcare provider [HCP]), and use of medications to treat migraine (e.g., medications indicated for acute treatment, prevention, or both; other analgesics). Medications were further subcategorized into migraine-specific acute (triptans, gepants, ergots, and ditans) and preventive (gepants and calcitonin gene-related peptide [CGRP] targeted monoclonal antibodies [mAbs]) medications. All analyses were descriptive in nature.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The study database included 911,128 individuals newly diagnosed with migraine, of whom 154,353 met all study eligibility criteria. Mean age was 46.1 years, 81.1% were female, and 66.3% were commercially insured. Common comorbidities included anxiety (40.5%), depression (28.2%), and sleep disorders (26.9%). The most common HCP specialty for the index migraine diagnosis was primary care (47.0%), followed by neurology (18.0%), and other (15.3%); diagnosis most often occurred in outpatient (89.5%) settings, followed by inpatient (7.7%), and emergency department (2.8%). Only 16.2% of individuals had a diagnostic test within 30 days before or after their index migraine diagnosis. A total of 111,345 (72.1%) individuals filled a prescription for a migraine medication in the 3 years after their index diagnosis, including 94,198 (61.0%) who received a medication for acute treatment and 62,596 (40.6%) who received a medication for prevention. The most commonly used acute migraine medication types prescribed first were NSAIDs (62.8%) and triptans (35.0%), while for prevention, it was beta blockers (23.2%) and anticonvulsants (21.6%). Migraine-specific preventive medications, CGRP-targeted mAbs (8.1%) and gepants (1.2%), were used first less frequently. A total of 71,199 (46.1%) individuals filled a prescription for an opioid in the 3 years after the index diagnosis of migraine, while 19,359 (12.5%) filled a prescription for butalbital.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: This study highlights the frequent utilization of medications that are not migraine-specific, both for acute treatment and preventive management of migraine. Increased efforts towards education for the optimal management of migraine should be implemented.

articles.title: Demographic Data Concordance: A Prospective Observational Study of Adolescents, Caregivers, and the Electronic Health Record.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: (1) To measure the concordance of patient demographic data in the electronic health record (EHR); and (2) to determine the level of agreement for patient demographic data between patient report-EHR and patients-caregivers.

abstract.label: STUDY DESIGN
abstract.text: We conducted a prospective observational survey of 295 patients (age 12 to 17 years) and caregiver dyads presenting to a pediatric emergency department. The primary outcome was concordance, reporting kappa statistics with 95% CI, of caregiver-reported patient race, ethnicity, and sex and the EHR. Secondary outcomes were concordance between: (1) patient report and EHR and (2) patient and caregiver report, including gender identity and preferred language. We surveyed dyads on the perceived impact of demographic characteristics on emergency care and caregivers on preferences for reporting data.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: For caregiver and EHR report of race, there was substantial agreement for Asian (κ=0.65, 95% CI: 0.44-0.86), Black/African American/African (κ=0.76, 95% CI: 0.66-0.86), and White (κ=0.66, 95% CI: 0.58-0.75) race and moderate agreement for Hispanic/Latino ethnicity (κ=0.53, 95% CI: 0.44-0.61). Patient report and the EHR had similar concordance for race and poor agreement for Hispanic/Latino ethnicity (κ=-0.17, 95% CI: -0.22 to -0.12). For patients and caregivers, there was strong concordance for race, ethnicity, language, and gender identity. Caregivers were more likely than pediatric patients to report that demographic factors affected emergency care. Most caregivers did not have preferences about demographic data reporting methods.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Concordance of patient race and ethnicity data in the EHR was variable and should be interpreted cautiously.

articles.title: What Does High F1 Mean in LLM-Based Pediatric Pneumonia Classification?
Comparison of visual estimation of ventricular systolic function with quantitative echocardiographic markers in newborn infants.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Neonatologist-performed echocardiography (NPE) is increasingly practiced. NPE operators typically use visual estimation of systolic function and, if indicated, confirm function using quantitative echocardiographic markers. This exploratory study aims to compare the concordance between qualitative and quantitative echocardiographic markers among NPE and non-NPE operators.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We studied a cohort of newborn infants, undergoing routine NPE by the authors at Homerton University Hospital and Aberdeen Maternity Hospital from April 2024 to October 2024. Blinded NPE and non-NPE operators independently assessed left and right ventricular systolic function visually. We compared visual estimation with standard quantitative echocardiographic markers such as shortening fraction, Simpson's ejection fraction and global longitudinal strain for left ventricle and tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion and fractional area change for right ventricle. We examined the concordance between visual estimation and quantitative echocardiographic markers for biventricular systolic function.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Sixty infants with a mean (SD) gestation and birth weight of 34 (6.2) weeks and 2311 (1319) grams respectively were examined. Sensitivity testing for all echocardiographic parameters ranged from 25% to 80% whereas specificity ranged from 38% to 78%. Sensitivity increased with worsening grades of LV dysfunction defined using shortening fraction. While concordance between NPE and non-NPE operator was generally limited across most echocardiographic parameters, test-retest reliability was acceptable for several quantitative measures, including Simpson's ejection fraction, global longitudinal strain and right ventricular fractional area change.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Visual estimation may be a useful bedside tool for detecting severe ventricular dysfunction in newborn infants; however; quantitative echocardiographic measures are likely to improve the assessment of mild to moderate dysfunction. Further studies should confirm these findings in a larger cohort with a higher representation of infants with ventricular dysfunction.

articles.title: Nonoperative Management of Juvenile Osteochondritis Dissecans Lesions of the Medial Femoral Condyle: Comparing Cylinder Cast, Hinged Knee Brace Locked Into Extension, and Activity Modification.
articles.journal_full: Clinical journal of sport medicine : official journal of the Canadian Academy of Sport Medicine

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: Compare nonoperative treatment options in juvenile osteochondritis dissecans (OCD) lesions of the medial femoral condyle.

abstract.label: DESIGN
abstract.text: Descriptive, retrospective cohort study.

abstract.label: SETTING
abstract.text: Single academic pediatric tertiary referral center.

abstract.label: PATIENTS OR PARTICIPANTS
abstract.text: Male/female patients ages 0 to 18 evaluated in the sports/orthopedic ambulatory setting who were found to have OCD lesions in the medial femoral condyle.

abstract.label: INTERVENTIONS OR ASSESSMENT OF RISK FACTORS OR INDEPENDENT VARIABLES
abstract.text: Cast immobilization, hinged knee brace locked into extension, and activity modification.

abstract.label: MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES
abstract.text: Nonoperative treatment effectiveness between the 3 groups was evaluated by radiographic healing and symptom resolution, with failure defined as progression to surgery.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 148 patients with 168 MFC JOCD lesions of the knee were identified. Median age was 11 years old. Patients were 65.5% male and 77% participated in sports. Sixty-two (37%) lesions were treated in a HKB locked into extension, 55 (32%) were casted in a cylinder cast, and 51 (31%) were treated with activity modification alone. Approximately 19% of HKB locked into extension, 22% of casted MFC JOCD, and 16% of activity-modified MFC JOCD lesions progressed to surgery. At 6 months, 76% of the HKB locked into extension, 71% of the cylinder cast, and 71% of the activity modification group had resolution of clinical symptoms and returned to activity.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: MFC JOCD lesions of the knee can be appropriately treated with a HKB brace locked in extension, cast, or activity modification with consistent success rates.

abstract.label: CLINICAL RELEVANCE
abstract.text: This study provides practical evidence regarding conservative management of MFC JOCD lesions.

abstract.label: LEVEL OF EVIDENCE
abstract.text: III.

articles.title: Enhanced wound healing potential of a carboxymethyl cellulose/gelatin-based hydrogel containing decellularized amniotic membrane and Matricaria chamomilla extract: A multifunctional composite dressing.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Chronic wound healing remains a complex biological process influenced by excessive inflammation, oxidative stress, microbial invasion, and insufficient tissue regeneration. Therefore, the design of multifunctional biomaterials that integrate structural support with biological regulation has emerged as a promising strategy in advanced wound care. This study sought to develop a composite hydrogel incorporating decellularized amniotic membrane (dAM)-derived extracellular matrix components alongside Matricaria chamomilla extract, with the goal of achieving enhanced regenerative and therapeutic outcomes.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A CMC/GEL-Chamomilla-dAM hydrogel was prepared using decellularized dAM and subsequently evaluated in terms of its physicochemical and biological characteristics. The effectiveness of the decellularization process and preservation of ECM components were first examined, followed by characterization of hydrogel morphology, rheological properties, swelling and degradation behavior, and pH stability. Its biological performance was further assessed through hemocompatibility, cytocompatibility, antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and antibacterial assays, as well as a full-thickness wound model.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Incorporation of dAM and chamomile extract resulted in a stable hydrogel with favorable physicochemical and biological characteristics. The decellularization procedure removed 97.9% of the DNA. The resulting composite hydrogel exhibited an average pore size of 78.3 ± 9.8 µm, and all hydrogel formulations showed hemolysis rates below the 5% threshold accepted for blood-contacting biomaterials, with values ranging from 3.8% to 4.5%. The composite hydrogel also supported enhanced fibroblast viability (109.6 ± 11.3%) and demonstrated antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and antibacterial activities against wound-associated pathogens. In vivo, treatment with CMC/GEL-Chamomilla-dAM accelerated wound closure (85.7 ± 6.3% at day 14) and supported tissue regeneration, outperforming both the dAM-containing hydrogel (78.9 ± 9.9%) and the commercial DuoDERM dressing (58.9 ± 4.5%), as evidenced by improved re-epithelialization, collagen deposition, angiogenesis, and early signs of tissue remodeling.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The CMC/GEL-Chamomilla-dAM hydrogel combines a dAM-containing extracellular matrix scaffold with chamomile-derived bioactive compounds, creating a favorable microenvironment for tissue repair. The addition of chamomile extract to the dAM-containing scaffold was associated with improved wound closure and tissue regeneration. While the present study design does not permit a definitive assessment of synergy between dAM and chamomile, these findings support the potential of this formulation as a multifunctional biomaterial platform for advanced wound healing applications.

articles.title: Tongue capillary refill time and imaging parameters for acute coronary syndrome identification: A prospective ED study.
articles.journal_full: The American journal of emergency medicine

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Rapid identification of acute coronary syndrome (ACS) in emergency department (ED) patients with chest pain remains challenging. Tongue capillary refill time (CRT) and tongue imaging may reflect systemic perfusion, but their value in ACS is unknown.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To evaluate the diagnostic performance of standardized tongue-derived perfusion, macroscopic, and imaging parameters for identifying ACS.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This prospective observational study enrolled 208 consecutive adult ED patients presenting with chest pain. Standardized tongue imaging and tongue CRT were assessed. A separate 20-patient pilot assessed interobserver reliability using ICC and kappa coefficients. Blinded ACS adjudication used clinical findings, serial high-sensitivity troponin measurements, electrocardiography, imaging studies, specialist consultations, and follow-up data. ROC analysis and multivariable logistic regression were performed.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 208 patients, 61 (29.3%) had ACS: 16 STEMI, 41 NSTEMI, and four unstable angina cases. Tongue CRT was significantly prolonged in ACS patients (2.6 [2.2-2.9] vs. 1.3 [1.1-1.6] seconds; p<0.001). Tongue CRT demonstrated excellent discrimination for ACS (AUC 0.941, 95% CI 0.903-0.980), outperforming the HEART score (0.860), admission troponin (0.831), and TIMI score (0.788). A CRT threshold ≥2s yielded 86.9% sensitivity and 93.2% specificity. Tongue CRT and macroscopically dry tongue remained associated with ACS after adjustment (both p<0.001). Quantitative RGB and HSV parameters showed no significant between-group differences.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Standardized tongue CRT showed excellent discrimination for ACS in this cohort, in which most ACS cases were myocardial infarction. Its diagnostic value in unstable angina and incremental clinical utility remain unestablished. External validation is required before routine clinical use.

articles.title: Substance-related acute care use among birthing parents with dependent children in Ontario, Canada, 2008 to 2024.
articles.journal_full: CMAJ : Canadian Medical Association journal = journal de l'Association medicale canadienne

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Limited data exist on substance use among parents, which can have major implications for parental and child health. We compared trends in substance-related emergency department care and hospital admission among birthing parents with dependent children and other females in Ontario, Canada, from 2008 to 2024.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: In this population-based, repeated cross-sectional study, we used linked health administrative data from ICES. We compared changes in annual age-standardized rates of substance-related acute care in birthing parents with dependent children (children aged < 19 yr) to rates in a 1:1 age-matched comparator group of other females. We used joinpoint regression to examine average annual percent change (AAPC) between birthing parents and other females, overall and by age and substance type.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The study included 5 025 622 eligible females across 2008 to 2024, of whom 46.9% were birthing parents. Between 2008 and 2024, substance-related emergency department visit and hospital admission rates increased more rapidly among the birthing parents than other females: emergency department visit rates increased from 387 to 894 versus 421 to 542 per 100 000 person-years, respectively (AAPC 4.8% v. 1.7%; p < 0.001), while hospital admissions increased from 99 to 259 versus 136 to 209 per 100 000 person-years, respectively (AAPC 6.0% v. 3.3%; p < 0.001). Rates increased more rapidly among birthing parents younger than 25 years than among other females younger than 25 years, but temporal trends were similar among birthing parents and other females aged 25 years and older. We observed growth in substance-related acute care across all substance types, but it was greatest for opioids, amphetamines, and cannabis.

abstract.label: INTERPRETATION
abstract.text: Substance-related acute care use increased disproportionately among birthing parents with dependent children, particularly younger birthing parents and for opioids, amphetamines, and cannabis. Addressing these harms will likely require more inclusive, responsive, and integrated substance use services, as well as upstream policies that strengthen supports for parental and family health.

articles.title: Cardiorespiratory Arrest in the Context of Graves' Disease: A Rare Presentation.

abstract.text: Thyroid storm is the most severe and life-threatening expression of thyrotoxicosis, and its diagnosis remains clinical. Although sinus tachycardia and atrial fibrillation dominate its cardiovascular manifestations, malignant ventricular arrhythmias are rare, and cardiorespiratory arrest as the presenting manifestation of Graves' disease has been reported only in a limited number of cases. We report the case of a 44-year-old man with a one-week history of symptoms consistent with hyperthyroidism who suffered a witnessed out-of-hospital cardiorespiratory arrest with ventricular fibrillation as the initial rhythm. Return of spontaneous circulation was achieved after three defibrillations, and urgent coronary angiography showed no obstructive coronary artery disease. Laboratory evaluation revealed severe thyrotoxicosis with positive thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH)-receptor antibodies, and thyroid ultrasound findings supported the diagnosis of Graves' disease. Thyroid storm was suspected and treated empirically, but the diagnosis could not be confirmed: the Burch-Wartofsky score reached the diagnostic threshold only when post-arrest coma was included, and the Japan Thyroid Association criteria were not met. Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging and an ajmaline provocation test did not identify structural heart disease, myocarditis, or a Brugada pattern. Thyroid hormone excess was therefore considered the most likely precipitant of the arrhythmia, although causality cannot be proven. The patient was maintained on antithyroid therapy, and a subcutaneous implantable cardioverter-defibrillator was implanted for secondary prevention following an individualized risk-benefit assessment. This case highlights the importance of considering thyrotoxicosis in the etiological workup of unexplained cardiac arrest. When a clearly established and reversible cause of the arrhythmia cannot be confirmed, management, including the decision on defibrillator implantation, should be based on an individualized risk-benefit assessment.

articles.title: Euglycemic SGLT2 Inhibitor-Associated Ketoacidosis in a Nondiabetic Patient: A Case Report.

abstract.text: We present the case of a 62-year-old nondiabetic woman receiving dapagliflozin for dilated cardiomyopathy presenting to the emergency department with severe hypoxemic respiratory failure because of suspected cardiogenic pulmonary edema. Despite treatment, she remained symptomatic and required intubation and intensive care admission. After intubation, high-anion-gap metabolic acidosis was unmasked. After exclusion of other common causes, SGLT2 inhibitor-associated ketoacidosis due to dapagliflozin was suspected. Marked ketonuria confirmed the diagnosis despite the absence of hyperglycemia. Dapagliflozin was discontinued, and intravenous insulin, glucose infusion, and early enteral nutrition were initiated. Metabolic acidosis resolved completely within 24 h. The patient was successfully extubated and discharged from the intensive care unit 48 h later. SGLT2 inhibitor-associated ketoacidosis should be considered in patients receiving sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors who develop otherwise unexplained high-anion-gap metabolic acidosis, irrespective of diabetic status or blood glucose concentration. Fasting and acute illness are relevant precipitating factors; prompt drug withdrawal, carbohydrate administration, insulin therapy, and nutritional support can lead to rapid resolution.

articles.title: Expanding Primary Care-Based Echocardiography Access in a Value-Based Care Network: Impact on Heart Failure Detection, Utilization, and Spending.

abstract.text: This retrospective observational study assessed whether expanding primary care-based echocardiography access within a rural Pennsylvania value-based care network was associated with differences in heart failure (HF) diagnosis patterns, health care utilization, and spending compared with internal controls and a state-level benchmark. Eligibility, medical, and pharmacy claims were analyzed from 2 sources: third-party payers covering the primary care network and Merative's MarketScan Medicare data as a state-level reference. Members with HF-related risk factors were identified using diagnosis codes and followed for 12 months after index risk factor documentation, and the inverse probability of treatment weighting was used, incorporating age, sex, risk score, HF risk-factor category, and eligibility duration to address baseline demographic and clinical differences. Among members with HF risk factors, 21.0% of internal study members received an incident HF diagnosis compared with 13.7% of MarketScan members (P < 0.01). Internal cohort diagnoses were less likely to occur in inpatient (IP) settings than MarketScan diagnoses (0.53% vs. 10.2%; P < 0.01) and occurred after longer intervals from risk factor documentation (202 vs. 142 days; P < 0.01). Among diagnosed members, the internal cohort had lower HF-related IP admissions (21 vs. 28 per 1,000 member-years; P < 0.01), fewer HF-related emergency department visits (34 vs. 49 per 1000 member-years; P < 0.01), and lower average monthly spending ($1,937 vs. $2,826; P < 0.01). These findings suggest that expanding primary care-based echocardiography access in a rural value-based care setting was associated with greater HF detection, more outpatient-based diagnosis, and lower downstream acute care use and spending, broadly applicable to health systems and payers investing in diagnostics.

articles.title: Acupuncture in the emergency department: A retrospective evaluation of patient-reported outcomes and healthcare utilization.
articles.journal_full: Acupuncture in medicine : journal of the British Medical Acupuncture Society

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To examine outcomes following acupuncture as a nonpharmacologic option in emergency departments during real-world implementation.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a retrospective analysis of a quality improvement program offering acupuncture to adult emergency department patients in 2023 across three intervention sites. Controls were drawn from the same emergency departments in 2022 and from matched nonparticipating emergency departments in 2022-2023. We used propensity score matched difference-in-differences models to estimate the average treatment effect on the treated for admission pain change. Secondary outcomes included emergency department analgesic-related discharge prescriptions and 30-day emergency department return or inpatient admissions. Intervention patients reported on pain, anxiety, stress and nausea before and after treatment and completed a brief post-treatment satisfaction survey.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The matched analytic sample included 358 intervention and 2702 matched control encounters. Acupuncture was associated with greater admission pain reduction (average treatment effect on the treated -1.35; 95% confidence interval -1.84 to -0.85). Among intervention patients, the pre- to post-acupuncture pain change averaged 2.4 points on a 0-10 numerical rating scale. There were no differences in discharge opioid or non-opioid prescriptions and no differences in 30-day emergency department returns or inpatient admissions. Satisfaction was high (with 98% indicating they would receive acupuncture again) and 64% stated they would pay out of pocket. Patients reported significant reductions in anxiety, stress and nausea following acupuncture.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: In real-world emergency department implementation, acupuncture was feasible and acceptable, and was associated with clinically meaningful within-patient symptom relief and a statistically significant incremental improvement in admission pain compared with usual care. High satisfaction and improvements in anxiety, stress and nausea indicate potential added patient-centered value beyond pain management.

articles.title: Variation in 90-day substance use disorder-related acute care events across United States opioid treatment programs: A Medicaid claims analysis.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND AND AIMS
abstract.text: Creating and tracking quality measures has improved outcomes in many areas of healthcare; however, quality measures specific to opioid treatment programs (OTPs) have not yet been developed. Based on the success seen in other fields, introducing quality measures in OTPs should help enhance positive outcomes and decrease negative outcomes. Substance use disorder (SUD) hospitalizations and emergency department (ED) visits are adverse and preventable outcomes for the populations that OTPs serve. Using Medicaid claims data, we created OTP-level quality measures that captured the percentage of newly treated patients that had a hospitalization or an ED visit for SUD within 90 days of initiation. We described and compared findings on this measure for OTPs across the United States.

abstract.label: DESIGN
abstract.text: Cross-sectional analysis.

abstract.label: SETTING
abstract.text: The study was conducted using Medicaid claims and enrollment data for patients treated at OTPs located across the United States.

abstract.label: PARTICIPANTS
abstract.text: The study population was Medicaid enrollees, excluding those dually eligible for Medicare, diagnosed with opioid use disorder who received care at an OTP.

abstract.label: MEASUREMENTS
abstract.text: The quality measure was defined as the percentage of an OTP's treatment episodes that had a hospitalization or an ED visit with a SUD diagnosis within 90 days of initiation.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: We calculated the measure for 1226 OTPs in measure-year 2024 using 412 411 new treatment episodes and 257 986 patients. At the OTP level, the median 90-day acute care event percentage was 5.0% in measure-year 2024 with 25th and 75th percentiles of 2.8% and 8.0%, indicating significant variability among OTPs. Casemix adjustment resulted in 46 of the 1226 OTPs moving from the 25th percentile to the 50th percentile and 20 OTPs moving from the 50th percentile to the 75th percentile.

abstract.label: SUMMARY
abstract.text: In 2024, at the median opioid treatment program (OTP), one in 20 United States Medicaid patients who newly initiated care at an OTP had evidence of an acute care event for a substance use disorder within 90 days. Substantial and reliable between-clinic variation was observed.

articles.title: Can posterolateral tibial plateau fractures be treated with an anterolateral approach? A biomechanical study on novel plating concepts in artificial tibia models.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: The aim of this study was to evaluate biomechanically whether fixation of posterolateral tibial plateau fractures (PLTPFs) through the more accessible modified anterolateral approach and by using a newly designed lateral plate with or without posterior plate extension or supplemental anteroposterior screw fixation, can provide comparable stability to direct posterolateral buttress plating.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: PLTPFs were simulated on 40 artificial tibiae and subsequently fixed with 5 different plating techniques (n = 8), namely using Variable Angle Locking Compression Plate (VA-LCP) Lateral Proximal Tibia Plate 3.5 (VA Lateral), Variable Angle Optimized Locking Technology (VOLT) Lateral Proximal Tibia Plate 3.5 (VOLT Lateral), VOLT Lateral Proximal Tibia Plate 3.5 with Posterolateral Extension (Hug), VOLT Posterolateral Proximal Tibia Plate 3.5 (PL), and VOLT Lateral Proximal Tibia Plate 3.5 with two anteroposterior parallel 3.5 mm locking screws placed superiorly to the plate's lateral-to-medial rafting locking screws (Jail) using a dedicated guide block. Biomechanical testing was performed under progressively increasing cyclic loading to failure. Interfragmentary movements were monitored via motion tracking.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Fragment displacement and its posterior tilt over the first 40,000 cycles did not differ significantly between Hug, PL, and Jail (all p > 0.999). Hug, PL, and Jail outperformed VA Lateral significantly in terms of fragment displacement over 40,000 cycles (p ≤ 0.004). In addition, Hug was associated with significantly less fragment displacement versus VOLT Lateral (p = 0.018). Posterior fragment tilting over 40,000 cycles was significantly lower in Hug, PL, and Jail versus VA Lateral and VOLT Lateral (p ≤ 0.014). Hug, PL, and Jail demonstrated significantly higher cycles to clinical failure and corresponding loads at clinical failure than VA Lateral and VOLT Lateral (p < 0.001), with no significant differences among Hug, PL, and Jail (p > 0.999). For catastrophic failure, Hug demonstrated significantly higher values than all other groups (p ≤ 0.045).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: From a biomechanical perspective, VOLT Lateral Proximal Tibia Plate 3.5 with Posterolateral Extension and VOLT Lateral Proximal Tibia Plate with supplemental jail screw fixation provide fixation stability comparable to VOLT Posterolateral Proximal Tibia Plate 3.5 with respect to fragment displacement, posterior tilt, and clinical failure. Whether PLTPFs could be addressed via the more accessible anterolateral approach without compromising the biomechanical stability of fracture fixation remains yet to be clinically validated. Standalone Lateral Proximal Tibia Plate 3.5 (VA-LCP or VOLT) performed inferiorly to their augmented alternatives.

articles.title: Where is trauma care delivered in New York state? A statewide analysis of distribution and outcomes by trauma center level.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Understanding where and how trauma care is delivered is critical to preventing and managing its disease burden. This study identified patterns in trauma care delivery by characterizing the relationship between trauma presentations and outcomes as a function of trauma center level, including trauma presentations at non-trauma centers.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A retrospective review of trauma inpatients aged ≥ 15 years across New York State from 2016 through 2020 was performed, utilizing a comprehensive New York State all-payer data reporting system, the Statewide Planning and Research Cooperative System (SPARCS). The primary endpoint for this study was mortality. Secondary endpoints included overall complications, discharge dispositions, and hospital length of stay.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 361,141 patients were included with 42.1% presenting to Level 1 and 37.3% to Non-Trauma Centers. Older adults were more frequently treated at Level 3 and Non-Trauma Centers, while younger patients and high-energy mechanisms (motor vehicle crashes and penetrating injuries) were more commonly managed at Level 1 and Level 2 Centers. The association between trauma-center group and mortality varied by severity of illness (SOI) (interaction p < 0.0001). Compared with Level 3 and Non-Trauma Centers, Level 1 and 2 Centers had higher adjusted mortality odds among hospitalizations with major SOI (aOR 1.43, 95% CI 1.12-1.83) and extreme SOI (aOR 1.39, 95% CI 1.18-1.62), with no significant difference in moderate SOI (aOR 0.83, 95% CI 0.62-1.11).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Differences in outcomes across trauma center levels are strongly influenced by case mix and severity. These findings highlight opportunities to improve triage, resource allocation, and system-level performance.

articles.title: Variations in hip fracture management at trauma vs. non-trauma centers.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Hip fractures represent a growing public health burden. Optimal management relies on timely surgical intervention coordinated by multidisciplinary care and appropriate resource availability, all of which may vary between hospital settings. Differences between trauma hospitals and non-trauma hospitals may influence outcomes, yet these variations have not been well characterized.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of hip fracture cases over a 2-year period (October 2022 to August 2024), comparing patient and procedural characteristics between a Level II trauma hospital (TH) (n = 104) and a non-trauma hospital (NTH) (n = 31). Polytrauma patients were excluded. Data were extracted from the electronic medical record (EMR). Primary outcomes were hospital length of stay (LOS) and time from admission to surgery. Group comparisons utilized chi-square or Fisher's exact tests for categorical variables and Mann-Whitney U or Welch t-tests for continuous variables, as appropriate. A multivariable random forest model was used to evaluate predictors of operative duration.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: ASA physical status distribution differed significantly between facilities (p = 0.03), with more ASA > 2 patients at the NTH (76.6% vs. 65.7%). Osteosynthesis was performed in 73.3% of NTH cases and 82.2% of TH cases; arthroplasty comprised 26.7% and 17.8%, respectively. LOS differed significantly by facility (p < 0.01), with a shorter mean stay at the NTH (4.3 vs. 5.9 days; mean difference, -1.73 days). Time to surgery also differed significantly (p < 0.001): mean 846 min (95% CI, 615-1078) at the NTH vs. 2686 minutes (95% CI, 2391-2981) at the TH. In multivariable modeling, procedure type was the dominant predictor of operative duration (permutation importance 0.686), followed by payer type (0.216); facility identity contributed minimally (0.034) after accounting for case mix.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Hip fracture care differed meaningfully between the TH and NTH within the same health care system. The NTH demonstrated significantly shorter time to surgery and LOS despite treating a proportionally higher-acuity patient population by ASA classification. These findings highlight opportunities for optimizing timeliness and resource allocation in hip fracture management across hospital settings and questions whether THs are the optimal location to treat these injuries.

articles.title: Comprehensive treatment approaches for traumatic tattoos: An integrative review.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Traumatic tattoos result from an injury that drives external pigment into the dermis. They often affect exposed sites such as the face and extremities. Pigment may persist for years within the dermis, complicating management and limiting cosmetic outcomes. Consequently, no optimal treatment technique has been identified, and long-term data remain limited.

abstract.label: AIM
abstract.text: To synthesise evidence on treatments for traumatic tattoos and to evaluate effectiveness and outcomes over the past 25 years.

abstract.label: DESIGN
abstract.text: Integrative review with narrative synthesis following Whittemore and Knafl's five stages.

abstract.label: DATA SOURCES
abstract.text: An electronic search of PubMed and Scopus was conducted from 2000 to November 2025 to identify original peer-reviewed research focusing on treatments for traumatic tattoos and to evaluate their effectiveness and outcomes.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Twenty-eight articles met the inclusion criteria, representing 27 studies, comprising largely case reports and small series, with one retrospective cohort study. Treatment approaches are grouped into laser-based therapies, acute or delayed mechanical debridement (including hydrosurgery), and other surgical or mechanical methods. Q-switched Nd:YAG, ruby, alexandrite, fractional CO2, and picosecond lasers commonly achieve good to excellent clearance with mostly transient adverse effects. Early debridement within 24 h often prevented or markedly reduced tattooing, whereas delayed intervention was associated with residual pigment. Alternative methods, such as microincisions, diamond drills, and diathermy, yielded mixed results and often required multiple sessions. Long-term outcome data were scarce.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Best practice appears to combine prompt removal of foreign material in the acute phase with appropriate laser therapy for established traumatic tattoos. The overall evidence is low-level and heterogeneous, and prospective comparative studies with longer follow-up are required.

articles.title: Patterns of depression screening, referral, and behavioral health follow-up after orthopaedic trauma.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To evaluate baseline patterns of depression, behavioral health referral, and behavioral health treatment among orthopaedic trauma patients at a Level I trauma center.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Design: Retrospective Cohort, Secondary Analysis Setting: Single Level 1 Trauma Center Patient selection criteria: Adult orthopaedic trauma patients who completed an ambulatory postoperative visit between September 2024 and November 2025. Outcome measures and comparisons: Demographic variables, PHQ-9 screening results, injury characteristics, behavioral health referral patterns, and referral completion were extracted from institutional electronic health records. Primary outcomes were the proportion of patients screening positive for depression (PHQ-9 >10), with moderately severe to severe depression (PHQ-9 ≥15) triggering behavioral health referral, and subsequent referral completion rates. Secondary outcomes included referral patterns by injury mechanism and six-month orthopaedic complications or unplanned healthcare utilization.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 528 patients, 44.7% (236/528) screened positive for depressive symptoms, and 21.2% (112/528) demonstrated moderately severe to severe depression triggering a behavioral health referral. 33.9% (38/112) of referred patients completed a behavioral health visit compared with 67.6% (115/170) of referred non-trauma orthopaedic patients. The severe depression cohort was on average younger and more likely to be female, black, and have Medicare/Medicaid insurance status. Injury Severity Score did not differ significantly across depression categories. Patients with ballistic injury had significantly higher rates of positive depression screening (51.9% vs. 41.8%; P = 0.040) and behavioral health referrals (34.0% vs. 18.0%; P < 0.001) than non-ballistic patients, though referral completion did not differ significantly by mechanism (25.0% ballistic vs. 38.2% non-ballistic; P = 0.198). Infectious and wound complications and unplanned healthcare utilization, driven by emergency department visits for wound complications, were significantly higher among patients who screened positive and failed to complete their referral compared with those who screened negative for depression (P < 0.001).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Significant gaps exist in the depression care cascade for orthopaedic trauma patients. Referral completion rates were approximately two-fold lower than non-trauma orthopaedic subspecialties, and referral non-completion was associated with significantly higher rates of infectious complications and unplanned healthcare utilization. Targeted, navigation-based interventions addressing structural barriers at the point of care are needed to close the gap between depression identification and treatment engagement in orthopaedic trauma.

abstract.label: LEVEL OF EVIDENCE
abstract.text: Level III.

articles.title: Predictors of 30-day mortality and complications following surgical treatment of pathologic hip fractures.

abstract.text: Pathologic hip fractures present complex challenges and are associated with higher postoperative complication rates and mortality compared with non-pathologic fractures. This study aimed to compare 30-day outcomes between pathologic and non-pathologic hip fracture patients and identify factors associated with 30-day mortality and postoperative complications among patients with pathologic hip fractures using the National Surgical Quality Improvement Program database. A retrospective analysis was conducted from 2006 to 2023. Patients aged ≥ 18 years undergoing hip fracture surgery were included. Patients with non-pathologic hip fractures were compared with those with pathologic hip fractures. Univariate analyses and multivariable logistic regression models were used to identify factors associated with pathologic hip fracture 30-day mortality and complications. Among 204,675 hip fracture patients, 6159 (2.9%) had pathologic hip fractures. Patients with pathologic hip fractures had higher rates of 30-day mortality (7.8% vs. 5.1%, p < 0.001), any postoperative complication (35.3% vs. 30.2%, p < 0.001), cardiac/transfusion complications (27.5% vs. 22.2%, p < 0.001), renal complications (0.5% vs. 0.3%, p = 0.017), and venous thromboembolic complications (3.4% vs. 1.7%, p < 0.001). Infectious complications and neurological complications were not significantly different between groups. In multivariable analyses, prominent protective factors associated with decreased 30-day mortality included absence of disseminated cancer (aOR 0.4, p < 0.001), independent functional status (aOR 0.2, p < 0.001), and absence of sepsis history (aOR 0.4, p = 0.02). Thrombocytopenia (aOR 1.9, p < 0.001) and anemia (aOR 1.9, p < 0.001) were prominent risk factors for 30-day mortality. Thrombocytopenia and anemia were also significant risk factors for any complications and cardiac/transfusion complications. These findings underscore the importance of comprehensive preoperative assessment and multidisciplinary care to optimize outcomes for patients with pathologic hip fractures. Patients with multiple risk factors for adverse postoperative morbidity and mortality should receive appropriately tailored care.

articles.title: Video-assisted resident education is associated with improved ankle joint reduction: A prospective controlled study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Proper fracture reduction and splinting technique is critical for soft tissue protection and fracture stability in the acute management of ankle fractures. However, residency education for acute ankle fracture reduction and splinting techniques remains poorly standardized and streamlined. This study evaluated the effect of implementing a video-assisted ankle fracture management education program administered to first-year orthopaedic residents on ankle joint reduction and splint quality.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This was a prospective controlled study conducted at a single level I trauma center. All consecutive ankle fractures (OTA/AO: 4F, 44) requiring the placement of a bivalved short leg cast or AO splint from January 1, 2019, to June 30th, 2022 were included. Exclusion criteria included skeletal immaturity, missing imaging, delayed fracture presentation more than two weeks from injury, concurrent ipsilateral injury/polytrauma interfering with ankle reduction, open fracture, or ankle fractures treated without an AO splint or cast. The primary outcome was joint reduction quality defined as radiographic post-reduction tibiofibular overlap, tibiofibular clear space, and medial clear space. Secondary outcomes included splint padding thickness and ankle dorsiflexion angle to assess splint quality.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 280 consecutive ankle fracture cases were included for evaluation of splint quality: 111 in the intervention group (mean age 46; [range 14-92]; 44% female) versus 169 in the control group (mean age 44; [range 14-90]; 41% female). Comparable injury severity was observed between groups. In the supination-external rotation IV (SER4) and type IV-equivalent (SER4e) subgroup, there was significant improvement in joint reduction quality in the intervention group as compared to control (55% versus 36%, respectively; Risk Ratio: 1.52, [95% CI: 1.03-2.25], p = 0.04). In the entire cohort, splint padding thickness was not significantly improved in the intervention group (p > 0.05), however, there was a significant increase in the percentage of ankles splinted in an appropriately dorsiflexed position (p = 0.03).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Implementation of video-assisted ankle fracture management education program was associated with improvements in overall ankle joint reduction quality. While the clinical significance of the improvements observed in ankle reduction remains yet to be established, orthopaedic surgery residency programs should consider incorporating video technique guides into their educational curricula.

abstract.label: LEVEL OF EVIDENCE
abstract.text: Level II, Therapeutic Study.

articles.title: An original closed reduction technique for acute shoulder dislocation: The FEAT method.
articles.journal_full: The American journal of emergency medicine

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: The objective of this study was to introduce a novel closed reduction technique, termed the FEAT (Fixation, External rotation, Alignment, Traction) method, for anterior shoulder dislocations and to evaluate its effectiveness, speed, reliability, and safety.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This prospective study enrolled 30 patients presenting with anterior glenohumeral dislocation at the Emergency or Orthopedics outpatient department of Hubei Provincial Hospital. Closed reduction was performed using the FEAT method without administering analgesics, muscle relaxants, or anesthetics. Only a single reduction attempt was permitted per patient. The time required for successful reduction was recorded, and patient-reported pain intensity during the procedure was assessed using a visual analog scale (VAS) ranging from 0 to 10.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: All 30 patients experienced successful reduction on the first attempt. The average time required for successful reduction was 54.3 s, with a mean VAS pain score of 3.67 during the procedure.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The FEAT method is an effective, rapid, and minimally painful technique for anterior shoulder dislocation reduction. Its simplicity and ease of mastery support its widespread clinical adoption.

articles.title: Ischemic severity rather than ischemic time is associated with major limb complications in traumatic popliteal artery injury: A retrospective case series.

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: Although prolonged ischemic time is considered a key determinant of limb loss in traumatic popliteal artery injury (PAI), it does not fully explain the variability in clinical outcomes. This study aimed to evaluate whether ischemic severity at presentation is associated with major limb complications in PAI.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We retrospectively reviewed patients with blunt PAI treated at a single trauma center between 2013 and 2025. Ischemic severity was assessed using the Rutherford classification and the presence of collateral circulation on computed tomography angiography (CTA). Patients were categorized into mild ischemia (Rutherford grade I-II) and severe ischemia (Rutherford grade III). Outcomes included extensive soft tissue defects requiring reconstruction and amputation.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Twenty-one limbs were included. Thirteen limbs were classified as mild ischemia and eight as severe ischemia. Collateral circulation was preserved in 17 limbs and absent in 4 limbs. The time to arterial reconstruction was comparable between groups. No major soft tissue complications occurred in the mild ischemia group. In contrast, 5 of 8 limbs with Rutherford grade III developed extensive soft tissue defects (p = 0.006). Absence of collateral circulation was also strongly associated with adverse outcomes, with all limbs without collateral flow developing major soft tissue complications (p = 0.002), despite a shorter time to revascularization.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Ischemic severity at presentation, particularly Rutherford grade III and absence of collateral circulation on CTA, is associated with major limb complications in traumatic PAI, whereas ischemic time alone may be insufficient to predict outcomes.

articles.title: Opportunistic assessment of bone quality using CT-derived hounsfield units in postmenopausal women with femoral trochanteric fractures.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: CT-derived Hounsfield unit (HU) measurements may provide an opportunistic assessment of bone density when dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) is difficult to obtain during acute treatment of femoral trochanteric fractures. We compared three femoral-head regions of interest (ROIs) and explored their ability to identify markedly low total hip bone mineral density (BMD).

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This single-center retrospective study included 87 women aged ≥ 65 years with AO/OTA type 31A1 (excluding A1.1) or 31A2 femoral trochanteric fractures treated with intramedullary nailing. Admission CT HU values were measured in three femoral-head ROIs on coronal and axial images and compared with contralateral hip DXA T-scores measured approximately 1 week after surgery. Pearson correlations and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analyses were performed. The prespecified total hip T-score thresholds were ≤ -2.5 and ≤ -3.3; the latter was used as an operational definition of markedly low BMD in this study.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Coronal whole-femoral-head HU values (ROI 1) showed a moderate correlation with total hip T-scores (r = 0.569). For the ≤ -2.5 threshold, 74 women met the criterion and only 13 did not; the ROI 1 coronal AUC was 0.841. For the ≤ -3.3 threshold, 51 women met the criterion and 36 did not. A coronal ROI 1 threshold of < 158.7 HU had an AUC of 0.765 (95% CI, 0.660-0.870), sensitivity of 84.3% (43/51), and specificity of 66.7% (24/36) for identifying a total hip T-score ≤ -3.3.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Whole-femoral-head HU values were moderately associated with DXA-derived T-scores in this cohort. Admission CT may help flag patients with markedly low BMD, but the threshold showed limited specificity and requires external validation. Its effect on surgical decisions or clinical outcomes was not assessed.

articles.title: Thoracic irrigation in managing traumatic hemothorax: A concise review of techniques and practice variations.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Retained hemothorax following tube thoracostomy occurs in up to one-third of thoracic trauma patients, often necessitating additional interventions. Thoracic irrigation has emerged as a potential adjunct to improve pleural drainage. The objective of this concise review is to evaluate the role of thoracic irrigation in the management of traumatic hemothorax by highlighting current standards of care and variations in techniques.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This review searched five search engines, screening studies published before September 26, 2025. Studies focusing on thoracic irrigation in the setting of trauma and hemothorax were included.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of six studies were included. Thoracic irrigation in the management of traumatic hemothorax showed significantly lower odds of secondary intervention (OR: 0.16, p < 0.001) and shorter hospital length of stay (7 days vs. 9, p = 0.04) in patients who received thoracic irrigation compared with standard chest tube drainage. Most patients underwent irrigation using medium to large-bore tubes, although one study showed no association between tube size and outcomes. Patients receiving ≥ 1000 milliliters (mL) of irrigation had more hospital-free days compared to those receiving < 1000 mL (p = 0.007), while another study found no significant differences.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Thoracic irrigation shows promise as an adjunct to tube thoracostomy in managing post-traumatic hemothorax, with evidence of reduced retained collections, fewer secondary interventions, and shorter hospital stays. Studies are needed to achieve standardized thoracic irrigation techniques and develop more comprehensive and consistent evidence-based guidelines.

articles.title: Do radiographic surrogates of pre-bend appropriateness influence outcomes after titanium elastic nailing in pediatric femoral mid-shaft fractures?

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: To investigate whether radiographic technical parameters reflecting pre-bend appropriateness are associated with radiographic and clinical outcomes after titanium elastic nailing (TEN) in pediatric femoral mid-shaft fractures.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective cohort included 85 children aged 5-11 years treated with TEN between 2015 and 2025. Constructs were classified as criteria-met (n = 38) or criteria-unmet (n = 47) using nail symmetry, a bend apex-fracture apex distance ratio ≤ 10%, and a metaphyseal spread ratio ≥ 50%. Separate exploratory multivariable models evaluated the composite classification and its components, adjusting for clinical and technical covariates.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Median coronal angulation was lower in the criteria-met group (2.0° vs 5.0°; p = 0.005). The adjusted mean difference (criteria-unmet minus criteria-met) was 3.42° (95% CI 0.98-5.87; p = 0.007). Other group comparisons were inconclusive. Exploratory component analysis associated greater spread with greater limb length discrepancy (3.61 mm per increase of 10 %age points; 95% CI 1.81-5.40; q = 0.002), although technical parameters were highly correlated. The complication risk ratio for criteria-unmet versus criteria-met constructs was 1.41 (95% CI 0.45-4.48).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Meeting the study-specific radiographic criteria was associated with lower coronal angulation, but its clinical importance remains uncertain. Overlapping criteria, correlated technical parameters, and limited precision preclude conclusions of equivalence or definitive independent effects.

articles.title: Scapular fracture and risk of great vessel injury in geriatric blunt trauma: A TQIP analysis.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Scapular fractures are markers of high-energy blunt thoracic trauma and may indicate severe intrathoracic injury. Despite the substantial mortality linked with great vessel injuries (GVI), data specifically examining scapular fracture and GVI in the geriatric population remain limited. We hypothesized that scapular fracture, particularly when accompanied by concomitant thoracic fractures, is independently associated with GVI in geriatrics with blunt trauma.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the American College of Surgeons Trauma Quality Improvement Program (ACS-TQIP) database (2017-2023). Patients aged ≥ 65 years with a blunt mechanism of injury and AIS severity 2-5 in the neck, thorax, or upper extremity were included. GVI was defined using specific AIS codes for major thoracic and cervical vessels. Multivariable logistic regression evaluated association between scapular fracture patterns and GVI, including isolated scapular fractures, those with concomitant sternal, rib or flail chest fractures. Models adjusted for age, sex, race, mechanism, ISS, shock index, and modified frailty index. Vessel-specific analyses were also performed. Primary outcome was GVI. Secondary outcomes were mortality and LOS.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 677,134 patients were included. Median age was 76 [70-82] years; 54.1% were female. Scapular fractures were identified in 5.0% of patients and GVI in 0.7%. In multivariable regression, isolated scapular fracture was associated with lower odds of GVI (aOR 0.783, 95% CI 0.704-0.871, p < 0.001), while scapular fracture with sternal fracture was associated with significantly higher odds (aOR 1.423, 95% CI 1.122-1.806, p = 0.004). Among vessel-specific analyses, subclavian artery injury demonstrated the highest association with scapular fracture (aOR 1.527, 95% CI 1.113-2.094, p = 0.009). GVI was associated with markedly higher in-hospital mortality (25.1% vs. 4.2%; OR 7.726, 95% CI 7.234-8.251, p < 0.001).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: In geriatric blunt trauma, isolated scapular fracture is not an independent predictor of GVI. After a fall, a scapular fracture without a sternal fracture does not by itself suggest a missed vascular injury. In contrast, combined scapular and sternal fractures represent a high-risk pattern that warrants a heightened index of suspicion and a low threshold for CT angiography, with particular attention to the subclavian vessels.

abstract.label: LEVEL OF EVIDENCE
abstract.text: Prognostic/Epidemiologic; Level III.

articles.title: Orthopedic trauma in patients with opioid use disorder: Current concepts in perioperative management.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Opioid use disorder (OUD) is an important challenge in orthopedic trauma, where acute injury intersects with preexisting opioid exposure, tolerance, complex pain, and barriers to continuity of addiction treatment. OUD has been associated with higher rates of complications, readmission, and treatment disruption, yet OUD-specific perioperative management remains inconsistently incorporated into orthopedic trauma practice. This review synthesizes the epidemiology, outcomes, and perioperative management evidence for this population.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A clinically oriented current concepts review synthesized peer-reviewed literature, prioritizing studies published from 2013 onward. PubMed and Embase were searched, supplemented by Google Scholar, Semantic Scholar, and manual review of reference lists from relevant articles. Studies examining perioperative outcomes, multimodal analgesia, and management of medications for OUD (MOUD) relevant to orthopedic trauma were included; studies limited to pediatric, elderly, or prenatal populations were excluded.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Preinjury opioid exposure is common among orthopedic trauma patients, whereas formally diagnosed OUD is less prevalent, affecting approximately 1% of operative trauma patients and up to 2.3% of patients with open lower-extremity fractures. OUD and opioid-related disorders are associated with higher rates of infection, nonunion, revision, prolonged hospitalization, and readmission. Consensus guidance and observational evidence support continuation of evidence-based MOUD, individualized opioid supplementation, multimodal nonopioid analgesia, regional anesthesia when appropriate, and early coordination with addiction and acute pain services. Guideline-based approaches to postoperative opioid prescribing, tapering, and patient education are also summarized.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Orthopedic trauma patients with OUD require individualized, multidisciplinary perioperative care. The strongest available evidence supports preservation of OUD treatment, multimodal analgesia, early addiction and pain consultation, and coordinated discharge planning rather than either opioid avoidance or opioid-only treatment. The review concludes with the authors' recommendations for the operating surgeon, including in-hospital and outpatient tapering plans, management of requests for additional opioids, and patient education.

articles.title: The downside of the pull-up: A 10-year national analysis of emergency department visits, 2015-2024.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: To characterize the epidemiology and clinical patterns of injuries related to pull-up and chin-up bars in a nationally representative emergency department (ED) dataset.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Retrospective cross-sectional analysis of the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission National Electronic Injury Surveillance System from January 1, 2015, to December 31, 2024. Cases were identified using product code 3277 with narrative filters for "pull-up," "chin-up," and "doorway bar," excluding barbells and playground equipment. NEISS sampling weights produced national estimates. Annual totals with 95 % confidence intervals were calculated and reported. Injury characteristics were summarized by age group, body region, diagnosis, location, disposition, and a narrative-derived mechanism category (fall, struck by bar, slip or detachment, other).

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: An estimated 40,987 ED visits were attributed to pull-up bar injuries, averaging about 4000 per year, with a peak in 2024 (5421; 95 % CI, 5315-5527). Patients were predominantly male (66.1 %) with a bimodal age distribution centered on children 5-14 years and adults 18-34 years. Craniofacial trauma predominated, with head and face together comprising nearly one-half of presentations, followed by upper-extremity involvement, including shoulder, wrist, and forearm. Laceration, internal head injury, and fracture were the leading diagnoses, with sprain or strain and contusion also frequent. Most incidents occurred in the home, and 93.8 % of patients were treated and released. Falls were the most common mechanism, followed by struck-by events and a subset explicitly involving bar slip or detachment.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Pull-up bar injuries constitute a consistent national burden of craniofacial and upper-extremity trauma concentrated in youth and young adults, largely managed nonoperatively in acute care settings. Improved recognition of exercise-associated injury mechanisms may assist diagnostic accuracy and reduce the burden on emergency and orthopedic services.

articles.title: How the cause of surgical delay affects mortality in fragility hip fractures: A cohort study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Prompt surgery for fragility hip fractures is a cornerstone of care and a key metric within the Best Practice Tariff (BPT) in the United Kingdom. Yet, since 2011, time to theatre has steadily increased, BPT adherence has fallen, and paradoxically, mortality has reduced. It is still unclear if surgical delay is an independent predictor of mortality. Emerging evidence suggests that the causes of surgical delays may be more important determinants of mortality than the delay itself.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A cohort study of 1769 hip fracture patients above the age of 60 was conducted in a single centre in England. This study collected demographic data, timing to theatre (<36 h vs ≥36 h), reasons for any delays, 30-day mortality and 1-year mortality between March 2020 and December 2024.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The most common cause of delay was insufficient theatre capacity (N = 365, 20.6%), followed by delays awaiting medical stabilisation (N = 102, 5.8%). Age (Χ2 71.638 p < 0.001), ASA grade (Χ2 37.045 p < 0.001), sex (Χ2 27.721 p < 0.001), pre-admission residence (Χ2 36.772 p < 0.001), and reason for delay (Χ2 27.495 p = 0.007) were significant predictors of mortality. Delays due solely because of theatre unavailability did not increase 30-day (OR 0.784 p = 0.398) or 1-year mortality (OR 1.123 p = 0.474). In contrast, delays due to medical optimisation were associated with markedly higher 30-day (OR 3.573, p < 0.001) and 1-year mortality (OR 2.144, p = 0.005).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: While early surgery remains beneficial, patients delayed solely due to administrative reasons did not demonstrate an associated increase in mortality. Mortality associated with operative delay was primarily associated amongst patients with concurrent acute illnesses and co-morbidities, independently increasing risk. To improve mortality, the focus must remain on pre-operative optimisation and robust orthogeriatric assessment, rather than surgical timing alone. Future iterations of the BPT may benefit from incorporating the cause of delay and physiological risk stratification to surgical timing targets to better align national incentives with clinical outcomes.

articles.title: An Audit on the Management of Adult Patients With Renal Colic Presenting to the Emergency Department.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Renal colic is a common emergency department presentation requiring timely assessment, appropriate analgesia, and investigation. This clinical audit evaluated adherence to predefined standards for pain assessment, timely analgesia, investigations, imaging, and medication selection, and assessed changes in practice following a structured implementation phase.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A retrospective, single-center, two-cycle clinical audit was conducted in an adult emergency department. The primary audit included 100 patients presenting between December 2020 and December 2024, and the re-audit included 100 patients presenting between March and September 2025, giving a total sample of 200 patients. Nine audit criteria were derived from the Royal College of Emergency Medicine (RCEM) and the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) guidance. Following the primary audit, departmental education, audit feedback, an educational infographic, and a standardized renal colic analgesia pathway were implemented. Categorical outcomes were reported as frequencies and percentages and compared between audit cycles using two-sided Chi-square or Fisher exact tests, as appropriate.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: First-line nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) administration increased from 39/100 patients (39.0%) in the primary audit to 60/100 patients (60.0%) in the re-audit, representing an absolute increase of 21.0 percentage points (95% CI: 7.5-34.5). This difference was statistically significant (χ²(1, N = 200) = 8.00; p = 0.005). Avoidance of first-line opioid administration increased from 89/100 patients (89.0%) to 94/100 patients (94.0%); however, this difference was not statistically significant (χ²(1, N = 200) = 1.03; p = 0.310). Pain-score documentation, timely analgesia, urine dipstick testing, laboratory investigations, computed tomography (CT) imaging, and avoidance of antispasmodic medication remained broadly consistent between the two audit cycles.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Following implementation of a standardized renal colic pathway, departmental education, an educational infographic, and audit feedback, first-line NSAID use increased significantly and first-line opioid use decreased. Other key measures of assessment, investigation, and analgesic care remained generally stable between audit cycles. These findings support the value of a structured departmental approach to promoting guideline-concordant analgesic prescribing and provide a basis for continued quality-improvement activity and future re-audit.
