articles.title: Associations between the development of severe acute pancreatitis and the risk scores on admission and inflammatory biomarkers in older patients: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.journal_full: Sao Paulo medical journal = Revista paulista de medicina

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Acute pancreatitis is an important cause of morbidity and mortality among patients presenting to the emergency department with abdominal pain.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: In this study, we aimed to compare the diagnostic performance of the Bedside Index for Severity in Acute Pancreatitis (BISAP) and Emergency Department SpO2, Age, and Systemic Inflammatory Response Syndrome (ED-SAS) score for predicting severe acute pancreatitis (SAP) in older patients diagnosed with acute pancreatitis in the emergency department. The predictive performances of inflammatory markers, including the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), systemic inflammation response index (SIRI), and pan-immune-inflammation value, were also evaluated.

abstract.label: DESIGN AND SETTING
abstract.text: This retrospective cohort study was conducted at a tertiary hospital in Türkiye.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Factors associated with SAP were evaluated using univariate and multivariate binary logistic regression analyses; odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals were calculated.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The study included 400 older patients with acute pancreatitis (SAP group, n = 80; non-SAP group, n = 320). The neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, SII, SIRI, pan-immune-inflammation value, ED-SAS score, and BISAP showed good discrimination for SAP, yielding area under the receiver operating characteristic curve values of 0.82, 0.83, 0.85, 0.86, 0.81, and 0.82, respectively. In the multivariate analysis, an SII of > 5796.25 (odds ratio, 13.59), SIRI of > 11.79 (odds ratio, 7.57), ED-SAS score of > 1 (odds ratio, 5.41), and BISAP of > 1 (odds ratio, 2.91) remained independently associated with SAP.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The SII, SIRI, ED-SAS score, and BISAP may support early risk stratification for SAP in geriatric pancreatitis. These parameters should be interpreted alongside clinical assessment rather than used as stand-alone diagnostic criteria.

articles.title: A modified Rapid Emergency Medicine Score incorporating C-reactive protein for mortality prediction in septic shock.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: The aim of this study was to evaluate the prognostic performance of the Rapid Emergency Medicine Score incorporating C-reactive protein for predicting 30-day mortality in patients with septic shock and to compare its performance with the Rapid Emergency Medicine Score, National Early Warning Score, Modified Early Warning Score, quick Sequential Organ Failure Assessment, and Sequential Organ Failure Assessment.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective observational study included 124 adult patients diagnosed with septic shock in a tertiary emergency department. Rapid Emergency Medicine Score incorporating C-reactive protein was calculated as Rapid Emergency Medicine Score +(C-reactive protein /50), using an a priori clinically determined C-reactive protein scaling factor.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The median age was 63 years, 52.4% of patients were female, and 76 patients (61.3%) died within 30 days. Rapid Emergency Medicine Score incorporating C-reactive protein had the highest numerical AUC (0.770), corresponding to moderate discrimination, followed by National Early Warning Score (0.755), Modified Early Warning Score (0.746), quick Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (0.688), Rapid Emergency Medicine Score (0.638), and Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (0.593). Rapid Emergency Medicine Score incorporating C-reactive protein had significantly higher AUCs than Rapid Emergency Medicine Score (ΔAUC=0.132, p<0.001) and Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (ΔAUC=0.177, p=0.049), whereas differences compared with National Early Warning Score, Modified Early Warning Score, and quick Sequential Organ Failure Assessment were not statistically significant. In the Firth-penalized logistic regression model, Rapid Emergency Medicine Score incorporating C-reactive protein remained associated with 30-day mortality (OR per 1-point increase, 1.22; 95%CI 1.11-1.36; p<0.001).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Rapid Emergency Medicine Score incorporating C-reactive protein showed moderate discrimination for 30-day mortality in this exploratory development cohort but did not demonstrate superior discrimination compared with National Early Warning Score, Modified Early Warning Score, or quick Sequential Organ Failure Assessment. Because Rapid Emergency Medicine Score incorporating C-reactive protein was developed and evaluated in the same cohort, these findings should be considered hypothesis-generating. Independent external validation is required before its clinical utility can be established.

articles.title: Potentially avoidable computed tomography after positive ultrasonography in appendicitis.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: The aim of this study was to determine the frequency of computed tomography performed despite a positive ultrasonography in histopathologically confirmed appendicitis (potentially avoidable computed tomography), and to assess its effects on radiation exposure, cost, and emergency department length of stay.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This single-center retrospective cohort study included 887 consecutive patients who underwent appendectomy for suspected appendicitis (January 2023-December 2025). Potentially avoidable computed tomography was defined as computed tomography following a positive ultrasonography result. As length of stay was non-normal, imaging strategies were compared using the Kruskal-Wallis test, and length of stay predictors were modeled using median (quantile) regression, with a log-link gamma generalized linear model as a sensitivity analysis. Imaging cost used national tariffs; radiation was estimated as ~8 mSv per abdominal computed tomography with age-specific BEIR VII multipliers.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Computed tomography was used in 87.6% (777/887) of cases. Of the 521 patients who underwent ultrasonography, the results were positive in 35.5%, inconclusive in 30.7%, and negative in 33.8% of cases. Potentially avoidable computed tomography was performed in 81/777 computed tomography examinations (10.4%). Notably, 43.8% (81/185) of patients with positive ultrasonography results subsequently underwent computed tomography scan, corresponding to ~648 mSv of avoidable radiation exposure and an associated cost of 26,667 TL (~US$811), with 49.4% of the affected patients being children. Length of stay did not differ across strategies (p=0.748), and computed tomography was not an independent length of stay predictor (+7.2 min; p=0.23), whereas business-hour arrival was (+15.3 min; p<0.001).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Computed tomography remained frequent even after ultrasonography established the diagnosis, with no effect on emergency department length of stay, generating avoidable radiation and costs concentrated in children. Reducing computed tomography after a positive ultrasonography is a feasible opportunity to improve resource utilization while preserving patient safety.

articles.title: Hyperbaric oxygen therapy for cervical spinal cord injury.

abstract.text: Hyperbaric oxygen therapy (HBOT) has been proposed as an adjunctive treatment for spinal cord injury (SCI). This case report is about a male in his early 50s who sustained an acute cervical SCI after a bicycle accident and presented with quadriparesis, sensory deficits, and American Spinal Injury Association Impairment Scale (AIS) grade B injury before surgery. Cervical magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) demonstrated C3-4 and C4-5 disc extrusions with associated intramedullary T2 hyperintensity consistent with cord edema. The patient underwent C3-6 anterior cervical discectomy and fusion one day after injury. HBOT was initiated approximately one week after surgery at 2.0 atmospheres absolute for 60-minute sessions, with treatment frequency varying over time. He completed 348 HBOT sessions across two treatment periods and also underwent rehabilitation and neuromuscular electrical stimulation. During follow-up, the patient demonstrated progressive recovery of ambulation and his AIS grade improved to grade D. Follow-up cervical MRI obtained during the course of HBOT demonstrated interval reduction in intramedullary T2 signal abnormality. Although the effect of HBOT on a spinal cord injury cannot be determined by a single case report, the observed clinical and radiological improvements support further investigation of its potential role as an adjunctive therapy within a multimodal treatment approach for acute cervical SCI.

articles.title: One-year mortality following emergency department visits for stimulant toxicity.
articles.journal_full: The American journal of emergency medicine

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: Rising stimulant-related overdose deaths and emergency department (ED) utilization highlight the need to better characterize outcomes following ED encounters for stimulant toxicity. We sought to determine one-year mortality after ED discharge for stimulant toxicity and to characterize the causes of death.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective cohort study used a linked statewide database of ED and hospital discharge records and death records. Patients discharged from the ED with a primary diagnosis of stimulant toxicity, identified by International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision (ICD-10) codes, were included. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality within one year of ED discharge, estimated using Kaplan-Meier analysis. A secondary reference analysis was performed among patients with ED visits for acute opioid toxicity to contextualize mortality estimates against a population previously associated with elevated post-discharge mortality.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 2356 patients met inclusion criteria. One-year mortality was 2.1% (95% confidence interval [CI] 1.6-2.8%). Among patients who died within one year, median age at the index visit was 35 years and median time to death was 118 days (interquartile range [IQR] 63-228 days). Overdose accounted for 67% of deaths, with opioids implicated in 54% and combined opioid-stimulant involvement in 37%. In the secondary reference cohort of 1665 opioid-related ED visits, one-year mortality was 6.9% (95% CI 5.8-8.3%).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Patients with ED encounters for stimulant toxicity experienced substantial one-year mortality in a relatively young population. Subsequent deaths were predominantly overdose-related and frequently opioid-involved, supporting consideration of opioid-focused harm-reduction interventions in this population.

articles.title: Disparities in investigation of physical abuse among trauma patients.
articles.journal_full: The American journal of emergency medicine

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Physical abuse is a significant public health issue in the United States, leading to poor health outcomes such as chronic illness, depression, and substance abuse. Research regarding how the medical system addresses physical abuse in the overall adult population is scarce. The objective of this study was to assess disparities in investigation of physical abuse among adult trauma patients.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This is a retrospective analysis of the 2017-2019 American College of Surgeons-Trauma Quality Program database. This study included all adult patients (≥18 years) who had a report of physical abuse by the medical team to authorities. Chi square and multivariate analysis were applied where appropriate to assess which characteristics showed disparities in investigation rate.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: On univariate analysis, there were disparities with regard to age, mechanism, race, ethnicity, payment method, and mental health or substance use disorder. On multivariate analysis, male sex, non-penetrating trauma, age ≥70, American Indian race, and presence of a mental health disorder were associated with decreased odds of investigation. Non-elderly adult patients made up a disproportionate amount of abuse victims.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: This study shows significant disparities in the escalation of a physical abuse report to an official investigation in the trauma setting. The authors recommend increased advocacy and resource allocation for these vulnerable populations in the clinical setting as well as further research regarding to what extent patient choice versus discretion of authorities influences these disparities. The authors also recommend a larger research focus on non-elderly adult victims of abuse.

articles.title: Smart Emergency Assistance System With Pre-Entry Access for Older Adults Living Alone: Simulation-Based Implementation Report.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Older adults living alone are at increased risk during medical emergencies, particularly due to delayed detection, information transmission, and physical access to the home. Digital health and Internet of Things (IoT)-based technologies offer opportunities to strengthen emergency response systems; however, evidence on the real-world implementation and performance of integrated home-based emergency assistance platforms remains limited.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: This study aims to describe the deployment and performance of a smart emergency assistance system for older adults living alone, and to evaluate key implementation outputs and performance indicators in a simulated environment.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We implemented an emergency assistance system integrating the IoT, 5G technology, and mobile internet. An intelligent distress button served as the core user-facing device, while a hospital-based rescue management platform functioned as the central coordination hub. The implementation strategy focused on rapid signal transmission, automated multichannel notification, and precise location tracking to support home-based emergency response. System performance was assessed using predefined key performance indicators, including response time, notification success, positioning accuracy, and operational efficiency.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: When the intelligent distress button was pressed continuously for at least 3 seconds, distress signals were transmitted to the hospital rescue management platform within 5 seconds. Notifications were automatically sent to the emergency medical services (EMS) and family contacts via SMS, with confirmation feedback completed within 10 seconds. The platform detected the GPS location of the person in distress with an error of less than 10 meters. Upon arrival of rescue personnel at the scene, system-enabled door unlocking was completed within 1 minute. The system demonstrated low hardware cost and low power consumption, with a distress trigger success rate of 97.78% (44/45) in simulated testing and 100% antimisoperation effectiveness.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: This implementation demonstrates the feasibility and scalability of a smart emergency assistance system for older adults living alone. By integrating emergency alerting, access control, and hospital-side coordination, the system supports rapid and efficient home-based emergency response and shows potential for scalable deployment in aging communities. However, several barriers to large-scale implementation remain, including incomplete integration with formal emergency dispatch systems, unvalidated hardware durability, and a lack of real-world user testing. Addressing these issues in future pilot deployments will be essential to transitioning from technical feasibility to operational readiness.

articles.title: The blunt truth: The role of marijuana in PTSD after intentional traumatic injury.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Survivors of interpersonal violence experience high rates of post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), and rates of marijuana use are rising among young adults. There is however, limited understanding of marijuana use patterns among survivors of interpersonal violence with PTSD. We evaluated relationships between PTSD and marijuana use following injury and hypothesized that PTSD-positive patients would report elevated follow-up marijuana use.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Between 10/2019 and 7/1/2024, we prospectively collected data on patient demographics, PTSD, substance use (including marijuana), and PROMIS-29 quality of life domains for adult trauma patients admitted to an urban, academic, level-1 trauma center. Participants were screened at baseline and at 6- or 12-month follow-up. Injury characteristics were collected from the institutional trauma registry. Among the intentionally injured, we compared patients by follow-up PTSD screening results. We excluded patients who screened positive for PTSD at baseline. Using multivariable logistic regression we assessed relationships between follow-up PTSD and marijuana use, including demographic and injury characteristics as covariates. Our primary outcome was dichotomized follow-up marijuana use.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 105 participants injured by intentional trauma with complete follow-up data, 69 screened negative for PTSD at baseline and therefore were included in this analysis. Patients who screened positive for PTSD at follow-up had greater marijuana use at baseline (29% vs 3%, p = 0.002) and follow-up (42% vs 13%, p = 0.007), and worse PROMIS-29 scores in all domains (p ≤ 0.01), compared to PTSD-negative patients. In multivariable analysis, screening positive for PTSD was associated with 7.1 times greater odds of marijuana use at follow-up (p = 0.007, CI:1.7, 29.5).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: PTSD and marijuana use were closely associated in survivors of interpersonal violence. Screening efforts should account for marijuana use specifically. Routine screening for marijuana use could improve recognition of psychological challenges after trauma and could help identify patients at risk for development of PTSD.

abstract.label: LEVEL OF EVIDENCE
abstract.text: Level III, prognostic/epidemiological.

articles.title: Communication practices and challenges of healthcare providers in febrile seizure counseling: A cross-sectional study.

abstract.text: Febrile seizures (FS) frighten parents, but few studies have examined how healthcare providers counsel families. We described providers' FS communication practices, confidence, challenges, and resource needs, and how these varied with provider characteristics. In this cross-sectional survey, 150 healthcare providers (81 pediatricians, 46 nurses, 14 general practitioners, and 9 emergency physicians) at 5 facilities in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia, completed a questionnaire. Descriptive statistics used 95% confidence intervals (CIs), chi-square and Kruskal-Wallis tests, and Firth, logistic, and ordinal logistic regression. Most providers used communication guidelines (85.3%) and verbal explanation (92.0%); other teaching methods were each used by <12.0%. After adjustment, >10 years of experience was associated with guideline use (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 6.97, 95% CI 2.08-30.08) and higher confidence (aOR 4.20, 95% CI 2.08-8.52), and >5 FS cases/month with guideline use (aOR 4.04, 95% CI 1.54-11.46). Pediatricians reported higher confidence than other professions (aOR 2.40, 95% CI 1.27-4.54). Providers in pediatric hospitals more often had formal communication training (aOR 2.44, 95% CI 1.17-5.08), and those in private clinics/hospitals counseled longer (aOR 3.81, 95% CI 1.35-10.79). The most frequent challenges were misinformation (43.3%), cultural beliefs (42.7%), and strong parental emotions (39.3%). Providers most often asked for better educational materials (53.3%) and standardized guidelines (52.0%). FS counseling relied mainly on verbal explanation. Experience and FS exposure were associated with guideline use, profession and experience with confidence, and workplace with training and counseling time. Whether standardized guidelines and better materials improve parents' understanding or anxiety needs testing in studies of parent outcomes.

articles.title: A qualitative assessment of learner experiences with a novel Paediatric Emergency Medicine curriculum in Kenya.
articles.journal_full: African journal of emergency medicine : Revue africaine de la medecine d'urgence

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Paediatric emergency and critical care (PECC) services are essential in reducing childhood mortality from treatable conditions, particularly in sub-Saharan Africa where the burden remains high. Despite this need, access to subspecialty training in PECC has been limited in the region. Launched in 2019 at the University of Nairobi, the PECC-Kenya fellowship is a novel subspecialty training program for regional paediatricians in both paediatric emergency medicine (PEM) and critical care. Curricular elements for PEM within the fellowship were adapted from international guidelines for local context. The objective of this study was to explore the perspectives of current fellows and recent graduates on the content of the PEM portion of their curriculum to inform improvements and future development for the program and the region.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Semi-structured interviews were conducted with current and former PECC-Kenya fellows. Program faculty developed an interview guide which included questions about perceptions on PEM, anticipated future practice, and strengths and opportunities within the curriculum. Interviews were conducted and recorded via Zoom by a non-faculty interviewer. Anonymized transcriptions were uploaded into Dedoose. After establishing inter-rater reliability, three reviewers coded the data, and key themes were identified.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Ten interviews were conducted in 2022 and 2023, revealing several themes. Fellows anticipated providing continuous care from the emergency department to the intensive care unit as the sole PECC specialist in their institution or region. They highlighted program strengths including high-quality live online lectures, in-person PEM intensive training, diverse clinical exposure, and establishment of a peer network. Fellows expressed a desire for more hands-on training and recognized the importance of point-of-care ultrasound in facilitating rapid diagnosis and assisting in procedures, with need for additional training.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: Given the innovative nature of this training program and its distinctive demands, these themes and findings could serve as valuable guidance for similar initiatives emerging in the region.

articles.title: Vagal maneuvers and pharmacological cardioversion in stable PSVT: A systematic review with implications for emergency nursing practice.

abstract.text: Paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardia (PSVT) is a common arrhythmic emergency for which vagal maneuvers offer a non-pharmacological route to cardioversion before drug escalation. This systematic review compared the effectiveness and safety of vagal maneuvers-particularly the standard and modified Valsalva maneuvers-against pharmacological cardioversion in adults with stable PSVT. Following PRISMA 2020 guidance, eleven studies published between 2014 and 2024 were identified across six databases and synthesized narratively owing to clinical and methodological heterogeneity. The modified Valsalva maneuver consistently achieved higher cardioversion rates than the standard technique and carotid sinus massage, with a favorable safety profile, while adenosine remained effective but more frequently associated with recurrence and discomfort. Effectiveness varied by age, arrhythmia subtype, and care setting. Collectively, the evidence supports the modified Valsalva maneuver as a safe, low-cost, first-line option before pharmacological escalation, with particular relevance to nurse-led management in emergency and prehospital care.

articles.title: Remimazolam for Procedural Sedation During Synchronized Electrical Cardioversion in the Emergency Department.
articles.journal: J Am Coll Emerg Physicians Open
articles.journal_full: Journal of the American College of Emergency Physicians open

abstract.text: Synchronized electrical cardioversion necessitates procedural sedation to ensure patient comfort and amnesia. Remimazolam is a novel, ultrashort-acting intravenous benzodiazepine with organ-independent esterase metabolism, a favorable safety profile, and flumazenil reversibility. Although, previously described in the electrophysiology laboratory, use of remimazolam has not been reported for electrical cardioversion in the emergency department. In this case, a 67-year-old man with sudden-onset paroxysmal atrial fibrillation presented in symptomatic atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response. Following rate and rhythm optimization, the decision was made to proceed with synchronized electrical cardioversion under procedural sedation. After consent was obtained, remimazolam (5 mg intravenously) was administered as a single bolus. Sedation onset occurred at 49 seconds, with adequate depth achieved at 1 minute 37 seconds. A single synchronized biphasic 200 joule electric shock was successfully delivered at 2 minutes 20 seconds, converting the patient to normal sinus rhythm. Eye opening occurred at 3 minutes 50 seconds, with return to baseline orientation at 4 minutes 30 seconds. No apnea, hypoxia, hemodynamic instability, or procedural recall was observed. Continuous end-tidal carbon dioxide monitoring confirmed uninterrupted spontaneous ventilation throughout. The rapid onset, hemodynamic stability, and remarkably brief recovery time observed support its potential as a first-line sedative for emergency department cardioversion. Further prospective study in this setting is warranted.

articles.title: WHO Basic Emergency Care (BEC) training in Liberia: pre-course, post-course, and one-year outcomes.
articles.journal_full: African journal of emergency medicine : Revue africaine de la medecine d'urgence

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Liberia faces persistent gaps in emergency care training. The World Health Organization (WHO) Basic Emergency Care (BEC) Course was developed in 2018 to support training of frontline emergency care providers in resource-limited settings. While prior studies have shown short-term knowledge gains and confidence improvements, limited data exists regarding longer-term retention. This study sought to evaluate knowledge acquisition, knowledge retention, and self-reported confidence immediately after and one year following WHO Basic Emergency Care training.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted two four-day WHO BEC trainings for graduating medical students and practicing providers at A.M. Dogliotti School of Medicine in Monrovia, Liberia. Participants completed knowledge tests, self-assessment surveys, and course evaluations before training, immediately after training, and at one-year follow-up. Paired pre/post comparisons were analyzed using Wilcoxon signed-rank tests, and cohort comparisons for post-course practical case scenarios and course evaluations used Fisher's exact test and unpaired t-tests, respectively.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Some 40 participants completed training, including 30 medical students, nine nurses, and one general practitioner. 33 of 40 participants (82.5%) completed the one-year follow-up assessment. Median knowledge scores increased from 76% pre-course to 96% immediately post-course and remained higher than baseline at one year (88%; all p < 0.0001). Self-reported confidence also improved substantially, including comfort managing emergency patients and preparedness to see emergency care patients, with gains sustained at one year. Improvements were observed across key emergency care domains, including shock, airway management, pediatric and adult emergencies, and emergency pharmacology. Course evaluations were highly positive across all domains, with mean ratings ranging from 3.8 to 5.0 out of 5.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: WHO BEC training was associated with substantial improvements in emergency care knowledge and confidence among Liberian providers, with evidence of knowledge retention at one year. These findings support implementation of WHO BEC training as a sustainable strategy to strengthen emergency care capacity in resource-limited African settings.

articles.title: The Efficacy of a Home Monitoring App for Children With Medical Complexity: Protocol for a Randomized Controlled Trial.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Children with medical complexity (CMC) experience frequent acute health deteriorations, leading to recurrent hospitalizations. Home monitoring has been suggested to help reduce hospitalizations among CMC, yet the benefits have not been demonstrated. MyChildCMC is a novel app, co-designed with parents, that supports CMC home monitoring to identify early warning signs of acute health changes to promote timely intervention.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: This study aims to assess the efficacy of the MyChildCMC intervention on child and parent outcomes and the sustainability of MyChildCMC use by parents and of the intervention's effects.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This is a 12-month, 2-arm randomized controlled trial recruiting 360 CMC (aged 1-18 years) and their parents: 180 child-parent dyads assigned to the MyChildCMC app and 180 to the control arm. Participants randomized to the MyChildCMC arm use a sensor and digital thermometer to record vital signs (temperature, heart rate, respiratory rate, and oxygen saturation) and symptoms (pain, feeding/fluid intake, mental status, and seizures) in the app daily and receive immediate feedback. Parents receive alerts for early signs of their child's health deterioration and can view summary reports and individual graphs about the child's health status in the app. Alerts are also sent to the care team, who can view, via a web-based dashboard, summary reports and individual graphs to support timely care. Participants randomized to the control arm use the sensor/thermometer to record the same clinical parameters daily in a diary. Both arms receive financial incentives for daily monitoring and for responding to surveys at baseline and at 3, 6, and 12 months. The efficacy will be assessed at 6 months. The monitoring incentive will be stopped at 6 months, but participants will continue with daily monitoring for 6 more months to assess sustainability at 12 months. The primary outcome is the number of hospital admissions among CMC. Secondary outcomes are assessed for the child (hospital days and quality of life) and the parent (stress, self-efficacy, and satisfaction with the child's care).

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: We will determine the extent to which the use (vs controls) of the MyChildCMC app leads to reduced emergency department/hospital admissions among CMC. We will also determine whether MyChildCMC use leads to improvements in secondary outcomes. Before the current full-scale study, we conducted a pilot trial, which showed promising results. However, the study was not powered to detect differences in hospital admissions. A larger, definitive study of MyChildCMC's impact was needed to confirm these results. Recruitment for the current study started on January 6, 2026, and will end by March 31, 2028. To date, 41 participants have been enrolled. We expect the last participant to complete the study by March 31, 2029, and thereafter we will analyze the data.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: The MyChildCMC app was designed to support CMC home monitoring and proactive care. If efficacious, it will serve as a new model for reducing hospital admissions, with the potential for broad dissemination.

articles.title: Rosie en Español, a Chatbot-Delivered Intervention for Spanish-Speaking, US-Based Latina Mothers: Pilot Randomized Controlled Trial.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Latina pregnant women and mothers of infants in the United States experience elevated risk for perinatal anxiety, stress, and depression alongside persistent barriers to culturally and linguistically responsive care. AI-powered digital health tools offer a potentially scalable approach to address these gaps, yet evidence on their acceptability and effectiveness for this population remains limited.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: We aimed to evaluate the feasibility, acceptability, and preliminary outcome changes of Rosie, a Spanish-language AI-powered chatbot designed with and for Latina mothers, on maternal mental health and healthcareuse outcomes.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a mixed methods pilot randomized controlled trial with 30 Spanish-speaking Latina participants who were pregnant or parenting an infant younger than 6 months. Participants were randomized 1:1 to the Rosie intervention or a comparison book club condition that provided monthly children's board books. Surveys administered at baseline and 3-month follow-up assessed depression (Patient Health Questionnaire-9), anxiety (Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7), perceived stress (Perceived Stress Scale), and health care use. Quantitative analyses examined within- and between-group changes, and qualitative feedback assessed acceptability and user experience.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Baseline mental health scores were low in both groups; however, several baseline demographic differences were observed between study arms, including age, pregnancy vs parenting status, marital status, education, and country of origin. Over 3 months, participants in the Rosie group demonstrated statistically significant within-group reductions in anxiety (mean baseline 3.27, SD 2.89; mean change -2.00, SD 2.94; P=.02) and perceived stress (mean baseline 30.00, SD 5.53; mean change -12.20, SD 12.99; P=.003). Depression scores declined modestly in both groups, with no significant between-group differences. No significant differences were observed in maternal emergency department use or adherence to well-baby visits. Engagement with Rosie was high, and qualitative feedback indicated that participants found the chatbot useful and supportive.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: This pilot study suggests that a culturally and linguistically tailored AI-powered chatbot is feasible and acceptable among Latina mothers during the perinatal period. Although anxiety and perceived stress decreased within the Rosie group, no significant between-group differences were observed. Within-group reductions in anxiety and perceived stress among Rosie participants are preliminary and should be interpreted cautiously because the trial was not powered to detect between-group effects and no statistically significant between-group differences were observed. Larger, adequately powered trials are needed to evaluate effectiveness.

articles.title: Patient Safety Culture in Hospital Settings During the COVID-19 Pandemic: Protocol for a Scoping Review.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Patient safety culture (PSC) is a foundational component of quality health care. It is characterized by health care workers' individual attitudes, team dynamics, and organizational practices that influence clinical outcomes. During the COVID-19 pandemic, hospitals worldwide faced sudden changes and crises. In this rapidly evolving environment, organizational models were revised, established procedures were challenged, and professional roles were redefined; therefore, many aspects of safety culture may have been reshaped and redefined by the pandemic. Despite a growing body of literature examining PSC during the COVID-19 era, no comprehensive synthesis has yet mapped how PSC was conceptualized, measured, operationalized, and sustained across hospital settings during the pandemic. This gap highlights the need for an integrated synthesis that captures the multiple dimensions of PSC as they were experienced and managed during the pandemic.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: This scoping review aims to map the literature on PSC in hospital settings during the COVID-19 pandemic. The specific objectives are to examine the theoretical frameworks and related constructs used to define and operationalize PSC during the pandemic; identify and categorize interventions implemented to strengthen or sustain PSC; describe monitoring activities, measurement instruments, and quality improvement approaches adopted in hospital settings; and synthesize the scope and characteristics of available evidence and identify knowledge gaps to inform future research and practice.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This scoping review will follow the methodological framework developed by Arksey and O'Malley, as updated by the JBI, and will be reported according to the PRISMA-ScR (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Extension for Scoping Reviews) guidelines. The research question was formulated using the population, concept, and context framework. Searches were conducted in the PubMed, Embase, and PsycInfo databases for records published from January 1, 2020, onward. Eligible evidence sources will include peer-reviewed empirical, interventional, measurement, review, and theoretical or conceptual publications addressing PSC or safety climate in hospital care during the COVID-19 pandemic. A total of 2 independent reviewers will conduct a 2-stage screening process, initially evaluating titles and abstracts for potential relevance, followed by a full-text assessment to determine final eligibility.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: This study commenced in April 2025 and is registered with the Open Science Framework. Database searches were completed in July 2025. Title and abstract screening commenced in July 2026. Full-text screening and data extraction are expected to be completed by September 2026, data synthesis by November 2026, and submission of the review findings in the fourth quarter of 2026.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: This scoping review will provide a structured overview of how PSC was maintained, adapted, or redefined in hospital settings during the COVID-19 pandemic. Mapping pandemic-era evidence on PSC may help hospitals translate crisis-related organizational learning into preparedness strategies, resilient safety systems, and quality improvement priorities for future public health emergencies.

articles.title: Acute Traumatic Pubic Ramus Fractures.

abstract.label: AIMS
abstract.text: Pubic rami fractures, common in the older person from low energy trauma, significantly impact morbidity through pain, reduced mobility, and increased injury risk. Effective management in the emergency department (ED) is essential for this population, but the lack of standardised guidelines can lead to inconsistent and potentially suboptimal care. This service evaluation aimed to review current management practices for isolated pubic rami fractures in our ED, identifying areas for improvement and guiding future protocol development.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We retrospectively reviewed electronic patient records. Over a twelve-month period (01/03/2023 - 29/02/2024), pelvic X-rays taken in the ED were screened for isolated pubic rami fractures, excluding duplicates and patients under 60. Cases were analysed for presentation, length of stay, management, discharge, and complications.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: From 1,135 pelvic X-rays, 42 (3.70%) patients with isolated fractures were included; 35 (83%) were female. Most injuries 37 (88.1%) resulted from falls under 2 metres. Of the patients, 29 (69%) were admitted, 11 (26%) were discharged from the ED (2 of whom were referred to the Silver Trauma outpatient clinic), and 2 (5%) were transferred directly to a rehabilitation unit. Of those admitted, 7 were subsequently transferred to rehabilitation facilities. The median ED length of stay was 12 hours 20 minutes (IQR 10:11-17:44). 4 (13.79%) of the admitted patients died.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Management was largely conservative, yet key outcomes including prolonged ED length of stay, high frailty burden and in-hospital mortality were identified. Standardised guidelines based on these findings could enhance care consistency and improve outcomes for older patients with pubic rami fractures.

articles.title: Timely Reperfusion in STEMI: A Closed-Loop Audit of Guideline Compliance and Practice Improvements.

abstract.label: AIM
abstract.text: Timely reperfusion is vital in STEMI care to reduce mortality. An initial audit showed patients transferred from emergency departments outside Dublin often exceeded the 120-minute reperfusion target. In response, Dublin Mid Leinster protocols were updated to recommend pre-transfer thrombolysis. This study evaluates the impact of these changes on reperfusion times and outcomes.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This observational study included STEMI patients admitted to St. James's Hospital from 2021-2023, compared to a prior cohort (2017-2020). The primary outcome was time from first ECG to reperfusion. Secondary outcomes included thrombolysis rates, success (TIMI 2/3 flow on angiography) and safety.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 1,301 patients, the median ECG-to-reperfusion time among patients transferred from outside Dublin fell from 124 minutes (IQR 96-166) to 113 minutes (IQR 78-151) (p<0.0001), while the proportion achieving reperfusion within 120 minutes increased from 235/507 (46.4%) to 308/530 (58.1%). Overall thrombolysis use increased from 27/1161 (2.3%) to 131/1301 (10.1%). Among thrombolysed patients, 85/131 (64.9%) achieved successful reperfusion and severe bleeding occurred in 2/131 (1.5%). Mapping demonstrated markedly lower rates of timely reperfusion at the periphery of the DML region.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: A regional protocol promoting thrombolysis substantially increased thrombolysis utilisation and improved overall timely reperfusion among STEMI patients transferred from outside Dublin. Persistent geographical disparities support further optimisation of regional pathways and consideration of prehospital thrombolysis strategies.

articles.title: Quantitative decision-support strategies to enhance emergency medical service accessibility in high-risk freeway tunnels.

abstract.text: Crashes inside road tunnels often result in more severe outcomes due to spatial constraints that delay prehospital emergency medical services (EMS) access. Emergency evacuation facilities, such as cross passages and emergency parking areas, are critical for ensuring timely EMS response during traffic congestion caused by in-tunnel crashes. This study presents a quantitative approach to develop targeted strategies for enhancing such facilities to improve EMS accessibility in tunnels. Nationwide in-tunnel crash data from Korean freeways over a four-year period were analyzed, and the limited number of severe crash cases was addressed using SMOTE-based data augmentation to balance severity levels in the prediction model. A SHAP-based XGBoost classifier was applied to identify the influence of key features related to EMS accessibility and emergency evacuation facilities on crash severity. The results showed that crashes occurring more than 1 km from the tunnel entrance and EMS response coverage within a 10-15 km range have a significant impact on increasing crash severity. The presence of emergency cross passages, three or more lanes, emergency parking areas, and properly spaced CCTV installations were found to help reduce crash severity. Based on these findings, tunnels with particularly limited EMS accessibility were prioritized, and tailored facility improvement measures were proposed. This study provides quantitative evidence to guide cost-effective upgrades of tunnel emergency evacuation facilities, enhancing prehospital EMS accessibility and emergency preparedness. The proposed methodology can also support decision-making on implementing road tunnel safety improvement policies.

articles.title: Assessment of Compliance With the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence Guidance in the Management of Patients Referred Following a First Suspected Seizure: A Retrospective Clinical Audit.

abstract.text: Introduction A first suspected seizure requires timely specialist assessment and appropriate investigation to establish an accurate diagnosis, identify seizure mimics, assess the risk of recurrence, and provide appropriate safety advice. The National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) guidance recommends urgent specialist assessment following a first suspected seizure, alongside appropriate electrocardiography, electroencephalography, neuroimaging, recurrence-risk assessment, and patient safety advice. This audit evaluated adherence to these standards within a first-seizure clinic. Materials and methods A retrospective clinical audit was undertaken on patients referred to a first-seizure clinic from the Emergency Department and Acute Medicine Unit over a three-month period from January to March 2025. Data were obtained from electronic patient records, clinic correspondence, and discharge documentation. Compliance with predefined standards from NICE guidance was assessed. The primary outcome measures were timely specialist assessment, 12-lead electrocardiography, documentation of individualized seizure recurrence risk, timely electroencephalography where clinically indicated, timely neuroimaging where indicated, and documentation of safety-netting and driving advice. Results Sixty-three patient records were initially identified. Ten patients did not attend or were lost to follow-up and were excluded from the final clinical analysis, leaving 53 patients. Five of 53 patients (9.4%) received specialist assessment within two weeks. A 12-lead ECG was documented in all 53 patients (100%), and an individualized seizure recurrence risk assessment was documented in all patients (100%). An electroencephalogram (EEG) was indicated in 17 patients, of whom one (5.9%) underwent EEG within 72 hours; 15 (88.2%) underwent EEG after 72 hours, and one patient did not attend. The mean time to EEG among those who eventually underwent the investigation was approximately 12.5 weeks. Neuroimaging was indicated in 41 patients, of whom 22 (53.7%) underwent imaging within six weeks and 19 (46.3%) underwent imaging after six weeks. Safety-netting, including documentation of driving/Driver and Vehicle Licensing Agency (DVLA) advice, was documented in all 53 patients (100%). Conclusion The audit demonstrated high compliance with core assessment and documentation standards but substantial delays in specialist review and time-critical investigations. The greatest gap was in timely EEG access, followed by delays in specialist assessment and neuroimaging. The findings support service-level interventions aimed at improving urgent access to first-seizure assessment and investigations. A repeat audit, following the implementation of targeted interventions, will be important to determine whether pathway changes improve compliance.

articles.title: Predictors of Blood Culture Ordering and Results for Febrile Infants Aged 91 to 365 Days in the Emergency Department.
articles.journal: J Am Coll Emerg Physicians Open
articles.journal_full: Journal of the American College of Emergency Physicians open

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: The risk of invasive bacterial infections has dropped significantly among febrile infants due to widespread vaccination efforts. In older infants (age 91 days and older), diagnostic guidance is limited, and blood culture ordering is based on clinical judgment. We sought to evaluate blood culture ordering practice, bacteremia incidence, and the patient characteristics of true positive blood culture results.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of febrile pediatric patients aged 91 to 365 days who presented to Kaiser Permanente Northern California emergency departments (EDs) between January 1, 2018, and December 31, 2019, who had blood cultures drawn. We identified variables related to blood culture ordering using a generalized linear mixed model and adjudicated all positive results to determine rates of true bacteremia or contamination, as well as clinical characteristics of children with true positive bacteremia.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 5543 febrile infants, 611 (11.0%) underwent blood culture testing. After adjustment for covariates, higher ED temperature (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 1.40, 95% CI, 1.30 to 1.50), presence of comorbidities (aOR 2.55, 95% CI, 2.00 to 3.25), and younger age (aOR 0.996, 95% CI, 0.995 to 0.998, P < .001) were associated with blood culture ordering. Of the 37 (6.1%) positive blood cultures, only 16 (2.6%) were true positives. All true positives occurred in infants with either an identifiable risk factor or a clinically evident source of infection. There were no cases of occult bacteremia identified.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: In febrile infants aged 91 to 365 days, true bacteremia was rare and associated with significant comorbidities or an obvious infectious source. Our findings suggest a more directed approach to ED blood culture ordering.

articles.title: Posterior Circulation Stroke in Patients With Dizziness: Diagnostic Challenges and Practical Considerations for Emergency Care.
articles.journal: J Am Coll Emerg Physicians Open
articles.journal_full: Journal of the American College of Emergency Physicians open

articles.title: Subcutaneous insulin for mild-to-moderate diabetic ketoacidosis: a scoping review and implementation framework.
articles.journal_full: The American journal of emergency medicine

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: Diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) is a common emergency department (ED) presentation associated with high morbidity, mortality, and healthcare utilization. While intravenous (IV) insulin remains the most common treatment, emerging data suggest subcutaneous (SUBQ) insulin may be a feasible alternative for patients with mild-to-moderate DKA. This scoping review summarizes current evidence of SUBQ insulin use across a broad range of clinical and operational outcomes in DKA and provides an implementation framework for SUBQ insulin for mild-to-moderate DKA in the ED.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a scoping review of PubMed from inception through February 2026 for adult studies evaluating SUBQ insulin for DKA. Two investigators independently screened studies, with disagreements resolved by consensus. Data were charted and synthesized across clinical, operational, and implementation outcomes.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 117 articles were identified and 13 included. Available evidence suggests SUBQ insulin may achieve similar time to DKA resolution, compared with IV insulin in select patients with uncomplicated DKA. SUBQ insulin offers potential operational benefits, including reduced intensive care unit (ICU) utilization, shorter ED length of stay, and improved resource optimization. Patient selection criteria, dosing and monitoring strategies, and implementation approaches are summarized. Limitations in the literature include small sample sizes, single-center designs, heterogeneous protocols, and the exclusion of several higher-risk patient populations.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Evidence suggests SUBQ insulin pathways achieve similar clinical outcomes and may reduce ICU utilization and improve operational efficiency in select patients with mild-to-moderate DKA. Because most evidence originates from small, single-center cohorts, future studies should focus on larger, more generalizable populations.

articles.title: Effects of Natural Ageing on the Dimensional, Mechanical, and Thermal Properties of Diving Neoprene.

abstract.text: This study examines the effects of natural ageing on thickness, flexibility, elongation, and thermal resistance of neoprene used in wetsuits. A natural ageing protocol was developed to simulate recreational diving conditions under controlled exposure. Thirty-three neoprene specimens representing 11 material types and three thickness categories were repeatedly immersed in seawater at 15 m depth for 45 min per cycle. Fifty immersion, cleaning, and drying cycles were performed, corresponding to 37.5 h of underwater exposure. Thickness decreased in the majority of samples (p = 0.00043; Cohen's d = 0.64), while pre- and post-ageing values remained very strongly correlated (r = 0.9987). Flexibility decreased significantly (p = 0.000084; Cohen's d = -0.74). Thermal resistance declined significantly (p = 0.00029; Cohen's d = 0.66), with greater losses observed in high-performance neoprene. Elongation showed the greatest ageing-related change, decreasing by approximately 25% (p < 0.000001; Cohen's d = 1.32). Thermal resistance was strongly associated with neoprene thickness, whereas thermal-resistance loss was not correlated with thickness reduction (r = -0.085). Overall, natural ageing affected dimensional, mechanical, and thermal properties through multiple degradation processes, highlighting the importance of long-term performance stability in neoprene material selection and wetsuit design.

articles.title: Point-of-Care Ultrasound Use in Confirmed Acute Aortic Syndrome: A Five-Year Retrospective Cohort Study at the Ljubljana Emergency Medical Unit.

abstract.text: Background/Objectives: Point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) is increasingly used in emergency care, but data on its use in acute aortic syndrome (AAS) remains limited. This single-center retrospective cohort described POCUS use among patients with confirmed AAS and explored factors associated with POCUS use and time to completion of diagnostic workup. Methods: Records coded ICD10 I71.0-I71.8 from the Emergency Medical Unit, University Medical Centre Ljubljana (2019-2023) were reviewed. Clinical, imaging, and outcome data were extracted, and diagnoses were confirmed by two investigators through manual chart review of ED documentation, radiology reports, and specialist consultation notes. Fisher's exact and Wilcoxon rank sum tests were used for comparisons. Associations with POCUS use and time to completion of diagnostic workup (defined from arrival at triage to completion of the emergency department workup) were assessed with univariable logistic regression and linear regression models, respectively. Survival was explored using univariable Cox proportional-hazards models. Statistical significance was set at p < 0.05. Results: Among 120,109 emergency department visits, 73 patients had confirmed AAS (type A: 48; type B: 17; intramural hematoma: 8). POCUS was performed in 62% of patients, more often in those who were hemodynamically unstable (87.5% vs. 54.4%; p = 0.020) or had unclear presentations (40% vs. 7%; p = 0.003). Median time to completion of diagnostic workup was shorter with POCUS (110 vs. 213 min), though not statistically significant (p = 0.069). Hemodynamic instability was associated with higher odds of POCUS use (OR 5.87, 95% CI 1.22-28.2; p = 0.028), whereas a clear clinical presentation was associated with lower odds of POCUS use (OR 0.12, 95% CI 0.02-0.55; p = 0.007). Lower triage level was associated with longer time to completion of diagnostic workup (time ratio 5.43, 95% CI 2.21-13.4; p < 0.001 for urgent vs. immediate triage), whereas very high D-dimer levels were associated with shorter time to completion of diagnostic workup (time ratio 0.44, 95% CI 0.21-0.93; p = 0.031 for highest vs. lowest quartile). In-hospital mortality was 14%, with only age associated with mortality (HR 1.06 per year, 95% CI 1.02-1.11; p = 0.007). Conclusions: In this single-center retrospective AAS cohort, POCUS was used more frequently in unstable and diagnostically unclear patients but was not associated with time to completion of diagnostic workup. Findings are descriptive and exploratory; they do not establish that POCUS accelerates diagnosis or improves outcomes.

articles.title: [A case report of acute hexazinone poisoning resulting in multiple organ dysfunction syndrome].
articles.journal: Zhonghua Lao Dong Wei Sheng Zhi Ye Bing Za Zhi
articles.journal_full: Zhonghua lao dong wei sheng zhi ye bing za zhi = Zhonghua laodong weisheng zhiyebing zazhi = Chinese journal of industrial hygiene and occupational diseases

abstract.text: Hexazinone is a low-toxicity forest herbicide; however, high-dose oral administration can still lead to severe systemic poisoning. This article reports a case of a patient admitted to the Emergency Department of Liaocheng People's Hospital approximately 28 hours after ingesting 200 ml of a 25% hexazinone aqueous solution. The plasma hexazinone concentration was 29.3 μg/mL; at admission, the patient exhibited acute kidney injury (creatinine: 425.9 μmol/L), acute liver injury (aspartate aminotransferase: 655 U/L), myocardial injury (myocardial troponin I: 0.16 ng/mL), rhabdomyolysis, and metabolic acidosis; the patient was diagnosed with severe acute hexazinone poisoning and multiple organ dysfunction syndrome. Following gastrointestinal lavage, hemoperfusion combined with continuous venovenous hemofiltration (CVVH+HP) for approximately 50 hours, along with comprehensive therapeutic measures including hepatoprotective and acid suppression therapies, all clinical parameters returned to normal, and the patient was discharged in full recovery. Currently, there is no specific antidote for hexazinone poisoning; early gastrointestinal decontamination and prompt initiation of CVVH+HP blood purification are critical for successful treatment.

articles.title: Association between transfer pathways and functional outcomes in severe trauma patients: a cohort study using the PATOS registry.
articles.journal_full: The American journal of emergency medicine

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: Optimal transport strategies for severe trauma remain debated, particularly in Asia. We evaluated the association between interhospital transfer and functional outcome and its consistency across Asian trauma systems.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This cohort study used the Pan-Asian Trauma Outcome Study (PATOS) registry. We analyzed patients with severe trauma (Injury Severity Score > 15) in South Korea, Malaysia, and Vietnam (2015-2022). The exposure was interhospital transfer (Transfer) versus direct transport to a definitive-care hospital (Direct). The primary outcome was a favorable functional outcome (modified Rankin Scale ≤3). The primary model was a country fixed-effect logistic regression estimating the total effect; country-specific estimates and a transport-pathway × country interaction were pre-specified.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 9857 patients (Direct, n = 6725; Transfer, n = 3132; 89.2% of transfers in South Korea), a favorable functional outcome occurred in 4701/6403 (73.4%) versus 1830/2991 (61.2%). Transfer was associated with lower odds overall (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 0.86, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.78-0.95), but estimates differed by country (South Korea 1.06, 0.95-1.18; Malaysia 0.53, 0.36-0.80; Vietnam 0.17, 0.11-0.25; interaction P < 0.001; I2 = 97.4%).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Interhospital transfer was associated with a lower likelihood of a favorable functional outcome, but this was not uniform across the three trauma systems and was dominated by Korean data, in which no association was observed. These findings require confirmation in analyses anchored at injury or first medical contact.

articles.title: Injury patterns and early operative demand in a combined military and civilian casualty cohort: A single-centre study from the first 11 weeks of the 2023 Israel-Hamas war.
articles.journal_full: The American journal of emergency medicine

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Modern asymmetric warfare and large-scale terror attacks produce distinctive wounding patterns that differ from conventional state-on-state conflict and impose specific early demands on receiving trauma systems. The 7 October 2023 attack on southern Israel and the ensuing war generated a compressed surge of combined civilian and military casualties. We characterized injury patterns and linked them to early in-hospital resource use at a single tertiary trauma centre across the opening weeks of the conflict.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We performed a retrospective descriptive cohort study of 192 consecutive trauma casualties admitted between 7 October and 24 December 2023. Demographics, mechanism of injury, injured anatomical regions, Injury Severity Score (ISS) and acute interventions were abstracted from the institutional trauma dataset. Mechanism and anatomical categories were not mutually exclusive. Variables were summarised as medians (IQR) or counts (percentages); missing data were not imputed and percentages were computed over non-missing observations.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Casualties were young (median age 24 years, IQR 21-35) and predominantly male (84.4%). Penetrating (43.2%) and shrapnel (31.2%) mechanisms predominated, followed by acoustic trauma (12.0%). Extremities were most often injured (lower limb 41.7%, upper limb 35.4%); 68.8% had at least one extremity injury and 37.0% had two or more injured regions. Median ISS was 9 (IQR 4-16); 26.5% of those with a recorded ISS had ISS ≥16. Blast and crush carried the highest median ISS (25 and 16). Early resource use was substantial: 23.4% required emergency surgery via direct emergency-room-to-operating-room transfer, 10.9% mechanical ventilation and 5.2% packed red-cell transfusion.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: This extremity-predominant, penetrating-and-shrapnel profile, with a small but disproportionately severe blast and crush subgroup and frequent acoustic trauma, translated into early demand for emergency surgery, ventilation and transfusion. These patterns support resourcing limb-salvage and damage-control surgery, blood-bank and intensive-care readiness, and audiologic follow-up in military and mass-casualty trauma planning.

articles.title: Preoperative Ballon Aortic Valvuloplasty vs. Conservative Management in Patients Undergoing Hip Fracture Surgery with Underlying Severe Aortic Stenosis.

abstract.text: Background: Old adults with hip fracture (HFx) and concomitant severe aortic stenosis (AS) represent a high-risk population in whom urgent orthopedic repair is usually required, while definitive valve replacement is rarely feasible preoperatively. The clinical benefit of balloon aortic valvuloplasty (BAV) as a bridging strategy remains uncertain. Methods: In this observational study, we included patients admitted to our Emergency Department for HFx who had concomitant severe AS. Management of severe AS consisted of either conservative therapy or preoperative BAV. The early clinical endpoints included 30-day mortality, time to surgery, length of intensive care unit and hospital stay and need for mechanical ventilation. The late clinical endpoint was 180-day all-cause mortality. Results: Among 3958 patients admitted for HFx fracture, 46 (1.2%) were found to have severe AS and fulfilled the inclusion criteria. Of these, 12 patients (26.1%) underwent preoperative BAV and 34 (73.9%) received conservative management. Thirty-day mortality was 8.3% in the BAV group and 23.5% in the conservative group (HR 0.32; 95%CI 0.04-2.60; p = 0.29). Time to surgery was longer in the BAV group (p < 0.001) with concomitantly longer hospital (p = 0.001) and ICU (p = 0.041) stays. Preoperative BAV was independently associated with lower 180-day mortality (HR 0.13; 95%CI 0.03-0.63; p = 0.011). Conclusions: In patients with severe AS undergoing urgent HFx repair, preoperative BAV was associated with reduced 180-day mortality, suggesting a potential long-term prognostic benefit, which warrants confirmation in larger prospective studies. However, it was not associated with significantly better 30-day survival and was accompanied by surgical delay and greater healthcare resource utilization.

articles.title: Magnesium sulfate therapy for adult emergency department patients with acute asthma: A narrative review.
articles.journal_full: The American journal of emergency medicine

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Magnesium sulfate (MgSO4) has been used for decades as an adjunctive bronchodilator in acute asthma exacerbations refractory to first-line therapy, but its role in adult emergency department (ED) care remains debated.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To review the evidence for intravenous (IV) and nebulized MgSO4 as adjunctive therapy in adults presenting to the ED with acute asthma, to clarify how the pooled analyses and the largest individual trial relate to one another, and to compare this evidence with current guideline recommendations.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This is a structured narrative review. Records were identified from a PubMed search using a single search phrase (19 records), supplemented by targeted Cochrane Library and guideline-body searches performed in August 2026 (14 records) and by backward citation searching. Screening and data extraction were performed by a single reviewer. After removing duplicates and one record excluded for population mismatch, 29 records were assessed for eligibility. Ten provided extractable magnesium-specific efficacy or safety data, 5 primary randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and 5 systematic reviews or meta-analyses, which are presented separately because the reviews pool overlapping trials. The remaining 19 records were used only as background. Eighteen additional eligible RCTs included in these reviews were not identified by our search; these are listed, and their contribution is represented only through the pooled estimates of the reviews that include them.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: In pooled analysis, IV MgSO4 was associated with a modest reduction in hospital admission (Cochrane 2014, 11 trials including the 3 Mg trial: OR 0.75, 95% CI 0.60-0.92; number needed to treat approximately 14) and some short-term improvement in lung function. The largest individual trial (3 Mg, n = 1109), which contributes to that pooled estimate, found a similar but non-significant reduction in admission with IV MgSO4 (OR 0.73, 95% CI 0.51-1.04), no benefit from nebulized MgSO4, and more adverse events with active treatment than with placebo (15.6% vs 10.1%; OR 1.68, 95% CI 1.11-2.52), most of which were minor. A larger lung-function benefit at the lowest baseline FEV1 was supported by one trial's prespecified interaction analysis, but a larger reduction in admission in the most severely obstructed patients rests on a small subgroup and was not confirmed by a test for subgroup differences across trials. A 2023 adult-specific meta-analysis found no statistically significant pooled lung-function benefit by either route. Commonly reported adverse effects were flushing, fatigue, nausea, headache, and transient hypotension.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: IV MgSO4 may provide a modest benefit in selected adults with severe asthma exacerbations that do not respond to initial therapy. A greater benefit in the most severely obstructed patients is plausible but has not been established. Nebulized MgSO4 has no convincing evidence of benefit in adults. Major guidelines (GINA 2026, BTS/SIGN 158 [2019], and NAEPP EPR-3 [2007]) support IV MgSO4 as a second-line adjunct for severe or life-threatening exacerbations unresponsive to initial therapy, and GINA has not recommended nebulized MgSO4 since its 2025 update. Clinicians using IV MgSO4 in severe refractory asthma should expect a modest and uncertain benefit and an excess of minor, but rarely serious, adverse events.

articles.title: Development and Internal Validation of a Preintubation Prediction Model for Postintubation Hypotension in Trauma Patients Undergoing Emergency Endotracheal Intubation: A Retrospective Cohort Study.

abstract.text: Background/Objectives: Postintubation hypotension (PIH) is an important complication of emergency endotracheal intubation in trauma patients. However, the applicability of preintubation predictors of PIH in trauma patients undergoing emergency endotracheal intubation in the emergency department (ED) remains uncertain. Here, we aimed to develop and internally validate a preintubation prediction model for PIH in such patients. Methods: This retrospective cohort included trauma patients aged ≥ 15 years undergoing emergency endotracheal intubation in the ED during 2015-2023. PIH was defined as systolic blood pressure < 90 mmHg within 30 min after intubation. Eight preintubation candidate predictors were evaluated using logistic regression with backward elimination. Internal validation used 2000 bootstrap resamples repeating the entire variable-selection procedure. Results: Among 348 patients, 60 (17.2%) developed PIH; 345 patients with 57 PIH events had complete data for model development. The final model retained systolic blood pressure, body temperature, hematocrit, and torso injury, with adjusted odds ratios of 1.19 per 10-mmHg lower systolic blood pressure, 1.48 per 1 °C lower temperature, 1.33 per 5-percentage-point lower hematocrit, and 3.26 for torso injury. The apparent and optimism-corrected areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve were 0.742 and 0.700, respectively. Conclusions: A four-variable preintubation prediction model demonstrated modest optimism-corrected discrimination and substantial model-selection uncertainty. External validation and assessment of clinical utility are required before clinical implementation.

articles.title: Comparison of qSOFA Score and NEWS for Predicting Hospital Admission and Mortality in the Emergency Department: A Prospective Observational Study.

abstract.text: Background/Objectives: This study compared the performance of the National Early Warning Score (NEWS) and the quick Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (qSOFA) score for predicting hospital admission and in-hospital mortality among adult patients triaged to the high-acuity area of the emergency department (ED). qSOFA was derived and validated in patients with suspected infection, and only 8.1% of this cohort carried a preliminary diagnosis of sepsis; its evaluation here is therefore exploratory. Methods: A total of 270 patients were included in this prospective observational study. Vital signs, Glasgow Coma Scale scores, and both scores were recorded at ED presentation. Discrimination was assessed by receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, with the two scores compared using the DeLong test. Sensitivity and specificity were then examined separately at both conventional and data-derived thresholds. Bootstrap internal validation, calibration plots, Brier scores and decision-curve analysis were also performed, all computed using the development dataset. Results: Of 268 patients evaluable for the admission outcome (two ED deaths were excluded as a competing outcome), 35.8% (n = 96) were admitted, and 7.0% (n = 19 of 270) died in the hospital. No statistically significant difference was found between the AUCs of the two scores for admission (0.709 vs. 0.695; p = 0.627) or mortality (0.900 vs. 0.862; p = 0.150). At the conventional qSOFA score threshold of ≥2, the expected high-specificity, low-sensitivity profile was reproduced for mortality (96.8% and 52.6%), whereas the cohort-derived qSOFA score threshold of ≥1 favored sensitivity (84.2%). Bootstrap correction showed modest optimism. Calibration assessment was limited by the small number of events, and both score-specific models showed apparent net benefit over treat-all and treat-none strategies across most thresholds examined. Each score was independently associated with mortality in exploratory score-specific models. Conclusions: NEWS and qSOFA showed no statistically significant difference in discrimination in this high-acuity ED cohort. With only 19 deaths, the mortality analyses and the cohort-specific thresholds are exploratory and require confirmation in larger, multicenter cohorts before any clinical use.

articles.title: Stroke mimics in the emergency department: Prevalence, etiologies, and clinical predictors in patients with suspected acute stroke.
articles.journal_full: The American journal of emergency medicine

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Stroke mimics present with acute neurological symptoms resembling stroke and remain a major diagnostic challenge in the emergency department (ED). Early differentiation from true stroke is important for timely treatment and appropriate resource utilization.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To determine the prevalence, etiologies, and clinical predictors of stroke mimics among patients presenting to the ED with suspected acute stroke within 9 h of symptom onset.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of adults who presented to the ED of Srinagarind Hospital, Thailand, between January 2021 and December 2024. Eligible patients were aged ≥18 years, had suspected acute stroke within 9 h of symptom onset, and were triaged through the institutional Stroke Fast-Track protocol. Demographic characteristics, comorbidities, presenting symptoms, physical examination findings, and neuroimaging results were extracted from electronic medical records. Attending neurologists determined the final diagnoses. Univariate and multivariable logistic regression analyses identified factors independently associated with stroke mimics.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 1615 patients, 347 (21.5%; 95% confidence interval [CI], 19.5-23.5%) were diagnosed with stroke mimics. Seizure-related disorders were the most common etiology (13.8%), followed by cardiovascular and cerebrovascular non-stroke conditions (11.2%) and infectious or inflammatory diseases (10.1%). In multivariable analysis, younger age, male sex, a history of migraine, psychiatric disorders, and epilepsy, along with lower diastolic blood pressure and higher heart rate, were independently associated with stroke mimics. Presenting features independently associated with stroke mimics included altered consciousness (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 1.71; 95% CI, 1.25-2.33), seizure (aOR 2.68; 95% CI, 1.79-4.00), vertigo (aOR 1.85; 95% CI, 1.28-2.65), and fever (aOR 3.10; 95% CI, 1.36-7.12). Conversely, limb weakness and speech disturbance were independently associated with confirmed stroke.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Stroke mimics accounted for 21.5% of suspected acute stroke presentations in the ED. Altered consciousness, seizure, vertigo, and fever were independently associated with stroke mimics, whereas limb weakness and speech disturbance favored confirmed stroke.

articles.title: Poison-Centre Scorpion-Sting Records in Turkey, 2014-2020: A Data-Quality Audit.

abstract.text: Poison-centre records can inform toxicovigilance, but their interpretation depends on stable definitions and complete fields. We audited scorpion-sting data published by Turkey's National Poison Control Centre (UZEM) and mapped record-design features in international publications. The detailed 2014-2018 appendix was analysed separately from 2019-2020 tables. It contained 7055 records; 51.0% involved males, 48.8% females, and 0.2% had unreported sex. May-September accounted for 74.1%, with July highest (17.9%). The source's unequal age intervals initially favoured wider adult categories; after harmonisation into 10-year bands, ages 0-9 became the largest band in every year and represented 21.8% overall. Aggregate tables separately reported 1451 records in 2019 and 1729 in 2020. The audit covered 191 analytic ledger entries across 39 variables and identified numerical conflicts, changing definitions, and gaps in clinical linkage. Clinical tables were available only for 2017-2018, with no symptom recorded for 50.6% and 37.6% of annual records, respectively. Management fields documented recommendations and limited post-antivenom feedback, but not complete linked administration, severity, disposition, or outcomes. We propose a draft field framework prioritising event identity, clinical trajectory, treatment, disposition, and outcome. The findings describe poison-centre reporting activity rather than population risk.

articles.title: Persistent Varicella Transmission in a High-Coverage Single-Dose Vaccination Program: Costa Rica, 2015-2024.

abstract.text: Background: Costa Rica introduced universal one-dose varicella vaccination in 2007 using a one-dose schedule administered at 15 months of age through the Costa Rican Social Security Fund (CCSS). A previous national study described epidemiological changes through 2014 by comparing pre- and post-vaccination periods; however, contemporary data on subsequent patterns and residual disease burden are limited. We characterized varicella epidemiology and healthcare burden in Costa Rica using the most recent nationally available data. Methods: We conducted a nationwide retrospective descriptive study using aggregated surveillance and administrative data. Outcomes included incidence of reported varicella cases (2015-2022), outpatient and emergency department visits (2019-2024), hospitalizations (2015-2024), in-hospital deaths with a recorded varicella diagnosis (2018-2020), institutional outbreaks, and first-dose vaccination coverage (2018-2024). Results: From 2015 to 2022, reported incidence declined by 84% in males and 83% in females, after increasing through 2019 and declining markedly during the COVID-19 pandemic. Children aged 1-9 years accounted for the largest proportion of reported cases. Among 354 hospitalizations, adults aged 20-44 years accounted for 30.5%. Hospitalizations among children aged ≤4 years decreased by approximately 56% between 2015-2018 and 2021-2024, while annual hospitalizations among adults aged 20-44 years increased from 7 in 2015 to 21 in 2024, representing a 200% increase over the study period. Three deaths occurred during hospitalizations with a varicella diagnosis, all among adults, and one institutional outbreak was identified. First-dose vaccination coverage averaged approximately 94% during 2018-2022 and remained high thereafter. Conclusions: Reported varicella incidence declined substantially during the study period, but circulation and healthcare burden persisted, with hospitalizations increasingly concentrated among adults. Because our analysis lacks a pre-vaccination comparator, these trends cannot be causally attributed to vaccination based on our data alone. The findings support maintaining high first-dose coverage and strengthening surveillance.
