Further information on individual vaccination history and population susceptibility is needed to evaluate the potential contribution of a two-dose vaccination strategy in Costa Rica.

articles.title: Development of a quality metric to measure bystander cardiopulmonary resuscitation in out of hospital cardiac arrest: A modified Delphi study.
articles.journal_full: International journal of nursing studies advances

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Out-of-hospital cardiac arrest remains a significant global public health challenge, with survival heavily dependent on early and high-quality bystander cardiopulmonary resuscitation. Current data collection frameworks lack standardised tools to assess the quality of bystander cardiopulmonary resuscitation.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: This study aimed to develop a preliminary consensus-based quality metric for use in both research and clinical practice.

abstract.label: SETTING
abstract.text: This study was conducted in the United Kingdom with international representation within the Delphi panel.

abstract.label: PARTICIPANTS
abstract.text: A total of 104 participants registered, with 62, 48, and 18 completing rounds one to three, respectively in the Delphi panel. The panel consisted of Doctors, advanced practitioners, Paramedics, Nurses and academics.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A modified Delphi method was employed to identify and define quality indicators. Criteria were developed from a literature review, stakeholder input, and panel consensus. A diverse expert panel, including clinicians, researchers, educators, and informed laypersons, participated in three iterative rounds (two online surveys and a final virtual consensus meeting). Consensus was defined as ≥75% agreement on a 1-5 Likert scale.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Eleven criteria achieved consensus for inclusion, encompassing core mechanical parameters (e.g., chest compression rate, depth, recoil) and contextual factors (e.g., dispatcher instruction, time from recognition to emergency call, and automated external defibrillator use). All criteria were agreed to be scored dichotomously. Two composite indicators were created to streamline overlapping elements.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The provisional metric reflects both established guidelines and evolving evidence on factors influencing bystander cardiopulmonary resuscitation effectiveness. The inclusion of time and system-based criteria acknowledges the broader context in which cardiopulmonary resuscitation is delivered. Once validated in future studies this metric has potential for practical relevance for feedback tools, service evaluation, and research standardisation. This study was not registered.

articles.title: From Routing to Weighting: Mask-Only Policies for Repairing Incomplete Photovoltaic Monitoring Records.

abstract.text: Repairing an incomplete photovoltaic monitoring record requires choosing an imputation operator, and the right choice depends on which evidence the fault left intact. The decision can use only what a monitoring system holds at repair time. We study mask-only policies, which read the observation mask (which cells are missing) and the clock but never the values being repaired, and ask how fine such a decision must be. Two policies are compared: a fault-aware router that diagnoses each missing cell into one of three regimes and dispatches it to one operator, and MAWC, a mask-aware weighted combination that predicts a convex weight over the whole operator pool per cell. Both are fixed on two desert development sites and evaluated once on four held-out sites spanning two further climates and cadences from 1 to 15 min, with mixed fault masks and time-contiguous evaluation segments, two protocol corrections without which a per-cell policy cannot be measured. The router improves on the operator that a deployer could have committed to at every held-out site and lies within 7% of the best fixed assignment of operators to its regimes at three of them. MAWC improves on the router at all four sites, significantly at three, improves on per-regime convex weights at all four, and falls below the regime oracle at two, which no hard router using those regimes can do. Its gain comes from hedging rather than finer selection: a selector trained to pick one operator per cell with the same features loses 15% to 34%. The advantage holds under retrained deep members, doubled replication, changed fault composition and a higher missing rate.

articles.title: Effect of Early Tourniquet Release on Hemolysis in Emergency Department Phlebotomy: The TOURNI-ED Randomized Trial.

abstract.text: Background and Objectives: Hemolysis is the most common preanalytical error in emergency department samples and can compromise diagnostic reliability. Evidence on tourniquet-release timing under standardized pressure is limited. We assessed whether initiating cuff deflation when blood enters the first tube and completing it as that tube fills reduces hemolysis. Materials and Methods: In a single-center, parallel-group, 1:1 randomized trial (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT07617103), 792 adults triaged as Emergency Severity Index (ESI) 3 to 5 underwent venipuncture with stasis applied at 60 mm Hg by sphygmomanometer. Cuff deflation was initiated when blood entered the first tube and completed as that tube filled (n = 396) or after the last tube filled (n = 396). The primary outcome was the proportion of serum separator gel tubes with a hemolysis index of 1+ or greater, assessed by personnel blinded to allocation. The primary complete-case analysis included 790 participants analyzed as randomized. Results: Hemolysis occurred in 68 of 395 patients (17.2%) with early release and 103 of 395 (26.1%) with late release (absolute risk reduction 8.9 percentage points; 95% confidence interval (CI), 3.1-14.5; p = 0.003; number needed to treat (NNT) 11.3). The adjusted odds ratio in the prespecified model was 0.58 (95% CI, 0.41-0.82), and the ordinal distribution also favored early release (p = 0.002). No early-release patient exceeded 60 s of stasis, versus 29.0% with late release. Complication estimates were imprecise (8.1% vs. 5.6%; risk difference +2.5 points; 95% CI, -1.0 to 6.1). Conclusions: In adult emergency department patients presenting with non-critical acuity (ESI 3-5) undergoing direct 21-gauge venipuncture under standardized 60 mm Hg cuff pressure, early cuff release significantly reduced specimen hemolysis (NNT 11.3 for preventing one laboratory-defined hemolyzed sample). These findings cannot be generalized to resuscitated patients (ESI 1-2), intravenous catheter blood draws, winged collection devices, or uncalibrated elastic tourniquets.

articles.title: Orthopaedic Consultation Versus No Consultation for Clavicle, Radial Head, and Proximal Humerus Fractures: Association with Post-Imaging Emergency Department Length of Stay.

abstract.text: Background/Objectives: To evaluate the association between orthopaedic consultation and Emergency Department (ED) length of stay among patients with clavicle, radial head, and proximal humerus fractures meeting criteria for nonacute management (discharge without orthopaedic consultation). Methods: All adult patients presenting to a single Level 1 trauma centre between 2019 and 2022 with a clavicle, radial head, or proximal humerus fracture that met criteria for nonacute management (discharge without orthopaedic consultation) were identified from an institutional database. Post-imaging ED length of stay, defined as time from radiograph completion to discharge or admission, was compared between patients discharged per protocol without orthopaedic consultation and those discharged after receiving orthopaedic consultation. A mixed-effects linear log regression model with orthopaedic surgery consult, age and sex as fixed effects and year of presentation as a random intercept was used to model the effect of not having an orthopaedic surgery consult on length of stay. A post hoc sensitivity analysis excluding patients who were admitted was performed. Results of the regression model are presented with corresponding 95% confidence intervals. Results: This study included 523 patients (average age 57 years, 58% female) with 115 clavicle, 269 proximal humerus, and 139 radial head fractures. Among patients meeting criteria for nonacute management, those who were discharged per protocol without orthopaedic consultation had a 59%, 56%, and 55% reduction in length of stay for clavicle, radial head, and proximal humerus fractures, respectively (all p < 0.001). Only 3/523 (0.6%) were admitted to orthopaedic surgery. Results were consistent in post hoc sensitivity analysis. Conclusions: Discharge without orthopaedic consultation among patients with clavicle, radial head, or proximal humerus fractures meeting criteria for nonacute management was associated with substantially shorter ED length of stay. Adherence to this protocol may aid in reducing overcrowding in the ED.

articles.title: Exertional heat stroke induces liver injury through the activation of the TLR4/NF-κB signaling pathway.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Exertional heat stroke (EHS) disrupts the intestinal barrier and facilitates lipopolysaccharide (LPS) translocation, thereby activating hepatic inflammatory signaling pathways and contributing to liver injury. This study aimed to investigate the role and mechanism of the Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4)/nuclear factor kappa B (NF-κB) pathway in EHS-induced liver injury.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: An EHS Sprague-Dawley rat model was developed through treadmill running, with EHS defined as achieving a core temperature of 42.9°C ± 0.1°C. The model rats were pretreated with either TAK-242 (10.0 mg/kg), a TLR4 inhibitor or saline prior to running. Real-time fluorescence quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR), immunohistochemistry, and Western blot (WB) analyses were performed to investigate the expression of the TLR4/NF-κB pathway in the liver and the tight junction proteins in the intestine. HepG2 cells under heat stress and LPS exposure were utilized to examine TLR4/NF-κB activation at transcriptional and protein levels.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: EHS rats exhibited significantly increased liver inflammation and elevated levels of ALT (Alanine Aminotransferase), AST (Aspartate Aminotransferase), TNF-α (Tumor Necrosis Factor-α), IL-1β (Interleukin-1β), and IL-6 (Interleukin-6) compared to the normal control group (all P < 0.05). There was a reduction in intestinal occludin, Zonula occludens-1 (ZO-1), E-cadherin and an increase in serum LPS levels, and upregulation of hepatic TLR4/NF-κB signaling (all P < 0.05). Pretreatment with TAK-242 reduced hepatic TLR4/NF-κB signaling and inflammation both in vivo and in vitro. However, it did not significantly restore occludin, ZO-1, and E-cadherin expression levels in EHS rats.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: EHS leads to liver injury through the activation of the TLR4/NF-κB signaling pathway. TAK-242 pretreatment attenuates liver inflammation by downregulating the TLR4/NF-κB signaling, supporting a mechanistic role for this pathway in EHS-induced liver injury.

articles.title: A Review on Glial Fibrillary Acidic Protein Biosensors for Point-of-Care Stroke Diagnosis.

abstract.text: Stroke is a major cause of mortality and disability worldwide, and rapid differentiation between IS, haemorrhagic stroke (HS), and SMs is essential for timely treatment. This narrative review examines the potential of GFAP as a biomarker for acute stroke diagnosis and evaluates biosensing strategies for its detection, with particular emphasis on PoC and pre-hospital applications, profiting from its coupling with microfluidic technologies. The biological role, temporal kinetics, and diagnostic and prognostic value of GFAP are first discussed in comparison with other stroke biomarkers. The suitability of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), serum, plasma, whole blood, urine, saliva, and sweat as biological matrices is then assessed. Finally, electrochemical, optical, mechanical, and other biosensor platforms developed for GFAP detection are reviewed in terms of sensing principles, analytical performance, biological matrices, assay duration, and potential clinical applicability. Overall, despite the heterogeneity of the data available in the literature, the reviewed evidence supports the potential utility of GFAP for hyperacute stroke assessment, owing to its rapid elevation following ICH and its ability to differentiate HS from IS and SMs. However, variability in sampling time, analytical methods, biological matrices, and patient populations limits direct comparison between studies. Further development of integrated and multiplexed PoC biosensors, also benefiting from the wide possibilities of advanced microfluidics' technologies, may facilitate rapid and accessible stroke diagnosis and patient stratification.

articles.title: Viscoelastic Hemostatic Testing as a Diagnostic Tool for Trauma-Induced Coagulopathy with a Focus on Arabian Gulf Countries: A Narrative Review.

abstract.text: Trauma-induced coagulopathy (TIC) at admission to the emergency department is associated with severe bleeding, massive transfusion, increased morbidity, and mortality. There are significant regional variations in the accessibility and acceptance of point-of-care technology, such as viscoelastic hemostatic testing (VET), for coagulation monitoring and bleeding management in the Arabian Gulf council countries (GCC). Notable regional differences among these countries are mainly due to variation in the awareness of the benefits of VET-guided bleeding management using rotational thromboelastometry (ROTEM) or thromboelastography (TEG), compared with a transfusion ratio-based approach using shock packs, rather than for economic reasons. This review highlights the superiority of VET-guided bleeding management in severe trauma over conventional coagulation tests (CCTs) for early TIC detection and the importance of monitoring hemostatic disorders, whether hypocoagulability or hypercoagulability. VET consistently outperforms traditional coagulation tests in detecting early coagulation abnormalities and predicting massive transfusion and mortality in major trauma. Besides hyperfibrinolysis, fibrinogen deficiency often represents the first issue in TIC. Recent meta-analyses consistently demonstrated a reduction in mortality by implementing VET-guided bleeding management algorithms in severe trauma. Several studies demonstrated that VETs are valuable tools for massive transfusion and mortality prediction in bleeding patients with severe trauma. There is a notable variation in VET adoption and practice across trauma settings in the Arab Gulf. GCC-specific primary evidence is limited, with the Qatar cohort representing the largest directly identified regional study.

articles.title: Beyond Age: Radiological and Inflammatory Factors Associated with Hospital Stay After VATS in Pediatric Complicated Pneumonia-A 10-Year Single-Center Experience.

abstract.text: Background/Objectives: We aimed to describe the clinical, laboratory, and radiological characteristics of children with complicated pneumonia/empyema who underwent video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) and to identify factors associated with length of hospital stay. Methods: We retrospectively reviewed 68 children who presented to the pediatric emergency department of a tertiary university hospital and underwent VATS between April 2015 and April 2025. Factors associated with length of stay were assessed using univariable and multivariable negative binomial regression. Results: Median age was 60 months (interquartile range 36-138), and 66% were male. On univariable analysis, C-reactive protein (CRP) was associated with length of stay (incidence rate ratio [IRR] = 1.03 per 100 mg/L; p = 0.034), whereas age was not (p = 0.542). In the multivariable model, CRP remained borderline associated (IRR = 1.03; 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.00-1.06; p = 0.049), whereas performance of computed tomography was not (p = 0.142). An atypical (gastrointestinal or pain-predominant) presentation occurred in 25%. Streptococcus pneumoniae was the most frequently detected bacterial pathogen, mainly by nasopharyngeal polymerase chain reaction. Conclusions: In this single-center, retrospective cohort, higher CRP at presentation, but not age, was modestly associated with a longer hospital stay; this small association needs confirmation in larger prospective studies, and most children (82%) were managed with VATS alone.

articles.title: Beyond Mallampati: From Universal Bedside Tests to Precision Airway Risk Stratification.

abstract.text: Airway management remains one of the few domains of anaesthetic practice still governed by universal, dichotomous screening thresholds applied to profoundly heterogeneous populations. Conventional bedside tests-the modified Mallampati test, thyromental distance and the upper lip bite test-retain modest and inconsistent diagnostic accuracy, leaving the majority of difficult intubations unanticipated while generating false alarms that drive resource-intensive contingency plans. This narrative review reframes preoperative airway evaluation as a problem of individualised risk stratification rather than population screening. We first summarise the performance limits of classical bedside predictors and the reasons for their ceiling effect, including low target prevalence, inter-observer variability, spectrum bias and heterogeneous outcome definitions. We then examine the data streams reshaping the field: point-of-care upper airway ultrasound, whose parameters provide operator-accessible and objective anatomical information; cross-sectional and craniofacial imaging; and machine-learning models based on clinical variables, facial images and voice analysis. For each we discuss accuracy, reproducibility, validation status and barriers to adoption. We then propose a phenotype-oriented framework in which assessment intensity is matched to pre-test probability, with dedicated pathways for obesity and obstructive sleep apnoea, obstetric, head-and-neck oncological and post-radiotherapy, critically ill and emergency, and paediatric populations. We map this framework onto the 2025 European Society of Anaesthesiology and Intensive Care and Difficult Airway Society recommendations and outline the validation, calibration and equity requirements-including algorithmic bias across skin tone, sex and ethnicity-that must be met before precision airway assessment can enter routine practice.

articles.title: Prehospital delay and thrombolysis rates in posterior circulation stroke: a multicenter Latin American study.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: We aimed to evaluate the delay to emergency arrival in adults with acute Posterior circulation ischemic strokes (PCS) and the likelihood of receiving intravenous thrombolysis compared to anterior circulation ischemic strokes (ACS) across six different hospitals in Latin America.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This multicenter study in Latin America hospitals including three hospitals in Peru (Cusco, Arequipa, and Lima City), one in Colombia (Bogotá), one in Chile (Valdivia), and one in Mexico City. We analyzed adult patients treated between 2018 and 2023 with a confirmed diagnosis of ischemic stroke (IS). We evaluated demographic characteristics, initial NIHSS score, onset-to-door time (ODT), rate of intravenous thrombolysis (IVT), and other stroke-related characteristics. Medians with interquartile ranges (IQR) were calculated. IVT (yes/no) was evaluated using Firth penalized logistic regression including stroke circulation, age, sex, admission NIHSS, ODT, previous stroke, and previous evaluation at another hospital as covariates. Continuous predictors were modeled per year, NIHSS point, and ODT hour, respectively. Adjusted odds ratios (aOR) with 95% CI were reported, with p < 0.05 considered statistically significant.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 1,460 patients were included, 501 (34.3%) of whom had PCS, with a median age of 70 years (IQR 59-80). We found significant differences in median ODT between PCS and ACS (13 h, IQR 5-46 vs. 8.5 h, IQR 4-20; p < 0.001) and in IVT rates. In the adjusted analysis, each additional hour of ODT was associated with lower odds of IVT (aOR 0.88, 95% CI 0.85-0.92), whereas stroke circulation was not independently associated with IVT (PCS vs. ACS: aOR 0.66, 95% CI 0.39-1.11). Higher admission NIHSS was associated with higher odds of IVT (aOR 1.06 per point, 95% CI 1.03-1.09).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Patients with posterior circulation stroke had longer prehospital delays and lower observed rates of intravenous thrombolysis than those with anterior circulation stroke. However, stroke circulation was not independently associated with IVT after adjustment for ODT and other clinically relevant covariates. These findings highlight early recognition and reduction of prehospital delay as potential targets for improving access to reperfusion therapy in Latin America.

articles.title: Effect of the CP@clinic program (Community Paramedicine at Clinic program) on health care utilization from administrative data during and after the intervention: a cluster-randomized controlled trial.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: The study objective was to compare the effects of the Community Paramedicine at Clinic (CP@clinic) program versus usual care on building-level health service utilization during a 12-month trial period and 12 months post-trial.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This study employed a longitudinal, repeated cross-sectional design within a cluster-randomized controlled trial (RCT). It involved 30 apartment buildings across five Ontario communities, housing low-income older adults. Buildings were paired and randomized to receive either the CP@clinic intervention or continuing with usual care. Data was derived from ICES-maintained administrative health databases, linked using unique identifiers. The sample included all residents aged 55 + in the study postal codes from the Ontario Health Insurance Plan (OHIP) Registered Persons Database (RPDB), excluding those aged 120+, ineligible for OHIP, and those with no health care encounters within 7 years. The primary health care utilization outcome was emergency department visits by ambulance and other outcomes included hospital admissions and primary care visits.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: CP@clinic buildings showed significantly lower hospital admission rates during both the 12-month RCT period (adjusted incidence rate ratio [aIRR]: 0.75 [0.61,0.91]) and the 12-month post-RCT period [aIRR: 0.82 (0.70,0.96)] compared to usual care buildings. Primary care visits were lower in CP@clinic buildings during the RCT (aIRR: 0.93 [0.88,0.99]) but higher in the post-RCT period (aIRR: 1.05 [1.00,1.10]). No significant differences were found in emergency department visits or the number of days admitted between groups in either period.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: CP@clinic was linked to a sustained reduction in hospital admissions and an increase in primary care visits beyond the RCT time period, reflecting a shift from reactive to preventive care among older adults residing in social housing. The lasting impact beyond the RCT period suggests that the CP@clinic Program can improve health system efficiency, primary care access, and reduce health inequities in vulnerable populations.

abstract.label: TRIAL REGISTRATION
abstract.text: ClinicalTrials.gov, Identifier: NCT02152891.

articles.title: Mapping the research landscape of UAV- and eVTOL-enabled emergency medical services: a bibliometric analysis, scoping review, and policy tool assessment.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Electric vertical takeoff and landing (eVTOL) aircraft and unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) are increasingly recognized as transformative technologies for emergency medical services (EMS). Despite a growing body of evidence on drone-delivered automated external defibrillators (AEDs), blood product logistics, and eVTOL air ambulance simulations, no study has comprehensively mapped this interdisciplinary research landscape while simultaneously analyzing the policy frameworks that govern its implementation.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a triple-method study integrating bibliometric analysis, a scoping review following PRISMA-ScR guidelines, and quantitative policy text analysis. Bibliometric mapping covered 2015 to 2026. The scoping review followed the Joanna Briggs Institute methodology with the PAGER (Patterns, Advances, Gaps, Evidence, Recommendations) synthesis framework, including 168 studies. Policy analysis applied the Rothwell and Zegveld policy tool classification and the Policy Modeling Consistency (PMC) Index to 62 Chinese policy documents related to low-altitude economy and emergency medical rescue (2020-2025), yielding 526 codable policy provisions.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The bibliometric analysis identified 683 publications across five thematic clusters, with exponential growth from 2022 onward. The scoping review of 168 studies synthesized evidence showing drone-delivered AEDs arrived before ambulances in 67% of cases (median lead time 3 min 14 s), blood product drone delivery reduced transport time by 61%, and eVTOL air ambulance simulations halved advanced life support response times. All 964 modeled drone networks were cost-effective under model assumptions, improving OHCA survival by 21%-46%. Policy analysis of 62 Chinese documents revealed structural imbalance: supply-side and environmental tools constituted 75.3% of provisions while demand-side tools accounted for only 24.7%. The mean PMC Index was 7.46 (SD = 0.89), with timeliness (0.73) and policy measures (0.72) as the weakest dimensions.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The evidence base for UAV/eVTOL-enabled emergency medical services is approaching the consistency needed to inform health systems planning, although no formal risk-of-bias appraisal was undertaken, and a critical disconnect persists between technological readiness and policy infrastructure. We propose a "dual-wheel drive, four-chain integration" framework encompassing scenario implementation and ecosystem cultivation across infrastructure, industrial innovation, institutional policy, and human capital dimensions. This framework offers a roadmap for translating fragmented pilot programs into sustainable, equity-enhancing emergency medical service systems.

articles.title: Peripheral nerve blocks reduce opioid requirements in the first 24 h following surgical fixation of acute tibial shaft fractures.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: To evaluate the effect of peripheral nerve blocks (PNB) on postoperative opioid use, length of stay (LOS), and incidence of acute compartment syndrome (ACS) in patients presenting with acute tibial shaft fractures treated with intramedullary nail (IMN) fixation.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Design: Retrospective cohort study Setting: Level 1 Academic Trauma Center from 2018 to 2022. Patient Selection Criteria: Patients aged 18-79 years with acute AO/OTA 42A-C tibial shaft fractures treated with IMN within 7 days of injury Outcome Measures and Comparisons: The primary outcome was postoperative opioid use, measured in morphine milligram equivalents (MME), during hospital stay, up to a maximum of 72 h after surgery. Patients who received a preoperative PNB were compared to those who did not receive a block. Secondary outcomes included postoperative LOS and incidence of ACS.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: 246 patients were eligible for analysis of which 78 (32%) received a PNB (PNB=yes) and 168 (68%) did not (PNB=no). Mean MME were significantly lower in the PNB=yes group compared to the PNB=no group at 24 h (73 vs. 138, p < 0.001). Controlling for age, Injury Severity Score (ISS), and time to surgery, a multivariable regression model demonstrated a 36% reduction in MME per hour for patients that received PNBs. There were 3 cases of ACS in PNB=No and 1 in PNB=Yes. All 3 patients without a PNB were diagnosed within 2 days of surgery and underwent uncomplicated fasciotomies. One patient with a PNB re-presented to the hospital 5 days postoperatively, underwent fasciotomies, and was found to have anterior and lateral compartment necrosis.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: PNBs for select acute tibial shaft fractures treated with IMN were associated with decreased opioid requirements in the first 24 h after surgery. No effect was noted beyond 24 h after surgery. Extreme vigilance is essential in patients with tibia fractures to monitor for ACS, especially when PNB is utilized.

articles.title: Undertriage of Pediatric Major Trauma at a Spanish Pediatric Trauma Center: A 10-Year Retrospective Cohort Study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Accurate field triage is a cornerstone of an inclusive trauma system, but pediatric undertriage remains poorly characterized outside North America. We aimed to estimate the rate of major trauma undertriage in a Spanish pediatric trauma center, to identify patient factors associated with it, and to explore its relationship with early clinical outcomes.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Retrospective cohort study (2016-2025) of children aged 0-14 years admitted to the pediatric intensive care unit (PICU) of the reference pediatric trauma center for the province of Granada, Spain. Major trauma was defined using a composite of the Cribari Matrix (ISS > 15) and/or the Need for Trauma Intervention (NFTI) criteria. Undertriage was defined as delayed (>2 h) or non-direct transport to the trauma center despite proximity (<30 min). The primary outcomes were the undertriage rate and the patient factors associated with it, examined by bivariate analysis and by Firth-penalized logistic regression with intercept correction (FLIC). Clinical outcomes (Glasgow Outcome Scale, PICU and total hospital length of stay) were prespecified as exploratory and analyzed with generalized linear models-binomial for binary outcomes and negative binomial for counts-and, as a sensitivity analysis, with targeted maximum likelihood estimation (TMLE).

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Out of 1716 PICU admissions during the study period, 157 (9.1%) were due to injury, 131 (7.6%) were eligible traumatic injuries and 94 (5.5%) children met major trauma criteria (median age 8.0 years; 73.4% male; 78.7% blunt trauma; and median ISS 18.5). The undertriage rate was 23.4% (22/94; 95% CI 15.3-33.3). No patient characteristic differed significantly between undertriaged and correctly triaged children. Undertriaged children tended to be older (median 11.0 vs. 7.0 years; p = 0.117), and the overall association between age category and undertriage did not reach significance in the FLIC model (p = 0.069). One child (1.1%) died in PICU and 75 (79.8%) achieved a good functional recovery (Glasgow Outcome Scale 5). Undertriage was not associated with functional outcome, PICU length of stay or total hospital length of stay in either unadjusted or adjusted analyses.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Nearly one in four children with major trauma who reached this pediatric trauma center met the predefined criteria for undertriage. This rate should be interpreted as undertriage conditional on arrival at the Pediatric Trauma Center and not as a system-level or provincial estimate. Multicenter prospective studies using standardized definitions and incorporating prehospital transport data are needed to better characterize the population-level burden and clinical impact of pediatric undertriage.

articles.title: Single crash, multiple stories: A finite mixture perspective of motorcycle injury severity with a focus on post-crash medical, rescue, human and roadway-environmental factors.

abstract.text: This study investigates the factors, including post-crash medical conditions (i.e., Glasgow Coma Score "GCS", Systolic Blood Pressure "SBP"), emergency response (i.e., pre-hospital time and mode of evacuation), human factors, and roadway-environment, affecting the Injury Severity Score (ISS) in motorcycle crashes. Utilizing a comprehensive hospital-based dataset in Karachi, Pakistan, and after addressing the issues of missing or inappropriate values via synthetic data generation, a Tobit regression (baseline) model was first employed in a corner solution setup. Harnessing 204,503 hospital-based motorcycle crash records (2007-2015) from Karachi (Pakistan), missing and inappaorpirate values were addressed through synthetic data generation. A baseline model and a finite mixture Tobit model (accounting for unobserved heterogeneity) were employed. The findings from the baseline model indicate that compared to mild/normal GCS (13-15) and SBP (> 89 mmHg), for crash victims with severe GCS (3-8) and severely low SBP (2-49 mmHg), the ISS significantly increases by 4.5249 and 7.8042 units, respectively. A positive non-linear association between prehospital time (PHT) and ISS was established. The baseline model recognizes over-speeding, nighttime crashes, wrong-way riding or driving, and involvement of multiple vehicles to significantly increase ISS by 0.1909, 0.0198, 0.0787, and 0.3333 units, respectively. The finite mixture Tobit model identifies two latent classes of crash victims with dissimilar ISS patterns and varying relationships of key correlates with ISS, indicating that reliance on a standard Tobit model could lead to misleading inferences. The practical implications are discussed in the paper.

articles.title: Effectiveness of a Physical Exercise Prescription Program in Primary Care to Improve Physical Fitness and Quality of Life in Adults Aged 65 Years and Older in a Rural Basic Health Area-Study Protocol for a Randomized Controlled Trial (PREFIS-AP).

abstract.text: Physical inactivity contributes substantially to morbidity, disability, functional decline, and premature mortality in older adults. General physical activity counselling in primary care does not necessarily translate into structured, individualized exercise prescription. PREFIS-AP evaluates a standardized Exercise Prescription Program embedded in routine rural primary care for community-dwelling adults aged 65 years and older. PREFIS-AP is a single-center, pragmatic, parallel-group randomized controlled trial with 210 planned participants allocated 1:1 to a 12-week individualized multicomponent Exercise Prescription Program or usual primary care. The intervention combines clinical and functional assessment, an electronic health record decision-support module, and multicomponent exercise. The primary outcome is the 12-week Six-Minute Walk Test (6MWT) distance adjusted for baseline distance. Secondary outcomes include physical activity, health-related quality of life, strength, lower-limb function, anthropometry, medication burden, and safety; rectus femoris morphology assessed by point-of-care ultrasound is exploratory. The primary analysis will follow the intention-to-treat principle and compare 12-week 6MWT distance between groups adjusted for baseline distance. PREFIS-AP will evaluate the clinical effectiveness and feasibility of integrating structured exercise prescription into routine rural primary care. Limitations include the single-center setting, inability to blind participants and intervention providers, additional exercise-professional support, and 12-week follow-up. Secondary and exploratory analyses are not independently powered.

articles.title: Remote patient monitoring and caregiver education for children with failure to thrive: a quasi-experimental study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Failure to Thrive (FTT), also known as growth or weight faltering, is characterized by inadequate weight gain, poor growth, and potential developmental delays. Affecting up to 10% of outpatient pediatric populations and 5% of hospitalized children, FTT is particularly common among children with medical complexity. Traditional management depends on frequent in-person visits, which create barriers and delay interventions. To address these barriers, this study evaluated Remote Patient Monitoring (RPM) combined with caregiver education as a proactive, cost-conscious approach to FTT management.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A quasi-experimental cohort study was conducted with children (ages 1-10 years) with FTT and requiring feeding tube support. Families transmitted weekly weight and feeding data using Bluetooth-enabled scales, supplemented by structured caregiver education. Outcomes included weight, hospital and emergency department (ED) utilization, and cost of care.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: All 15 participants completed the six-month RPM program. Forty-two percent of participants (n = 6) achieved upward weight trends, 50% (n = 8) maintained stable weights, and 8% (n = 1) experienced a weight decline. Hospitalizations averaged 0.33 per patient pre-intervention, 0.60 during the intervention, and 0.33 post-intervention. Median hospitalizations were 0 (Q1 = 0, Q3 = 0) pre-intervention, 0 (Q1 = 0, Q3 = 1) during the intervention, and 0 (Q1 = 0, Q3 = 0.5) post-intervention. Emergency department visits averaged 1.07 pre-intervention, 0.60 during the intervention, and 0.87 post-intervention. Median ED visits were 0 (Q1 = 0, Q3 = 1) pre-intervention, 0 (Q1 = 0, Q3 = 1) during the intervention, and 1 (Q1 = 0, Q3 = 2) post-intervention. Median costs increased during the intervention phase before declining in the post-intervention period, despite mean costs being skewed upward by high utilizers.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: An RPM program integrated with caregiver education demonstrated feasibility in supporting proactive management of pediatric FTT. The intervention supported weight monitoring in this medically complex pediatric population, although healthcare utilization and costs varied across study periods. These preliminary findings support RPM may be a useful approach for managing pediatric FTT.

articles.title: Case Report: Longitudinal multimodal imaging and microperimetry findings in PAMM: apparent capillary rarefaction and persistent sensitivity loss across 28 months.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Paracentral acute middle maculopathy (PAMM) is classically associated with retinal vascular occlusion or systemic vasculopathy. We describe an atypical presentation of isolated PAMM occurring in close temporal association with the abrupt withdrawal of systemic pharmacotherapy in the setting of isolated marked proteinuria, including a 28-month longitudinal analysis of structural and functional outcomes.

abstract.label: PATIENT PRESENTATION
abstract.text: A 37-year-old male with a history of asymptomatic proteinuria presented with acute paracentral scotomas shortly after discontinuing a short course of azilsartan and hydroxychloroquine. Multimodal imaging, including spectral-domain optical coherence tomography (SD-OCT) and OCT angiography (OCTA), revealed focal inner nuclear layer (INL) infarction and deep capillary plexus (DCP) hypoperfusion, consistent with isolated PAMM in the absence of macroscopic vascular occlusion. The patient received hyperbaric oxygen therapy (HBOT) during the acute phase; a subsequent transient improvement in localized retinal sensitivity was observed, but best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) stabilized at 20/40. However, serial microperimetry demonstrated a transient improvement in localized macular sensitivity from 3 weeks to 9 weeks post-onset, followed by a marked secondary decline from 9 weeks to 28 months. This late-stage functional loss was topographically coupled with progressive INL and outer plexiform layer (OPL) atrophy, alongside apparent capillary rarefaction on OCTA.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Acute hemodynamic changes following medication withdrawal, combined with a potential hypercoagulability or prothrombotic risk from proteinuria, may have contributed to the development of isolated PAMM. The long-term visual prognosis is closely associated with progressive microvascular dropout and retinal atrophy. Serial microperimetry is essential to evaluate the true functional impairment in these patients.

articles.title: Locating automated external defibrillators in urban areas: considering different travel modes.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) is a time-critical emergency in which rapid access to automated external defibrillators (AEDs) can improve survival. However, most AED location studies assume a single travel mode and often use population alone as a proxy for demand. This study investigates how travel-mode assumptions affect AED accessibility and optimal deployment and develops a risk-informed multimodal spatial optimization framework.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Using Wuhan, China, as a case study, an age-risk-weighted potential OHCA demand surface was constructed from 17,842 ambulance dispatch records and age-stratified population data across 1,161 1-km grid cells. The existing 3,569 AEDs were treated as fixed facilities. Accessibility was evaluated under driving, cycling, walking, Drive + Walk, and Cycling + Walk scenarios using a 4-min response threshold. Multimodal extensions of the Location Set Covering Problem (LSCP) and Maximal Covering Location Problem (MCLP) were applied to identify full-coverage requirements and priority locations.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Baseline demand-weighted coverage varied substantially by travel mode: 85.07% for driving, 68.27% for cycling, 31.55% for walking, 53.65% for Drive + Walk, and 45.41% for Cycling + Walk. The additional AEDs required for universal coverage ranged from 68 under driving to 521 under walking, with 327 required under Drive + Walk. Under the first-phase MCLP strategy, 65 new AEDs increased Drive + Walk demand-weighted coverage to 73.31%. Sensitivity analysis confirmed that the main findings were robust to alternative mode weights.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: AED accessibility and optimal deployment are highly sensitive to responder mobility assumptions. Incorporating heterogeneous travel modes and age-specific OHCA risk can support more realistic, spatially targeted, and resource-efficient AED planning.

articles.title: Supporting adolescents with self-harm: practitioners' experiences of delivering a rapid brief psychological intervention to adolescents presenting to Emergency Departments.
articles.journal_full: Frontiers in child and adolescent psychiatry

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: The risk of suicide is increased amongst young people following attendance at the Emergency Department (ED) for self-harm. Evidence is limited for effective interventions. Early intervention is crucial before self-harm becomes established as a coping mechanism. The Supporting Adolescents with Self-Harm (SASH) intervention focuses on supporting young peoples' agency and resources-comprising Therapeutic Assessment, Enhanced Safety Planning and Solution-Focused Follow-Up sessions-and was evaluated in a randomised controlled trial.

abstract.label: AIM
abstract.text: To explore the experiences of CAMHS crisis team practitioners delivering the SASH intervention to young people presenting to EDs with self-harm in the SASH trial.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: The trial assessed the effectiveness of the SASH intervention. This study forms part of the qualitative process evaluation exploring the experiences of practitioners delivering the intervention. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 15 practitioners who delivered the intervention and four senior staff members. Interviews were analysed using thematic analysis.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Six overarching themes were identified: (1) A transformation in practice, bridging the gap in crisis care by offering an immediate therapeutic intervention and time to build rapport and work with the system around young people; (2) Patient-centred care that builds shared understanding of the reasons underlying self-harm between the young person, carer and practitioner; (3) Harnessing young people's strengths and motivating change; (4) Carer involvement in individual/joint sessions leads to better outcomes when the young person wants them involved and they are available; (5) SASH worked well for most young people, although it may be less suited to those who are less able to express themselves, or have complex difficulties or difficulties that are outside their control; and (6) At first, a paradigm shift for practitioners from focusing on problems to solutions, but over time practitioners gained confidence and motivation in using the SASH intervention and continue to use it in their practice.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: The SASH intervention offers continuity of care after ED attendance for young people following a self-harm crisis by focusing on building shared understanding of the underlying reasons for self-harm and harnessing their strengths, bridging the gap in crisis care. Supporting carers may also improve outcomes for young people.

abstract.label: CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION
abstract.text: https://www.isrctn.com/, identifier ISRCTN81846131.

articles.title: Predicting documented prior intentional self-harm in emergency departments: an interpretable gradient boosting approach using European injury surveillance data.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Prior intentional self-harm history is the strongest predictor of completed suicide, yet this information frequently goes uncommunicated during emergency department (ED) presentations. We developed an interpretable gradient boosting model (XGBoost) to predict whether a patient's record in the European Injury Database (EU-IDB) carries a documented prior self-harm flag, using injury characteristics, demographics, and clinical features available at ED attendance.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: The raw dataset comprised 62,467 attendances for intentional self-harm from 18 countries (2008-2023), with 86.2% of outcomes coded Unknown. Formal missingness analysis showed that observed outcome missingness was overwhelmingly explained by country membership (country alone: pseudo-R2 = 0.537, AUC = 0.948) and that documentation was positive-biased: across countries, the sparser the documentation, the higher the positivity among documented records (Spearman ρ = 0.882). A three-step "Third Way" strategy excluded three countries with structurally absent outcome protocols and defined the target as a documented positive flag vs. its absence, yielding an analytical dataset of 26,554 records (prevalence 13.7%), three times larger than the complete-case alternative.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: XGBoost achieved AUC-ROC = 0.800 (95% CI 0.783-0.816), AUC-PR = 0.380, and Brier score = 0.100, significantly outperforming logistic regression (DeLong p = 3.93 × 10-10). At the optimised threshold (0.080), sensitivity was 80.8%, specificity 62.8%, NPV 95.4%. A time-zero model restricted to variables available at triage achieved AUC-ROC = 0.762 (0.745-0.780) and retained its advantage over the linear baseline (0.729, 0.712-0.746). SHAP analysis identified proximal risk factor documentation, place of occurrence, and patient age as dominant predictors, and a sensitivity analysis excluding the ProximalRiskFactor variable (AUC-ROC = 0.765) confirmed robustness to a potentially circular feature. A country prediction test (95.3% accuracy, 14.3× chance) quantified substantial implicit geographic encoding in the clinical features, offering a plausible explanation for the gap between test-set AUC-ROC (0.800), temporal validation (0.674) and group-aware cross-validation (0.658). Country-stratified assessment revealed adequate calibration in most settings but miscalibration in low-volume countries, and fairness analysis identified lower sensitivity in older adults (68.0%; AUC-ROC 0.722, 95% CI 0.617-0.822) as a critical limitation.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: This model could serve as a decision support layer within ED workflows, but requires local validation, country-specific recalibration, and embedding within structured post-identification care pathways before deployment.

articles.title: Verbal de-escalation techniques for the prevention and management of workplace violence in healthcare: a systematic review.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Workplace violence (WPV) remains a significant and escalating challenge across healthcare settings, threatening the safety, well-being, and retention of frontline healthcare professionals (HCPs). Verbal de-escalation is widely promoted as a first-line strategy to prevent or manage aggressive patient behavior. However, the scope, implementation, and effectiveness of these techniques have not been consistently synthesized.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This systematic review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA guidelines. Studies were eligible if they examined verbal de-escalation as a primary strategy for preventing or managing WPV in healthcare settings, including hospitals, emergency departments, psychiatric units, long-term care, and outpatient clinics. All study designs were considered, including empirical research and structured descriptive guidance relevant to clinical practice. Searches were conducted in Ovid MEDLINE ALL, Embase, Emcare, PsycINFO, and CINAHL from database inception, with results downloaded on August 29, 2024, and updated on January 30, 2026. Of 15,987 records identified, 9,096 were screened following duplicate removal, 446 underwent full-text review, and 36 studies met inclusion criteria. Methodological quality was appraised using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT).

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Substantial heterogeneity was observed in how verbal de-escalation was defined, delivered, and evaluated. Intervention studies commonly assessed structured training programs delivered through didactic sessions, interactive workshops, simulation-based education, technology-enhanced learning, or clinical unit-based training. These studies frequently reported improvements in staff knowledge, confidence, and preparedness to manage aggression. Observational and descriptive studies emphasized communication behaviors used during escalated encounters and highlighted recurring strategies, such as empathetic listening, calm verbal tone, validation, and collaborative problem-solving. Outcome measures varied considerably across studies, limiting direct comparison.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Verbal de-escalation represents a central component of WPV prevention in healthcare, yet implementation approaches and evaluation methods remain inconsistent. The evidence suggests associations with improved clinician confidence, reduced patient agitation, and enhanced perceptions of safety. Healthcare organizations can use these findings to strengthen training curricula, integrate de-escalation within broader safety frameworks, and support sustainable workforce protection strategies.

articles.title: Diagnostic and therapy gaps in BPPV care: a retrospective analysis and feasibility evaluation across a London NHS trust.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Benign paroxysmal positional vertigo (BPPV) is the most prevalent cause of peripheral dizziness, yet it remains poorly assessed and treated in acute settings. Despite the availability of validated bedside tools such as the Dix-Hallpike test (DHT) and canal repositioning manoeuvres (CRM) such as the Epley, diagnostic variability is high, neuroimaging is overused, and vestibular suppressants are frequently prescribed. This two-part evaluation characterised BPPV assessment and management across a London NHS Trust and assessed the feasibility of incorporating DHT into an existing AHP-led falls pathway within the emergency department (ED).

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A two-part evaluation was conducted across a large London NHS teaching hospital. Part 1 comprised a retrospective review of electronic patient records to characterise current BPPV assessment and management practices and identify potential service gaps. Part 2 was a prospective feasibility study evaluating the incorporation of AHP-led DHT screening into routine falls assessments for patients aged ≥65 years presenting to the ED.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Part 1 identified 128 cases (mean age 63.4 years; 61.7% female). BPPV was the most common discharge diagnosis, 45.3% (95% CI 37.0-53.9%), yet full assessment and treatment were documented in only 14.8% of cases (95% CI 9.7-22.0%). Vestibular suppressants were prescribed in 43.8%, neuroimaging performed in 71.9 and 18.8% left without a definitive diagnosis. Readmission for dizziness within three months occurred in 13.3% (95% CI 8.5-20.2%). Part 2 included 102 patients, 79 with complete records (mean age 84.6 years; 54% female). DHT was completed in 62% (63/102 attempts; 95% CI 52.1-70.6%); BPPV was identified in 8% (95% CI 4.0-14.7%) and all received CRM. No dizziness-related readmissions occurred at three months.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: This evaluation identifies consistent gaps in acute BPPV assessment and management, including overuse of neuroimaging and vestibular suppressants alongside underutilisation of validated bedside tools. Physiotherapy led DHT screening is feasible in a busy ED setting, even in older adults with multiple comorbidities, and the absence of readmissions in this small feasibility cohort is an encouraging finding that warrants evaluation in a larger, controlled cohort.

articles.title: The HALF-IT score: proposing a simplified mechanical thrombectomy triage tool for basilar artery occlusion.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Basilar artery occlusion (BAO) is a devastating subtype of stroke with poor prognosis. Current patient selection tools for endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) are multi-tiered with interrater variability and limited validation studies. The HALF-IT score is a novel, simplified, dichotomized triaging tool focusing solely on the brainstem level. This study investigated the utility of the HALF-IT score to predict functional outcomes of EVT in patients with BAO.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a multicenter, retrospective, cohort study including patients with acute BAO presenting to four comprehensive stroke centers between 2021-2025. Acute infarction of ≥50% of any brainstem section on any axial or coronal slice of MRI was considered HALF-IT positive, whereas < 50% was considered HALF-IT negative. The primary efficacy outcome was a favorable functional outcome, defined as a modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score of 0-3 at 90 days; functional independence (mRS 0-2) was analyzed as a secondary outcome. Reperfusion was graded with the modified Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction (mTICI) scale. Primary safety endpoints included symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage at 24 h and all-cause mortality at 90 days. Multivariable logistic regression was performed to identify independent predictors of the primary efficacy outcome.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: 37 patients (23 HALF-IT negative; 14 HALF-IT positive) met the inclusion criteria. The rate of 90-day mRS 0-3 was significantly lower in the HALF-IT positive compared with HALF-IT negative group [14.3% vs. 68.2%, OR 0.08 (0.01-0.45), p = 0.004]. HALF-IT positive status remained associated with a lower rate of 90-day mRS 0-3 after adjusting for age, initial NIHSS, onset-to-reperfusion time, intravenous thrombolysis administration complete reperfusion (final mTICI 3) [adjusted OR 0.02, 95% CI 0-0.84, p = 0.02]. Safety events were numerically higher in the HALF-IT positive group but the difference did not reach statistical significance. The two groups differed substantially at baseline in age, presenting NIHSS, and intravenous thrombolysis exposure, whereas stroke etiology (p = 0.28) and level of basilar occlusion (p = 0.63) were similarly distributed.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: In this small, retrospective, hypothesis-generating cohort, HALF-IT positivity was associated with worse 90-day functional outcomes after EVT for BAO. Further prospective validation in larger cohorts is required before the score can inform treatment decisions.

articles.title: Interprofessional collaboration in emergency department nursing care for patients with diabetic ketoacidosis: a narrative review.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) is an acute metabolic emergency requiring timely risk recognition, fluid resuscitation, insulin therapy, electrolyte correction, dynamic monitoring, and coordinated care transitions. These interdependent tasks pose substantial challenges to emergency nursing. This narrative review aimed to synthesise current evidence on interprofessional collaboration in emergency DKA nursing and propose a conceptual framework to support coordinated care.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A structured narrative review was conducted using literature retrieved from PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, CINAHL, and the Web of Science Core Collection from database inception to July 10, 2026. DKA-specific clinical and implementation evidence was integrated with broader literature on interprofessional collaboration, communication, and healthcare implementation. The evidence was synthesised using Donabedian's structure-process-outcome framework.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Current collaborative approaches include nurse-led standardised pathways, risk-stratified subcutaneous insulin and non-intensive care unit management, collaborative medication management, laboratory and point-of-care monitoring, structured communication, digital decision support, and multidisciplinary discharge planning. Available evidence suggests that standardised collaborative pathways may improve the timeliness and consistency of care, shorten emergency department length of stay, and reduce intensive care resource use. However, evidence evaluating complete interprofessional nursing teams and nursing-sensitive outcomes remains limited. Based on the synthesis, a conceptual closed-loop collaboration framework comprising six interconnected stages was proposed: recognition and activation, shared risk stratification, coordinated monitoring and execution, escalation, care transition, and recurrence prevention.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: Effective interprofessional DKA nursing requires shared clinical information, explicit responsibility, timely feedback, and predefined escalation procedures, with emergency nurses serving as continuous information integrators and process coordinators. The proposed framework provides an evidence-informed approach to organising collaborative emergency care. However, it has not been prospectively validated, and further implementation research is required to evaluate its feasibility, safety, and effects on nursing-sensitive and patient outcomes.

articles.title: Case Report: Severe acute hypermagnesemia following inadvertent bath agent ingestion rapidly resolved by emergent hemodialysis.

abstract.text: Severe acute hypermagnesemia from excessive magnesium (Mg2+) exposure is rare but life-threatening and requires prompt recognition. We report a 54-year-old previously healthy man who presented to the emergency department with acute altered consciousness and generalized weakness. Physical examination showed stupor, hypothermia, hypotension, and generalized areflexia. Initial laboratory testing demonstrated mixed respiratory and metabolic acidosis, a normal serum creatinine concentration, and severe hypermagnesemia (serum Mg2+ concentration, 15.8 mg/dL). The initial 12-lead ECG demonstrated diffuse ST-segment depression, and an artificial intelligence-enabled electrocardiography (AI-ECG) model identified an estimated mortality risk above the 99th percentile. Nasogastric decompression retrieved minimal gastric contents, and initial treatment with intravenous calcium, saline, and a loop diuretic did not produce meaningful neurological improvement. Emergent hemodialysis resulted in rapid recovery of consciousness and a decrease in serum Mg2+ to 4.9 mg/dL during treatment, together with neurological improvement and a marked decline in AI-ECG-predicted mortality risk. Subsequent history-taking indicated inadvertent ingestion of approximately 100 mL of a private-label artificial hot-spring mineral preparation, for which spa personnel reported a nominal formulation of 30% magnesium chloride, 33% magnesium sulfate, and 10% potassium sulfate. He recovered without residual complications. This case emphasizes that a normal serum creatinine concentration at presentation does not preclude life-threatening magnesium toxicity after a large acute Mg2+ exposure. Timely hemodialysis should be considered when severe symptoms persist despite initial therapy.

articles.title: Zolpidem Intoxication Associated with Probable Reverse Stress-Induced Cardiomyopathy and QT Prolongation: A Case Report.

abstract.text: Zolpidem is a widely prescribed non-benzodiazepine hypnotic. A 49-year-old woman presented to the emergency department with altered mental status after intentional ingestion of approximately 300 mg of zolpidem; the blood zolpidem concentration was 674 µg/L approximately 8 h after ingestion. The initial ECG already showed QTc prolongation (499 ms). She developed chest discomfort and modest high-sensitivity troponin T elevation, and echocardiography showed transient left ventricular dysfunction (ejection fraction 42%) with basal-to-mid regional wall motion abnormalities and relative apical sparing, suggestive of probable reverse stress-induced cardiomyopathy. Coronary computed tomography angiography showed no coronary plaque or significant stenosis. On hospital day 2, telemetry captured a brief monomorphic ventricular run and QTc later peaked at 681 ms. Follow-up echocardiography on hospital day 5 showed recovery of left ventricular systolic function (LVEF 60%) and resolution of the regional wall motion abnormalities. These findings cannot be attributed solely to zolpidem. Stress may have contributed to the cardiomyopathy. Mild hypokalemia and left ventricular dysfunction may have reduced repolarization reserve. The peak QTc occurred after blood zolpidem concentrations had substantially decreased and may have reflected evolving stress-induced cardiomyopathy or concurrent exposure to cardiovascular medications. Cardiac evaluation and continuous monitoring should be considered when zolpidem intoxication is accompanied by cardiac symptoms, biomarker elevation, or ECG abnormalities.

articles.title: Personalized Management Strategies in Traumatic Spinal Cord Injury: From Resuscitation to Definitive Surgical Care.

abstract.text: Personalized management of traumatic spinal cord injury (TSCI) is an emerging approach in modern spine and trauma care. Unlike traditional protocol-driven approaches that apply uniform resuscitation, imaging, and surgical strategies across heterogeneous injury patterns, individualized care pathways that account for biological, physiological, and injury-specific variability may improve neurological outcomes and resource utilization. This review summarizes contemporary concepts in personalized TSCI management spanning prehospital and initial hospital care, resuscitation, imaging, and definitive surgical decision-making. The proposed framework is informed by evidence from clinical trials, observational studies, and emerging consensus statements, emphasizing stratified approaches based on neurological status, injury mechanism, physiological reserve, and imaging biomarkers. Selective spinal motion restriction, hemodynamic support within guideline ranges, and early decompression are supported by current guidelines, albeit based largely on low-quality evidence, whereas individualized hemodynamic targets, advanced neuroimaging, blood-based biomarkers, and artificial intelligence-based risk stratification remain emerging strategies that require prospective validation before routine clinical use. In conclusion, personalized management across the continuum of TSCI care provides a rational framework with potential clinical applications, although its effect on patient outcomes remains to be demonstrated.

articles.title: Combined Approach with Ultrasound and Pressure-Volume Loops to Manage Mechanical Ventilation in Acute Hypoxemic Respiratory Failure.

abstract.text: Acute hypoxemic respiratory failure (AHRF), particularly acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), is characterized by marked heterogeneity in lung morphology and mechanics, requiring individualized mechanical ventilation strategies that balance adequate gas exchange with the prevention of ventilator-induced lung injury (VILI). Lung ultrasound (LUS) has become a cornerstone of critical care imaging, allowing differential diagnosis, quantitative assessment of lung aeration, phenotyping of ARDS morphology, and monitoring of disease evolution and complications. However, imaging alone does not provide direct guidance for optimizing ventilator settings. Some modern ventilators enable the rapid bedside acquisition of tidal pressure-volume (PV) loops, allowing tidal hysteresis to be measured and thereby providing complementary physiological information by identifying cyclic opening and closing of lung units and signs of overdistension. Emerging evidence supports the use of tidal hysteresis thresholds to identify insufficient positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP) associated with tidal recruitment/derecruitment and to guide individualized PEEP titration during decremental PEEP trials. This review discusses the rationale and practical implementation of an integrated approach combining critical care ultrasound and PV loops throughout the management of mechanically ventilated patients with AHRF. We describe how ultrasound can support diagnosis, phenotyping, monitoring of lung aeration, and detection of ventilation-related complications, while PV loops provide a practical physiological framework for optimizing ventilator settings. This approach may provide a comprehensive, non-invasive, and repeatable bedside assessment of lung morphology, aeration, and respiratory mechanics, potentially facilitating personalized mechanical ventilation strategies aimed at reducing the risk of VILI and optimizing patient management.

articles.title: Peripheral vascular trauma in a civilian Asian trauma centre: Epidemiology, management and outcomes over 9 years.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Peripheral vascular injuries (PVI) are uncommon but potentially limb-threatening complications of extremity trauma. Most existing literature originates from military settings or Western trauma systems. We aimed to describe the epidemiology, management strategies, and outcomes of traumatic PVI in a civilian tertiary trauma centre in Singapore.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A retrospective cohort study was conducted using the institutional trauma registry of Tan Tock Seng Hospital between January 2013 and December 2021. Patients presenting with upper or lower extremity vascular injuries were identified using Abbreviated Injury Scale (AIS) coding. Demographics, injury characteristics, anatomical injury patterns, interventions, and outcomes including limb salvage, complications, and inpatient mortality were analysed. Comparisons between upper and lower limb injuries were performed using appropriate statistical tests.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 77,990 trauma admissions, 180 patients sustained PVI (incidence 0.23%). Median age was 36 years and 87% were male. Overall, penetrating trauma was more common (58.9%), but lower limb injuries were predominantly due to blunt trauma (68%), particularly road traffic accidents. Lower limb PVIs were associated with higher injury severity than upper limb PVIs (p < 0.001). Operative management was required in most arterial and venous injuries. Primary repair and endovascular interventions demonstrated excellent limb salvage, whereas bypass procedures were associated with lower salvage rates. Overall limb salvage for lower limb PVI was 88%, with an amputation rate of 10% and mortality of 3%. Most (93%) were functionally independent at discharge.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: PVI predominantly affects young male patients and are commonly associated with blunt trauma from road traffic accidents. Despite significant injury severity, favourable limb salvage and functional outcomes can be achieved with timely multidisciplinary management. These findings highlight the importance of coordinated multidisciplinary trauma care in optimizing outcomes following extremity vascular trauma.

articles.title: Intestinal Mature B-Cell Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma Presenting as an Acute Surgical Abdomen in Children: A Case Series.

abstract.text: Intestinal mature B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma (B-NHL) is the most common pediatric gastrointestinal lymphoma, but presentation as acute mechanical bowel obstruction remains rare and still challenging. Evidence guiding emergency surgical management in children is limited to small retrospective series and case reports. This case series describes three children with intestinal B-NHL presenting with acute mechanical bowel obstruction, or intussusception. All three patients presented to the emergency department with signs of bowel obstruction and an acute abdomen, and in one patient initial diagnosis suggested appendicitis. Imaging revealed either intussusception with a lead mass or large obstructing abdominal tumors. Surgery within 8-48 h consisted of segmental bowel resection with primary anastomosis in all cases. The final diagnoses were Burkitt lymphoma in two patients and diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) in one. The wider literature confirms that lymphoma-related intussusception and obstructing ileal masses occur predominantly in older children, are frequently misdiagnosed preoperatively, and often require emergency surgery both for diagnosis and for treatment of obstruction. Available literature has examined outcomes after emergency surgery for intestinal lymphoma, but the present case series cannot determine its independent effect on long-term oncologic prognosis. Pediatric intestinal B-NHL can present as acute mechanical bowel obstruction or intussusception suggesting common surgical conditions. Surgeons play a crucial role in early recognition, appropriate extent of resection, and timely transition to oncologic care. Further multicenter studies are needed to optimize surgical decision-making and quantify outcomes in this rare but life-threatening presentation.

articles.title: Operational review of WHO health emergency response in Sudan.
articles.journal_full: Eastern Mediterranean health journal = La revue de sante de la Mediterranee orientale = al-Majallah al-sihhiyah li-sharq al-mutawassit

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: The armed conflict in Sudan has disrupted essential health services and displaced millions of people since April 2023, with an estimated 30.4 million people requiring humanitarian assistance as of 2025.

abstract.label: AIM
abstract.text: To assess the operational strengths, challenges and gaps in the WHO-led health emergency response in Sudan across incident management system domains.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: From July to August 2025, we conducted a descriptive operational review of WHO and partner documents on the health emergency response in Sudan for April 2023 to July 2025 and held a structured consultation with 48 WHO headquarters, Eastern Mediterranean regional office and Sudan country office staff. We analysed the findings using the WHO Emergency Response Framework 2.1 and 6 incident management system domains.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Through the WHO-supported services, nearly 300 000 people received treatment for trauma and emergency conditions, more than 500 000 received primary health care and nearly 294 000 were reached through the mobile health teams. More than 700 000 people have received medicines for chronic diseases. Insecurity, funding shortage, workforce gaps, weak surveillance, and logistic constraints have limited service coverage, particularly in hard-to-reach areas. Fragmented coordination and data systems further reduced operational effectiveness.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Strengthening leadership, coordination, surveillance, financing, and operational systems is essential to sustain lifesaving interventions and reduce morbidity and mortality in Sudan.

articles.title: Hyperbaric oxygen therapy timing, early neurohemodynamic response and functional outcome in acute ischemic stroke.

abstract.text: The optimal timing of HBOT initiation after AIS remains uncertain, particularly in relation to early cerebral hemodynamic responses and subsequent functional outcome. The present study determined whether hyperbaric oxygen therapy (HBOT) initiation timing was associated with early neurohemodynamic response and 90-day functional outcome among patients with acute ischemic stroke (AIS) who received HBOT within 72 h of symptom onset. In the present single-center, retrospective, exposure-stratified cohort study, patients were grouped according to HBOT initiation at <24 h, 24 to <48 h or 48 to 72 h following symptom onset. No non-HBOT comparator was included. The primary outcome was favorable functional status at 90 days, defined as a modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score of 0-2. Secondary analyses assessed early transcranial Doppler (TCD)-defined hemodynamic response, early neurological response, ordinal 90-day mRS shift, an exploratory treatment-emergent integrated early neurohemodynamic response phenotype and safety. Multivariable logistic regression, ordinal logistic regression and robustness analyses used the 48 to 72 h window as the reference. Among the 429 patients, HBOT initiation at <24 h (odds ratio (OR)=2.68; 95% CI, 1.55-4.63; P<0.001) and 24 to <48 h (OR=1.72; 95% CI, 1.04-2.82; P=0.033) was associated with greater odds of a favorable 90-day functional outcome than initiation at 48 to 72 h. Both earlier windows were also associated with greater odds of a lower 90-day mRS category (common OR=2.44; 95% CI, 1.53-3.88; P<0.001; common OR=1.68; 95% CI, 1.09-2.57; P=0.017). TCD hemodynamic response was more frequent in both earlier windows (P<0.001 and P=0.043), whereas a higher rate of early neurological response and a lower rate of early neurological deterioration were observed only in the <24 h window (P=0.003 and P=0.025, respectively). The exploratory integrated early neurohemodynamic response phenotype was associated with favorable functional outcome at 90 days (OR=2.95; 95% CI, 1.76-4.92; P<0.001). Safety outcomes did not differ significantly across initiation windows. Among HBOT-treated patients with AIS, earlier initiation was associated with more favorable early neurohemodynamic and neurological responses and improved 90-day functional outcomes, without evidence of increased safety events. As the present observational study included no non-HBOT comparator, the present findings do not establish HBOT efficacy relative to standard care without HBOT or a causal benefit of earlier initiation. Residual confounding and treatment-selection bias remain possible.

articles.title: Adjunctive hyperbaric oxygen therapy for post-stroke cognitive impairment: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To evaluate the effects of adjunctive hyperbaric oxygen therapy (HBOT) on cognitive, neurological, and functional outcomes in patients with post-stroke cognitive impairment (PSCI), and explore potential sources of heterogeneity.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Eight databases were searched from inception to July 15, 2026. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating adjunctive HBOT in patients with PSCI were included. The primary outcome was the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA); secondary outcomes included the Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE), National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS), Modified Barthel Index (MBI), and Barthel Index (BI). Random-effects meta-analyses, prespecified subgroup analyses, and meta-regression were performed. Sensitivity analyses, funnel plots, Egger's tests, and GRADE assessments were conducted.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Thirty-five RCTs involving 3,036 participants, all conducted in China, were included. Adjunctive HBOT was associated with higher MoCA scores (MD = 2.90, 95% CI: 2.47-3.33; p < 0.00001; I 2 = 84%) and MMSE scores (MD = 2.68, 95% CI: 2.20-3.16; p < 0.00001; I 2 = 83%). Improvements were also observed in NIHSS (MD = -2.61, 95% CI: -3.34 to -1.89; p < 0.00001; I 2 = 93%), MBI (MD = 6.64, 95% CI: 3.76-9.52; p < 0.00001; I 2 = 82%), and BI (MD = 8.77, 95% CI: 4.72-12.82;p < 0.00001; I 2 = 82%). No statistically significant subgroup differences were observed for MoCA (p = 0.10) or MMSE (p = 0.43). Higher baseline MoCA scores tended to be associated with smaller treatment effects in meta-regression (β = -0.1411, p = 0.0637; R 2 = 15.42%). Substantial heterogeneity remained largely unexplained. Evidence certainty was low for MoCA, MMSE, and MBI and very low for NIHSS and BI.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Adjunctive HBOT may provide cognitive and functional benefits in patients with PSCI. However, substantial unexplained heterogeneity, low-to-very-low certainty of evidence, and the exclusively Chinese evidence base warrant cautious interpretation and limit generalizability. Further well-designed RCTs involving diverse populations are needed.

abstract.label: SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION
abstract.text: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261473579, PROSPERO, CRD420261473579.

articles.title: The predictive model of intra-arrest blood markers for the sustained return of spontaneous circulation in patients with out-of-hospital cardiac arrest.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: This study aimed to investigate the predictive value of intra-arrest blood markers, including blood routine, blood biochemistry, and coagulation profile, during cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) for the return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) in patients with out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA).

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A retrospective cohort of patients who experienced OHCA and admitted to the emergency department of a tertiary hospital in Zhejiang Province, China, between January 2021 and December 2025 was assembled. Their clinical and demographic data were collected, and missing values were addressed using multiple imputation. Physiologic laboratory markers obtained during resuscitation were compared between the sustained ROSC and non-ROSC groups. Candidate predictors were selected based on clinical relevance, previous literature, availability at the intended prediction time point, and univariable screening, with age and gender retained as prespecified demographic covariates. Model discrimination for the prediction of sustained ROSC was evaluated using a receiver operating characteristic analysis and the area under the curve (AUC).
