Internal validation was performed using bootstrap resampling to assess model stability and quantify potential overfitting.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 283 patients were included, and among them, 94 (33.22%) achieved sustained ROSC. Missing data were handled using multiple imputation (m = 20). In univariable analyses, the sustained ROSC group had higher PCO2, platelet count, white blood cell count, and absolute lymphocyte count; higher admission glucose, fibrinogen, and serum calcium levels; shorter chest compression duration and prothrombin time; and lower epinephrine dose, serum potassium level, and international normalized ratio than the non-sustained ROSC group (all P < 0.05). A multivariable logistic regression model incorporating age; gender; white blood cell count; platelet count; blood PCO2 measured during CPR; capillary blood glucose level on admission; and fibrinogen, serum potassium, and serum calcium levels yielded a mean apparent AUC of 0.832 across the imputed datasets. After internal validation with 500 bootstrap resamples, the optimism-corrected AUC was 0.807 and the bootstrap-derived calibration slope was 0.853. The final model is given as follows: logit[P(ROSC=1)] = -2.65-0.002 × age-0.790 × gender + 0.076 × white blood cell count + 0.001 × platelet count + 0.010 × PCO2-0.011 × admission glucose + 0.145 × fibrinogen-0.247 × serum potassium+0.633 × serum calcium.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: In patients who experienced OHCA, higher white blood cell count and lower serum potassium levels were associated with a higher incidence of sustained ROSC. Female patients were more likely to achieve sustained ROSC than male patients. Although the model showed certain predictive value for sustained ROSC, further multicenter, large-scale studies are needed in the future.

articles.title: Reported infant safety information and perinatal service engagement among birth partners and co-parents. An exploratory cross-sectional survey at a large UK teaching hospital.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Infant mortality in the United Kingdom is higher in areas of socioeconomic deprivation and within several minority ethnic groups. Preventive strategies rely in part on safety information reaching families during the perinatal period. The extent to which birth partners and co-parents report exposure to that information is not well characterised.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To describe self-reported exposure to selected infant safety topics and reported engagement with perinatal services among birth partners and co-parents attending one large UK teaching hospital, and to explore variation across respondent profiles defined by ethnicity and parity.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: An exploratory cross-sectional survey of 73 birth partners and co-parents was conducted at University Hospitals Leicester NHS Trust between October 2022 and July 2023. Eight self-reported knowledge or awareness items and six self-reported engagement items were collected. Item-level proportions were summarised with Wilson 95 percent confidence intervals. Group comparisons used Fisher's exact test with Haldane-corrected prevalence ratios and Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment applied separately within each demographic comparison. Composite Knowledge Proportion Scores and Engagement Proportion Scores were computed for respondents with at least half of the relevant items answered. Internal consistency was estimated with the Kuder-Richardson 20 coefficient, association with Spearman's rank correlation, and group differences with the Mann-Whitney U test. Reporting follows the STROBE statement for cross-sectional studies.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Reported exposure was highest for smoking risk (69.9 percent, 95 percent CI 58.6-79.2) and lowest for basic bystander life support (17.8 percent, 95 percent CI 10.7-28.1). Engagement was highest for NHS website use and post-birth breastfeeding support (both 61.6 percent, 95 percent CI 50.2-71.9) and lowest for antenatal classes (24.7 percent, 95 percent CI 16.2-35.6). Composite scales showed high internal consistency (KR-20 of 0.94 for knowledge, 0.93 for engagement). The two composite scores were strongly correlated (Spearman's ρ = 0.965, p < 0.001). Ethnicity and parity were completely confounded in the usable sample, with all first-time parents identifying as White British and all respondents in the combined Other category identifying as experienced parents. Observed differences between these respondent profiles cannot be attributed independently to ethnicity or parity.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: In this exploratory single-site sample, self-reported exposure to practical infant emergency-care topics was low. Substantial differences were observed between two contrasting respondent profiles, although the confounded design and small convenience sample do not support causal claims about ethnic inequities or infant mortality risk reduction. The findings are hypothesis-generating and support the case for larger, more diverse studies designed to separate the contributions of ethnicity, parity, and other social determinants.

articles.title: Case Report: Favorable long-term outcomes of autologous PRF-augmented delayed replantation for traumatic avulsion of three mandibular anterior teeth with 10-year follow-up.

abstract.text: The first-line treatment for permanent tooth avulsion is immediate replantation. Delayed replantation is associated with a high risk of survival-related complications, such as root resorption. Autologous platelet-rich fibrin (PRF) may promote the periodontal healing of delayed-replanted avulsed teeth and may potentially reduce the occurrence and progression of early root resorption. This case report explores the dental treatment process of autologous PRF-assisted delayed replantation in an adult patient with the avulsion of three mandibular anterior teeth. After an accident, the patient wiped the roots of the avulsed teeth and stored them in dry tissue. Two hours later, the patient visited the emergency department for treatment. On the same day, PRF granules were prepared, and the teeth were replanted with the granules and fixed with semi-elastic splints. The treatment was based on the 2012 guidelines of the International Association of Dental Traumatology. Two weeks later, the patient returned, and root canal treatment was performed, the fixation device was removed at the same visit. Two weeks after intracanal medication with calcium hydroxide, root canal filling was completed. Follow-up visits at 3, 6, and 12 months and up to 10 years after the trauma revealed no clinical symptoms in the affected teeth, and radiography showed no sign of root resorption. The patient expressed satisfaction with both the esthetic and functional outcomes. This case report describes a favorable outcome following PRF-assisted replantation of delayed-replanted avulsed teeth. The findings suggest a potential adjunctive role of PRF in promoting periodontal healing, which warrants further investigation.

articles.title: Sacral Fractures Are Increasing in Frequency, with Females and Falls Comprising the Majority: A NEISS Cross-Sectional Study from 2003 to 2022.

abstract.text: Background/Objectives: Sacral fractures are clinically important injuries that may be occult at presentation and may occur after both low-energy falls and higher-energy trauma. National emergency department data describing temporal trends, mechanisms, associated fractures, and disposition remain limited. Methods: A retrospective cross-sectional study was performed using the National Electronic Injury Surveillance System from 2003 to 2022. Sacral fracture emergency department visits were identified using diagnosis and body-part codes with narrative confirmation of sacral involvement. National estimates were generated using NEISS survey weights. The primary outcome was population-based ED visits per 100,000 United States population, overall and stratified by sex. Secondary outcomes included mechanism category, injury location, concurrent vertebral or hip fracture, and emergency department disposition. Results: A total of 1747 sacral fracture emergency department visits were identified, representing an estimated 72,215 national visits. Low-energy falls accounted for 67.9% of presentations. Mean age was 61.1 years, and 70.0% of patients were female. Injuries most commonly occurred at home (50.5%). Annual ED visit rate increased from 2003 to 2022, with a steeper rise among females than males. Disposition varied by mechanism. Motor vehicle or transport-related injuries had the highest admission or hospitalization proportion (54.6%), whereas high-energy falls had the highest treated-and-released proportion (62.0%). In survey-aware multinomial regression, increasing age was associated with lower odds of high-energy falls, motor vehicle or transport injuries, and non-fall other injuries compared with low-energy falls. Male sex was associated with motor vehicle or transport mechanism. Conclusions: National emergency department presentations for sacral fractures increased from 2003 to 2022 and were dominated by low-energy falls among older female patients. However, transport-related and higher-energy mechanisms showed distinct demographic and disposition patterns. These findings supported trauma-system awareness, mechanism-informed co-injury screening, and orthopedic or spine referral pathways for sacral fracture presentations.

articles.title: Impact of frequent emergency department visits on resource utilization.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Emergency department (ED) utilization continues to rise globally, and a disproportionate share of visits is attributable to a small subgroup of patients. This subgroup is referred to throughout the present report by the single term high-frequency users (HFUs), defined as patients with four or more ED visits within a 12-month period. Characterizing the clinical profile, utilization patterns and cost structure of HFUs is relevant to emergency care planning and resource allocation.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective, single-center observational study analyzed all adult ED presentations at a high-volume urban tertiary hospital over a 12-month period. HFU status was defined at the patient level as four or more ED visits within the study period. The unit of analysis was specified for every comparison: age, sex, the ICD-10 diagnostic spectrum and all logistic regression models were analyzed at the patient level (one observation per unique patient), whereas triage category, timing of presentation, mode of arrival, resource utilization and per-visit costs were analyzed at the visit level. For the regression models, visit attributes and diagnostic categories were aggregated to the patient level as ever/history indicators. Groups were compared using the Mann-Whitney U and Pearson chi-square tests, with effect sizes reported alongside p values.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 466,884 unique adult patients accounting for 726,696 ED presentations, 26,871 patients (5.8%) were HFUs. HFUs represented 5.8% of adult patients but accounted for 148,322 of 726,696 presentations (20.4%) and approximately one-fifth (21.0%) of cumulative laboratory, imaging and medication costs. Total cost per visit was similar between groups (median 6.39 USD in both; p = 0.647), and differences in individual cost components, although statistically significant, were small in practical terms (rank-biserial correlations +0.03 for laboratory, -0.05 for radiology and +0.08 for medication cost). A higher proportion of HFU than non-HFU presentations involved any laboratory test (29.3% vs 26.7%) and any medication order (57.8% vs 51.4%), whereas any radiologic imaging was less frequent among HFUs (40.5% vs 44.7%). HFUs were marginally younger, presented more often during the night shift and were less likely to arrive by ambulance (3.5% vs 5.0%). Yellow-triage presentations predominated among HFUs, and symptom-based and pain-related diagnoses were over-represented. In the patient-level multivariable model, male sex, a history of yellow- or red-triage presentation, a history of evening- or night-shift presentation and multiple symptom-based diagnostic groups were associated with HFU status, whereas a history of ambulance arrival was associated with lower odds.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: HFUs constitute a small proportion of adult ED patients but account for a disproportionate share of presentations and of cumulative diagnostic and pharmacologic resource use. Because total cost per visit was similar between the groups and the differences in individual cost components were small in practical terms, the principal finding is the cumulative resource burden associated with repeated attendance rather than a higher cost of the individual encounter. This pattern is consistent with a contribution of out-of-hours access and symptom-driven presentation; however, the present observational data cannot establish these mechanisms or identify which interventions would reduce frequent ED use.

articles.title: Latent class phenotypes and emergency department disposition for patients with traumatic subdural hematoma and midline shift.
articles.journal_full: The American journal of emergency medicine
authors: Johns Hopkins Neurotrauma Research Group (Tej D. Azad)

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Guidelines recommend surgical evacuation for traumatic subdural hematoma (SDH) with >5 mm midline shift (MLS), but emergency department (ED) triage varies between the operating room (OR) and the intensive care unit (ICU). We investigated whether ED disposition to the OR versus ICU was associated with differences in outcomes and whether distinct patient phenotypes modified these associations.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We retrospectively identified adult patients from the ACS TQIP dataset with traumatic SDH, MLS >5 mm, and ED disposition to either the ICU or OR. We defined patient phenotypes using latent class analysis (LCA) and investigated associations between ED disposition and outcomes (inpatient mortality, favorable discharge) using risk-adjusted hierarchical logistic regression. We tested for interaction between patient phenotype and ED disposition and repeated these analyses among patients undergoing an ICU stay ≥1 day and cranial surgery.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 9582 patients, 29% (N = 2794) were triaged to the OR. Two LCA-informed phenotypes emerged: class 1 (older-mild injury) and class 2 (younger-severe injury). There was an interaction between ED disposition and patient phenotype, such that younger-severe patients had lower mortality with OR triage (P < 0.001). In the subgroup of 4573 patients (48%) with ≥1 day of ICU stay who underwent cranial surgery, there was a significant interaction between OR triage and the older-mild phenotype indicating increased mortality (P = 0.003).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: For traumatic SDH with MLS >5 mm, triage the OR was associated with improved outcomes only among younger, severely-injured patients, while older, mildly-injured patients may benefit from early ICU stabilization. These findings support phenotype-guided ED triage strategies to optimize outcomes.

articles.title: Prioritizing Emergency Medical Conditions for Health Policy Using a Stepwise Treatable-Death Framework: A Nationwide Analysis in Korea, 2018-2022.

abstract.text: Background/Objectives: Limited emergency-care resources require priorities based not only on mortality rates or death counts but also on the potential mortality reduction under explicit targets. We applied the age- and sex-standardized domestic short- and mid-term components of a stepwise treatable-death framework across severe emergency conditions in Korea. Methods: This retrospective nationwide study used NEDIS aggregate data from 16 regions during 2018-2022. The 20 conditions with the highest numbers of in-hospital deaths were represented as 17 groups by replacing sepsis (A41), bacterial pneumonia (J15), pneumonia of unspecified organism (J18), and pneumonitis due to solids and liquids (J69) with an extended-sepsis composite. Treatable deaths were the positive difference between observed and target-based expected deaths. National rates in 10-year age-group and sex strata were applied to regional distributions. The short-term target assumed that regions with an age- and sex-standardized mortality ratio (SMR) above 1.0 achieved the national reference level (SMR = 1.0), whereas the mid-term target assumed that all regions achieved the lowest regional SMR for the corresponding condition and year. Five-year cumulative estimates were the primary outcome measure. Results: Across the 17 groups, summed condition-level patient counts totaled 3,384,529 and in-hospital deaths totaled 357,404 (ratio of summed death counts to summed patient counts, 10.56%). Five-year cumulative short-term estimates were highest for extended sepsis (2387), bronchus and lung cancer (1984), and cardiac arrest (1662). Mid-term estimates were highest for cardiac arrest (21,547), extended sepsis (19,340), and severe trauma (7010). Conclusions: After accounting for regional differences in age and sex distributions, extended sepsis remained the condition with the largest short-term and the second-largest mid-term treatable-death burden, supporting its consideration for further policy-priority evaluation. Each treatable-death estimate is an operational policy-scenario estimate rather than an estimate of causally preventable mortality.

articles.title: Epidemiology, Clinical Characteristics, and Hospitalization Patterns in Children Aged ≤72 Months with Traumatic Head Injury: A 16-Year Single-Center Study.

abstract.text: Purpose: To characterize hospitalized children aged ≤72 months with traumatic head injury at a Serbian tertiary pediatric center, evaluate factors associated with severe clinical course as the primary patient-level outcome, and describe temporal patterns in hospitalization among head-injury presentations. Methods: This retrospective single-center study covered 2010-2025. Patient-level data were available for hospitalized children, while annual aggregate counts described head-injury presentations. Severe clinical course was defined as recorded GCS ≤ 8 on admission, surgical intensive care unit admission, and/or surgical intervention. Multivariable logistic regression evaluated associated factors, and quasi-binomial regression examined temporal changes in hospitalization proportions. Results: A cohort of 971 hospitalized children was analyzed. Over the study duration, a decrease in the absolute number of head injury evaluations was observed, whereas the proportion of hospitalizations increased from 11.6% to 58.0%. The predominant mechanism of injury was domestic falls from heights. Most children (98.2%) were managed conservatively. A severe clinical course was documented in 70 children (7.2%). Factors significantly associated with higher odds of a severe clinical course included infancy (age ≤ 12 months), ambulance transport, inter-institutional transfer, and traffic-related incidents. Conclusions: The distinctive finding was a rising hospitalization proportion despite fewer head-injury presentations. This describes changing service use rather than establishing an increase in injury severity or identifying avoidable admissions. The findings support evaluation of local admission and observation pathways and improved clinical documentation; the causes of the temporal trend require further study.

articles.title: Factors Associated with Complications in Pediatric Foreign Body Ingestion: A Retrospective Cohort Study of 754 Children.

abstract.text: Background/Objectives: Foreign body (FB) ingestion is a common reason for pediatric emergency department visits. Although most ingested FBs pass spontaneously, a minority cause serious complications, and rapid identification of high-risk ingestions is crucial. We aimed to describe the management strategies and to identify clinical and FB-related factors associated with complications. Methods: We retrospectively reviewed 754 children aged <18 years who presented to a tertiary pediatric emergency department with FB ingestion between 2016 and 2022. FB types, anatomical locations, clinical findings, interventions, and complications were analyzed. Univariate logistic regression was used to screen candidate variables, followed by a parsimonious multivariable model limited to a single non-redundant variable per clinical domain to identify factors independently associated with complications. Results: Of the 754 children, 434 (57.6%) were male, with a median age of 3.6 years. Coins were the most commonly ingested objects (41.8%). Spontaneous passage occurred in 572 (75.9%) cases, while 182 (24.1%) required intervention, most commonly endoscopy (18.0%). Complications occurred in 29 children (3.8%), including 9 (1.2%) with major complications. Major complications occurred almost exclusively with button batteries in the upper esophagus and with multiple magnets and sharp objects in the stomach or intestines. Although intervention was required in 22.5% of coin ingestions, the complication rate was only 0.3%. In multivariable analysis, vomiting (odds ratio [OR], 5.65), sharp or pointed objects (OR, 6.34), and pharyngeal or esophageal location (OR, 12.57) were independently associated with complications. Conclusions: These interrelated features may help emergency physicians identify children who need closer evaluation, but they require prospective validation before being used for clinical prediction.

articles.title: Gastrointestinal point-of-care ultrasound for enteral nutrition management in critically ill adults: a scoping review.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Gastrointestinal point-of-care ultrasound has been investigated as a non-invasive, bedside adjunct for gastrointestinal assessment and enteral-feeding decision-making in critical care; however, existing protocols and their outcome reporting remain fragmented. This scoping review mapped the existing evidence landscape on the use of gastrointestinal point-of-care ultrasound in the management of enteral nutrition in critically ill adults.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Comprehensive searches in 10 databases (PubMed, EMBASE, Web of Science, Cochrane, CINAHL, Scopus, China National Knowledge Infrastructure, Wanfang, VIP, China Biological Medicine Literature Database) identified 5,123 records. Studies focusing on ultrasound-assessed gastrointestinal function to guide enteral nutrition, or to predict enteral nutrition intolerance and clinical prognosis, were screened, summarized, and descriptively analyzed.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: 49 unique studies were identified, including 36 interventional and 13 observational studies. Geographically, the synthesized evidence was heavily concentrated in China. Ultrasound indicators for gastrointestinal function included the gastric antrum (gastric residual volume, motility index, cross-sectional area), colon (colon diameter and peristaltic frequency), small intestine (small intestine diameter, wall thickness, peristalsis), and superior mesenteric artery hemodynamics. Observational studies showed Area Under the Curve point estimates frequently around or above 0.70, with substantial heterogeneity and no independent external validation reported for enteral nutrition intolerance and mortality. Among interventional studies, time to achieve feeding goals and intensive care unit length of stay were the most frequently evaluated outcomes (27/36), whereas in-hospital mortality was evaluated in only 8 of 36 studies; outcome reporting was heterogeneous and is presented descriptively.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The synthesized literature suggests the potential utility of gastrointestinal point-of-care ultrasound as an objective, non-invasive bedside tool for gastrointestinal assessment and feeding protocol modulation. However, because no formal critical appraisal or pooled comparative or diagnostic analysis was performed, this review cannot establish clinical effectiveness, universal thresholds, or patient-important benefit. Future research priorities include consensus definitions and acquisition standards, effect estimates with confidence intervals and patient-important outcomes, inter-operator reliability and training evaluation, and external validation across diverse health systems.

articles.title: Population aging and the spatial equity of prehospital emergency medical resources: evidence from Shanghai's five new towns.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: China is undergoing rapid urbanization and profound population aging, presenting the prehospital emergency medical system with the dual challenges of inadequate capacity and spatial mismatch. Shanghai's five new towns are strategic vehicles for the spatial restructuring of a megacity; however, evidence is still lacking as to whether their prehospital emergency systems can meet the aging-driven increase in demand.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To evaluate the spatial equity of emergency medical resource allocation in the five new towns and to analyze its associations with population aging and future demand.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Based on 2024 data, the Gini coefficient and Theil index were used to evaluate equity; population projections were performed using the cohort-component method in PADIS-INT (population analysis software); resource requirements were estimated in stages according to policy standards; and coverage gaps were identified through isochrone analysis in QGIS (open-source geographic information system).

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The population-based Gini coefficients across the five districts ranged from 0.03 (substations) to 0.10 (physicians), indicating relatively equitable per capita allocation. However, after including all 16 districts of the municipality, the area-based Gini coefficient for substations reached 0.61, reflecting a gradient in substation density between the urban core and the suburbs. Under the medium scenario, the population aged 65 years and older in Jiading increases from 13.18% to 19.15% (2035), and the demand for R1 standard ambulances in Jiading New City is projected to rise from 24 vehicles in 2025 to 29 vehicles in 2035. In Fengxian, patients aged 60 years and above accounted for 48.49% of emergency calls. Highly aged subdistricts spatially overlapped with 8 min coverage blind spots. Notably, stratified emergency response time (ERT) analysis showed that in two of the three districts, the differences in ERT between cardiac arrest and non-emergency patients were not statistically significant (p > 0.05), suggesting limited implementation of dispatch prioritization.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The five new towns exhibit a dual-track pattern of equity in population terms but inequity in spatial terms. Population aging exacerbates inequity through demand expansion, changes in the disease spectrum, and spatial overlap.

articles.title: Natural history and literature review of primary intracranial CIC-rearranged sarcomas: case report.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Intracranial sarcomas are particularly rare primary central nervous system malignancies. Here we report the complete oncologic course of a patient diagnosed with a primary intracranial CIC-rearranged sarcoma with subsequent intracranial spread.

abstract.label: CASE PRESENTATION
abstract.text: A 36-year-old female patient with a prior history of melanoma presented to the emergency department with sudden-onset headaches and paresthesia. After workup demonstrated an intracranial lesion, she underwent gross total resection, with pathology showing primary intracranial sarcoma. She completed adjuvant radiation with an excellent local response. Unfortunately, she developed distant intracranial parenchymal lesions, managed by further resection, radiotherapy, and systemic therapy. One year after initial diagnosis, she presented with profoundly altered mental status with both local and distant intracranial failure, and she passed away a few days later.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: CIC-rearranged sarcomas are very rare malignancies and should be managed by a multidisciplinary team. While aggressive local failures are reported in these malignancies, here we report an anomalous pattern of rapid distant intracranial spread.

articles.title: Exploring the impact of legislative absences on the working environment of gig workers in South Africa.

abstract.text: This study pursues two objectives. Empirically, it examines how legislative exclusion is produced in South Africa and how gig workers experience it in their everyday working lives. Theoretically, it develops an interpretive account of the relationship between political and economic processes that are ordinarily treated as separate domains, reading political and regulatory exclusion as constitutive of the forms of economic insecurity and precarity that participants describe rather than as their determinant. The study is framed by the concept of legislative exclusion, understood as the process through which state action constitutes a category of workers as falling outside the scope of labor law; precarity, platform capitalism and algorithmic management are used to elaborate the processes through which that exclusion operates and the conditions with which it is associated. A qualitative phenomenological design was adopted. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 10 purposively sampled gig workers in Johannesburg working across e-hailing, delivery, freelancing and content creation, and the data were analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis. The sample spans two structurally distinct segments of platform labor, which are analyzed separately throughout: location-based work (e-hailing and delivery), which is geographically tethered, capital-intensive for the worker and in principle regulable by the national state; and remote online work (digital freelancing and social media content creation), which is contracted across borders and mediated by clients and monetization programs rather than by dispatch algorithms. The analysis reads exclusion as actively produced rather than merely absent: a statutory definition of the employee that platform work is arranged to fall outside, a jurisdictional architecture that renders the responsible corporate entity difficult to reach, and a recent transport regulation that recognizes e-hailing while leaving the employment relationship untouched. These instruments do not bear on the two segments equally: the transport regulation reaches location-based drivers alone, whereas remote online workers are addressed by no domestic instrument at all. Exclusion is in turn bound up with unbounded working hours, exclusion from employment benefits and the absence of any accessible dispute-resolution forum, though it is lived differently in each segment. Location-based participants described unreviewable deactivation and the transfer of vehicle, fuel and licensing costs; online participants described client non-payment, unenforceable informal agreements and dependence on opaque monetisation and visibility rules. The study contributes an interpretive account in which legislative exclusion is understood as a structuring condition through which risk is transferred to workers, platform and client authority is rendered unreviewable, and disadvantage is compounded over time.

articles.title: A Simplified Physiology-Laboratory Score (PLS4) for Early Risk Stratification in Acute Cholangitis.

abstract.text: Objectives: Acute cholangitis is a common biliary infection in the emergency department (ED) that can progress rapidly to septic shock and multiorgan dysfunction. The Tokyo Guidelines 2018 (TG2018) is the current reference standard for severity assessment but may be cumbersome during the initial ED encounter. We aimed to develop a simplified physiology-laboratory score (PLS4) computable from four routine bedside variables and to compare its early risk-stratification performance with TG2018. Materials and Methods: This single-center retrospective observational cohort study included 482 adult patients with acute cholangitis (International Classification of Diseases, 10th Revision code K83.0) presenting to a tertiary university hospital ED between January 2016 and December 2021. Primary outcomes were ICU admission, vasopressor use, and prolonged hospital stay (length of stay ≥ 14 days); intubation was analyzed as an exploratory outcome. PLS4 assigned 1 point each for albumin < 3.5 g/dL, systolic blood pressure ≤ 100 mmHg, heart rate ≥ 100/min, and prothrombin time-international normalized ratio ≥ 1.2 (range 0-4). Discrimination was assessed by receiver operating characteristic curves, with bootstrap 95% confidence intervals and bootstrap optimism-corrected internal validation. Results: ICU admission occurred in 81 patients (16.8%), vasopressor use in 53 (11.0%), and prolonged stay in 111 (23.0%). The areas under the curve (AUCs) for ICU admission were 0.850 for TG2018 and 0.800 for PLS4 (p = 0.116), and the optimism-corrected AUC of PLS4 was 0.779. For vasopressor use, which is part of the TG2018 grade III definition, the AUCs were 0.936 and 0.843. When PLS4 was added to TG2018, the AUC for ICU admission increased to 0.886. At PLS4 ≥ 3, specificity reached 0.978 for ICU admission and 0.970 for vasopressor use, with event rates rising stepwise from 5.96% to 100% and 2.55% to 90.0%, respectively. Conclusions: In this single-center derivation study, PLS4 showed high specificity and added prognostic information to TG2018. It should be validated in other centers before clinical use.

articles.title: Telemedicine in Disaster Medicine-Use of Paramedics as Tele-Consultants to Guide Personnel with Limited Medical Training at the Disaster Site.

abstract.text: Background/Objectives: Disaster medicine is frequently constrained by shortages of highly qualified medical personnel. Telemedicine may extend advanced expertise to less-qualified responders, but previous disaster telemedicine models have predominantly relied on physicians as remote consultants. This study compared patient care outcomes under telemedical support provided by experienced Paramedics with tele-physician support, conventional on-site physician care, and EMT-only care. Methods: A prospective, simulation-based, controlled quasi-experimental study was conducted during a 7.5-h mass casualty exercise in Hamburg, Germany. Seven treatment tents were assigned to four groups: on-site physician (CONT), EMT-only care (IV 1), tele-physician support (IV 2), and tele-Paramedic support (IV 3). Outcomes comprised time to first treatment order, indicated treatments addressed, analgesia management, and patient contact frequency by the most highly qualified team member. Results: A total of 151 simulated patients were included. Time to first treatment order did not differ significantly between groups (p = 0.09). The proportion of indicated treatments addressed differed significantly (p < 0.001), with rates of 56% in CONT, 8% in IV 1, 57% in IV 2, and 51% in IV 3. Analgesia was addressed in 68%, 7%, 59%, and 60% of patients with an indication, respectively (p < 0.001). Increasing pain intensity significantly increased the likelihood of analgesia in CONT, IV 2, and IV 3 but not in IV 1. Recorded patient contact frequencies were descriptively higher in the telemedicine groups, although contacts were operationally defined differently between telemedicine and non-telemedicine models. Conclusions: Tele-physician and tele-Paramedic support showed similar observed performance across selected outcomes to conventional physician-led care and substantially better rates of indicated treatments addressed and analgesia provision than EMT-only care. The findings indicate that experienced Paramedics may represent a valuable additional resource for telemedical disaster response. Larger studies are needed to confirm these results, define the appropriate scope of practice, and evaluate tiered consultation models in which tele-Paramedics provide first-line support and tele-physicians remain available for escalation of complex cases.

articles.title: Association between polypharmacy and perceived multidimensional social support in geriatric patients with minor trauma.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: This study aimed to examine the relationship between polypharmacy, perceived social support, and medication adherence among geriatric patients presenting to the emergency department with minor trauma.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A total of 72 geriatric individuals (≥65 years) presenting with minor trauma were included. Participants completed the Morisky Medication Adherence Scale-8 (MMAS-8; coded so that higher scores indicate poorer adherence) and the Multidimensional Scale of Perceived Social Support (MSPSS). Sociodemographic characteristics, living arrangement, place of residence, and medication use were recorded.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The mean age was 78.0 ± 7.82 years, and 54.2% of participants were female. The mean MMAS-8 score was 1.69 ± 2.38 (median = 0), indicating a highly right-skewed distribution. Medication adherence did not differ significantly across medication-count categories or by polypharmacy status (all P > 0.05), although MMAS-8 scores were numerically lower among participants with polypharmacy (≥5 medications). Perceived social support was substantially lower among participants living alone (all MSPSS subscales, P ≤ 0.001). MMAS-8 scores showed a weak negative correlation with family support (rₛ = -0.243; P = 0.040), whereas correlations with significant-other support and total support were not statistically significant (P > 0.05). Higher educational attainment was associated with higher perceived social support.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Among older adults presenting with minor trauma, perceived social support - particularly family support -was associated with better medication adherence, while living alone was linked to substantially lower support. The observed trend toward better adherence in the polypharmacy group should be interpreted cautiously. Multidisciplinary approaches integrating medication review and attention to social support may be beneficial in both emergency and primary care settings.

articles.title: Paramedic attitudinal profiles regarding pediatric pain management: A latent class analysis in a standardized emergency medical services system.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: Pediatric pain is frequently under-recognized and undertreated in prehospital emergency care despite guideline-based recommendations, and practice variation may persist even within standardized emergency medical services (EMS) systems.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a prospective, cross-sectional survey of paramedics working in a nationally standardized EMS system in Türkiye to identify latent attitudinal (self-reported) profiles related to pediatric prehospital analgesia and to examine whether profile membership differed by demographic or professional characteristics. Attitudinal items underwent exploratory dimensionality assessment and were then modeled using latent class analysis.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 129 paramedics, two profiles were identified: proactive/system-oriented (57.4%) and conservative/low-engagement (42.6%). The proactive/system-oriented profile reported higher endorsement of decision-support tools (mobile drug-dosing applications and in-ambulance analgesia algorithms), more consistent self-reported post-analgesia vital sign monitoring, and greater self-reported use of non-pharmacologic adjuncts. The conservative/low-engagement profile reported lower intended engagement with these self-reported practices and greater reliance on perceived barriers. Profile membership was not associated with age, sex, years of EMS experience, or prior training.

abstract.label: CONCLUSİON
abstract.text: Distinct attitudinal (self-reported) profiles regarding pediatric prehospital analgesia were identified; whether these profiles translate into objectively observed analgesia delivery requires validation using routine documentation and, where feasible, linked ED outcomes.

articles.title: Systemic epinephrine toxicity following topical epinephrine gauze use during burn debridement.

abstract.text: A 54-year-old male with extensive burns caused by a high-voltage alternating current electrical injury underwent three surgical debridement procedures. During the first operation, he developed intraoperative hypertension and tachycardia, followed postoperatively by hypotension, lactic acidosis, hyperglycemia, and hypokalemia, which improved with fluid resuscitation and vasopressor support. Similar hemodynamic and metabolic disturbances recurred during the second debridement. A detailed review of the anesthetic records revealed that epinephrine-soaked gauze had been applied intraoperatively for hemostasis, with vital sign changes occurring shortly thereafter. These findings suggested systemic epinephrine toxicity, followed by hypotension related to antihypertensive therapy. After discussion with the plastic surgery team, topical epinephrine was avoided during the third procedure and replaced with thrombin-soaked gauze, with no recurrence of complications. This case highlights that topical epinephrine used for hemostasis in extensive burn wounds can cause clinically significant systemic toxicity and underscores the importance of interdepartmental communication in preventing perioperative adverse events.

articles.title: Interpreting P values in clinical research: A practical guide for clinicians.

abstract.text: Accurate interpretation of medical literature is essential for evidence-based clinical practice. Among statistical measures, the P value remains one of the most frequently used and most frequently misunderstood concepts in clinical research. Conventionally, a P < 0.05 was considered the primary criterion for determining statistical significance. However, reliance on this threshold alone may lead to overestimation of clinically unimportant findings or failure to recognize clinically meaningful effects in underpowered studies. Recent recommendations emphasize the importance of interpreting P values together with confidence intervals, effect sizes, and study design characteristics. This review discusses the basic principles of P values, common misconceptions, statistical errors, practices that threaten scientific validity, and complementary statistical approaches that can improve clinical interpretation. The aim is to provide clinicians and researchers with a practical framework for evaluating statistical findings in medical studies.

articles.title: A rare cause of pneumomediastinum and descending necrotizing mediastinitis: Untreated odontogenic abscess.

abstract.text: Pneumomediastinum is the presence of free air within the mediastinum and may be primary or secondary. Secondary pneumomediastinum typically follows trauma, invasive procedures, mechanical ventilation, or dental interventions using pressurized air; odontogenic causes without prior intervention are exceptionally rare. We report the case of a 52-year-old male with liver cirrhosis who presented with chest and neck pain 2 days after being diagnosed with a dental abscess and receiving antibiotics, with no dental procedure performed. He had fever, cervical swelling with crepitus, odynophagia, and dysphagia. Computed tomography revealed extensive subcutaneous emphysema tracking from the cervical region into the mediastinum, and inflammatory markers were elevated. He was diagnosed with secondary pneumomediastinum complicated by descending necrotizing mediastinitis and underwent mediastinal exploration and surgical drainage. Cultures grew Parvimonas micra. Postoperatively, he required intensive care and mechanical ventilation for 8 days. With culture-directed antibiotics and multidisciplinary management, he recovered fully and was discharged without sequelae. Anaerobic bacterial gas production may contribute to this rare complication. Clinicians should consider secondary pneumomediastinum in patients with chest and neck pain in the setting of odontogenic infection, even without preceding dental procedures, as early recognition, prompt imaging, surgical drainage, and definitive source control are critical for favorable outcomes.

articles.title: Predicting outcomes in undifferentiated prolonged fever presenting to the emergency department: A prospective study from North India.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: Undifferentiated prolonged fever presenting to the emergency department (ED) poses significant diagnostic and prognostic challenges, particularly in low- and middle-income countries. We aimed to describe the clinical spectrum and in-hospital outcomes of adults presenting to the ED with undifferentiated prolonged fever and to identify the baseline predictors of mortality.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: In this prospective observational study, consecutive patients aged ≥13 years who fulfilled Durack and Street's criteria for fever of unknown origin were enrolled between March 2022 and September 2024 at the ED of a tertiary care center in North India. Patients with immunosuppressive states or nosocomial fever were excluded. All patients underwent a standardized diagnostic evaluation guided by potentially diagnostic clues. Baseline demographic, clinical, and laboratory variables recorded at ED presentation, including complete blood count-derived inflammatory indices, were evaluated as potential predictors of in-hospital mortality using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis and multivariable logistic regression.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 100 patients were enrolled (mean age: 39 years; 57% male), with a median fever duration of 45 days (interquartile range: 30-90). Infections were the most common etiology (37%), with tuberculosis predominating, followed by malignancies (21%), predominantly advanced hematological malignancies, and noninfectious inflammatory diseases (19%), which frequently presented with multisystem involvement, most commonly systemic lupus erythematosus and Still's disease. Despite extensive evaluation, 19 patients (19%) remained undiagnosed. Overall, 25 patients (25%) died during hospitalization, with the highest mortality observed among undiagnosed cases (8/19, 42%). In the univariate analysis, neutrophil percentage, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), aspartate transaminase, and lactate dehydrogenase levels were significantly higher in the mortality group, whereas total protein and albumin levels were significantly lower. ROC analysis demonstrated modest discriminatory ability for NLR (area under the curve: 0.651). In multivariable analysis, admission NLR emerged as the only independent baseline predictor of in-hospital mortality (odds ratio: 1.089 per one-unit increase; 95% confidence interval: 1.006-1.178; P = 0.034).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Undifferentiated prolonged fever presenting to the ED is associated with substantial in-hospital mortality and diagnostic uncertainty. Admission NLR was independently associated with mortality, but discrimination was modest; it may have adjunctive value for early risk stratification pending external validation.

articles.title: Emergency department extracorporeal membrane oxygenation: Current concepts, systems-based implementation, and future directions.

abstract.text: Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) has emerged as a time-critical resuscitative strategy for carefully selected patients with refractory cardiac arrest and other reversible causes of circulatory or respiratory failure. As the role of emergency department ECMO (ED ECMO) continues to expand, emergency physicians have become integral members of multidisciplinary extracorporeal resuscitation teams. This review aims to summarize the current evidence on ED ECMO while highlighting practical considerations for program implementation, workflow optimization, and future directions. This invited narrative review synthesizes contemporary evidence regarding the indications, patient selection, cannulation strategies, pericannulation management, and postcannulation physiological challenges of ED ECMO, with particular emphasis on extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation. In addition to published literature, practical aspects of ED ECMO implementation, including multidisciplinary team organization, operational governance, workflow optimization, quality metrics, and institutional experience, are discussed. Emerging concepts such as artificial intelligence-assisted decision support, digital twin-enabled system modeling, and regional implementation strategies are also reviewed. Current evidence indicates that successful ED ECMO depends not only on technical proficiency but also on timely patient selection, standardized protocols, efficient multidisciplinary coordination, and optimized operational systems. Contemporary implementation frameworks emphasize integrated governance, continuous quality improvement, and structured performance metrics to enhance clinical effectiveness. Emerging digital technologies, including artificial intelligence and systems modeling, may further improve patient selection, operational efficiency, and program scalability. ED ECMO should be regarded as a comprehensive, systems-based resuscitation strategy rather than a standalone rescue procedure. Future progress is likely to depend on the integration of evidence-based patient selection, standardized workflows, multidisciplinary collaboration, intelligent operational systems, and continuous quality improvement. The development of regional ED ECMO networks supported by robust emergency medical service infrastructure may improve timely access to extracorporeal resuscitation and optimize patient outcomes.

articles.title: Inferior vena cava peak velocity versus collapsibility index to predict volume status in patients with gastrointestinal bleeding: A pilot study.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: Patients presenting to the emergency department (ED) with hemorrhagic shock secondary to acute gastrointestinal (GI) bleeding represent a substantial proportion of the critically ill population. Accurate evaluation of intravascular volume status in these patients is crucial for guiding fluid resuscitation. However, the limitations of invasive methods and inferior vena cava (IVC) diameter/collapsibility measurements in assessing intravascular volume have been widely discussed in the literature. Despite their validation, noninvasive hemodynamic monitoring techniques remain underutilized in the ED. Therefore, the present study aimed to investigate the predictive value of IVC blood flow velocity measured by Doppler ultrasonography in intravascular volume assessment and to compare it with the IVC collapsibility index. Electrical velocity measurement was used as a surrogate marker of volume deficit.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Eighteen patients presenting with a preliminary diagnosis of acute GI bleeding were included in the study. The study population consisted solely of patients with suspected hypovolemia; therefore, no normovolemic control group was included in the study. Demographic, vital, and laboratory data were recorded, along with IVC diameter, collapsibility, IVC peak velocity measured by continuous-wave Doppler, and noninvasive hemodynamic monitoring parameters at admission, at the 30th and 60th min, and immediately after completion of fluid replacement. All data were subjected to statistical analysis.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A significant correlation was observed between initial IVC peak velocity and stroke volume variation at admission (P = 0.009). The measurement demonstrated a specificity of 100% and a sensitivity of 84%, although the confidence interval was wide due to the small number of patients without volume deficit. No statistically significant differences were detected at the other time points. This can be explained by the ongoing bleeding and the lack of a valid gold standard.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Measurement of IVC peak velocity was found to be a significant predictor of hypovolemia, although it showed limited utility for volume monitoring. Furthermore, it demonstrated superior performance compared to IVC diameter and collapsibility measurements. However, the study does not evaluate its ability to distinguish hypovolemia from true normovolemia.

articles.title: Early emergency department risk signals in upper gastrointestinal bleeding: The hemoglobin-to-red cell distribution width ratio.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: Upper gastrointestinal bleeding (UGIB) is a common emergency associated with substantial morbidity and mortality. Early risk assessment is important, but some established scores require laboratory or endoscopic data not immediately available. We evaluated whether the hemoglobin (Hb)-to-red cell distribution width ratio (Hb/RDW) at emergency department presentation was associated with intensive care unit admission or mortality during the index episode.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective single-center study included adults presenting with UGIB between 2019 and 2023. Patients with incomplete evaluation, missing Hb or RDW values, or non-UGIB bleeding sources were excluded. Hb/RDW was calculated at presentation. Group comparisons, receiver operating characteristic analyses, and multivariable logistic regression were performed for the primary composite outcome. Additional adjusted models compared Hb/RDW with Hb and RDW individually.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 942 patients, the primary composite outcome occurred in 121 (12.8%). Hb/RDW was lower in patients with the primary outcome (0.398 [0.296-0.539] vs. 0.568 [0.411-0.780]; P < 0.001). Discrimination was moderate (area under the curve: 0.712, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.664-0.757); a threshold near 0.593 yielded sensitivity 0.851 and negative predictive value 0.956. Hb/RDW remained independently associated with the primary outcome (adjusted odds ratio: 0.023, 95% CI: 0.007-0.073; P < 0.001). It performed better than Hb alone and similarly to RDW, with the greatest incremental discrimination when added to the clinical base model. Lower values were also observed in variceal bleeding.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Lower Hb/RDW at presentation was independently associated with adverse outcomes in UGIB and may serve as an adjunctive early triage marker.

articles.title: A case report of autosomal recessive methemoglobinemia in a child.

abstract.text: Methemoglobinemia is a rare hematologic disorder characterized by impaired oxygen delivery due to oxidation of hemoglobin iron from the ferrous (Fe2+) to the ferric (Fe3+) state, leading to elevated methemoglobin (MetHb) levels and cyanosis. We report the case of a 3-year-old female with a history of congenital cyanotic heart disease who presented with worsening cyanosis and was found to have a MetHb level of 49.3%. She responded initially to methylene blue therapy, but levels fluctuated over the following week. Whole-exome sequencing revealed a homozygous missense variant in the cytochrome b5 (CytB5) reductase 3 gene, consistent with autosomal recessive methemoglobinemia due to CytB5 reductase deficiency. The identified variant has not been previously reported and was classified as a variant of uncertain significance. This case underscores the importance of considering hereditary methemoglobinemia in children with unexplained cyanosis and persistent MetHb elevation. Genetic evaluation remains essential in suspected hereditary cases to inform prognosis, guide long-term care, and support family counseling.

articles.title: Heat stroke during the 2025 summer heatwave in Northwestern India: A tertiary care emergency department case series.

abstract.text: Heat stroke is a life-threatening medical emergency, characterized by a core body temperature above 40°C with central nervous system dysfunction. Population living in arid and northwestern regions are particularly vulnerable during prolonged summer heatwaves. This case series describes the clinical spectrum and outcomes of patients with heat stroke presenting to the emergency department of a tertiary care teaching hospital in such a region during the 2025 heatwaves. We retrospectively reviewed 10 consecutive patients with heat stroke admitted between May 1, 2025 and July 31, 2025. Data on demographics, clinical presentation, cooling methods, laboratory parameters, complications, and outcomes were extracted from the medical records. Ten patients (7 male and 3 female) ranged in age from 22 to 78 years; six had classic (nonexertional) heat stroke; and four had exertional heat stroke (EHS). All presented with hyperthermia (mean 41.2°C) and altered mental status, ranging from agitation to coma. The complications were frequent: acute kidney injury occurred in 70% of patients, severe rhabdomyolysis (creatine phosphokinase >10,000 U/L) in 40% (all EHS), hepatic dysfunction in 80%, and disseminated intravascular coagulation in 20%. Rapid, active cooling was initiated in all cases. The overall in-hospital mortality was 20%. This series highlights the severe, multisystem nature of heat stroke in this setting and underlines the importance of early recognition, prompt cooling, and aggressive supportive care.

articles.title: Emergency medicine literature in the Web of Science category "emergency medicine": A bibliometric analysis (1980-2024).

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: The objective is to describe long-term trends in emergency medicine (EM) research output from 1980 to 2024 and to map study designs, conceptual domains, and collaboration structures within the Web of Science (WoS) Category "EM."

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a retrospective bibliometric analysis of records indexed in the WoS Core Collection from January 1, 1980, to December 31, 2024, using the WoS Categories filter "EM." The search was performed on October 3, 2025. Only records with WoS document type "Article" were included. Bibliographic data, including publication year, journal, country, institutions, citations, and indexed keywords/metadata, were extracted. A rule-based text-mining algorithm classified study designs and conceptual domains and was internally validated against a manually reviewed sample of 240 records, showing 75.8% agreement (κ = 0.638) for study design and 86.3% agreement (κ = 0.828) for conceptual domain. Descriptive statistics and VOSviewer-based co-authorship, co-citation, and keyword co-occurrence analyses were performed.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 161,842 records initially identified, 102,561 articles met eligibility criteria. Annual EM publication counts increased after 2000. Health services and systems research and observational clinical studies predominated, whereas randomized controlled trials and qualitative or mixed-methods studies remained uncommon. Trauma, resuscitation, cardiovascular emergencies, and sepsis were longstanding core domains, while digital health, artificial intelligence, point-of-care ultrasound, disaster medicine, and global EM gained prominence after 2010. Collaboration expanded over time, but multinational co-authorship remained limited, and affiliations from low- and middle-income countries were underrepresented.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: EM has evolved into a high-volume, thematically diverse field, but its evidence base remains predominantly observational and geographically imbalanced.

articles.title: Artificial intelligence-guided design of high-entropy materials from bulk to nanoscale.

abstract.text: High Entropy Materials (HEMs) have provided a breakthrough in materials science, moving beyond single-principal-element design to multielement (>5) design with multiple elements in near-equiatomic ratios. This compositional complexity introduces high configurational entropy, stabilizing single solid-solution phases and providing outstanding thermal, mechanical, and functional characteristics to alloys, oxides, carbides and nitrides. Although traditional empirical methods are the cornerstone of materials design, they are less efficient in exploring the vast compositional and processing space in the sphere of HEMs. The recent development of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) has altered the field of HEM research by allowing data-driven prediction of phase stability, structure-property relationships, and processing results, which has tremendously accelerated the process of materials discovery. With the combination of thermodynamic descriptors, including, but not limited to, ΔS mix, mixing enthalpy (ΔH mix), atomic size mismatch (δ), phase purity (Ω), and valence electron concentration (VEC), AI models enable researchers to perform composition and property optimization more easily than ever before. The AI-guided frameworks, despite their limitations like the lack of data, can enable autonomous and high-throughput design of HEMs. This viewpoint reflects recent developments, examples of energy and catalytic processes, and the future outlook and the potential transformative nature of AI to provide next-generation high performance entropy-stabilized materials.

articles.title: Admission Route and In-Hospital Mortality Among Trauma Patients Admitted to a Regional Trauma Center in South Korea: A Retrospective Cohort Study.

abstract.text: Background: Studies comparing interhospital transfer with direct admission have reported inconsistent associations with mortality, and Korean evidence is limited. We evaluated admission-route associations with in-hospital mortality among patients admitted to a South Korean regional trauma center and explored mortality-associated factors after transfer. Methods: This retrospective receiving-center cohort included trauma admissions during 2022-2024. Patients arriving in cardiac arrest who died without return of spontaneous circulation were excluded. Logistic regression estimated adjusted associations; additional analyses varied adjustment sets and cohort restrictions, and transferred-subgroup analyses were exploratory. Results: Among 2464 patients, 1504 arrived directly and 960 were transferred; mortality was 18.6% vs. 12.0%. Transfer was associated with lower adjusted mortality odds (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 0.54; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.39-0.75) within this selected receiving-center cohort. Omitting arrival physiology and injury-to-center time yielded an aOR of 0.42 (95% CI, 0.32-0.55). Age and arrival Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) scores were associated with mortality among transferred patients (aOR, 2.03 [95% CI, 1.68-2.46] for age 70 vs. 60 years and 0.75 [0.71-0.79] per 1-point GCS increase). Conclusions: In this receiving-center cohort, transfer was associated with lower in-hospital mortality. Among transferred patients, older age and lower arrival GCS scores were exploratory prognostic markers. These associations should not be interpreted as causal, because transferred patients had to survive until arrival, prehospital severity was unmeasured, and arrival measures may reflect prior care.

articles.title: Hospital Transfer Decision-Making for Residents with Dementia in Long-Term Care: A Qualitative Study of Interprofessional Perspectives.

abstract.text: Background: Hospital transfers of residents with dementia may provide them with access to acute diagnosis and treatment but also disrupt their continuity of care, which is essential for residents' stability, safety, and quality of care. The aim of this study was to examine how transfer decisions are produced within the organizational context of long-term dementia care and how they may affect continuity of care. Methods: A qualitative descriptive design was used, supplemented by retrospective referral data. The study was conducted in a 200-bed dementia-specialist long-term care facility. Referral records over three years were reviewed to describe transfer patterns, reasons, and outcomes. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 15 nurses and 2 physicians. Referral data were analyzed descriptively, and interviews were analyzed using Reflexive Thematic Analysis (RTA). Results: A total of 578 referrals to hospital emergency departments were identified; 34.9% resulted in hospitalization. Three themes were identified: (1) From recognition to authorization, describing interprofessional hierarchy in referral decision-making; (2) When uncertainty becomes risk, describing how limited diagnostic and treatment capacity shifted decisions toward transfer; and (3) Protecting continuity, describing staff concerns about the disruptive effects of transfer. Overall, decisions were shaped by clinical uncertainty, organizational conditions, and continuity-of-care concerns. Conclusions: Transfer decisions for residents with dementia are context-dependent organizational judgments, not solely responses to acute clinical deterioration. Strengthening institutional capacity, decision-support tools, staff training, and advance care planning may help preserve continuity of care, reduce avoidable disruption, and improve resident safety and quality of care.

articles.title: Comparison of Pulse Palpation and Paramedic-Performed Doppler Ultrasonography for Assessing Distal Circulation After Tourniquet Application: A Randomized Crossover Study.

abstract.text: Background/Objectives: Accurate assessment of distal circulation is essential for confirming effective arterial occlusion after tourniquet application in patients with life-threatening extremity hemorrhage. Although distal pulse palpation is commonly used in prehospital settings, its accuracy may be affected by examiner experience and environmental conditions. This study aimed to compare manual pulse palpation and paramedic-performed Doppler ultrasonography for assessing distal circulation after tourniquet application, using assessor-performed Doppler ultrasonography as the reference assessment. Methods: A prospective randomized crossover study was conducted among 41 actively practicing paramedics. Participants were randomly assigned to one of two assessment sequences: pulse palpation followed by Doppler ultrasonography or Doppler ultrasonography followed by pulse palpation. After standardized tourniquet application to the upper extremity, distal circulation was independently assessed using both methods. Assessor-performed Doppler ultrasonography served as the reference assessment. Sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, positive predictive value (PPV), and negative predictive value (NPV) were calculated for each method. Agreement between the two index tests was evaluated using percent agreement and Cohen's kappa, and assessment times were compared between methods. Results: Among the 41 participants, the reference standard identified distal flow in 18 (43.9%) and absence of distal flow in 23 (56.1%). Relative to the assessor-performed Doppler reference assessment, pulse palpation demonstrated a sensitivity of 66.7% (95% CI, 41.0-86.7), specificity of 87.0% (95% CI, 66.4-97.2), and accuracy of 78.0% (95% CI, 62.4-89.4). In comparison, paramedic-performed Doppler ultrasonography demonstrated a sensitivity of 88.9% (95% CI, 65.3-98.6), specificity of 91.3% (95% CI, 72.0-98.9), and accuracy of 90.2% (95% CI, 76.9-97.3). The PPV and NPV were 80.0% and 76.9% for pulse palpation and 88.9% and 91.3% for Doppler ultrasonography, respectively. Agreement between the two methods was 82.9%, with a Cohen's kappa of 0.65. Mean assessment time was 14.2 ± 6.1 s for pulse palpation and 28.5 ± 10.4 s for Doppler ultrasonography. Conclusions: Paramedic-performed Doppler ultrasonography showed greater concordance with assessor-performed Doppler ultrasonography than pulse palpation for assessing distal circulation after tourniquet application, although it required additional assessment time. Because assessor-performed Doppler ultrasonography served as the reference assessment rather than an independent physiological gold standard, these findings should be interpreted as reflecting agreement with the reference Doppler assessment rather than definitive diagnostic superiority. Handheld Doppler ultrasonography may therefore have a potential role as an adjunct to pulse palpation, particularly when palpation findings are equivocal or objective reassessment of distal flow is required. Further studies using independent reference standards and conducted in real-world prehospital environments are warranted to evaluate its clinical utility, feasibility, and safety.

articles.title: Evaluating a Large Language Model for Emergency Triage Using Synthetic Clinical Dialogues: Toward a Multimodal Clinical Safety Framework.

abstract.text: Background/Objectives: Prioritizing patient safety through accurate emergency triage is critical during mass-gathering events such as Hajj and Umrah, where high patient volumes can significantly increase the risk of clinical errors. Although the Emergency Severity Index (ESI) provides a standardized triage protocol, it remains dependent on human judgment, while traditional artificial intelligence (AI) models often struggle to capture the nuanced clinical context embedded in patient narratives. To address this gap, this study evaluates GPT-5.2 using synthetically generated dialogues as a step toward a conceptual clinical decision-support framework that bridges structured electronic health records (EHRs) with triage interactions through clinical dialogues. By combining narrative inputs with structured physiological indicators, it explores the potential to support more informed clinical decision-making under controlled simulation conditions. Methods: To evaluate this contribution, we systematically assessed the role of clinical dialogues in triage performance using a balanced and stratified dataset of 1000 simulated Hajj-context scenarios. Results: The results demonstrate that incorporating clinical dialogues can significantly improve triage performance, with a 79.7% relative reduction in under-triage across all ESI levels. A more noticeable improvement was observed in high-acuity cases, with a 91.9% relative reduction in under-triage. In addition, the model achieved a high-acuity recall of 94.5%, highlighting its ability to identify critical "red-flag" symptoms that are often not captured in structured data. These findings suggest that narrative context may contribute to more accurate triage assessment and improved identification of high-acuity cases. Conclusions: Consequently, when evaluated within a controlled decision-support setting, this study suggests that large language model (LLM)-based systems may improve triage reliability and may contribute to safer triage decision-making in high-demand clinical environments.

articles.title: Management of transfusion in traumatic hemorrhagic shock.

abstract.label: PURPOSE OF REVIEW
abstract.text: Traumatic hemorrhagic shock remains the leading preventable cause of early trauma death, with most deaths occurring within the first 24 h. This review summarizes recent advances in prediction tools, transfusion protocols, blood products and monitoring strategies for transfusion management.

abstract.label: RECENT FINDINGS
abstract.text: Transfusion management relies on early activation of major hemorrhage protocols and rapid delivery of balanced blood components to limit coagulopathy and restore oxygen delivery. Prehospital transfusion appears most beneficial in the most severely injured patients, particularly with prolonged transport times, though its mortality benefit varies across trauma systems and patient phenotypes. Low-titer group O whole blood simplifies logistics and may improve early hemostasis, but randomized trials have not shown a clear survival advantage over component therapy. Viscoelastic testing complements empirical algorithms by enabling faster, targeted correction of fibrinogen and factor deficiency. Emerging data also highlight the prognostic impact of ionized calcium disturbances and the potential of machine-learning models for early risk stratification.

abstract.label: SUMMARY
abstract.text: Current evidence supports a time-critical, system-based approach in which standardized transfusion bundles are triggered early and refined using viscoelastic guidance. Future work should prioritize prospective validation of decision-support tools, phenotype-specific strategies, clarification of whole blood's role, and rigorous evaluation of emerging blood products.

articles.title: Multistage Limb Salvage After Severe Cottonmouth (Agkistrodon piscivorus) Envenomation: A Case Report.
articles.journal_full: Journal of the American Podiatric Medical Association

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Cottonmouth envenomation typically produces prominent local tissue injury, with systemic toxicity occurring less commonly. We report a limb-threatening presentation with delayed deterioration after initial antivenom therapy.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A man in his 50s sustained a suspected cottonmouth bite to the plantar midfoot and received 10 vials of Crotalidae immune F(ab')2 (equine) antivenom during his initial hospitalization.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Five days after the bite, severe edema, progressive pain, paresthesia, pallor, delayed capillary refill, and nonpalpable pedal pulses raised clinical concern for delayed compartment syndrome and threatened tissue viability. Compartment pressures were not obtained. Operative drainage and debridement were independently indicated by plantar necrosis and suspected secondary infection after contaminated floodwater exposure. Surgery confirmed purulent fluid under pressure and nonviable tissue. The patient subsequently received adjunctive hyperbaric oxygen therapy, acellular fish-skin grafts, and definitive split-thickness skin grafting.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: This case underscores the importance of serial examinations and laboratory monitoring following pit viper envenomation, toxicology-guided antivenom management, careful distinction between suspected compartment syndrome and established necrosis or infection, and staged reconstruction for severe soft-tissue injury.

articles.title: Sustaining agency after a fall: navigating healthcare and adjusting everyday life - a qualitative interview study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Falls among older adults are a major public health concern and are associated with recurrent falls, functional decline, fear of falling, and reduced quality of life. Older adults presenting to emergency departments (EDs) following a fall are often discharged directly home despite ongoing rehabilitation and support needs. Although person-centred approaches are recommended in international guidelines, less is known about older adults' and relatives' experiences following an ED visit for a fall. This study aimed to describe older adults' and their relatives' experiences of a fall, including the ED visit and the transition back home.

abstract.label: METHOD
abstract.text: A qualitative study design was used, involving semi-structured interviews with older adults aged 75 years and older and their relatives. Participants had attended the ED following a fall but were discharged without hospital admission. Seventeen participants (11 older adults and 6 relatives) were recruited. Data were analysed using qualitative content analysis according to Graneheim and Lundman.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The analysis generated one overarching theme, Sustaining agency through recovery across care and everyday life, which reflected how older adults and their relatives sought to manage daily life following a fall. Both groups described addressing immediate care needs while simultaneously adapting to longer-term changes in everyday life. Participants described difficulties navigating healthcare services to access follow-up care and rehabilitation, contributing to feelings of insecurity, financial strain, and increased responsibility. A persistent fear of falling affected daily activities and required adaptations and new roles for both older adults and their relatives. Despite these challenges, many participants demonstrated resilience and an ability to manage daily life following injury. Individual coping strategies and support from relatives were described as central to managing everyday life and healthcare contacts.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Older adults discharged home after a fall may benefit from coordinated, person-centred follow- up that supports rehabilitation, recovery, and fall prevention. Despite variation in support needs, participants described a common need for clearer guidance and improved support structures, while also demonstrating considerable resilience and capacity for self-management.

abstract.label: CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER
abstract.text: Not applicable.

articles.title: Young ERC Masterclass Journal Club Article: The EVIDENCE Trial.
Sex-based differences in clinical outcomes for non-prescription drug-associated out-of-hospital cardiac arrest.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Non-prescription drug toxicity contributes to a substantial proportion of out-of-hospital cardiac arrests (OHCAs). Among OHCAs overall, previous reports have shown lower survival among females, compared to males. We examined sex-based differences in outcomes among non-prescription drug-associated OHCA (DA-OHCA).

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: In this population-based observational cohort study using data from the BC Cardiac Arrest Registry (2019-24), we included emergency medical services (EMS)-treated OHCAs that had evidence of recent non-prescription drug use. The primary outcome was favorable neurological outcome, and secondary outcomes included survival at hospital discharge, prehospital return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC), and ROSC at emergency department (ED) arrival. We assessed the association between female sex (vs male) and outcomes using multivariable logistic regression models, adjusted for Utstein variables.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 47,051 EMS-Assessed OHCA, there were 4926 adult EMS-assessed DA-OHCA. We included 3133 adult EMS-treated DA-OHCAs, of whom 864 (28%) were female and 2269 (72%) were male, with a median age of 38 (interquartile range [IQR] 30-49) and 40 (IQR 32-52) years, respectively. Favorable neurological outcomes occurred in 108 (13%) females and 212 (9.6%) males. Female sex was not associated with favorable neurological outcome (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 1.32, 95% CI 0.97, 1.79), prehospital ROSC (aOR 1.00, 95% CI 0.83, 1.19), or ROSC at ED arrival (aOR 1.01, 95% CI 0.84, 1.22), but was associated with an increased odds survival to hospital discharge (aOR 1.34; 95% CI 1.01, 1.77).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Among DA-OHCA, female sex was not independently associated with favorable neurological outcomes, but was associated with a higher odds of survival to hospital discharge.

articles.title: Trends in Patient Complaints in a Pediatric Emergency Department: Comparison of Pre- and Post-Pandemic Periods.
