abstract.text: GFAP represents a transformation tool for objective risk stratification and decision-making in the ED. However, its transition from a research tool to a standard clinical pillar requires the standardization of assay platforms, established reference materials, and large-scale validation of clinical thresholds.

articles.title: Developing a Model for Hospital Staff Preparedness in Patient Evacuation During Disasters: A Mixed-Methods Study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Hospital staff preparedness for patient evacuation during disasters is a component of healthcare resilience. Current protocols may lack evidence-based foundations and tend to rely on static, checklist-driven approaches. Competency-based models have been proposed as an alternative, but empirical evidence supporting their effectiveness is limited.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: This study aimed to develop a model for hospital evacuation readiness, grounded in global evidence and local expertise.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: An explanatory sequential mixed-methods design was conducted in Iran (2023-2025) across five phases: 1) systematic review; 2) qualitative interviews with hospital staff; 3) data integration and expert refinement using a Modified Nominal Group Technique; 4) Delphi consensus validation with specialists; and 5) final model design. The model was developed as a theoretical framework; empirical testing of its effectiveness was beyond the study's scope.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 52 initially identified components, 50 were validated through Delphi consensus. The framework identifies five domains: individual factors; education and empowerment; resources; evacuation processes; and communication and coordination. The model introduces practical elements such as stress-tested drills, preemptive resource mapping, and structured near-miss learning.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: This research proposes a reconceptualization of evacuation preparedness as an evolving, competency-driven system. The framework offers hospitals strategies to strengthen training, optimize resources, and institutionalize near-miss learning. However, its effectiveness compared with static approaches remains theoretical and requires longitudinal empirical evaluation. Hospitals in resource-constrained regions may particularly benefit from its emphasis on adaptive capacity and low-cost, simulation-based training.

articles.title: Factors Associated with Emergency Department Revisit and Urologic Intervention Following Discharge of Renal Colic Patients: A Retrospective Cohort Study from a Military Hospital in the Kingdom of Bahrain.

abstract.text: Background Renal colic is one of the most frequent urologic presentations to the emergency department (ED). While most patients can be safely discharged with symptomatic management, a subset return to the ED or require urologic intervention within 14 days. Identifying factors associated with these outcomes is essential for informed disposition planning. Objectives The objectives of the study are to determine 14-day ED revisit and urologic intervention rates among discharged renal colic patients and to identify independent clinical and imaging predictors of each outcome. Methods A retrospective cohort study of patients aged ≥14 years discharged with renal colic from the Royal Medical Services (RMS) Military Hospital ED, Bahrain, in 2025. Demographic, clinical, laboratory, and CT imaging data were extracted. Univariate and multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed. Results In this study, 609 patients were included (mean age 42.5±12.7 years; 71.4% men). The 14-day ED revisit rate was 18.4% (n=112) and the urologic intervention rate was 14.1% (n=86). Independent predictors of ED revisit were male sex (adjusted odds ratio (aOR) 1.79; 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.06-3.01), previous stone history (aOR 1.88; 95% CI 1.22-2.89), and opioid use at index visit (aOR 2.11; 95% CI 1.31-3.40). Stone size ≥5-7 mm and presence of obstruction independently predicted urologic intervention. Pain severity was not a predictor of either outcome. Conclusion Opioid use, prior stone history, and male sex predict ED revisit; stone size and obstruction predict urologic intervention. These findings support risk stratification and discharge planning for renal colic patients.

articles.title: Adjunctive Hyperbaric Oxygen Therapy During Femoral Limb Lengthening in a Child: A Case Report.

abstract.text: Hyperbaric oxygen therapy (HBOT) has several established clinical applications, including treatment of severe anemia, crush injuries, and necrotizing soft tissue infections. Increasing interest also exists in its potential to enhance bone regeneration, as demonstrated in animal models. Improved regenerate formation and maturation could shorten treatment time during distraction osteogenesis (DO). We describe the feasibility and application of HBOT as an adjunct during femoral limb lengthening with a magnetic lengthening nail in a pediatric patient. A pediatric patient underwent two sequential femoral lengthening procedures with a magnetic lengthening nail at ages 6 and 10 years. HBOT was used as a patient-initiated, self-referred adjunctive therapy during both treatments to promote regenerate bone formation. Outcomes assessed included pixel value ratio (PVR), bone healing index (BHI), time to full weight-bearing (FWB), lengthening rate and duration, radiographic and clinical findings, hardware function, and complications. The patient completed 46 HBOT sessions during the first lengthening and 36 during the second. Regenerate PVR remained consistently above 0.85 relative to surrounding bone throughout distraction and consolidation. The length gained was 4.0 cm and 4.8 cm, respectively. BHI was 27.25 days/cm for the first procedure and 18.54 days/cm for the second. Full weight-bearing was achieved by 12 weeks postoperatively. This case demonstrates the novel use of HBOT as an adjunct in human lower extremity DO. In this patient, HBOT was feasible and associated with robust regenerate formation and early recovery. Further study is warranted to determine whether HBOT can improve outcomes in limb lengthening patients.

articles.title: Acute-on-Chronic Limb Ischemia Mimicking Cellulitis: A Diagnostic Pitfall.

abstract.text: Acute-on-chronic limb ischemia may present with clinical features that overlap with inflammatory conditions, potentially delaying recognition of arterial compromise. We report a case of an elderly woman with long-standing polycythemia treated with hydroxyurea who presented with progressive right foot pain, marked swelling, erythema, tenderness, and bluish discoloration of the hallux. She was discharged from the emergency department but returned the next night with worsening pain. Soft-tissue ultrasonography demonstrated diffuse subcutaneous edema without a localized collection, supporting an initial provisional diagnosis of cellulitis. Despite preserved motor function and sensation, progressive ischemic discoloration, prolonged capillary refill, and abnormal distal pulse findings prompted further vascular assessment. Computed tomography angiography (CTA) demonstrated a 6.2-cm right popliteal arterial thrombus with impaired distal perfusion. Her D-dimer was within the laboratory reference range at 0.40 µg/mL FEU, while the hematocrit was markedly elevated at 55.3%. Intravenous unfractionated heparin was initiated, resulting in improvement in pain and swelling and clinical stabilization, while definitive revascularization options were considered. The patient subsequently elected to pursue definitive treatment in her home country, precluding assessment of long-term limb-salvage outcomes. This case emphasizes the importance of careful and repeated vascular assessment in a painful, discolored limb, particularly before neuromotor deficits develop. Laboratory findings, including D-dimer, should be interpreted within their validated clinical context and should not supersede clinical evidence of impaired arterial perfusion.

articles.title: Migraine in Real-World Clinical Practice: Patient Burden, Healthcare Utilization and Unmet Needs-A Cross-Sectional Analysis of the I-GRAINE Study.
authors: Italian Migraine Registry I-Graine Study Group

abstract.text: What are the main findings?Migraine care in Italy is characterized by a mismatch between healthcare resource utilization and clinical needs, with limited primary-care involvement, repeated specialist consultations, and healthcare nomadism.Healthcare resource utilization is substantial, including extensive diagnostic testing-predominantly brain imaging-as well as emergency department visits, detoxification cycles, and repeated access to headache centers.

articles.title: Diagnostic Challenges and Uterus-Conserving Surgical Management Following Systemic Multi-dose Methotrexate for a Left Interstitial Pregnancy.

abstract.text: Interstitial ectopic pregnancy is an uncommon form of ectopic pregnancy and can be associated with a high risk of rupture and hemorrhagic death due to its deep myometrial location. Diagnosis can be challenging because transvaginal ultrasonography (TVUS) may fail to initially identify the implantation site until late in gestation, and the presentation can closely mimic that of an early intrauterine pregnancy or spontaneous abortion. We report the case of a 27-year-old gravida 2 para 1 (G2P1) woman who presented to the emergency department (ED) with vaginal spotting and pelvic cramping at an estimated seven weeks gestational age. Serial serum beta-human chorionic gonadotropin (β-hCG) measurements demonstrated an initial suboptimal rise followed by a plateau and subsequent decline (3,954 → 6,136 → 5,863 → 5,028 mIU/mL). Repeat TVUS identified no intrauterine pregnancy and no discrete adnexal mass, constituting a pregnancy of unknown location (PUL). Following stabilization in the Rapid Decision Unit, the patient was discharged with urgent outpatient obstetrics and gynecology (OB/GYN) follow-up. Interval repeat TVUS raised concern for a left interstitial ectopic pregnancy, prompting hospital readmission for diagnostic laparoscopy, which confirmed a 3-4 cm unruptured left interstitial ectopic pregnancy. Given hemodynamic stability and the high vascularity of the interstitial mass, intraoperative conservative management was elected in lieu of immediate wedge resection. Postoperatively, she received multi-dose systemic methotrexate with leucovorin rescue under co-management with maternal-fetal medicine and was discharged in stable condition. Although β-hCG declined to undetectable levels, interval imaging identified a persistent adnexal mass and a newly developed left hydrosalpinx. Given the patient's desire for future fertility, she underwent laparoscopic left salpingectomy with wedge resection of the left uterine cornu as uterus-conserving definitive management. This case illustrates the diagnostic limitations of TVUS and the critical role of serial β-hCG kinetics in PUL, as well as the feasibility and limitations of uterus-conserving medical and surgical management for interstitial ectopic pregnancy, including the need for long-term surveillance and the role of definitive surgery when resolution after methotrexate is incomplete.

articles.title: Benefit and Harm in the Early Management of Suspected Cervical Spine Injury: A Narrative Review.

abstract.text: Suspected cervical spine injury is managed with a bundle applied largely by reflex: a rigid collar, sequential imaging, and, in some settings, corticosteroids, alongside interventions whose benefit depends on speed. This review sets the strength of evidence behind each component against the readiness with which it is applied. Sources were identified by targeted searching of PubMed/Medical Literature Analysis and Retrieval System Online (MEDLINE) and by reference tracking; the review is not systematic. The interventions applied most reflexively are the least supported. Prehospital immobilisation has never been shown to reduce neurological deterioration, spinal cord injury, or mortality, and the only study to compare an immobilising with a non-immobilising system found less neurological disability in the patients who were not immobilised. Pooled data across 25 studies give a pressure ulcer prevalence of 7% with prolonged collar use, and collar application raises intracranial pressure by 4.43 mmHg. MRI after a normal CT finds abnormalities in 17% of patients and changes management in 4%, with heterogeneity above 90%, and a practice management guideline has already concluded that the collar may be removed in obtunded patients after a negative high-quality CT alone. Methylprednisolone produces no long-term motor recovery and increases gastrointestinal bleeding. The interventions that do alter outcome are those most easily lost to delay: decompression within 24 hours yields 4.0 additional motor points, and 2.57-fold odds of two-grade improvement in impairment grade; hypotension carries a 2.71-fold risk of adverse functional outcome, and specialist referral reduces pulmonary embolism from 5.4% to 0.7%. Three national and consensus bodies have already moved away from routine rigid immobilisation. Initial management would be improved less by adding investigation than by withdrawing interventions of unproven benefit and protecting those that are time-dependent.

articles.title: Atypical Presentation of a Meningioma Masquerading as Trigeminal Neuralgia: A Diagnostic Challenge in the Emergency Department.

abstract.text: A woman in her mid-40s presented to the Emergency Department (ED) following a sudden new-onset three-hour episode of numbness over the left maxilla and jaw, followed by electric shock-like facial pain triggered by talking and chewing. This occurred on a background of approximately four months of intermittent left-sided headache. Although the presentation initially suggested trigeminal neuralgia (TN) with concomitant pain, the prolonged sensory disturbance, left-sided proptosis, periorbital symptoms, and diplopia on left lateral gaze were clinically atypical and prompted further evaluation. Clinical examination demonstrated tenderness over the left ophthalmic (V1) and maxillary (V2) divisions of the trigeminal nerve, together with left-sided proptosis and diplopia on left lateral gaze. Neuroimaging was therefore undertaken. Computed tomography (CT) demonstrated an expansile sclerotic lesion involving the left greater wing of the sphenoid with a ground-glass appearance, initially raising suspicion of fibrous dysplasia. Subsequent magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) revealed a large en plaque meningioma involving the left sphenoid wing and middle cranial fossa, with orbital extension and compression of the left optic nerve, necessitating specialist neurosurgical evaluation. A separate right cerebellopontine angle meningioma was also identified. The patient underwent surgical resection of the symptomatic lesion, with histopathology confirming a World Health Organization (WHO) grade one meningioma. This case highlights the importance of thorough neurological assessment and early neuroimaging in patients presenting with atypical features of TN to exclude secondary causes of cranial nerve pathology more consistent with TN-like pain secondary to a structural lesion and enable timely management of any underlying lesions.

articles.title: The 2025 Model of the Clinical Practice of Emergency Medicine.
Potential harms to rescuers during cardiac arrest response and resuscitation: a scoping review.
authors: International Liaison Committee on Resuscitation Basic Life Support Task Force†
International Liaison Committee on Resuscitation Basic Life Support Task Force

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Rescuer safety during cardiac arrest response and resuscitation is an important consideration that may influence willingness to intervene. This scoping review identifies potential unintentional harms to rescuers responding to cardiac arrest and performing resuscitation.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This scoping review was reported in accordance with PRISMA-ScR guidelines. We searched EMBASE, Medline, and Cochrane from inception to June 16, 2026, including all human studies reporting physical harms during cardiac arrest response or resuscitation (compressions, ventilation, defibrillation). Two investigators screened studies and extracted data. Synthesis was guided by Joanna Briggs Institute methods, with narrative synthesis by harm category.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Twenty studies were included: sixteen provided direct evidence from cardiac arrest or resuscitation, and four provided indirect evidence from elective cardioversion. Of the direct-evidence studies, nine examined infection transmission during CPR, two evaluated electrical exposure from implantable cardioverter-defibrillators (ICDs) during CPR, two reported physical injuries en route to arrest, and three documented drowning during rescue. Infection transmission rates varied by pathogen but were mitigated by personal protective equipment (PPE). CPR near implantable cardioverter-defibrillators (ICDs) showed potential for higher leakage. In the four indirect-evidence studies, current leakage to rescuers during external shocks delivered for elective cardioversion remained below safe thresholds. One study reported minor injuries from incorrect opening of locked AED cabinets, and another found that injuries en route to patients were rare (<0.7%). Rescue-related drowning fatalities ranged from 0.02 to 0.08 per 100,000 population annually.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: This scoping review suggests harms to rescuers during response or resuscitation are rare. Fatal harms have been reported during water rescue. Minor harms include unsafe AED removal, current leakage during ICD shock delivery, performing CPR without appropriate PPE, and minor injuries en route to a cardiac arrest. Indirect evidence from elective cardioversion suggests external defibrillation poses minimal electrical risk.

articles.title: MRSA Knowledge, Infection-Prevention Practices, and Antibiotic Use Without Clinician Consultation Among Hajj Pilgrims Arriving in Madinah, Saudi Arabia: A Cross-Sectional Study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Hajj is an international mass gathering in which infection prevention and antimicrobial stewardship intersect. Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) was selected as the organism-specific focus because it is a clinically important antimicrobial-resistant pathogen associated with skin and soft-tissue infections, wound care, and transmission through close contact and sharing of personal items. Hajj studies have also documented MRSA-related carriage and broader antimicrobial-resistance concerns among pilgrims and other mass-gathering populations. However, the relation between general infection awareness, MRSA-specific knowledge, and self-reported antibiotic-use behaviour remains less well described. This study assessed these three domains among Hajj pilgrims arriving in Madinah, Saudi Arabia.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A questionnaire-based cross-sectional study was conducted during Hajj 1446H (2025). The study dataset comprised 342 completed questionnaires. Item-level descriptive analyses were used because no validated composite scoring algorithm was documented in the available study records. The primary exploratory outcome was an undated, self-reported history of taking antibiotics without consulting a doctor. Modified Poisson regression with robust variance estimated adjusted prevalence ratios (aPRs), with sex, age group, education, healthcare employment, and MRSA awareness entered simultaneously as prespecified covariates.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 342 respondents, 213 (62.3%) were male, 155 (45.3%) were aged 46-60 years, 181 (52.9%) reported postgraduate education, and 51 (14.9%) worked in healthcare. General awareness of crowding-related bacterial-infection risk was high (256/342, 74.9%), whereas MRSA-specific knowledge was lower: 110 (32.2%) had heard of MRSA, 137 (40.1%) identified personal-item sharing as a transmission route, and 124 (36.3%) recognised that MRSA can cause serious or fatal infection. Handwashing ≥ 3 times/day was reported by 310 respondents (90.6%), and 327 (95.6%) reported not sharing personal items. However, 143 respondents (41.8%) reported taking antibiotics without consulting a doctor. In the adjusted model, the prevalence of this outcome was higher among participants aged > 60 years than among those aged < 46 years (aPR 1.86, 95% CI 1.35-2.56) and among those who had not heard of MRSA (aPR 3.60, 95% CI 2.10-6.18) or did not know whether they had heard of MRSA (aPR 3.40, 95% CI 1.84-6.30), compared with those who had heard of MRSA.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Among pilgrims arriving in Madinah, general infection-prevention awareness and self-reported hygiene practices coexisted with limited MRSA-specific knowledge, and a substantial proportion of respondents reported taking antibiotics without consulting a doctor. The observed associations are cross-sectional and non-causal; they neither establish the timing or appropriateness of antibiotic use nor demonstrate that an education intervention would change behaviour. They identify a hypothesis for prospective evaluation of multilingual Hajj education linking MRSA transmission, wound care, and antibiotic stewardship.

articles.title: Hybrid Spinal-General Anesthesia With a Supraglottic Airway in Severe Rheumatoid Arthritis: A Case Report.

abstract.text: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) can present significant challenges during airway management because of cervical spine involvement, restricted neck mobility, temporomandibular joint disease, and limited mouth opening. We report the perioperative anesthetic management of a patient with severe deforming RA and multiple predictors of an anticipated difficult airway undergoing laparoscopic cholecystectomy. A 54-year-old woman with long-standing RA had a Mallampati grade IV airway, approximately 1.5 cm mouth opening, a short neck, and markedly restricted cervical spine movement. A comprehensive difficult airway strategy was formulated with immediate availability of videolaryngoscopy, fiberoptic bronchoscopy, supraglottic airway devices, and emergency front-of-neck airway equipment. Following spinal anesthesia with 3.2 mL of 0.5% hyperbaric bupivacaine and 15 μg of fentanyl, light general anesthesia was induced while preserving spontaneous ventilation. Neuromuscular blockade was avoided, and a size 3 i-gel second-generation supraglottic airway was successfully inserted on the first attempt. Anesthesia was maintained with sevoflurane while spontaneous ventilation was preserved throughout laparoscopic surgery. Pneumoperitoneum was established gradually with intra-abdominal pressure maintained below 12 mmHg. The procedure was completed uneventfully without desaturation, airway obstruction, or significant hemodynamic instability. The i-gel was removed after recovery of consciousness and adequate airway reflexes. Postoperative recovery was uncomplicated, with satisfactory analgesia and no respiratory, neurological, or airway-related complications. This case illustrates that hybrid spinal-general anesthesia using a second-generation supraglottic airway while preserving spontaneous ventilation may be a useful alternative in carefully selected patients with an anticipated difficult airway. Such an approach requires meticulous preoperative airway assessment, experienced anesthetic management, and immediate availability of appropriate rescue airway equipment.

articles.title: Demographics and Infection Sources in Coding-Defined Sepsis at a Romanian County Emergency Hospital: A Retrospective Single-Center Study.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Sepsis is one of the major causes of hospital morbidity and mortality, and its epidemiology varies with local patient populations. Descriptive data from Romanian county hospitals remain limited. We have described the demographic profile, infection sources, and hospital service distribution of patients with coding-defined sepsis at a Romanian county emergency hospital over a full calendar year.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This was a retrospective, single-center study at the "Sf. Apostol Andrei" Emergency County Clinical Hospital, Constanța, Romania. Using the hospital electronic discharge registry (Hipocrate OPIS Externari), discharge records were filtered by infectious-disease diagnostic category and individually reviewed by clinicians, yielding 1,147 records of patients presenting to the emergency department with infection-related diagnoses during the 2025 calendar year. The study included patients with sepsis as their primary diagnosis (International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision (ICD-10) A40-A41). We recorded and deidentified age, sex, discharge service, primary infection source, and length of stay. The analysis is primarily descriptive. We excluded toxic shock syndrome and other specified infections.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 1,147 infection-related discharge records reviewed, 129 (11.2% of infection-related records; 0.39% of all 33,250 emergency department admissions during the study period) carried a principal discharge diagnosis of coding-defined sepsis (ICD-10 A40 or A41). The cohort was predominantly adult (115/129, 89.1%); among adults, the mean age was 60.2 years (standard deviation (SD), 16.7), while the combined mean age, including 14 pediatric patients, was 54.3 years (SD, 23.2). Of the 129 patients, 82 (63.6%) were male and 45 (34.9%) were female patients, and sex was indeterminate in two (1.6%). General surgery (36%) and urology (32%) were the most frequent discharge services. The leading infection source was urinary (41%), followed by abdominal (26%) and skin and soft tissue (16%). Median length of stay was seven days (interquartile range, 4-14 days; mean 10.0 days; n = 126 of 129).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Over a full calendar year at this Romanian county clinical emergency hospital, sepsis predominantly affected older patients managed by general surgery and urology, with urinary and abdominal sources dominating. These descriptive regional data add to the limited hospital-based descriptive evidence on sepsis in Romania.

articles.title: Addressing COVID-19 in Inmates at Women's State Prison in Indonesia.

abstract.text: Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19), caused by Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), is characterized by symptoms such as cough, fever, fatigue, and myalgia. COVID-19 became widespread in Indonesia, with the highest incidence recorded in the Daerah Khusus Ibukota (DKI) Jakarta Province. The movement of individuals into and out of prisons, overcrowding, inadequate sanitation, and limited access to fresh air and physical activities, among other factors, contribute to the high risk of COVID-19 transmission in correctional facilities. Consequently, this study examines the frequency of COVID-19 among prisoners at the Women's State Prison in Jakarta. Responses from a previously published survey were analyzed. The research employed a cross-sectional study design, surveying 105 prisoners within the facility. The primary data were obtained through completion of a structured questionnaire. Chi-square analysis demonstrated a significant association between a history of contact and COVID-19 infection (p < 0.01, odds ratio [OR] = 17.21). In contrast, conventional COVID-19 preventive behaviors (p = 0.35, OR = 1.70) and access to facilities and amenities (p = 0.77, OR = 1.23) were not significantly associated with COVID-19 infection among inmates. These findings have important policy implications for the prevention and control of epidemics in female prisoners in Indonesia.

articles.title: Cycling-related injuries demonstrate the highest hospitalization proportion, whereas exercise-related activities account for the largest injury burden: a 12-year national epidemiological analysis.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Sports- and recreation-related injuries represent a substantial public health burden, yet comprehensive national analyses comparing high-volume activities across all age groups remain limited. The purpose of this study was to describe temporal patterns, demographic distributions, injury patterns, and hospitalization profiles of the five most common sports and recreational activities associated with emergency department (ED) visits in the United States.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A retrospective epidemiological analysis was conducted using data from the National Electronic Injury Surveillance System (NEISS) between 2013 and 2024. Injuries associated with basketball, bicycle and accessories, exercise/exercise equipment, football, and playground equipment were included. Weighted national estimates were generated using NEISS sampling weights. Outcomes included injury type, injured body region, and hospitalization status. Multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to evaluate independent associations of activity type, age, sex, and body region with fracture, strain/sprain, dislocation, and hospitalization outcomes. Hospitalization status was evaluated as an indirect proxy for injury severity.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: An estimated 21.8 million sports- and recreation-related injuries were identified during the study period. Exercise-related activities (5.49 million estimated injuries) and cycling-related activities (5.31 million estimated injuries) accounted for the greatest injury burden. Individuals aged 5 to 14 years represented the most affected age group, and males accounted for 71.9% of injuries. Strain/sprain injuries predominated overall, particularly in basketball (37.1%) and exercise-related activities (27.8%), whereas fractures were more common in playground-related (34.4%) and cycling-related injuries (23.6%). Head/neck injuries were most frequent in cycling-related (30.1%) and playground-related injuries (34.3%). Cycling-related injuries demonstrated the highest hospitalization proportion (11.1%), whereas basketball demonstrated the lowest proportion (1.6%). Multivariable analysis confirmed that cycling-related injuries were associated with higher odds of hospitalization than basketball, football, and exercise-related injuries, whereas hospitalization odds were comparable to playground-related injuries. Advancing age, particularly age ≥ 65 years, was associated with greater odds of hospitalization among ED-treated injury cases. Temporally, injury volumes declined sharply in 2020, followed by a rebound exceeding pre-pandemic levels.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Exercise-related activities accounted for the greatest overall injury volume, whereas cycling-related injuries demonstrated the highest hospitalization proportion, an indirect proxy for injury severity. Injury burden was greatest among individuals aged 5-14 years, whereas advancing age was associated with greater odds of hospitalization among ED-treated injury cases.

articles.title: A Retrospective Review of Emergency Department Coronavirus 2019 Cases vs. County-Wide Cases to Demonstrate a Temporal Correlation.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: To better prepare for future Coronavirus 2019 (COVID-19) variants, new forms of surveillance are necessary to predict outbreaks and prepare communities and hospitals.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: We examined the temporal correlation between emergency department (ED) and county COVID-19 cases and determine if ED COVID-19 trends can serve as an indicator to predict county-level outbreaks.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A retrospective analysis of COVID-19 data from March 2020 to April 2023 was conducted, comparing hospital COVID-19 positive cases to local county positive cases. Data were analyzed using two metrics: a positivity cutoff and a cross-correlation analysis. We set the positivity cutoff (percent of positive tests to total tests) at 4% threshold based on guidelines from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) and identified dates when ED and county positivity surpassed this threshold. The cross-correlation analysis between the county and the ED determined the time lag interval (in days) that had the strongest correlation between daily ED and county positive case volume per outbreak.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: There were both seven ED and county dates that met the positivity cutoff but only five that corresponded to the same outbreaks. The county outbreaks preceded ED outbreaks, ranging from 2 to 59 days, with a mean of 42 days prior. The cross-correlational analysis underwent an additional sensitivity analysis, resulting in an R-squared value ranging 0.8435-0.9271, averaging 8.25 days of county precedence.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: ED data is not a suitable predictor of county-level COVID-19 cases; however, the strong correlation of county precedence can prove helpful to prepare hospitals for future outbreaks.

articles.title: Sex and Age-Based Effect on Outcomes in the Setting of Traumatic Hemorrhage.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Survival differences between injured females and males have been demonstrated.

abstract.label: STUDY OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: To analyze trauma survival stratified by sex and age for a given transfusion volume.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: The Trauma Quality Improvement Program registry was analyzed from 2020 to 2023. Patients ≥15 years who received any volume of blood products within 4 hours were included.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: There were 13,987 patients (3165/13,987, 22.6% female) who received 75-600 mL/kg of all blood products within the first 4 hours of admission, i.e., the range where a difference in cumulative 24-hour survival between males and females was observed. In this range, the cumulative probability of 24-hour survival was lower for females compared to males (46 vs. 51%, respectively). This difference was not observed in the adjusted analysis (odds ratio 0.93, 95% confidence interval 0.84-1.02). In the unadjusted age and sex subanalysis, females >50 years had the highest mortality of any of the four groups of patients once ∼100 mL/kg of blood products had been transfused. Both males and females aged 15-50 years had the lowest mortality for any volume of transfusion; males >50 years had intermediate mortality. In the regression analysis performed on patients who received a total volume of 100-600 mL/kg of transfusion, 15- to 50-year-old males had significantly lower 24-hour survival compared to similarly aged females. There was no difference in this parameter between the females and males who were >50 years.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Adjusting for differences did not reveal a difference in overall survival between males and females; younger males had lower survival compared to similarly aged females.

articles.title: Forum November/ December- Air Medical Journal (YMAM).
Heart Under Pressure: From Scene to Scalpel in Cardiac Tamponade From a Left Ventricular Stab Injury.

abstract.text: Penetrating cardiac injuries carry exceptionally high mortality, especially when the left ventricle is involved, and survival hinges on rapid diagnosis and immediate surgical intervention. We describe a case of penetrating cardiac trauma with acute tamponade, emphasizing the role of coordinated care from scene to operating theatre. A 30-year-old male presented with multiple precordial stab wounds, in hemorrhagic shock with severe hypoxemia; prehospital teams prioritized rapid stabilization and transport. On arrival, extended focused assessment with sonography for trauma (eFAST) identified left hemopneumothorax and circumferential pericardial effusion consistent with tamponade, and the massive transfusion protocol was activated. Emergency median sternotomy revealed a grade IV left ventricular laceration, which was repaired primarily without cardiopulmonary bypass, and the patient recovered well, with progressive hemodynamic stability and favorable metabolic parameters postoperatively. This case illustrates that survival from penetrating left ventricular injury requires rapid diagnosis via point-of-care ultrasound, immediate median sternotomy, and intensive postoperative management, and demonstrates that favorable outcomes are achievable through coordinated multidisciplinary care within an organized trauma system. Penetrating cardiac injuries remain time-critical emergencies, and early recognition via point-of-care ultrasound, prompt surgical access, and a well-rehearsed trauma protocol can achieve survival even when severe ventricular injuries are present.

articles.title: Pulmonary edema during cesarean delivery secondary to Takotsubo syndrome revealing pheochromocytoma: a case report.

abstract.text: Acute pulmonary edema during delivery is a serious condition with a wide range of etiologies, including Takotsubo syndrome (TTS), a form of transient left ventricular dysfunction most often presenting as apical ballooning. We report the case of a 35-year-old woman who developed severe hypertension (205/130 mmHg), polypnea, and a drop in oxygen saturation to 80% during cesarean delivery under spinal anesthesia. She received noninvasive ventilation while the cesarean section continued and was transferred to the intensive care unit. Point-of-care ultrasound showed a left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of 35% with apical ballooning and diffuse B-lines on lung ultrasound. Computed tomography identified a right adrenal mass. A diagnosis of pulmonary edema complicating TTS was made, and the patient received furosemide and oxygen therapy. Further investigations, including urinary catecholamine metabolites, confirmed the diagnosis of pheochromocytoma. One week later, LVEF had recovered to 57% with mild residual apical hypokinesia and complete clinical recovery. The patient was then transferred to the surgical unit for management of the pheochromocytoma. This case demonstrates that TTS can cause pulmonary edema in the peripartum period, and that timely diagnosis is essential for a favorable outcome. Point-of-care ultrasound can be instrumental in guiding the assessment of such critical situations, and noninvasive ventilation may be of particular value in selected pregnant patients. This case also underscores the importance of an etiological workup and prompt treatment of hypertensive disorders in pregnancy, especially when pheochromocytoma is suspected, since anesthesia and surgery can precipitate decompensation.

articles.title: Evaluating Culturally Tailored Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR) Training in Racial and Ethnically Diverse Communities.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Bystander cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) is a critical determinant of survival following out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA). However, racial and ethnic minority populations in the United States are less likely to receive bystander CPR and experience disproportionately poorer outcomes.

abstract.label: STUDY OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: The objective of this study was to pilot and evaluate the feasibility of a culturally tailored hands-only CPR curriculum and assess changes in self-reported confidence and perceived difficulty of CPR among Indian American, Chinese American, and African American participants.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a single-cohort pre-post study among three groups. Community-specific focus groups informed cultural adaptations to a standard emergency services hands-only CPR curriculum, and trainings were delivered at Hindu temples, Chinese language schools, and African American churches. Primary outcomes, measured by 10-point Likert scales, were changes in confidence in four main CPR skills and perceived difficulty of CPR.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The study included 104 participants: 47 (45%) Indian American, 23 (22%) Chinese American, and 34 (33%) African American participants. Confidence increased across the four main CPR skills, with the largest improvements observed in the connect an automated external defibrillator (AED) skill (+4.5; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 3.80-5.22). Perceived difficulty of CPR also decreased (-2.65; 95% CI: 1.97-3.33).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: This pilot study provides preliminary evidence for the feasibility and acceptability of culturally tailored hands-only CPR training in community settings, with participants reporting improved confidence and reduced perceived difficulty of CPR after training. These exploratory findings warrant further evaluation in adequately powered comparative studies to determine whether cultural tailoring offers benefit beyond standard CPR instruction for racial and ethnic minority communities and can contribute to reducing disparities in cardiac arrest outcomes.

articles.title: A Novel Governance Model for Real-Time Clinical Decision-Making in Viral Hemorrhagic Fever Outbreaks: Ethiopia's 2025 Marburg Virus Disease Response.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: In November 2025, Ethiopia declared its first Marburg Virus Disease outbreak. With no licensed vaccines or specific therapeutics, the Ministry of Health established a novel dual-advisory governance structure for case management.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: This case study examines the development, implementation, and associated outcomes of Ethiopia's dual-advisory governance model during the 2025 Marburg outbreak.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a qualitative case study using thematic synthesis of official government documents, meeting minutes, and clinical logs from November 13, 2025, to January 26, 2026. The Ministry of Health granted access; all patient data were anonymized.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The dual-advisory model comprised two parallel bodies: a strategic Technical Working Group for national guideline development, and a tactical National Advisory Team providing daily consultation to frontline clinicians. A ``morning meeting'' mechanism enabled bidirectional communication. During the response, Remdesivir was deployed within 6 days (278 post-exposure prophylaxis [PEP] courses, 10 treatment courses); monoclonal antibody MBP091 was operationalized within 8 days. The outbreak resulted in 14 confirmed cases, five survivors, and three healthcare worker infections (two deceased).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Ethiopia's dual-advisory governance model demonstrated the ability to bridge strategic planning and tactical clinical action. The separation of functions, institutionalized daily communication, and links to resource mobilization represent potentially transferable principles for outbreak governance. However, as a descriptive case study, observed outcomes cannot be attributed to the model, and further evaluation is needed.

articles.title: 9-1-1, what is your emergency? Human-centered artificial intelligence, language access and health policy.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Emergency medical dispatch (EMD) is a critical yet understudied entry point into the US healthcare system. Given the increasing adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) in healthcare, we examine 9-1-1 telecommunicators' perspectives on AI integration in EMD.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a qualitative analysis of open-ended responses from a cross-sectional electronic survey of 9-1-1 telecommunicators who primarily manage emergency medical calls at three 9-1-1 call centers in California between February and April 2026.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Eight themes emerged from the study: (1) 9-1-1 telecommunicators generally viewed human-centered AI as a tool to supplement, rather than replace human expertise; (2) the importance of maintaining human connection and empathy; (3) concerns related to liability, accountability, and data security; (4) the need to differentiate between emergency and non-emergency calls; (5) 9-1-1 caller location identification; (6) 9-1-1 caller language identification; 7) delays in connecting with interpreters; and (8) AI performance under "less-than-ideal" conditions.

abstract.label: POLICY IMPLICATIONS
abstract.text: These findings highlight the importance of human-centered, equity-focused approaches to AI integration in EMD, including proactive policy development, implementation, and evaluation.

articles.title: Using Checklists to Improve Turnaround Times in Time-Critical Interhospital Transfers.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: Time-critical interhospital transfer is operationally and clinically high-stake. Variation in referring-hospital preparation can prolong in-hospital turnaround time and delay definitive care. In 2022, time-critical interhospital transfers accounted for 1.5% of cases attended by a UK Helicopter Emergency Medicine Service (HEMS) organisation. Twenty-three patients were transferred, including 3 children. Our key performance indicator (KPI) of hospital turnaround time being less than 45 minutes was achieved in only 12 transfers (52%).

abstract.label: SETTING
abstract.text: A UK HEMS organisation that undertakes time-critical interhospital transfers from district general hospitals to regional tertiary centers.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Two checklists (referring-team "Pre-arrival" and transport-team "Pre-departure") were developed. High-fidelity simulated time-critical transfer scenarios were undertaken in a simulation suite to improve crew familiarity before their introduction. The checklists were introduced into operational practice, and a post-intervention retrospective service evaluation of all interhospital helicopter transfers between January 1, 2024 and December 31, 2024 was then performed using routinely collected operational data (turnaround defined as landing-to-departure time at the referring hospital).

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: In simulated scenarios, the < 45-minute turnaround KPI was consistently achieved. In 2024, after the introduction of the checklists, 11 interhospital transfers were completed by air (2 paediatric), representing 0.6% of all missions. The < 45-minute turnaround KPI was achieved in 7 (64%) time-critical transfers. Fisher exact test showed that the difference in KPI achievement did not reach statistical significance.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Checklist-supported preparation may improve the reliability of meeting time-critical transfer KPIs while maintaining safe transfer standards. Owing to the relatively rare occurrence of these transfers, the absence of statistical significance should not be interpreted as an absence of a clinically meaningful effect. In routine practice, performance was influenced by outlier delays, suggesting a focus on reducing variability and embedding consistent pre-arrival preparation at referring sites.

articles.title: Left behind: Association of prehospital field undertriage and outcomes after injury.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Despite the perception of the negative effects of field undertriage for injured patients, relatively little literature exists documenting worse outcomes, and trauma registry data are limited by missing patients who never arrive at a trauma center. Our objective is to evaluate the impact of undertriage on outcomes in a population-based data set.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This was a retrospective cohort study of injured adult patients in the 2023 Pennsylvania state discharge database (Pennsylvania Health Care Cost Containment Council). Undertriage was defined as patients not being transported initially to a level I/II trauma center who met anatomic and mechanism of National Field Triage Criteria using the International Classification of Diseases, 10th Revision codes and external cause of injury codes. Our primary outcome was in-hospital mortality. Secondary outcomes were hospital length of stay and discharge disposition (home versus nonhome). The association between outcomes and undertriage was determined using doubly robust targeted maximum likelihood estimation, adjusting for age, sex, race, mechanism of injury, distance to hospital, major operative procedures, and injury severity.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 59,095 trauma patients were included, with an undertriage rate of 53%. Targeted maximum likelihood estimation demonstrated a 19% increased relative risk of in-hospital mortality associated with undertriage (adjusted risk ratio, 1.19; 95% confidence interval, 1.07-1.33) but shorter length of stay (-0.29 days; 95% confidence interval, -0.42 to -0.15). For discharge disposition, a generalized additive model identified a significant change in the effect of undertriage at 60 years old. For patients older than 60 years, undertriage is associated with a lower risk of discharge home (adjusted risk ratio, 0.95; 95% confidence interval, 0.93-0.97).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: We demonstrate among injured adults transported to both trauma and nontrauma centers in Pennsylvania that prehospital field undertriage based on the National Field Triage Guidelines is associated with an increased risk of mortality and lower likelihood of discharge home among older adults.

articles.title: Recurrent Pneumococcal Meningitis Without Cerebrospinal Fluid Pleocytosis and With Fulminant Septic Shock: A Case Report.

abstract.text: Bacterial meningitis is typically diagnosed via lumbar puncture. It usually occurs with cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) abnormalities. This report describes the case of a 68-year-old man with recurrent pneumococcal meningitis and absence of significant CSF pleocytosis. Despite a thorough search, no infectious focus was identified. The patient lacked typical meningeal signs, such as neck stiffness, and did not initially present with marked alteration of consciousness. Prompt antibiotic therapy was initiated; however, the patient died on the day of admission. On the day after his death, Gram-positive diplococci were detected in blood, urine, and CSF cultures and were subsequently identified as Streptococcus pneumoniae. The CSF examination showed no findings strongly suggestive of meningitis. Atypical presentations of meningitis may lead to delays in diagnosis and treatment. To the best of our knowledge, reports of such cases are rare.

articles.title: Between the Siren and the Silence.
Cavernous Sinus Thrombosis in a Three-Year-Old Male.

abstract.text: Cavernous sinus thrombosis (CST) is a rare disorder that can follow head and neck infections such as acute sinusitis, peritonsillar abscess (PTA), otitis media, and mastoiditis. The clinical presentation is variable, making CST difficult to recognize at initial presentation. This case report presents a three-year-old otherwise healthy male who presented to the emergency department with two weeks of intermittent fever and rhinorrhea and one day of lethargy and left-sided ptosis. Evaluation and workup in the emergency department included computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), which revealed a right-sided PTA, pansinusitis, and CST with dural involvement. The patient underwent PTA drainage, bilateral ethmoidectomy, adenoidectomy, and maxillary antrostomy in the operating room. This report highlights the importance of recognizing this low-incidence, high-morbidity diagnosis in the younger pediatric population and initiating early intervention to improve patient outcomes.

articles.title: Heart in Distress: How Different Shock States Converge on Cardiac Dysfunction.

abstract.text: Shock is traditionally classified according to its primary etiology-septic, hypovolemic, obstructive, or cardiogenic-yet these syndromes frequently converge on a common feature: disturbances of cardiac performance, ventricular loading, and tissue perfusion. Despite distinct initiating mechanisms, altered preload and afterload, ventricular interdependence, vascular dysfunction, maladaptive neurohormonal responses, and, in selected states, impaired myocardial contractility may ultimately reduce effective forward flow and tissue perfusion. Echocardiography provides a rapid, noninvasive bedside tool for characterizing these evolving cardiovascular effects. It enables assessment of left and right ventricular function, cardiac filling, preload responsiveness, pulmonary and systemic venous congestion, fluid tolerance, and broader hemodynamic profiles while facilitating recognition of reversible causes such as cardiac tamponade, acute pulmonary embolism, or severe hypovolemia. This allows clinicians to move beyond static etiologic classifications toward a physiology-based assessment of shock. Beyond diagnosis, echocardiography can inform fluid resuscitation and vasoactive or inotropic therapy. Serial assessment also permits evaluation of therapeutic response and evolving hemodynamic phenotypes. This review synthesizes the mechanisms of cardiac involvement across shock syndromes and highlights echocardiography as a unifying tool for their evaluation and management. By integrating pathophysiology, bedside imaging, and hemodynamic treatment, we propose a physiology-based framework that complements traditional shock classification and may improve diagnostic precision and individualized management in critically ill patients.

articles.title: Self-Rated Health and Burnout Dimensions Among Prehospital Emergency Medical Services Physicians: A Cross-Sectional Study.

abstract.text: This study examined associations between self-rated health (SRH) and burnout dimensions among prehospital emergency physicians. This cross-sectional study included a convenience sample of 151 physicians from one emergency medical service in Belgrade, Serbia. Burnout was assessed using the Maslach Burnout Inventory-Human Services Survey and SRH using a single SF-36 general-health item. Ordinal models examined three ordered SRH categories (excellent/very good, good, and fair/poor), with burnout dimensions entered separately and jointly, adjusting for age, sex, professional qualification, and chronic disease. Binary sensitivity analyses compared fair/poor with excellent/very good/good health. Higher emotional exhaustion was associated with less favourable SRH in the separate adjusted ordinal model (OR per 10-point increase: 1.31; 95% CI 1.04-1.64). After mutual adjustment for burnout dimensions, the estimate remained similar but was less precise (OR 1.30; 95% CI 0.96-1.75). Evidence was also inconclusive in the adjusted binary analysis. Depersonalisation and reduced personal accomplishment showed no clear adjusted associations with SRH. Unadjusted associations of shift work and daily working hours with SRH were inconclusive. Emotional exhaustion may be associated with physicians' perceived health, although the evidence varied across models. The cross-sectional design precludes conclusions about direction or causality; longitudinal studies are needed.

articles.title: Epidemiology of Nephrolithiasis Among United States Emergency Departments Over a 9-Year Period.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Nephrolithiasis is a common emergency department (ED) presentation, yet contemporary national data on management trends are limited.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: To characterize recent trends in diagnostic evaluation, management, and disposition for adult ED patients with nephrolithiasis.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This cross-sectional study analyzed United States ED encounters from January 1, 2016 to December 31, 2024 using the Epic Cosmos database, including all adult patients (≥18 years) with an ICD-10 diagnosis of nephrolithiasis. Outcomes included hospital admission, imaging utilization, urine culture collection, medication administration, discharge prescription, and procedural intervention. Descriptive statistics were utilized to characterize the study population. To account for the longitudinal expansion of the database, time-stratified odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated using the general ED population as a background comparator. Significance of temporal shifts was assessed using Cochran-Armitage tests.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 248,564,812 ED encounters, 2,762,879 (1.1%) were for nephrolithiasis. Hospital admission rates increased from 8.9% in 2016 to 12.7% in 2024. Computed tomography (CT) utilization increased (73.8-89.8%), outpacing general ED trends (OR 27.2-45.6), while ultrasound declined (5.8-3.8%). In the ED, opioid use fell (61.5-49.7%), exceeding background reductions (OR 6.6-4.8), while ketorolac was the most common analgesic administered (61.6%). Tamsulosin remained the top discharge prescription (47.2%). Procedural interventions were uncommon, though stent placement increased from 3.0% to 6.8%.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: We identified rising hospital admission rates and an increase in CT utilization, while there was a decline in ultrasound. This divergence between practice patterns and evidence-based guidelines, highlights critical opportunities for quality improvement.

articles.title: An Unsuspected Adult Intestinal Malrotation Presenting With Left-Sided Appendicitis, With the Diagnosis First Suggested by Purulent Drainage From the Appendiceal Orifice During an Elective Colonoscopy.

abstract.text: Acute appendicitis typically presents with right lower quadrant abdominal pain. Congenital abnormalities of intestinal rotation may alter the position of the cecum and appendix, resulting in atypical clinical manifestations and potentially delaying diagnosis. Intestinal malrotation is usually diagnosed during childhood but may remain asymptomatic and undetected until adulthood. We report the case of a 63-year-old man who underwent elective colonoscopy following a positive fecal occult blood test. He reported abdominal pain beginning approximately 24 hours before the procedure, which he initially attributed to bowel preparation. During colonoscopy, purulent material was observed filling the appendiceal orifice, raising suspicion of acute appendicitis. The patient was referred to the emergency department, where examination revealed isolated tenderness of the left iliac fossa without right-sided abdominal pain. Laboratory evaluation showed no leukocytosis, 76% neutrophils, and an elevated C-reactive protein level of 6.7 mg/dL. Computed tomography demonstrated intestinal malrotation, with the colon predominantly located on the left side of the abdomen and pelvis, and an inflamed appendix arising from the abnormally positioned cecum to the left of the midline. Laparoscopic appendectomy was performed using right-sided working ports. Intraoperative findings demonstrated acute phlegmonous appendicitis without exudate, and histopathological examination confirmed acute phlegmonous appendicitis with focal serositis. The postoperative course was uncomplicated, and the patient was discharged on the first postoperative day. This case illustrates an unusual presentation of acute appendicitis associated with previously undiagnosed intestinal malrotation, in which the initial diagnostic suspicion arose incidentally during colonoscopy. Recognition of anatomical variants and appropriate use of cross-sectional imaging are important when evaluating atypical presentations of common surgical emergencies.

articles.title: Beyond the Threatened Limb: Acute Limb Ischemia as a Diagnostic Attractor.

abstract.text: Acute limb ischemia is a time-sensitive vascular emergency, but in older patients with active cancer and multimorbidity, the threatened limb can become a diagnostic attractor: a correct specialized diagnosis that narrows attention before whole-patient physiology is integrated. We report an 81-year-old man with metastatic cecal adenocarcinoma receiving folinic acid, fluorouracil, and oxaliplatin (FOLFOX) who presented on day one with three days of progressive left lower limb claudication, coldness, discoloration, absent pulses, preserved motor and sensory function, and no rest pain. The presentation was clinically compatible with Rutherford I-IIa acute limb ischemia; bedside Doppler signals were not documented, precluding a definitive retrospective distinction between these categories. Concurrent findings included new atrial fibrillation, basal crackles, peripheral edema, markedly elevated N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide and troponin, bilateral pleural effusions, and radiological concern for low cardiac output. Computed tomography angiography (CTA) showed severe distal superficial femoral artery stenosis, long popliteal occlusion, slow distal flow, and limited runoff, favoring an acute-on-chronic ischemic process. On day two, a 6 mm x 60 mm covered stent was placed across the distal superficial femoral artery lesion. The treated lesion had a satisfactory technical result, but distal runoff remained severely compromised. Therapeutic anticoagulation initiated on day one was not maintained; discharge treatment on day three included prophylactic-dose enoxaparin and aspirin, with no rationale for the change documented in the available record. He returned on day five with recurrent coldness and toe necrosis despite normal lactate. No repeat vascular imaging was available to define the mechanism. Care became palliative on day 13, and he died on day 58. This case illustrates that a correct vascular diagnosis should not terminate integrative emergency reasoning. We propose that a vascular-plus-physiology cross-check may help preserve attention to systemic physiology and goals of care, but it is an educational framework rather than a validated clinical algorithm.

articles.title: Prehospital factors associated with calcium derangements upon arrival to the trauma center from scene - A subanalysis of a multicenter prospective study.
articles.journal_full: The American journal of emergency medicine

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Existing data suggests that hypocalcemia may be a factor in the lethal diamond of trauma. This could offer a potential opportunity for prehospital interventions to address these derangements. We performed a preplanned secondary analysis of data from a prospective multicenter study on calcium derangements in hemorrhage patients upon arrival at trauma centers.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a prospective multicenter observational study of trauma patients admitted at the highest level of activation for three participating centers where an ionized calcium level was measured upon arrival. Data from the prehospital records were collected from the Emergency Medical Services reports. We compared study variables between patients who were hypocalcemic, eucalcemic, and hypercalcemic.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: There were 1270 participants enrolled in our primary study, of whom 1047 arrived by EMS from the scene meeting inclusion for this analysis. Of these, 235 were hypocalcemic and 39 were hypercalcemic upon arrival. Patients with calcium derangements had lower survival compared to patients without derangements. Of those who were hypocalcemic, 32.8% received prehospital blood products, compared to 25.6% of those who were hypercalcemic upon arrival. There were 5 (12.8%) who were hypercalcemic that received prehospital calcium, potentially indicating iatrogenic hypercalcemia. Elevated prehospital shock indices were associated with both derangements. Of the 718 who received no fluids or blood, 116 (16.1%) were hypocalcemic and 27 (3.7%) were hypocalcemic with 2 hypercalcemic participants receiving calcium. Of those 136 that received a blood product prehospital, 77 were hypocalcemic (56.6%) with 1 receiving calcium, and 10 (7.4%) were hypercalcemic with 3 receiving calcium, and the remaining were eucalcemic with 4 (2.9%) receiving calcium.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Both hypocalcemia and hypercalcemia occurred in the setting of blood product and no blood product administration. Our study suggests that currently available assessment methods are inadequate for predicting the presence of a calcium derangement, both high and low.

abstract.label: CLINICALTRIALS
abstract.text: gov registration: NCT05885256.

articles.title: [Mild traumatic brain injury in prehospital primary care emergency services: care pathway and the opportunity of point-of-care biomarkers].

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To describe the initial management of adult patients with mild traumatic brain injury attended by mobile primary care emergency units and to explore the potential role of point-of-care biomarkers of acute brain injury as a future support tool for risk stratification.

abstract.label: MATERIALS AND METHODS
abstract.text: A retrospective, observational, and descriptive study was conducted using clinical records from the mobile emergency units of Cádiz and San Fernando over the full period from January to December 2025. A total of 107 episodes coded as traumatic brain injury were reviewed. After excluding patients younger than 18 years and cases with an initial Glasgow Coma Scale score of ≤13, considered non-mild traumatic brain injury for the operational purposes of this analysis, 91 adult patients with mild traumatic brain injury, defined as a Glasgow Coma Scale score of 14-15, were included. Demographic variables, cardiovascular risk factors, antithrombotic treatment, prehospital disposition, hospital referral, cranial CT, traumatic findings, observation, admission, and final outcome were analyzed. No GFAP or UCH-L1 biomarker measurements were performed in any of the included patients.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The mean age was 71.1 years (SD 20.5) and the median age was 75 years; 46 patients were male (50.5%). Hypertension was present in 57 patients (62.6%), dyslipidemia in 37 (40.7%), and diabetes mellitus in 30 (33.0%). Thirty-three patients (36.3%) were receiving antithrombotic treatment. Hospital referral was the predominant decision, with an overall rate of approximately 88%. Among the 80 patients evaluated in hospital, cranial CT was performed in 61 cases (76.3%). Most patients were discharged after emergency assessment or brief observation. Three patients required admission for traumatic neurological pathology, without neurosurgical intervention.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: In this series, hospital referral and cranial CT were frequent, whereas traumatic neurological admissions were uncommon. As no biomarker measurements were performed in this cohort, the potential role of GFAP and UCH-L1 should be interpreted in this study as a hypothesis for future prospective prehospital research rather than as a conclusion directly supported by the observed data.

articles.title: Occupational Health Interventions for Critical Incident Stress in Emergency Care Nursing: A Decision-Oriented Scoping Review.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: This scoping review examined occupational health interventions addressing critical incident stress in emergency care nursing, with particular attention to the timing and focus of interventions (pre-incident and post-incident), to describe current practice patterns and identify priority areas for occupational health decision-making.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This review was reported in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Extension for Scoping Reviews guidelines. Literature searches were conducted in PubMed, CINAHL, and Google Scholar for studies published from January 2015 to April 2025. Peer-reviewed English-language articles examining interventions for critical incident stress among nurses in emergency, trauma, or intensive care settings were included. Data on study characteristics, intervention timing, content, and outcomes were extracted and synthesized descriptively.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Seven studies met the inclusion criteria. Most interventions focused on post-incident strategies, with only 1 study evaluating a preventive approach. Three studies included elements of critical incident stress management, but these were used as partial or reactive solutions rather than comprehensive systems. Critical incident stress debriefing was the most common post-incident method reported to reduce isolation and facilitate emotional processing, although its effectiveness was inconsistent. Quantitative evidence was scarce, with most results being qualitative. The reported benefits included enhanced coping skills, increased well-being, and resilience.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: This review indicates that current approaches to critical incident stress in emergency care nursing are largely reactive, despite critical incident stress being a predictable occupational hazard. Preventive and organization-level interventions were rarely identified, highlighting an imbalance in existing occupational health practices. Although the evidence base remains limited, these findings help to describe priority areas for future occupational health planning and research, rather than recommend specific interventions.

articles.title: Point-of-Care Ultrasound of Upper Airway Changes During Cardiopulmonary Bypass in Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting: A Randomized Controlled Trial.

abstract.text: Background and Objectives: Elevated endotracheal tube (ETT) cuff pressure impairs tracheal mucosal perfusion and may contribute to upper airway soft-tissue changes. During cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB), the cuff usually remains inflated although ventilation is suspended, yet the relevance of cuff pressure management during CPB is unclear. We compared two ETT cuff pressure strategies during CPB (0 vs. 20-30 cmH2O) on point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) measurements of upper airway soft tissue in patients undergoing coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG). Materials and Methods: In this single-center, prospective, randomized, observer-blinded trial, 76 patients (ASA III-IV, aged 18-80 years) undergoing elective CABG were randomized 1:1 to a 0 cmH2O or 20-30 cmH2O ETT cuff pressure strategy throughout CPB (n = 38 per group). Transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) was not used in any patient. POCUS measurements of lateral pharyngeal wall (LPW) thickness, tongue thickness, parapharyngeal distance, midsagittal tongue area, and tongue width were obtained at four time points (T0-T3). The primary analysis was the omnibus group × time interaction for LPW thickness in a generalized estimating equations (GEE) model; the between-group difference in change from T0 to T2 was a planned supporting contrast. Results: All 76 randomized patients completed the study and were analyzed. The group × time interaction for LPW thickness was significant (p < 0.001); the between-group difference in the increase in LPW thickness from T0 to T2 was 1.50 mm (95% CI 1.27 to 1.73), and 1.00 mm (95% CI 0.82 to 1.18) at postoperative hour 2. Parapharyngeal distance and tongue thickness showed the same pattern. No multiplicity-adjusted between-group difference in LPW thickness was detected at T0 or T1, and a sensitivity analysis using the pre-intervention time point (T1) as baseline gave consistent results (T2 vs. T1: 1.43 mm, 95% CI 1.30 to 1.57). In an exploratory, unadjusted secondary analysis, difficult extubation occurred in 0/38 vs. 7/38 patients (absolute risk difference 18.4 percentage points, 95% CI 5.4 to 33.4; p = 0.012). Conclusions: Complete cuff deflation during CPB was associated with smaller ultrasonographic upper airway soft-tissue changes after CPB. The trial was not powered for clinical outcomes; the lower frequency of difficult extubation is hypothesis-generating, and these data do not support a change in routine practice before confirmation in trials with patient-centered endpoints.

articles.title: Repeated Internal Validation and Interpretation of Models Predicting Surgery Documented at a Study Institution Within 90 Days After Acute Knee Trauma: A Secondary Analysis.

abstract.text: Background and Objectives: A previous study using this cohort evaluated threshold-dependent performance and clinical decision utility for predicting surgery after acute knee trauma. This secondary analysis assessed the stability of discrimination, probabilistic accuracy, calibration, model ranking, and predictor importance under repeated internal validation. Materials and Methods: We analyzed 905 adults with acute knee trauma, including 163 (18.0%) who had a qualifying surgical procedure documented at the study institution within 90 days of the index emergency department visit. Logistic regression, random forest, and gradient-boosted trees were evaluated using 50 repetitions of stratified five-fold cross-validation with identical folds across models. Each patient's 50 out-of-fold predictions were averaged. Confidence intervals and paired model differences were estimated using 2000 patient-level stratified bootstrap resamples. Random-forest predictor importance was evaluated by validation-fold permutation. Results: Logistic regression and random forest had AUROCs of 0.762 and 0.757, AUPRCs of 0.430 and 0.443, and Brier scores of 0.125 and 0.123, respectively. Paired comparisons between these two models did not indicate statistically significant differences in any of the three metrics. Random forest had a higher AUPRC and lower Brier score than gradient-boosted trees. Calibration-in-the-large was close to 0 for all three models, whereas the calibration slope was compatible with 1 for logistic regression and random forest but was below 1 for gradient-boosted trees. Knee swelling, limited range of motion, and injury mechanism were the most influential random-forest predictors. Conclusions: Repeated internal validation did not identify a uniformly superior model. Logistic regression most often ranked first for AUROC, whereas random forest most often ranked first for AUPRC and Brier score; however, paired comparisons did not identify significant differences between these two models. External validation is required before clinical use.

articles.title: Low-Dose CT in the Age of Artificial Intelligence: Techniques, Evidence, and Clinical Impact.

abstract.text: Low-dose computed tomography (LDCT) is essential for reducing potential radiation-associated risks, but increased noise and artifacts can compromise diagnostic confidence. This review examines how AI is reshaping LDCT by improving reconstruction, denoising, protocol optimization, and workflow integration. It outlines the evolution from FBP to IR and then to deep learning methods that better preserve anatomical detail while reducing noise. The review also considers emerging applications in photon-counting CT (PCCT) and discusses clinical use in screening, pediatric imaging, oncology, cardiac imaging, and emergency care. These developments may support safer imaging, improve consistency across studies, and reduce the need for repeat examinations. However, important challenges remain, including limited generalizability across scanners and patient populations, the potential loss of subtle findings, changes in quantitative imaging features, and the need for careful validation before widespread clinical adoption. Further research should focus on multicenter validation, task-based performance assessment, and integration into routine clinical workflows.

articles.title: Enhancing High-Fidelity Simulation Flight-Based Training for Critical Care Paramedics in EMS Aviation: A Systematic Review.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: High-fidelity simulation (HFS) is used with critical care paramedics (CCPs) to enhance preparedness in high-stake scenarios. This systematic review aims to assess the evidence on the role and effectiveness of HFS flight-based training, evaluating its application in education for CCPs operating within emergency medical services aviation settings.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A systematic literature search was performed using a set of inclusion and exclusion criteria, resulting in 7 articles which were appraised using the Critical Appraisal Skills Programme tool.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: HFS training equips learners with skills relevant to their practice. CCPs register improved expertise, engagement and motivation, responsiveness, and general mood. There was insufficient evidence on whether this modality enhances self-awareness.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: HFS learning is feasible in training CCPs in emergency medical services aviation. However, there is limited evidence on the performance of CCPs trained using HFS learning in the prehospital setting. The findings suggest that standardizing training and assessment methods is recommended to optimize skill acquisition, improve team performance, and enhance patient safety in high-acuity emergencies.

articles.title: Relative Energy Deficiency in Sport and its Implications for the Foot and Ankle Surgeon.

abstract.text: Relative energy deficiency in sport (RED-S) is a syndrome caused by low energy availability that affects multiple physiologic systems in both male and female athletes. Stress fractures of the foot and ankle are often the first signs of RED-S; therefore, it is crucial that orthopedic surgeons are aware of and able to identify this disorder. This article focuses on RED-S and provides a framework for understanding the disorder, it's relevancy to the orthopedic foot and ankle surgeon, and offers suggestions for diagnostic strategies and treatment approaches that are imperative for safe return to play.

articles.title: Outcomes of Pediatric Surgeries for Dental Caries by Site of Care and Race and Ethnicity in the United States.

abstract.text: Purpose To compare outcomes of pediatric surgical procedures for dental caries performed in ambulatory surgery centers (ASCs) to hospital outpatient departments (HOPDs) within and across racial and ethnic groups in the US. Methods: This cross-sectional study, using 2016 to 2020 Medicaid data from 28 states, examined days from the last dental visit to surgery, payment, and postprocedure emergency department (ED) visits and hospitalizations. Regression compared outcomes in ASCs and HOPDs within and across eight racial and ethnic groups: Hispanic, American Indian and Alaska Native, Asian, Black, Hawaiian or other Pacific Islander, Multiracial, and White. Results: ASC use relative to HOPDs was associated with better or equivalent outcomes within each racial and ethnic group-meaning procedures in ASCs had shorter times from last dental visit to surgery (range=6.1 to 14.8 days sooner), lower payments (range=$42 to $1,010 less), and lower probabilities of ED visits and hospitalizations postprocedure than in HOPDs. Differences in outcomes associated with ASC (versus HOPD) use were experienced similarly across nearly all outcomes for all racial and ethnic groups compared to White children. Conclusions: Benefits to ambulatory surgery center use relative to hospital outpatient departments were observed among Medicaid-insured children across racial and ethnic groups. ASCs can improve access and reduce costs.

articles.title: Utilization of a Novel Inter-Specialty Consultation Service with Dentistry: A Descriptive Cross-Sectional Study.
